candidates.snippet:
Constellation Energy Corporation reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $1.835 billion, compared with $930 million a year earlier, as the company benefited from favorable market conditions and the addition of Calpine. The energy producer also raised the midpoint of its full-year adjusted operating earnings guidance while advancing major nuclear power agreements with Amazon and Google.
The post Constellation Energy: $1.8 Billion Q3 Net Income, Raised 2026 Guidance, And $5 Billion Nuclear Financing Commitment appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Constellation Energy: $1.8 Billion Q3 Net Income, Raised 2026 Guidance, And $5 Billion Nuclear Financing Commitment
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:01 AM
Constellation Energy: $1.8 Billion Q3 Net Income, Raised 2026 Guidance, And $5 Billion Nuclear Financing Commitment
Constellation Energy Corporation reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $1.835 billion, compared with $930 million a year earlier, as the company benefited from favorable market conditions and the addition of Calpine. The energy producer also raised the midpoint of its full-year adjusted operating earnings guidance while advancing major nuclear power agreements with Amazon and Google.
For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Constellation reported GAAP earnings of $5.19 per share, compared with $2.97 in the prior-year period. Adjusted operating earnings increased to $1.792 billion, or $5.06 per share, from $952 million, or $3.04 per share, a year earlier.
The company narrowed its full-year adjusted operating earnings guidance to $12.50 to $12.80 per share, raising the midpoint for the second time in 2026.
Constellation attributed its quarterly performance primarily to favorable market and portfolio conditions and the addition of Calpine, which it acquired in January 2026. Higher interest costs and unfavorable nuclear production tax credit portfolio effects partially offset those benefits.
Beyond its financial results, Constellation highlighted several agreements intended to expand electricity generation capacity and support growing demand from technology companies and other large energy customers.
In September, Constellation announced a 20-year, 690-megawatt power purchase agreement with Amazon, along with a related retail supply agreement supporting Amazon’s operations in the PJM electricity market. The arrangement will enable more than $3 billion in infrastructure investments at the Calvert Cliffs Clean Energy Center, including facility improvements and a 190-megawatt capacity expansion expected between 2030 and 2032.
In October, Constellation announced a separate 20-year power purchase agreement with Google supporting more than $4.3 billion in investments across 11 nuclear generating units in Illinois, Pennsylvania, and New Jersey.
The Google agreement is expected to add approximately 890 megawatts of incremental nuclear generation capacity to the PJM grid, with the first uprate scheduled for 2028. Constellation also entered into a 15-year financial energy load-following agreement with Google covering 2,700 megawatts.
Together, the Amazon and Google arrangements support more than 1,000 megawatts of additional nuclear generating capacity.
Constellation also signed a conditional loan commitment with the U.S. Department of Energy for up to $5 billion to finance nuclear uprates. Subject to execution of a final loan agreement, the financing would involve a 30-year loan from the Federal Financing Bank, backed by a federal guarantee.
The company additionally agreed to acquire the Rhode Island State Energy Center from Shell Energy North America for $715 million, subject to customary adjustments and regulatory approvals. The 609-megawatt natural gas-fired facility operates in the ISO New England wholesale electricity market and would become part of Constellation’s merchant generation portfolio.
Another development was Constellation’s first Peak+ agreement, a 20-year arrangement covering 270 megawatts of energy, capacity, and nuclear attributes beginning in 2028. Peak+ combines additional generation and demand-response capabilities with energy products tailored to large customers.
Operationally, Constellation’s nuclear fleet generated 46,677 gigawatt-hours of electricity during the quarter, compared with 46,477 gigawatt-hours a year earlier. Excluding its Salem and South Texas Project interests, its nuclear facilities achieved a 97.2% capacity factor, up from 96.8% in the comparable period.
Constellation operates a diversified generation portfolio totaling approximately 55 gigawatts of capacity, spanning nuclear, natural gas, oil, geothermal, hydroelectric, wind, and solar facilities.
KEY QUOTES
“This past quarter Constellation announced agreements that are helping meet one of the nation’s greatest challenges – powering a growing economy while protecting existing customers. These agreements add more than 1,000 megawatts of new, emissions-free generation to the grid and help ensure the continued operations of existing clean power for generations to come. The new megawatts, which are the equivalent of a new large-scale nuclear plant, are coming online with no costs being borne by existing customers. We’re building on that progress with Peak+, an integrated solution that brings together new capacity, including new generation and demand response, with energy products to help large customers meet their evolving needs. Our approach proves we can power the growing digital economy while strengthening our electric grid – all with private investment.”
Joe Dominguez, Chairman, President And Chief Executive Officer, Constellation Energy
“Third quarter adjusted operating earnings were $5.06 per share, compared with $3.04 a year ago. This strong performance allowed us to raise the midpoint of our adjusted operating earnings guidance range for the second time this year. Our disciplined capital allocation strategy, including accretive organic growth through nuclear uprates, the acquisition of Rhode Island State Energy Center and our continued aggressive pace of share repurchases, positions us to deliver sustained earnings growth.”
Shane Smith, Executive Vice President And Chief Financial Officer, Constellation Energy

candidates.text:
Pfizer: Up To $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement With Blackstone Life Sciences To Advance Monthly GLP-1 Obesity Drug
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 2:21 PM
Pfizer: Up To $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement With Blackstone Life Sciences To Advance Monthly GLP-1 Obesity Drug
Pfizer and Blackstone Life Sciences have entered into a strategic funding agreement under which funds managed by Blackstone will provide up to $1.5 billion through 2028 to support the clinical development of berobenatide, Pfizer’s investigational monthly GLP-1 receptor agonist for chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions.
The agreement will help Pfizer advance its obesity drug development program while maintaining financial flexibility to invest in other therapeutic areas. In exchange for its funding commitment, Blackstone will become eligible for milestone-based payments tied to U.S. regulatory approval and commercial performance.
Berobenatide is being developed as a potential first-in-class monthly injectable GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide. Pfizer is evaluating the treatment for chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions, including knee osteoarthritis and obstructive sleep apnea.
The transaction represents a significant investment in Pfizer’s cardiometabolic pipeline as the pharmaceutical company advances a broad portfolio of investigational obesity therapies.
How The $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement Works
Under the agreement, Blackstone-managed funds will cover up to $1.5 billion in development expenses associated with berobenatide through 2028.
In return, Blackstone will be eligible to receive payments if the drug achieves specified regulatory and commercial milestones.
These payments are contingent on U.S. regulatory approval of monthly injectable berobenatide monotherapy for chronic weight management and the achievement of certain sales targets.
Any milestone payments earned by Blackstone would be distributed over multiple years.
The structure allows Pfizer to obtain external funding for a major clinical development program without selling ownership or commercial rights to the investigational medicine.
Pfizer will retain full operational control and decision-making authority over berobenatide, including its clinical development strategy.
The agreement also does not provide Blackstone with an ownership interest in the drug.
Funds managed by Blackstone’s perpetual private equity strategy, BXPE, will participate alongside funds managed by Blackstone Life Sciences.
The arrangement illustrates an alternative approach to financing pharmaceutical research, in which investment firms provide capital to support clinical development in exchange for payments linked to future milestones.
For Pfizer, the agreement provides an opportunity to share development costs while retaining control over a potentially important pipeline asset.
Berobenatide Targets Monthly GLP-1 Treatment
Berobenatide is an investigational GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide being studied for chronic weight management and related medical conditions.
GLP-1 receptor agonists act on biological pathways involved in appetite regulation, blood glucose control, and other metabolic processes.
Existing treatments in this drug class have established a significant market for obesity and metabolic disease therapies.
Pfizer is developing berobenatide as a potential monthly injectable treatment, which could offer a different administration schedule from therapies requiring more frequent dosing.
The company is pursuing an extensive clinical development program to evaluate the drug’s safety and effectiveness.
Pfizer plans to advance more than 20 clinical trials involving obesity and associated medical conditions during 2026.
These include 10 ongoing and planned Phase 3 trials for berobenatide.
The studies are intended to evaluate the treatment across chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions.
Pfizer is also investigating berobenatide in combination with other investigational therapies.
The company is studying combinations involving nutrient-stimulated hormone peptides, including amylin analogs.
These approaches are part of Pfizer’s broader strategy to develop treatments that act on multiple biological pathways associated with weight regulation and metabolic health.
Berobenatide remains investigational, and its safety, effectiveness, and potential approval have not yet been established by regulators.
Expanding Pfizer’s Cardiometabolic Pipeline
Pfizer is positioning berobenatide as a central component of its cardiometabolic research and development portfolio.
The company is evaluating the therapy both as a standalone treatment and in combination with other investigational medicines.
Its development strategy extends beyond weight loss to conditions associated with obesity.
Knee osteoarthritis and obstructive sleep apnea are among the conditions included in the clinical research program.
Obesity can contribute to a range of medical complications, creating opportunities for therapies that improve weight management and potentially address related health outcomes.
Pfizer’s clinical program is intended to generate evidence about berobenatide’s potential across different patient populations and treatment settings.
The agreement with Blackstone provides additional resources to support this work through 2028.
Pfizer said the funding arrangement will also allow it to maintain capacity for investment across its broader pharmaceutical pipeline.
By supplementing internal research spending with external capital, the company aims to pursue multiple development priorities simultaneously.
Blackstone Life Sciences Expands Its Pharmaceutical Financing Partnerships
Blackstone Life Sciences provides investment capital and operational expertise to pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical technology businesses.
The platform manages approximately $18 billion in assets and invests across different stages of life sciences development and commercialization.

candidates.text:
Rowan Digital Infrastructure: $1.5 Billion In New Financing To Accelerate 5.5 GW Hyperscale Data Center Pipeline
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 3:43 PM
Rowan Digital Infrastructure: $1.5 Billion In New Financing To Accelerate 5.5 GW Hyperscale Data Center Pipeline
Rowan Digital Infrastructure, a Denver-based developer of hyperscale data center campuses, has secured more than $1.5 billion in new corporate financing capacity to accelerate development of its 5.5-gigawatt project pipeline across the United States. The financing includes a $600 million expansion of its holding company term loan led by Apterra Infrastructure Capital, along with a new $590 million revolving credit facility and a $355 million letter of credit facility led by Citibank.
The transactions provide Rowan with additional financing flexibility to secure land, obtain power commitments, purchase equipment, and advance early-stage development activities across its portfolio of hyperscale data center projects.
With the latest transactions, Rowan has secured more than $8 billion in financing from over 40 lenders during the past 18 months.
The company’s development pipeline includes multiple large-scale data center campuses designed to support major technology companies and hyperscale computing operators.
Rowan has already contracted more than 1.2 gigawatts of capacity with major technology customers.
The additional corporate financing is intended to help the company accelerate the development of new facilities while maintaining access to capital across multiple projects.
$600 Million Term Loan Expansion
Rowan expanded its existing holding company credit facility by $600 million, increasing the total facility size to $900 million.
The original $300 million facility was established in September 2025 to support early-stage development activities.
Apterra Infrastructure Capital served as lead arranger for the expanded financing.
The additional term loan capacity provides Rowan with resources to support project development before individual campuses reach the construction financing stage.
These activities can include land acquisition, infrastructure planning, engineering, permitting, and coordination with electricity providers.
Early-stage financing is particularly important in hyperscale data center development because projects can require significant capital commitments before construction begins.
Rowan’s expanded corporate facility allows the company to pursue additional opportunities while progressing existing projects through development.
New $945 Million Credit Facilities Led By Citibank
In addition to the term loan expansion, Rowan established two new corporate credit facilities totaling $945 million.
The financing consists of a $590 million revolving credit facility and a $355 million letter of credit facility.
Citibank served as lead left arranger and administrative agent for both facilities.
The revolving credit arrangement provides Rowan with access to liquidity that can be borrowed, repaid, and borrowed again as its project pipeline develops.
This structure is intended to reduce the need for the company to obtain separate financing for every new development site.
The letter of credit facility provides financial support for obligations associated with project development.
These can include utility interconnection deposits, equipment vendor commitments, and other collateral requirements.
Letters of credit can help developers satisfy certain financial obligations without immediately posting equivalent amounts of cash.
Both facilities include provisions allowing for potential future expansion.
Subject to applicable conditions, Rowan may increase the revolving credit facility to as much as $2 billion and the letter of credit facility to as much as $1 billion.
These potential increases are not part of the initially committed $945 million.
The lender syndicate includes Citibank, Mizuho Bank, MUFG Bank, Goldman Sachs Bank USA, Societe Generale, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, and Huntington National Bank.
Several participating banks have previously supported Rowan’s project-level financing transactions.
Supporting A 5.5 GW Data Center Development Pipeline
Rowan is developing a portfolio of hyperscale data center campuses across multiple U.S. markets.
Its pipeline totals approximately 5.5 gigawatts of planned capacity, with more than 1.2 gigawatts already contracted.
The company specializes in build-to-suit infrastructure designed to support hyperscale operators requiring substantial computing capacity.
These facilities typically require extensive electrical infrastructure, specialized cooling systems, and significant investment in equipment and construction.
Access to electricity and the ability to deliver operational capacity quickly have become increasingly important factors in data center development.
Rowan’s business model emphasizes securing strategic locations and coordinating infrastructure development to meet customer requirements.
The new financing will help support these activities across the company’s growing portfolio.
Rowan is actively developing campuses ranging from approximately 300 megawatts to more than one gigawatt in capacity.
The company’s broader strategy is supported by investment partnerships with Quinbrook and Blackstone.
More Than $8 Billion In Recent Financing Activity
The latest corporate financing transactions build on several major project-level funding milestones completed during 2026.
In May, Rowan secured approximately $2.9 billion for its 300-megawatt Temple data center campus.
The transaction represented the largest financing in the company’s history and was completed under Rowan’s Green Finance Framework.
Earlier in February, the company obtained $550 million in construction financing for its 300-megawatt Cinco campus in Medina County, Texas.
Rowan also secured $925 million for the third phase of its Bauxite development in Frederick County, Maryland.

candidates.snippet: Whitecap Resources raises 2026 production guidance and dividend after posting record Q3 funds flow of $1.2 billion Energies Media
candidates.text:
Oil & Gas
Whitecap Resources raises 2026 production guidance and dividend after posting record Q3 funds flow of $1.2 billion
By Kelly Lippke · November 15, 2026 · 8:45 AM · 5 min read
Written by Kelly Lippke
Calgary-based Whitecap Resources (TSX: WCP) posted Q3 2026 funds flow of $888 million USD (CAD 1.2 billion) — a company record, and a 32% per-share jump from the same quarter a year ago . Production averaged 390,720 boe/d, beating internal forecasts for the period.
Off the back of those results, Whitecap’s board raised full-year 2026 production guidance to 392,000 boe/d — the third upward revision of the year. They also bumped the monthly dividend about 1.5% to $0.046 USD ($0.0617 CAD) per share and approved a 2027 capital budget of $1.78–$1.92 billion USD (CAD 2.4–2.6 billion), targeting average output of 400,000–410,000 boe/d.
Q3 2026 production and financial results
Whitecap’s Q3 2026 output of 390,720 boe/d — 61% liquids — cleared internal forecasts and improved on the 374,623 boe/d from Q3 2025. Funds flow hit $866 million USD (CAD 1.17 billion) , or $0.71 USD ($0.96 CAD) per diluted share, a 32% per-share increase year-over-year. The headline number was strong, and the underlying details held up just as well.
The board raised the monthly dividend about 1.5% to $0.046 USD ($0.0617 CAD) per share, or $0.55 USD ($0.74 CAD) annualized, starting with the November 2026 payment.
Free funds flow reached $474 million USD (CAD 640 million) after $394 million USD (CAD 533 million) in capital expenditures. Through the first nine months of 2026, free funds flow totaled $1.41 billion USD (CAD 1.9 billion) — a solid cash generation pace for a company actively investing in growth.
Net income came in at $241 million USD (CAD 326 million), or $0.20 USD ($0.27 CAD) per share. A non-cash unrealized loss of roughly $222 million USD (CAD 300 million) on commodity contracts — driven by rising forward prices during the quarter — held that figure back. Stripping out that accounting item leaves an even cleaner underlying operating picture.
Drivers behind the outperformance
Several factors pushed production above forecast. Strong base and new well performance at Gold Creek and Kaybob Duvernay, combined with solid output from the Conventional division, moved volumes above plan. Higher light oil and condensate prices lifted realized revenues significantly — crude oil and condensate averaged $84.28 USD ($113.89 CAD) per barrel in Q3 2026, compared to $62.41 USD ($84.34 CAD) per barrel in Q3 2025.
Faster capital cycle times allowed Whitecap to run its drilling program ahead of schedule , and that efficiency showed up directly in per-boe operating costs: $7.56 USD ($10.22 CAD) in Q3 2026, down from $8.79 USD ($11.88 CAD) in Q2 2026. The company also commissioned the Lator 04-13 battery in early Q4 2026 — slightly ahead of schedule and within budget — securing a useful operational win heading into 2027. Related

Solar Wisconsin’s 1.3-GW solar settlement adds 750 acres of habitat safeguards and $1 million to protect greater prairie chickens
Updated 2026 guidance, dividend increase, and balance sheet
With Q3 momentum behind it, Whitecap raised full-year 2026 production guidance to 392,000 boe/d — the third upward revision of the year. That implied Q4 output of 395,000 to 400,000 boe/d. To support that pace, the company increased its 2026 capital budget by about $74 million USD (CAD 100 million) to roughly $1.63 billion USD (CAD 2.2 billion), with incremental activity focused on Kaybob, Lator, and Saskatchewan light oil assets.
The board raised the monthly dividend about 1.5% to $0.046 USD ($0.0617 CAD) per share, or $0.55 USD ($0.74 CAD) annualized, starting with the November 2026 payment. The increase added around $9.6 million USD (CAD 13 million) per year in dividend costs — modest, but a clear signal of confidence in the cash flow outlook .
The balance sheet improved substantially over the first nine months of 2026. Net debt fell by about $962 million USD (CAD 1.3 billion) since year-end 2025 to $1.55 billion USD (CAD 2.1 billion), putting the net debt-to-annualized funds flow ratio at 0.4 times. Whitecap’s undrawn $1.85 billion USD (CAD 2.5 billion) credit facility remains fully available, providing genuine financial flexibility heading into 2027.
2027 capital budget and production targets
The board approved a 2027 capital budget of $1.78 to $1.92 billion USD (CAD 2.4 to 2.6 billion), targeting average production of 400,000 to 410,000 boe/d at 60% liquids. On a per-share basis, that works out to roughly 3% annual production growth — or about 5% excluding a planned major turnaround at the Kaybob 15-07 gas plant in Q3 2027, which is expected to shave around 8,000 boe/d off the annual average .
The program includes drilling 127 Unconventional (Montney and Duvernay) wells and 205 Conventional wells, with about 75% of capital going to the Unconventional division. That segment is forecast to average roughly 265,000 boe/d in 2027 — up about 8% from 2026 — led by the Lator ramp-up and Kaybob capacity expansion to 135,000–140,000 boe/d by year-end 2027.
At US$80 per barrel WTI, Whitecap forecasts 2027 funds flow of about $3.03 billion USD (CAD 4.1 billion), generating around $1.18 billion USD (CAD 1.6 billion) in free funds flow after capital spending . That serves as the base case before any potential policy-driven uplift. Related

Databento raised $100 million in a Series C round that values the market data platform at $1.1 billion. The company, which employs 39 people, counts five of the six largest frontier AI labs among its enterprise customers.
Databento, a market data platform serving the financial industry, raised $100 million in a Series C round that values the company at $1.1 billion.
Fifth Down Capital, which first backed Databento before it generated revenue, led the round. Most existing investors returned, including NEA, DRW Venture Capital, Tribe Capital and Hedosophia. Fitch Ventures joined as a strategic investor, bringing the perspective of a large financial information business with experience in credit ratings, financial data and market analysis.
The round closed months after a $97 million Series B. Since that earlier deal, Databento more than doubled its revenue and stayed profitable.
Databento's customers include quantitative trading firms, brokerages, asset managers, commodities businesses and digital asset firms. The company also holds enterprise agreements with five of the six largest frontier AI labs.
The company employed 39 people when the Series C closed. It reached the $1.1 billion valuation with a workforce smaller than those of conventional market data vendors.
"In this AI era, we're seeing remarkably small teams build billion-dollar companies, but that level of efficiency is unprecedented in the market data industry. Until now, reaching this milestone required hundreds of employees given the sheer scale of physical infrastructure involved. I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished, and we'll continue to prioritize exceptional talent as we grow," Christina Qi, co-founder and CEO, said.
"Fifth Down first invested in Databento pre-revenue, as we recognized early on that the company had an opportunity to challenge the established model for delivering financial market data. Our confidence has only grown as Databento's traction and execution have demonstrated it can serve demanding institutional customers, sustain rapid growth, and build a profitable business. Databento's performance has reinforced our original thesis and strengthened our conviction in the company. We are thankful to Christina and Luca for the opportunity to increase our investment and involvement by leading the Series C financing," Andrew Spellman, founder and CEO of Fifth Down Capital, said.
Databento plans to spend the new capital on its market data infrastructure and on expanding coverage into more asset classes. The platform delivers live and historical data for futures, options, equities and indices through a single API. Because it controls each layer of its technology, from the original data source to final delivery, Databento says it is the first service of its kind to combine the speed and reliability that top trading firms require with a simpler experience for developers.

Plural Raises USD 1.1 Billion to Invest in Europe's AI, Robotics and Defense Startups
Plural, a UK venture firm, raised EUR 1 billion (USD 1.10 billion) for its third fund. Two-thirds goes to early-stage startups, and the rest backs current portfolio companies. It targets energy, AI infrastructure, defense and healthcare. Six tech founders and executives lead the firm.
Written By:
Murali Teja
Reviewed By:
Manisha Sharma
Published on :
16 Nov 2026, 12:35 pm
Updated on :
16 Nov 2026, 12:35 pm
Copied
UK-based venture capital firm Plural has raised EUR 1 billion (USD 1.10 billion) for its third fund. The money will back technology startups across Europe. The firm plans to focus on energy, AI infrastructure, defense and healthcare.
The new fund shows that investors are paying more attention to European tech. Many of them want companies that build tools for key industries.
Pural Sets its Investment Priorities
Plural will put two-thirds of the fund into early-stage startups. The rest will go to companies it already backs. This extra money will help them grow.
The firm wants to find startups that can become large businesses. Its list of interests is wide. It includes AI infrastructure, chip making, the factories that produce chips, robotics and defense technology.
The firm does not plan to bet on just one area. It wants to back founders who know their field well and who want to build companies that compete around the world.
Six Partners Lead Plural's Investment Strategy
A group of tech founders and business leaders started Plural in 2022. Since then, it has invested in several European companies . These include Helsing, Proxima Fusion, OLIX and The Exploration Company.
Six partners lead the firm. They are Taavet Hinrikus, who co-founded Wise, and Sten Tamkivi, who co-founded Teleport. Ian Hogarth, who co-founded Songkick, is also a partner. So is Khaled Helioui, a former chief executive of Bigpoint. Carina Namih, who co-founded HelixNano, and Pierre-Dimitri Gore-Coty, a former Uber executive, complete the team.
Hinrikus said the firm has no fixed view on which sector will produce the next big company. Instead, the partners want to work with founders who have deep knowledge of their own industries.

A Boost for Europe's Strategic Technology Ambitions
The new fund adds fresh money to Europe's startup scene. Its focus on energy, chips, robotics and defense also fits a wider need. Europe wants stronger industry and more control over key technology.
For founders, the news means more support is available as they try to grow. For Plural, it means more room to back new ideas and to stand by the companies already in its portfolio.

candidates.text:
Estonia’s Plural raises €1bn to back Europe’s next technology giants
Plural’s team. The Tallinn- and London-based investment firm has raised €1 billion to back European technology companies in sectors including defence, energy, space and artificial intelligence. Photo: Plural.
By
Silver Tambur
· November 16, 2026 · Business · 4 minutes of reading
Share
Tweet
LinkedIn
Email
Plural, the investment firm co-founded by Estonian entrepreneurs Taavet Hinrikus and Sten Tamkivi, has raised €1 billion to back a generation of European technology companies seeking to compete on the world stage.
The firm, which operates from Tallinn and London, will invest in businesses tackling some of the continent’s most demanding technological challenges, from fusion energy and artificial intelligence infrastructure to defence and space.
The fundraising is the largest in Plural’s history and, according to figures cited by the Estonian business newspaper Äripäev, exceeds the amount raised by the entire Baltic private equity and venture capital industry last year.
It also carries a broader ambition: to help Europe build more of the companies on which its prosperity and security depend.
“For two decades, most of the world’s most valuable technology companies have been built in the US and China,” Plural said in its announcement. “Europe has been a customer rather than a creator, and that has cost us prosperity and bargaining power.”
A billion-euro commitment
The new capital is almost four times the €260 million Plural raised for its first fund in 2022 and double the €500 million raised for its second in 2024.
It will be divided roughly two to one. The larger share will finance new early-stage investments through Plural’s third fund; the remainder will go into a separate fund designed primarily to increase its stakes in leading companies already in its portfolio.
Plural’s proposition is to support founders from the outset and continue backing them as their companies grow.
“For too long, Europe has funded its best ideas in small instalments,” Carina Namih, a Plural partner, said in comments reported by Äripäev. “Founders raise a little, prove a little and then have to raise again. That is no way to build something complex.”
A field test by Estonian defence start-up Frankenburg Technologies, one of the companies backed by Plural, which has raised €1 billion in new capital. Photo: Frankenburg Technologies.
The firm’s portfolio includes Helsing in defence, Proxima Fusion in energy, The Exploration Company in space and Frankenburg Technologies, the defence company with roots in Tallinn. Plural-backed businesses have raised more than €3 billion in follow-on funding over the past year, according to the firm.
Growing ambitions
For Estonia, the fundraising offers evidence that its technology industry is developing beyond the generation of companies that established its international reputation.
Hinrikus co-founded Wise and was Skype’s first employee. Tamkivi was an early Skype executive and later co-founded Teleport. Their investment firm now backs founders attempting to build businesses in fields far removed from money transfers and internet calls.
“Several of the founders behind that success are building companies again, this time tackling much tougher challenges. Global ones,” Tamkivi told Äripäev. “Frankenburg is a good example of how a company founded in Tallinn can become an international player in the defence industry.”
Half of Plural’s team is based in Estonia, according to Hinrikus, and its funds are licensed and regulated there.
“We can see first-hand that the quality of companies coming out of Tallinn keeps improving: they are exceptionally strong technically and think globally from the outset,” he said.
Taavet Hinrikus (left) and Sten Tamkivi. Photo by Takuya Sogawa.
The scale of the fundraising is striking in its regional context. A market review by KPMG Baltics and the three Baltic countries’ private equity and venture capital associations found that their funds raised a combined €749 million in 2025. Venture capital funds accounted for €247 million of that total.
Hendrik Reimand, chairman of the Estonian Private Equity and Venture Capital Association, said Plural’s success could help other local investment firms attract international backing.
“Major investors watch one another,” he told Äripäev. “Once one has decided that Tallinn can be a base for managing capital on a European scale, others will start looking more closely at our region too.”
The trillion-dollar ambition
Plural’s partners believe attitudes towards Europe’s most technically ambitious founders are changing.
“When we started Plural, a European founder building a fusion reactor or a space exploration company was considered too risky to back,” said Khaled Helioui, another partner. “Now they are among the most sought-after founders in the world.”
The firm believes such entrepreneurs could eventually build Europe’s first trillion-dollar company. Raising capital is only one step towards that ambition; turning complex technology into commercially successful businesses remains the larger test.
Plural’s stated goal, however, is deliberately bigger than the success of any individual investment: “GDP-level impact on Europe.”

Mirendil Raises $1B to Democratize Frontier AI R&D
News provided by
Mirendil
Nov 12, 2026, 12:30 ET
Share this article
Share this article
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, we're announcing that we've raised $1B in a Series A, led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, with participation from Battery Ventures, Doerr Capital, Gil & Co, Google, M13, Pear VC, and S32, among other new and existing investors.
We believe making AI R&D more accessible is the most direct path to AI that solves humanity's most pressing problems across science and technology. We're building tools to democratize frontier AI R&D and help put it within reach of every scientist and engineer.
Over the past three weeks, we've shared our first results, and they point to the same shift: when agents do the hands-on work, the size of your team stops limiting what you can build. One researcher, working with agents, pretrained Mirendil-Base , a competitive coding model, from scratch in 3.5 months with less than $10M in compute. We then post-trained it into Fern , which holds up to 10M tokens of context, enough for days of an agent's work. And Lor , now in private beta, brings this way of working to everyone else: hundreds of agents writing code and running experiments for days at a time. Mirendil runs on Lor every day.
This round lets us go further, toward a world where one person can take on what used to need a team, a team what used to need an institution, and we can help accelerate science and technology in a more direct way than we've done before.
We're still a small team with a singular focus. If you want to help make frontier AI R&D accessible to everyone, join us . If you'd like to build with Mirendil, we'd like to hear from you at [email protected] .

Key points
Mirendil raised a $1 billion Series A led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, with Battery Ventures, Doerr Capital, Gil & Co, Google, M13, Pear VC and S32 also investing; it did not disclose a valuation [1] .
The round follows a $200 million seed in June at a $1 billion valuation, co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins with Nvidia joining [5] ; reports in September said Mirendil was seeking up to $1 billion at a $5 billion valuation [6] .
Mirendil says one researcher working with agents pretrained its Mirendil-Base coding model from scratch in 3.5 months for less than $10 million in all-in compute, with agents writing more than 99% of the code [2] .
Its products are Fern, a model with a context window of up to 10 million tokens, and Lor, a private-beta platform that runs hundreds of agents writing code and running experiments for days [1] [3] [4] .
Mirendil, a startup founded by two former Anthropic researchers to automate the work of building AI, has raised $1 billion in a Series A round led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, the company said on Thursday, Nov. 12 [1] . Battery Ventures, Doerr Capital, Gil & Co, Google , M13, Pear VC and S32 also invested, along with other new and existing investors. Mirendil did not disclose its valuation [1] .
The round comes five months after a $200 million seed at a $1 billion valuation, which Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins co-led and Nvidia joined [5] . In September, reports said the company was in talks to raise up to $1 billion at a $5 billion valuation with Kleiner Perkins leading [6] ; Mirendil's announcement confirms the size and the lead but not the price.
One researcher, 3.5 months, under $10 million
Mirendil's pitch is that agents can now do most of the hands-on work of an AI lab, so a small team can build what used to take an institution. "When agents do the hands-on work, the size of your team stops limiting what you can build," the company wrote [1] .
Its main evidence is Mirendil-Base, a coding model it published results for on Oct. 21. Mirendil says a single researcher, working with agents, pretrained it from scratch in 3.5 months with less than $10 million in compute, a figure it describes as all-in, including the agents' token spend, data processing and every small-scale experiment [2] . Agents wrote more than 99% of the code, ran experiments and diagnosed failures, while the researcher decided what to try and what to trust; the company says it used only publicly available data, no distillation and no licensed datasets [2] . These are Mirendil's own figures and have not been independently replicated.
Mirendil then post-trained the base model into Fern, which it says can hold up to 10 million tokens in context, about half a million lines of code or days of an agent's work at once [3] . Fern 0.1 is listed at 0.1 to 0.5 trillion parameters, with access "coming soon"; larger Mirendil-Base-Large and Mirendil-Base-XL models, at up to 2 trillion and 10 trillion parameters, are still in pretraining [3] . The company corrected two figures in its Fern post on Oct. 27 to "more accurately reflect" its training results [3] .
Lor, the product it plans to sell
Lor, in private beta, is the platform Mirendil uses internally and wants to sell. It runs hundreds of agents at a time that write code, run experiments and iterate for days, provision their own GPUs and split jobs across dozens of sub-agents [4] . It works with outside frontier models, including Anthropic's Claude Opus and Claude Fable, OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra, and open models such as Kimi, DeepSeek and GLM, as well as Mirendil's own [4] . In one example, 102 agents built training environments from 100 PyTorch pull requests in an average of eight minutes each [4] .
Neyshabur, the chief executive, and Mehta met at Google in 2019, moved to Anthropic in late 2024 and left in December 2025 [5] . Neyshabur spent more than five years at Alphabet co-leading reasoning research for Gemini, and Mehta built the first version of Anthropic's internal AI-research platform [5] . Mirendil launched with about 20 researchers and engineers from Anthropic, xAI, Google DeepMind and OpenAI [7] , and it still calls itself "a small team" [1] .
The company frames its goal as handing frontier AI research to scientists and engineers outside the big labs [1] . That puts it in the most contested part of AI development: Anthropic has described recursive self-improvement, in which AI systems speed up their own development, as a potential danger, while Mirendil's founders call it the shortest path to faster science and a risk that can be supervised [5] . Thinking Machines Lab is chasing a related market; last week it released Inkling 2 Small, a model built to run AI training jobs ( our story ).

candidates.text:
CKX Lands: $1 Billion Brad Jacobs Investment To Launch New Public Company Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:15 AM
CKX Lands: $1 Billion Brad Jacobs Investment To Launch New Public Company Platform
Jacobs Private Equity II and minority co-investors have agreed to invest $1 billion in CKX Lands, creating a public company platform that Brad Jacobs plans to use to build a business in an industry that has not yet been selected.
Jacobs Private Equity will provide $900 million, while co-investors led by HRTG Partners will contribute $100 million. Jacobs Private Equity will hold a majority interest following the transaction.
Brad Jacobs will become chairman and chief executive officer of CKX while continuing to serve in the same roles at building products distributor QXO.
CKX will be renamed and operate as a separate public company. Before closing, it will convert from a Louisiana corporation to a Delaware corporation, complete a holding-company reorganization, and conduct a 4.1744380-for-1 reverse stock split.
The investors will receive voting convertible perpetual preferred shares convertible into approximately 219 million common shares at $4.57 per post-split share. They will also receive warrants to purchase approximately 219 million additional shares at exercise prices ranging from $4.57 to $13.70.
Following closing and before warrant exercises, Jacobs Private Equity and its co-investors will own approximately 99.78% of the company on a fully convertible and exchangeable basis.
CKX will declare a $20.8 million cash dividend, equal to $10.1312 per existing share, before the transaction closes. Existing investors will retain exposure to CKX’s land business while participating in the potential future company.
The board unanimously approved the investment, and shareholders representing approximately 28% of voting power agreed to support it. Completion is expected in early 2027, subject to shareholder approval and other conditions.
Jacobs has founded or led eight billion-dollar or multibillion-dollar companies and participated in approximately 500 acquisitions. The new platform would become his ninth company.
KEY QUOTES
“I love building multibillion-dollar market leaders, and this $1 billion investment marks the launch of my ninth company. After concluding my chairmanships of XPO, GXO, and RXO last year, I now have the capacity to create this new venture while continuing to lead QXO to its massive potential.”
Brad Jacobs, Founder of Jacobs Private Equity II
“We believe this investment will create compelling outcomes for our stakeholders, including the opportunity for our stockholders to receive a substantial upfront cash payment as part of a $20.8 million dividend. We expect our stockholders will benefit from retaining the value of our existing land business while also participating in the potential upside of Brad Jacobs’ future plans for the company.”
William Gray Stream, President of CKX Lands

Joanna Glasner

Want to keep track of the largest startup funding deals in 2026 with our curated list of $100 million-plus venture deals to U.S.-based companies? Check out The Crunchbase Megadeals Board .
This is a weekly feature that runs down the week’s Top 10 announced funding rounds in the U.S. Check out last week’s biggest funding deal roundup here .
It was another big week for AI-related startup financings. Mirendil , a developer of agentic AI for R&D, led the pack with a $1 billion series A, followed by Mercor , which secured $750 million to connect AI developers with human experts.
Overall, the vast majority of this week’s largest rounds were AI-related, though we did see some biotech, fintech and enterprise software in the mix.
1. Mirendil , $1B, AI for R&D: Mirendil, a developer of agentic AI technology for research and development, secured $1 billion in a Series A funding. Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital led the round for the San Francisco-based startup.
2. Mercor , $750M, human-led AI training: Mercor, a platform that connects AI developers with human experts for model training and evaluation, raised $750 million in Series D funding. The round, backed by a long list of venture investors, set a $20 billion valuation for the San Francisco-based company, which was founded less than four years ago.
3. Torus , $500M, AI infrastructure: Salt Lake City-based Torus, a manufacturer of distributed power and compute infrastructure, announced a $500 million growth financing led by Magnetar Capital . It also introduced a product called Foundry, described as modular AI infrastructure for inference compute.
4. (tied) Path Robotics , $300M, AI for manufacturing: Path Robotics, a developer of physical AI technology for robotics and manufacturing, with initial expertise in welding, picked up $300 million in Series E financing. Georgian led the round, which set a $2.45 billion valuation for the Columbus, Ohio-based company.
4. (tied) LangChain , $300M, agentic AI: LangChain, developer of a platform to run, improve and govern AI agents, closed on $300 million in Series C funding at a $3 billion valuation. CapitalG led the round for the 4-year-old, San Francisco-based company.
6. Nominal , $240M, hardware engineering tools: Nominal, a developer of intelligence tools for hardware engineering, raised $240 million at a $3 billion valuation. Lightspeed Venture Partners and Insight Partners led the round for the Austin-based startup.
7. (tied) Imprint , $130M, fintech: Imprint, a payments, loyalty and customer intelligence platform for brands, landed $130 million in new funding at a $1.9 billion valuation. Khosla Ventures led the financing for the 6-year-old, New York-based company.
7. (tied) Mavria , $130M, AI infrastructure: Mavria, a startup focused on standardizing how AI infrastructure is developed, built and deployed, launched publicly and said it has raised $130 million in pre-seed and seed funding to date. Its latest round, led by Paradigm , sets a $1 billion valuation for the startup, whose founders formerly worked at the U.S. Department of Energy .
9. (tied) Delix Therapeutics , $100M, biotech: Delix Therapeutics, a startup that says it has “reverse-engineered and optimized psychedelics” to develop treatments for psychiatric and psychological disorders, closed on $100 million in Series C funding. Johnson & Johnson Innovation and SV Health Investors ’ Dementia Discovery Fund led the financing for the Bedford, Massachusetts-based company.
9. (tied) Rox , $100M, sales automation: San Francisco-based Rox, developer of an AI revenue agent for enterprise sales, announced a $100 million Series B financing led by General Catalyst and March Capital .
9. (tied) Databento , $100M, financial market data: Databento, a finance data platform, secured $100 million in Series C funding at a $1.1 billion valuation. Fifth Down Capital led the round for the Salt Lake City-based company.
Methodology
We tracked the largest announced rounds in the Crunchbase database that were raised by U.S.-based companies for the period of Nov. 7-13, 2026. Although most announced rounds are in the database, there may be a small time lag, as some rounds are reported late in the week.

Corma Hits $1B Valuation on $125M Series A
Marcus Bell
Updated Nov 17, 2026 · 14 min read
Photo: Ynhockey, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
Corma, an Israeli-founded cybersecurity startup that builds AI models and agents for defense, has raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation, Ynetnews reported . NEA led the round, announced on November 16, 2026, and existing investors Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures and Coatue took part. The Corma $1 billion valuation arrives about three months after a $60 million seed round, which lifts total disclosed funding to $185 million.

Related Coverage
The company was founded in 2025 and works from Tel Aviv and San Francisco. That is a short road from founding to unicorn status, and it says as much about investor appetite for defensive AI as it does about any single product. This article sorts what the reports confirm from what they leave open, and it tells you which parts of the story are analysis rather than fact.
The timing matters. The deal lands in a week already crowded with large AI numbers, including our look at the Anthropic IPO and Nvidia earnings week ahead . Against that backdrop, a 2025-founded security company reaching a billion-dollar price tag will draw attention from buyers, rivals and other investors alike.

Corma Series A at a Glance: Round, Investors, Valuation
Start with the numbers that appear consistently across the coverage. The table below lists only the details that hold up across the available reports. Anything the reports do not settle stays out of it.
Item What the reports say
Company Corma, Israeli-founded, AI models and agents for cyber defense
Round $125 million Series A
Valuation $1 billion
Lead investor NEA
Participating existing investors Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, Coatue
Earlier funding $60 million seed, about three months before the Series A
Total disclosed funding $185 million
Founded 2025
Locations Tel Aviv and San Francisco
Announcement date November 16, 2026
The sums check out. A $60 million seed plus a $125 million Series A equals $185 million, and the Series A makes up roughly two thirds of everything the company has raised. If the $1 billion figure is a post-money valuation, which the reports do not specify, the new round represents about 12.5% of the company. Treat that last figure as arithmetic, not as a disclosed ownership stake.

Kalshi Raises $1B at $40B Valuation [2026]
Several practical details remain undisclosed. The reports give no revenue figure, no named customers, no headcount we can verify and no pricing. They also do not settle the official name of the product. One secondary report uses the label “Corma Workforce,” but its official status is unclear, so this article refers only to Corma’s models and agents.
How a $1 Billion Valuation Arrived in About Three Months
The headline on TechCrunch’s report captures the pace: a cybersecurity AI startup reaching a $1 billion valuation in about three months. Seed-stage companies rarely reprice that fast. Most security startups spend years proving that customers will pay before a late-stage investor writes a check at unicorn scale.
Two readings compete here. The optimistic one says investors saw early demand and moved quickly to secure a position in a scarce category. The skeptical one says a hot sector and a founder with a clear story can pull capital ahead of evidence. Public reporting does not let us pick between them, because no revenue, retention or deployment data has been disclosed.
The step-up in check size tells its own story. The Series A is about 2.1 times the seed, and the company has now raised $185 million in total. That is a large war chest for a business founded only a year ago. Money at that scale usually funds three things: compute, research talent and enterprise go-to-market. Which of those dominates the budget is unconfirmed, and spending breakdowns have not been disclosed.
Speed also changes the risk profile. A company valued at $1 billion after roughly a year in existence has little room to miss. Investors will expect visible customer wins within a few quarters, and the next financing round will price those wins hard. Founders in this position often find that the headline valuation helps recruiting and sales credibility, then hurts when growth normalizes.
NEA, Sequoia, Khosla and Coatue: Reading the Cap Table
NEA led the Series A. Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures and Coatue participated as existing investors. The mix is a mainstream Silicon Valley lineup, and it signals that the company is being priced as a platform bet rather than a niche security tool.

In Brief

3:32 PM PST · November 16, 2026
Image Credits: TechCrunch (AI-generated)
Julie Bort
Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months
Three months after introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corma has raised a $125 million Series A round at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA, the company said. Corma offers AI models and agents trained for cybersecurity defense. It has now raised a total of $185 million from backers, including Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Coatue.
The startup came out of stealth in August. Interest in its product skyrocketed after a series of security incidents sent chief information security officers scrambling on October 21 when a critical flaw was found in PHP , a popular web programming language. Another flaw was found in Node.js , the open source JavaScript runtime environment. Popular open source tool LiteLLM, a proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, also disclosed a security incident. Other incidents were disclosed that day, too. The day showcased the kind of onslaught on security that AI has enabled.
Corma isn’t the only company using AI to play defense. Other examples include Kevin Mandia’s new startup Armadin , as well as Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and other established players, and too many other startups to count. Still, it’s a young market and a necessary one. Corma says it stands out from the crowd by being a frontier AI research lab focused on protection.

Private equity firm EQT-backed Indian renewable energy platform Resolven on Tuesday said it has mobilised USD 900 million (about Rs 8,550 crore) financing this year so far, backed by an expanding lender base.
The funds have been mobilized from a set of 15 lenders including public sector banks, private banks, MNC banks and infrastructure financing institutions, a company statement said.
Resolven became an independent renewable energy company earlier this year.
Of USD 900 million, about USD 700 million is fund-based debt financing, and USD 200 million group level non-fund lines.
In March 2026, the company’s financing journey began with closing of Rs 450 crore refinancing of its 136 MW operating assets with an Infrastructure Debt Fund which reduced the company’s interest costs and locked-in fixed rates in a volatile environment.
Abhinav Agarwal, Chief Financial Officer, Resolven, said: "During the course of this year, we have been able to onboard several domestic and international lenders to back us on our growth journey. This is a reflection of our strong pedigree, robust governance and team’s execution capabilities. We are grateful for the trust placed by lenders on us and gives us the strength to deliver on what we have promised."
Resolven is targeting more than 1.5 GW of new renewable capacity annually across solar, wind, hybrid and battery storage, and aims to reach 10 GW by 2030.
It is powered by EQT, one of the world’s largest private markets firms, with 270 billion euros in total assets under management. Comments

candidates.snippet: Recognition comes amid a period of significant momentum for Positron, following its $875 million Series C and expanding AI inference deployments RENO, Nev., Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Positron AI, the AI inference hardware company built to make generative AI dramatically cheaper and...

Positron AI Named to the Inaugural 2026 AI 100 List of Top Private AI Companies
News provided by
Positron AI
Nov 12, 2026, 14:45 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Recognition comes amid a period of significant momentum for Positron, following its $875 million Series C and expanding AI inference deployments
RENO, Nev. , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Positron AI , the AI inference hardware company built to make generative AI dramatically cheaper and more energy-efficient, today announced it has been named to the inaugural 2026 AI 100 , the definitive ranking of the top 100 private AI companies in the world, published by Newcomer in collaboration with Bessemer Venture Partners .
The inaugural AI 100 recognizes leading private companies driving innovation across the AI ecosystem. Positron's inclusion reflects its progress in bringing purpose-built inference technology to market as growing AI adoption drives demand for more cost- and energy-efficient infrastructure.
"We're honored to be recognized among the companies shaping the future of AI," said Mitesh Agrawal, CEO of Positron AI. "Making AI inference profitable, scalable and accessible takes advanced technology and a business and supply chain built to serve some of the world's largest technology companies. Positron combines deep semiconductor and systems expertise with customer-driven development and investor backing to position us for growth. I'm proud of the business we're building as we serve customers today and develop our next generation of technology, and grateful to our team, customers, partners and investors for their support."
Positron's recognition follows a series of major company milestones. In September, the company announced an $875 million Series C financing at a $5 billion valuation to accelerate development of its next-generation Asimov silicon, ramp production of Titan and expand manufacturing capacity. Positron has also deployed more than 50 racks of Atlas, its first-generation inference system, at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Most recently, the company announced a partnership with General Compute, which is purchasing Atlas systems and has committed to adopting Titan to support next-generation AI workloads.
The inaugural AI 100 evaluated nominated companies and recognized category leaders across four factors: market leadership (35%), estimated valuation (30%), operating metrics (20%), and people & culture (15%). Only independent AI companies that have not had a majority strategic or private equity M&A transaction or a public listing were eligible. Honorees span foundation models, AI infrastructure and compute, developer tools and agents, AI apps, vertical AI, security, physical AI and robotics, and deeptech and AI for science.
"The artificial intelligence startup set plays by its own rules: there are upstarts with unprecedented revenue growth, companies profiting off of seemingly insatiable inference spending, highly valued speculative research labs, and wildly ambitious robotics companies. These AI native startups are already reshaping the global economy. With our friends at Bessemer, we rethought what matters for the AI age, bringing together the most promising startups harnessing foundation models to transform our digital and physical world," said Eric Newcomer, founder of Newcomer.
"The AI 100 puts a spotlight on the top 100 companies driving the AI economy forward, built by a generation of founders moving at a speed and scale we've never seen before. We're already seeing that exponential value creation play out across infra, AI applications, and physical AI. The remarkable part is that it's still early: this inaugural cohort is just the starting point, a natural evolution of our decade-long Cloud 100 franchise," said Byron Deeter, partner at Bessemer Venture Partners.
The inaugural AI 100 is published at ai100.newcomer.co , and was unveiled live onstage at the Cerebral Valley AI Summit in San Francisco.
About Positron AI
Positron AI builds hardware and software to make AI inference dramatically cheaper and more energy efficient. The company's shipping product, Atlas, is deployed at hyperscaler scale today, and its next-generation custom silicon, Asimov, tapes out in late 2026 with production in the second half of 2027. Asimov powers Titan, a multi-terabyte-memory inference system for long-context and next-generation AI workloads. Positron's energy-efficient architecture allows its systems to be deployed in air-cooled or liquid-cooled data centers at varying rack densities, without dependence on constrained HBM or CoWoS supply chains. Learn more at positron.ai .
About Newcomer
Newcomer is a media company covering the business of startups and venture capital, founded by independent journalist Eric Newcomer. We write a newsletter, produce a podcast, host technology summits, and more. https://www.newcomer.co/
About Bessemer Venture Partners
Bessemer Venture Partners helps entrepreneurs lay strong foundations from inception to build enduring companies. With more than 155 IPOs and 450-plus portfolio companies across industries, Bessemer supports founders and CEOs from seed through every stage of growth. Bessemer has backed industry-defining companies including Anthropic, Abridge, Canva, LinkedIn, Perplexity, Pinterest, RocketLab, Shopify, ServiceTitan, Toast, and Twilio, and has $20 billion of assets under management. Bessemer invests globally, with investment teams located in San Francisco, Silicon Valley, New York, Boston, London, Bangalore, and Tel Aviv. www.bvp.com

candidates.text:
Eldridge: Stonebriar Closes $869 Million Equipment Asset-Backed Securitization
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 2:47 PM
Eldridge: Stonebriar Closes $869 Million Equipment Asset-Backed Securitization
Eldridge Capital Management has announced the closing of an $869 million equipment asset-backed securitization by Stonebriar Commercial Finance, an Eldridge-managed company. The financing, designated SCFET 2026-1, represents Stonebriar’s 16th equipment asset-backed securitization and expands the firm’s access to capital for financing essential business equipment across multiple industries.
Eldridge Diversified Credit Fund II also participated in the transaction, bringing together two components of Eldridge’s diversified credit platform.
The securitization is backed by leases and loans secured by essential-use assets across the marine, mining, energy, manufacturing, and technology sectors.
These financing arrangements support businesses that require substantial capital investments in specialized equipment and other income-producing assets.
Asset-backed securitizations allow lenders to package financial assets into securities purchased by institutional investors, creating an additional source of funding for their lending activities.
For Stonebriar, the approach has become an established component of its financing strategy.
The latest transaction builds on approximately $11 billion of asset-backed securities placed through the platform since 2016.
Stonebriar’s securitization program supports its ability to originate large equipment financing transactions while managing funding costs and maintaining access to capital markets.
The participation of Eldridge Diversified Credit Fund II represents an additional opportunity to connect the firm’s private credit investment activities with Stonebriar’s established financing infrastructure.
Eldridge believes the arrangement can provide benefits to its diversified credit strategy by leveraging the funding capabilities Stonebriar has developed over the past decade.
The securities issued through SCFET 2026-1 received ratings from Fitch Ratings and KBRA.
Bank of America served as sole structuring agent and lead bookrunner for the transaction.
BNP Paribas, Truist, and Wells Fargo participated as joint lead bookrunners.
The financing highlights continued institutional demand for securities backed by equipment loans and leases involving essential business assets.
Since 2015, the broader Eldridge platform has originated more than $19 billion in large-ticket equipment finance transactions on behalf of Stonebriar and Eldridge’s diversified credit funds.
The platform finances assets supporting activities such as manufacturing, transportation, electricity generation, chemicals, and other capital-intensive operations.
According to Monitor’s 2026 rankings cited by Eldridge, the firm operates North America’s largest private, independent equipment finance platform by both assets and origination volume.
Eldridge manages a broader portfolio of businesses and investments spanning asset management, infrastructure, insurance, defense and security, minerals, and media.
The latest securitization provides Stonebriar with additional funding capacity while demonstrating how Eldridge can coordinate its equipment finance and private credit activities.
As companies continue investing in essential industrial and technology infrastructure, the transaction reinforces Stonebriar’s position as a provider of financing for large, mission-critical assets.
KEY QUOTE:
“Bringing EDCF II into Stonebriar’s financing technology is an innovative step for us. The EDCF program gets the benefit of Stonebriar’s cost-effective funding, built over a decade, and we remain grateful to the funding partners who have supported us in placing almost $11 billion of ABS bonds since 2016.”
Nicholas Sandler, Co-President And Co-Head Of Diversified Credit At Eldridge Capital Management

AEVEX Raises 2026 Revenue to $840 Million with Drone Growth
Published on: 14 November، 2026
AEVEX
AEVEX raised its revenue expectations to $840 million in 2026, with growing demand for drones and the expansion of autonomous marine systems.
American uncrewed defense systems company AEVEX has raised its 2026 revenue expectations to $840 million, after recording a 56.5% year-over-year growth in third-quarter revenue, signaling expanding military demand for drones and autonomous systems alongside the company’s expansion into maritime fields.
The company announced revenue of $189.7 million during the third quarter, compared to $121.2 million in the same period of 2025, while adjusted EBITDA rose to $30.8 million, compared to $17.8 million.
AEVEX raised its annual revenue guidance range to $820–$840 million, compared to $700–$720 million previously, and also increased its adjusted EBITDA guidance to $128–$132 million.
Growth Beyond Reliance on Ukraine Programs
One of the most significant shifts in AEVEX’s results is the growth of its core business outside of Ukraine programs, reflecting a broadening customer base and U.S. military orders.
Management stated that core revenue, excluding the Phoenix Ghost and EUCOM Deep Strike programs, reached $137 million in the third quarter, compared to $49 million in the first quarter of the year; new orders for core business also rose to $250.2 million during the third quarter, compared to $65.8 million in the first quarter, reflecting accelerating demand for the company’s systems.
According to management, core revenue surpassed Ukraine-related revenue for the first time since the second quarter of 2025 during the third quarter, marking an important shift toward a more diversified revenue base; the company expects Ukraine revenue of about $36.3 million in the fourth quarter before such revenue declines later, while targeting core revenue between $440 million and $460 million during 2026.
$400 Million Contract… But Actual Value Tied to Orders
AEVEX announced a multi-year U.S. contract with a ceiling value of approximately $400 million to supply uncrewed aircraft systems and related services. The contract represents a flexible framework allowing the customer to issue orders according to operational needs, but it does not mean the entire value has been funded or converted into confirmed revenue.
Management stated that it expects orders related to the contract to be issued during the upcoming period, with potential timing delays due to contractual procedures, but it views the agreement as bolstering revenue opportunities through 2027. The deal derives its importance from reflecting the shift in military demand toward systems that can be manufactured in large quantities and adapted to various mission requirements, rather than relying on fixed-use platforms.
BlackSea Expands AEVEX from Air to Sea
AEVEX’s acquisition of BlackSea Technologies represents one of the most prominent strategic shifts for the company during 2026, adding the marine systems sector to its portfolio and expanding its scope of activity from drones to surface and subsurface systems.
AEVEX expects the Maritime Systems sector to generate revenue of approximately $150 million during 2026, with continued growth the following year. The company relies on integrating autonomy, command, control, and mission planning technologies across its various platforms, allowing for the development of systems capable of operating in a more coordinated manner across air and maritime domains.
This shift represents an opportunity to expand the scope of contracts from selling platforms to providing software updates, mission packages, operational and maintenance services, and ongoing support.
U.S. Navy Continues Investing in Uncrewed Maritime Systems
Developments in the GARC contract illustrate the scale of commercial opportunity that may arise following initial platform deliveries; BlackSea completed the delivery of 325 uncrewed vessels to the U.S. Navy during 2025, in the first large-scale procurement of this class of vessels in U.S. Navy history.
However, investment did not stop at vessel delivery; the total contract value rose to approximately $350 million during 2026, following the addition of funding of nearly $135 million to upgrade systems and expand their operational capabilities.
Upgrades include transitioning to the Lynx architecture, adding autonomy and command and control capabilities, and integrating new mission packages, alongside continued vessel operation and support.
The company also secured a $41.6 million contract to provide GARC platforms and new marine systems with mine countermeasures packages, enabling the execution of integrated missions from mine detection to neutralization.
This reveals an economic model that goes beyond equipment sales, relying on upgrading existing platforms and turning them into multi-mission systems, creating additional revenue opportunities after initial delivery.
$16.6 Billion Pipeline… Future Opportunities, Not Confirmed Revenue
AEVEX’s volume of future commercial opportunities rose to approximately $16.6 billion, compared to $10.5 billion in the previous quarter, an increase of nearly 58%.
These opportunities include long-range drone projects, one-way attack systems, maritime systems, and support missions for several U.S. military commands.
However, this figure represents potential multi-year commercial opportunities, encompassing funded and unfunded programs, and does not represent confirmed contracts or guaranteed revenue.
In contrast, the funded backlog of contracts reached approximately $444.3 million at the end of the quarter, while the company holds about $1.1 billion in awarded contracts that have not yet received full funding.
Management expects to convert about $410 million of these unfunded contracts into revenue by the end of 2027, providing greater growth visibility without factoring in any new competitive contracts.

Sofinnova Partners, a European life sciences venture capital firm, has completed the final close of Sofinnova Crossover II at €725 million, equivalent to approximately $815 million. The fund exceeded its original fundraising target and will invest primarily in European clinical-stage biotechnology and medical technology companies preparing for later-stage development, global expansion, and commercialization.
The post Sofinnova Partners: $815 Million Crossover II Fund Closes To Back Late-Stage Life Sciences Companies appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Sofinnova Partners: $815 Million Crossover II Fund Closes To Back Late-Stage Life Sciences Companies
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:29 AM
Sofinnova Partners: $815 Million Crossover II Fund Closes To Back Late-Stage Life Sciences Companies
Sofinnova Partners, a European life sciences venture capital firm, has completed the final close of Sofinnova Crossover II at €725 million, equivalent to approximately $815 million. The fund exceeded its original fundraising target and will invest primarily in European clinical-stage biotechnology and medical technology companies preparing for later-stage development, global expansion, and commercialization.
The new vehicle is expected to support approximately 15 companies over its investment period.
While its primary focus will be Europe, the fund will also pursue selected opportunities in the United States and other international markets.
Sofinnova believes the successful fundraising reflects increasing investor confidence in European life sciences businesses developing technologies with global commercial potential.
The fund will provide capital to companies approaching important stages of clinical development and business growth.
Supporting Clinical Development And Commercialization
Life sciences companies frequently require substantial financing to advance experimental therapies and medical technologies through clinical testing, regulatory approval, and commercialization.
Sofinnova Crossover II is designed to support businesses during these later stages of development.
Its investment strategy focuses on companies with promising scientific foundations, clinical validation, and leadership teams capable of expanding internationally.
Sofinnova believes the European market is producing an increasing number of competitive healthcare companies that need access to substantial growth capital.
The firm’s investment approach combines financial backing with industry expertise and strategic support.
Building On Crossover I
Sofinnova’s first crossover fund invested in several companies that subsequently completed significant corporate transactions or public market milestones.
These include LimFlow, acquired by Inari Medical; Calliditas Therapeutics, acquired by Asahi Kasei; and Amolyt Pharma, acquired by AstraZeneca.
The portfolio also included Abivax, which achieved a Nasdaq listing.
These investments demonstrate the firm’s strategy of backing life sciences companies as they advance toward larger commercial markets.
Crossover II has already invested in Hemab Therapeutics, CellCentric, and Neurent Medical.
The fund will continue seeking opportunities among biotechnology and medical technology companies with differentiated products and clinical development programs.
Investment Leadership And Institutional Support
The Crossover II strategy is led by Sofinnova partners Joe Anderson, Kinam Hong, Cedric Moreau, Jacques Theurillat, and David Evans.
The fund is supported by the European Tech Champions Initiative, a fund-of-funds managed by the European Investment Fund.
Sofinnova Partners was founded in 1972 and operates from Paris, London, and Milan.
The firm has invested in more than 500 companies across its history and currently manages more than €4 billion in assets.
Its investment activities span life sciences and sustainability, from early-stage company formation through later-stage development.
The new €725 million fund strengthens Sofinnova’s capacity to support European life sciences companies seeking to compete internationally.
KEY QUOTES:
“The scale of this fund reflects both the maturity of the European life sciences ecosystem and the rising demand for capital that can help companies to reach global markets. Europe is producing a growing number of world-class life sciences companies, and we believe they should have access to investors that can support them through the critical stages of growth and commercialization.”
Antoine Papiernik, Chairman And Managing Partner Of Sofinnova Partners
“We continue to see exceptional opportunities emerging across European life sciences. Many companies now have scientific strength, clinical validation, and leadership teams needed to compete on a global stage. With Sofinnova Crossover II, we are well positioned to support that next generation of leaders while maintaining the disciplined investment approach that defined our first fund.”
Kinam Hong, Partner At Sofinnova Partners
