Agile Robots Hits $8.5bn Valuation as SoftBank and NVIDIA Back $500m Funding Round
The Munich-based robotics company Agile Robots has secured $500 million in fresh funding, putting it among Europe’s most highly valued private robotics businesses as investors look beyond generative AI towards industrial automation.
Munich, 15 November 2026 – Agile Robots , the German Physical AI company, has raised $500 million in a Series F funding round at a valuation of $8.5 billion , according to an announcement issued on 12 November.
Led by SoftBank Group, the round attracted investment from NVIDIA, Hitachi Group – including Hitachi and Hitachi Ventures – and T.Capital, among others. It brings the Munich-based company’s total funding raised to $2 billion.
The investment comes as the artificial intelligence industry increasingly turns its attention to machines capable of performing physical tasks. For Agile Robots, the challenge is no longer simply developing intelligent robotics technology, but producing and deploying it economically at industrial scale.
Agile Robots Funding: Key Facts
Company: Agile Robots
Headquarters: Munich, Germany
Founded: 2018
Funding round: Series F
Capital raised: $500 million
Company valuation: $8.5 billion
Total funding raised: $2 billion
Lead investor: SoftBank Group
Other investors: NVIDIA, Hitachi Group and T.Capital
Industry: Physical AI, robotics and industrial automation
Global deployments: More than 20,000 industrial robotic solutions, according to the company
Expansion plans: United States, Germany and additional international markets
Funding announcement: 12 November 2026
From Artificial Intelligence to Physical AI
Founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), Agile Robots develops robotic systems that combine artificial intelligence, sensors and precision engineering.
Its products range from industrial robotic arms and dexterous hands to mobile and humanoid robots, supported by proprietary software and AI models.
The distinction between conventional automation and Physical AI is commercially significant. Traditional industrial robots generally perform predefined tasks in structured environments. AI-enabled systems aim to interpret changing conditions and adapt their behaviour accordingly.
That could open up more complex activities in manufacturing, logistics and electronics assembly, where tasks have historically depended on human dexterity and judgement.
Yet technical capability alone will not determine adoption. Manufacturers must be convinced that these systems can operate safely, reliably and at a cost that justifies replacing or supplementing existing processes.
SoftBank and NVIDIA Back Industrial-Scale Robotics
SoftBank’s decision to lead the latest funding round, alongside NVIDIA’s participation, puts Agile Robots in the spotlight as investors seek commercial applications for artificial intelligence beyond software.
The new capital will finance international expansion, further robotics development and additional manufacturing capacity.
Dr Zhaopeng Chen, founder and chief executive of Agile Robots, sees Physical AI as a fundamental shift in how industrial work is organised.
“Physical AI will fundamentally change how the world builds, moves and makes things. Our vision is intelligent robots working alongside people in factories and warehouses everywhere, and Agile Robots is determined to lead that shift,” Chen said.
Dennis Chang, Managing Partner at SoftBank Investment Advisers, highlighted the importance of translating research into commercial deployment.
“We believe Physical AI will transform industries. Agile Robots combines deep robotics expertise with the ability to execute at industrial scale, enabling it to bring Physical AI into everyday operations,” Chang said.
The participation of prominent technology investors gives Agile Robots additional financial backing, although the announcement does not disclose individual investment amounts or the terms of the funding round.
Germany Remains Central to Manufacturing Plans
Agile Robots is investing in manufacturing capacity as it prepares for greater demand.
Earlier in 2026, the company opened a production facility in Fürstenfeldbruck, near Munich. According to Agile Robots, the site can manufacture up to 10,000 legged and wheeled humanoid robots annually.
That is a statement of production capacity, not confirmed annual output.
The distinction matters. Building a factory capable of producing thousands of advanced robots is different from securing sufficient orders, maintaining consistent production quality and delivering machines that operate economically in customers’ facilities.
Germany’s established engineering expertise and industrial supply chains provide a potential advantage, particularly as European manufacturers examine how automation could help address productivity pressures and labour shortages.
For Agile Robots, the immediate challenge is converting manufacturing capacity into sustained commercial demand.
An Established Industrial Business, Not Just a Robotics Concept
Unlike robotics ventures still primarily focused on laboratory prototypes, Agile Robots already operates across several industrial markets.
Its customers include businesses in automotive manufacturing, consumer electronics, logistics and other sectors.
The company reports more than 2,000 research and development specialists and a portfolio of over 650 patents.
It has also expanded through acquisitions, including Franka Robotics, known for its robotics research platform, and Krause Automation, an industrial automation specialist acquired from thyssenkrupp.

candidates.title: Agile Robots raises $500 million led by SoftBank
candidates.snippet: Agile Robots raises $500 million led by SoftBank CASRAI
candidates.text:
Munich-based Agile Robots announced on November 12, 2026 that it had closed a $500 million Series F led by SoftBank Group, with NVIDIA among the participants. The financing supports international expansion and manufacturing, putting fresh capital behind a robotics business whose research connections include Franka Robotics and a Google DeepMind partnership. Reuters confirmed the announcement .
A $500 million round for expansion and production
The round values Agile Robots at $8.5 billion and takes its total funding to $2 billion. Alongside SoftBank and NVIDIA, participants include Hitachi Group, comprising Hitachi and Hitachi Ventures, and T.Capital. The company’s November 12 announcement says the proceeds will support a larger presence in the United States, additional production capacity including in Germany, and entry into new markets.
Founder and chief executive Zhaopeng Chen described the financing as a way to accelerate expansion and bring intelligent robots into industrial production. SoftBank Investment Advisers managing partner Dennis Chang said Agile combines robotics expertise with industrial execution, adding: “We believe Physical AI will transform industries.” These are the company’s and investor’s expectations for the business.
Tech.eu’s November 12 report places the investment in an existing industrial operation: Agile’s machines assemble products, handle components, inspect equipment and move materials through factories. Its portfolio extends across robotic arms, hands, autonomous mobile robots and humanoids, together with their software and AI models.
Factory capacity and installed systems measure different things
Reuters reported that Agile opened its Fürstenfeldbruck factory, near Munich, earlier in 2026. The company says it can produce up to 10,000 legged and wheeled humanoid robots annually. That is a stated capacity ceiling, rather than a report of annual output or shipments.
Separately, Agile reports more than 20,000 robotic solutions installed worldwide. Its announcement describes deployments across automotive, consumer electronics, logistics and other industries; it does not identify that total as humanoid installations. Treating the two numbers as interchangeable would obscure the difference between the company’s established industrial business and its humanoid manufacturing ambitions.
The financing release also gives no allocation of the proceeds between the United States, German production and other markets. It therefore establishes the expansion priorities without quantifying how much additional capacity each location will receive.
A research spin-off with an academic hardware connection
Agile was founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center, according to Reuters and Tech.eu. The company reports more than 2,000 research and development specialists and over 650 patents. Its path from a public research institution into industrial automation provides a concrete technology transfer connection for universities following the investment.
There is also a direct research equipment link. Franka Robotics says it has belonged to Agile Robots since 2023. Franka describes its Research 3 system as a force-sensitive platform for robotics and AI, giving researchers low-level access to robot control and learning capabilities. Its website also says Agile’s Diana 7 now supports the Franka Control Interface, extending the ecosystem to a robot with greater reach and payload capacity.
The funding follows earlier DeepMind and NVIDIA announcements
The Series F is a financing development alongside earlier technical collaborations. On March 24, Agile announced a research partnership with Google DeepMind to combine Gemini Robotics foundation models with its hardware. The partners described an initial focus on industrial and manufacturing tasks, using deployment, data collection, training and iteration to improve their systems.
In that announcement, DeepMind robotics head Carolina Parada presented the collaboration as a step toward bringing AI into real-world applications across sectors. The research mechanism matters: operational robot data is intended to inform model development, rather than the partnership consisting only of installing a fixed model on a machine.
A separate Agile release published October 27 says NVIDIA announced plans to invest on October 19. It dates the introduction of the Agile ONE SN research humanoid at NVIDIA GTC Berlin to October 21. Those October events provide background to NVIDIA’s participation in the November round.
What this means for universities and research offices
For robotics laboratories, the connection is unusually specific: the funded group includes a research arm platform and is developing a humanoid reference platform. Agile says ONE SN uses NVIDIA’s Isaac GR00T development platform and Jetson Thor computing. Its October release also describes Diana arms supporting the Franka Control Interface, linking the company’s industrial portfolio to an interface already offered for research.
For research offices, the practical distinction is between investment, equipment access and collaboration terms. The March partnership explicitly involves operational data and model iteration. That makes data use and project outputs relevant subjects for a research collaboration agreement ; the Series F announcement itself does not supply those terms or announce university grants. This is an implication of the described research workflow, rather than a new funding opportunity for institutions.
The next stated milestone is early 2027
Agile’s October release places planned ONE SN availability in early 2027. It also describes a pilot involving Agile, Audi, Dassault Systèmes and NVIDIA at Audi’s Ingolstadt plant, where mobile humanoids pick and sequence parts. The company describes testing the workcell in a virtual twin before physical deployment.

SoftBank Leads $500 Million Funding Round for Agile Robots in Germany
By: Asia Business Outlook Team | Thursday, 12 November 2026
Japanese investment group SoftBank has led a US$500 million funding round in German robotics company Agile Robots , valuing the company at US$8.5 billion.
The funding round also saw participation from semiconductor company Nvidia , Japanese technology firm Hitachi and T. Capital.
The investment comes as interest in artificial intelligence and robotics continues to grow, with more companies looking to use these technologies in manufacturing and other industries.
Agile Robots plans to use the funds to expand its business in the United States, increase production in Germany and develop new industrial applications.
The company is looking to benefit from the growing demand for automation technology across manufacturing, logistics and other sectors. The investment is also expected to help it strengthen its position in the global robotics market .
Key Highlights
SoftBank Leads $500 Million Funding Round in German Robotics Firm Agile Robots
Agile Robots Reaches $8.5 Billion Valuation After SoftBank-Led Investment
Nvidia and Hitachi Join SoftBank in $500 Million Investment in Agile Robots
SoftBank and Nvidia Support Agile Robots' Expansion
Founded in 2018 by researchers from the German Aerospace Center, Agile Robots develops robotic systems that combine artificial intelligence with advanced hardware. Its products include industrial robotic arms , robotic hands, autonomous transport systems and humanoid robots used for different industrial applications.
The company has more than 3,500 employees across over 25 locations worldwide. It also says that more than 20,000 of its automation solutions are currently in use globally. Agile Robots holds over 650 patents related to its technology.
With the latest investment, the company has raised approximately US$2 billion since its establishment. SoftBank had previously led a US$220 million Series C funding round in Agile Robots in 2021, helping it expand its operations.
Nvidia's participation is another important part of the deal. The chipmaker has been increasing its investments and partnerships in robotics as it looks to expand the use of AI beyond computers and data centres. This includes physical AI , which allows machines to understand their surroundings and carry out tasks in the real world.
Agile Robots has also partnered with Google DeepMind to improve the capabilities of its robotic systems. The collaboration is aimed at developing robots that can perform more complex tasks in industrial settings.
Company Plans to Increase Production in Germany
Agile Robots will use the new funding to expand its operations in the United States and increase its manufacturing capacity in Germany. It also plans to develop more applications for its robotic systems as manufacturers look for ways to improve productivity and reduce manual work.
Earlier this year, the company opened a manufacturing facility in Fürstenfeldbruck, near Munich. The facility is designed to produce up to 10,000 humanoid robots annually. This will help Agile Robots increase production and prepare for growing demand.
The company sees humanoid robots as an important part of the future of industrial automation . Designed to work in spaces built for humans, these robots could be used in factories, warehouses and other workplaces to handle different tasks.
The investment also reflects SoftBank's growing interest in artificial intelligence and robotics. The Japanese group has been backing companies developing technologies that combine AI software with physical machines. Its agreement to acquire ABB's robotics division for US$5.4 billion is another example of its interest in the sector.
Agile Robots is entering a competitive market, with several companies investing in humanoid robots and industrial automation. As manufacturers look to improve efficiency and reduce operating costs, demand for these technologies is expected to increase.

With the latest US$500 million funding, Agile Robots plans to expand its international operations, increase production and develop more advanced robotic systems. Its ability to turn these investments into commercial growth will be important as competition in the global robotics market continues to increase.

Peak 10 Energy: $500 Million Facility To Finance Oil And Gas Acquisitions
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:14 AM
Peak 10 Energy: $500 Million Facility To Finance Oil And Gas Acquisitions
Peak 10 Energy has established a financing partnership with U.S. Bank that provides as much as $500 million for acquisitions of producing oil and gas assets across the U.S.
The acquisition finance facility will support Peak 10’s strategy of consolidating packages weighted toward proved developed producing properties. These assets have established production and can generate more predictable cash flows than undeveloped acreage.
U.S. Bank structured the facility to support later asset-backed securities issuances. That approach could provide longer-term institutional financing after Peak 10 completes and assembles acquisitions.
Peak 10 was founded in 2023 and has completed 12 acquisition and divestiture transactions involving operated properties, non-operated interests, and mineral assets across U.S. onshore basins.
The new facility will allow the company to pursue larger transactions and close acquisitions more quickly. Peak 10 said it encountered additional opportunities during 2026 that it could have acquired if the facility had already been available.
The company also maintains a commodity hedging relationship with U.S. Bank. Hedging can help stabilize cash flow from acquired properties and support financing by reducing exposure to oil and gas price volatility.
Peak 10’s strategy focuses on extending the productive lives of existing fields and infrastructure. The company expects this approach to support domestic energy production without depending solely on new exploration.
Legacy Star Capital Partners backs Peak 10 and views the combination of producing-asset consolidation and asset-backed financing as a long-duration investment strategy.
Petrie Partners originated the transaction and advised Peak 10. Baker Botts served as Peak 10’s legal adviser, while Haynes Boone represented U.S. Bank.

“This facility and our commodity hedging relationship with U.S. Bank give us the financial firepower to close acquisitions at a scale that matches the opportunity we see in the market.”
Kyle McQuire, Chief Executive Officer of Peak 10 Energy

William Eustis, Co-Head of Asset-Backed Securities at U.S. Bank

candidates.text:
VICI Properties: $500 Million Unsecured Term Loan Refinances 2027 Debt And Improves Revolving Credit Facility Pricing
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 5:35 PM
VICI Properties: $500 Million Unsecured Term Loan Refinances 2027 Debt And Improves Revolving Credit Facility Pricing
VICI Properties, a real estate investment trust specializing in gaming, hospitality, entertainment, and experiential properties, has secured a new $500 million unsecured term loan through its subsidiary VICI Properties L.P. The financing will be used to partially refinance the company’s outstanding senior unsecured notes maturing in February 2027, while an accompanying amendment reduces borrowing costs under its existing $2.5 billion revolving credit facility.
The new loan matures on January 31, 2032, extending a portion of VICI’s debt maturity profile by approximately five years.
The loan initially carries an interest rate of the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) plus 90 basis points, based on a pricing grid tied to the subsidiary’s credit ratings.
The agreement also includes an improvement in pricing when the company’s total leverage ratio is at or below a specified threshold.
VICI drew the entire $500 million at closing and entered into swap agreements covering the full principal amount.
These arrangements establish an effective all-in fixed interest rate of approximately 5.20%.
The financing will help VICI address a meaningful portion of its February 2027 debt maturity by partially redeeming and refinancing its 5.75% senior unsecured notes.
By replacing part of the approaching maturity with longer-dated financing, VICI is seeking to improve its debt maturity schedule and maintain financial flexibility.
The transaction also diversifies the company’s available funding sources.
Alongside the term loan, VICI amended its existing $2.5 billion unsecured revolving credit facility.
The amendment lowers the applicable interest rate from SOFR plus 85 basis points to SOFR plus 80 basis points, subject to the company’s ratings-based pricing grid and leverage-related adjustments.
The revolving facility’s borrowing capacity and maturity remain unchanged.
These changes provide VICI with improved pricing on a significant source of corporate liquidity.
Wells Fargo Securities served as sole bookrunner for the term loan, while Wells Fargo Bank acted as administrative agent.
Wells Fargo Securities, Mizuho Bank, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, and Truist Securities served as joint lead arrangers.
Additional participating financial institutions included Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase Bank, Capital One, Citizens Bank, Scotiabank, Barclays, Citibank, Goldman Sachs Bank USA, and Texas Capital Bank.
VICI Properties maintains one of the largest portfolios of experiential real estate assets in North America.
The company’s holdings include 103 experiential properties, comprising 63 gaming properties and 40 other experiential assets across the United States and Canada.
Its portfolio encompasses approximately 130 million square feet and includes more than 67,000 hotel rooms and over 700 restaurants, bars, nightclubs, and sportsbooks.
Major holdings include Caesars Palace Las Vegas, MGM Grand, and the Venetian Resort Las Vegas.
The company leases its properties to gaming, hospitality, and entertainment operators under long-term triple-net lease agreements.
VICI also maintains real estate and financing partnerships with operators across recreational and experiential sectors, including Great Wolf Resorts, Canyon Ranch, Kalahari Resorts, Club Med, Chelsea Piers, and others.
The latest refinancing supports VICI’s broader balance sheet management strategy as it continues operating and expanding its experiential real estate portfolio.
By extending debt maturities, securing a fixed borrowing rate, and lowering revolving credit facility pricing, VICI is strengthening its financial position while maintaining access to capital for future opportunities.
KEY QUOTE:
“We are very pleased to close this Term Loan, which diversifies our funding sources and addresses a meaningful portion of our February 2027 maturity at an attractive fixed cost and extends our debt maturity profile. We greatly appreciate the continued support and confidence of our bank group, and the improved pricing on our Revolving Credit Facility reflects the strength of our investment grade balance sheet.”
David Kieske, Executive Vice President And Chief Financial Officer Of VICI Properties

PARIS and SAN CARLOS, Calif. , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Genesis AI , a global robotics company, today announced it has raised $500 million in Series A funding at a $3.5 billion post-money valuation. The round was co-led by Premji Invest , Khosla Ventures and Eclipse , with participation from Durable Capital Partners , T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc. ¹, Bpifrance , HSG , NVIDIA , AMD Ventures , Zoom , Samsung Next and Ericsson , as well as visionary leaders including former Google CEO Eric Schmidt , Zoom CEO Eric Yuan , Jerry Yang, former CEO of Yahoo!, French tech entrepreneur Xavier Niel , and former Tesla CFO Zach Kirkhorn .
Continue Reading
Genesis AI co-founders Zhou Xian and Théophile Gervet announce the company's $500M Series A
"Our mission is to remove the physical limits on human ambition," said Zhou Xian , Co-Founder and CEO of Genesis AI. "To accomplish this, we're working to build the world's best general-purpose robot, one that works reliably in the real world, day after day. That requires the intelligence, hardware, and everything that goes into training and testing the robots to work as one system. By building it all ourselves, we can obsess over every detail and improve the entire robot faster in one closed loop. This funding will accelerate our efforts to deploy our robots in the real world at scale."
The funds will fuel the company's next phase of growth, with a focus on:
Expanding data acquisition and large-scale training to vastly extend the range and complexity of tasks robots can perform
Solving human-level physical manipulation in robots across a full range of environments and use cases, unlocking true physical AI
Deploying Eno , the company's AI-powered general-purpose robot, at scale with customers
Hiring additional world-class AI researchers, robotics experts and engineers to build the next generation of general-purpose robots
Advancing from Development to Deployment
"What stood out to us was watching Genesis robots complete long, multi-step tasks on their own at the same speed a person would, with smooth and natural movement," said Vedant Agrawal , Partner at Premji Invest. "Completing full tasks in real time, not just short clips, is what turns a robot into something a business can rely on."
"General-purpose robotics has the potential to fundamentally transform how we live and work, and Genesis is helping shape that future," said Eric Schmidt , former CEO of Google and Genesis investor. "I've believed in this team's vision since the beginning, and what they've accomplished in such a short time is extraordinary. This funding marks an important milestone as Genesis moves closer to bringing robots with human-level capabilities into the real world at scale."
Genesis is currently ramping up production of Eno, which the company is initially focused on rolling out in industrial environments including manufacturing, logistics and laboratories, before expanding into the hospitality and healthcare industries, followed by consumer and outdoor applications.
The Full-Stack Approach to Unlocking General-Purpose Robotics
As robots move from individual tasks to months of autonomous operation across entire workflows, reliability becomes a much harder challenge. The system is only as reliable as its weakest part, from hardware and controls to AI, data and evaluation. That's why Genesis builds the entire stack in-house: to optimize every layer together, avoid supplier constraints and improve faster in one closed loop. This integrated approach enables a seamless customer experience and a scalable robotics ecosystem serving a wide range of industries and applications.
"The next generation of robotics won't be built by improving hardware or AI models in isolation. It requires rethinking how AI, data and hardware work together," said Vinod Khosla , Founder of Khosla Ventures. "Genesis uniquely understands this, and its full-stack approach gives the company a real opportunity to solve the challenges that have held back general-purpose robotics for years."
"General-purpose robotics is a systems problem, and Genesis is attacking the whole system: a data engine built for massive scale, world-class simulation, human-like dexterity and Eno's remarkably beautiful form factor." Charly Mwangi , Partner at Eclipse. "Each layer makes the others better. But my strongest conviction is in the team. The talent density, speed of execution and obsessive attention to detail are exceptional. They understand the physics, sweat the details and build at a pace few teams can match. They far exceeded my expectations from a year ago."

GENE , its AI foundation model and the industry's most advanced robotic brain, enables robots with human-level physical manipulation capabilities to perform the most complex tasks ever achieved by robots .

MUNICH , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Munich-based Physical AI company Agile Robots has closed a Series F funding round, raising $500 million at a valuation of $8.5 billion. The SoftBank Group-led round, with participation from NVIDIA, Hitachi Group (Hitachi and Hitachi Ventures), T.Capital and others, brings the company's total invested capital to $2 billion.

Agile Robots’ $500M Series F announced on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) screens
Agile Robots builds and deploys Physical AI – humanoid and mobile robots, robotic arms and hands, and the software and AI models behind them – to help industrial customers automate tasks that have traditionally relied on human dexterity and judgment.
"Physical AI will fundamentally change how the world builds, moves and makes things," said CEO and Founder Dr. Zhaopeng Chen. "We bring Physical AI out of the lab and into industrial production, across logistics, automotive, electronics and manufacturing. This funding allows us to accelerate our global expansion, strengthen our presence in key markets and build out production capacity."
Building capacity and strengthening in strategic markets
Agile Robots plans to strengthen its presence in the United States and accelerate the development of innovative robotics applications. To expand capacity in Germany, the company opened a new production site in early 2026 at Fürstenfeldbruck, near Munich, with the capacity to produce up to 10,000 legged and wheeled humanoid robots annually.
"We believe Physical AI will transform industries. Agile Robots combines deep robotics expertise with the ability to execute at industrial scale, enabling it to bring Physical AI into everyday operations," said Dennis Chang, Managing Partner at SoftBank Investment Advisers.
Building on 20,000 deployed industrial robotic solutions
Founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), Agile Robots has deployed 20,000 industrial robotic solutions for customers in the automotive, consumer electronics, logistics and other industries. The company has over 2,000 R&D experts and over 650 patents. By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:51 AM
Ballistic Ventures: $490 Million Fundraising Target For Two New Cybersecurity Funds Amid AI Security Boom
Ballistic Ventures, a San Francisco-based venture capital firm specializing in cybersecurity investments, is seeking to raise $490 million across two new investment funds as artificial intelligence drives demand for technologies that protect businesses against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. According to a TechCrunch report , the firm has filed documents with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission seeking $360 million for its third flagship fund and an additional $130 million for a separate investment vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund B.
The regulatory filings indicate that neither fund had recorded any capital sales at the time of submission, meaning the amounts represent fundraising targets rather than completed capital commitments.
The proposed fundraising follows Ballistic Ventures’ earlier investment vehicles, including a $300 million inaugural fund announced in 2022 and a $360 million second flagship fund raised in 2024.
The firm also previously raised approximately $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund A, according to PitchBook data cited by TechCrunch.
The new fundraising initiative would provide additional capital for investments in cybersecurity companies developing technologies for AI security, enterprise protection, and emerging digital threats.
Ted Schlein And Cybersecurity Industry Veterans Lead Ballistic Ventures
Ballistic Ventures was founded in late 2021 by a team of experienced cybersecurity executives and investors.
Its founding team includes Ted Schlein, a former partner at Kleiner Perkins, where he spent more than two decades investing in technology companies.
Other founders include Barmak Meftah, former President of AT&T Cybersecurity, and Roger Thornton, who co-founded cybersecurity companies Fortify Software and AlienVault.
The firm’s leadership brings experience in cybersecurity company development, enterprise software, and venture capital investing.
Ballistic Ventures focuses specifically on cybersecurity, differentiating its investment strategy from firms pursuing opportunities across multiple technology categories.
Its approach emphasizes identifying companies developing technologies designed to address evolving security challenges.
The firm has developed a portfolio spanning enterprise security, AI-related threats, and other cybersecurity applications.
Previous Investments Include Talon And Pangea
Ballistic Ventures has backed several cybersecurity companies that have subsequently been acquired by major industry participants.
Its portfolio includes Talon Cyber Security, which was acquired by Palo Alto Networks.
The firm also invested in Pangea, a security company acquired by CrowdStrike.
These transactions illustrate Ballistic Ventures’ participation in companies developing technologies attractive to established cybersecurity vendors.
Other portfolio companies include Armadin, GetReal, Nudge Security, and Oligo Security.
The businesses operate across different areas of cybersecurity, reflecting the firm’s interest in emerging security requirements.
Ballistic Ventures’ investments also provide exposure to technologies designed to help organizations manage risks associated with increasingly complex software and IT environments.
The firm’s potential new funds would build on its existing portfolio and investment strategy.

AI applications can help businesses automate workflows and improve operational efficiency, but they can also create new vulnerabilities.
The growing deployment of autonomous AI agents introduces additional security considerations because these systems may interact with sensitive information, enterprise applications, and external services.
Organizations are increasingly evaluating security technologies that can monitor AI activity, control access to critical systems, and protect proprietary information.
At the same time, attackers are using AI to increase the speed and scale of malicious activities.
Microsoft’s October 2026 Digital Defense Report warned that cybercriminals are increasingly using AI for phishing, social engineering, and malware development.
Although many underlying attack techniques remain familiar, AI can make them easier to execute at greater volume.
These developments are creating opportunities for cybersecurity startups developing new defensive technologies.

According to a JPMorgan Chase report citing PitchBook data, U.S. cybersecurity startups raised approximately $11.5 billion in 2025.
That represented the industry’s highest annual fundraising total since 2022.
The report also highlighted the growing role of AI-enabled cybersecurity companies.
Through May 2026, AI-enabled businesses accounted for approximately 72% of U.S. cybersecurity venture deals, compared with 36% in 2019.
This shift indicates that artificial intelligence has become an increasingly important component of cybersecurity venture capital investment strategies.
Investors are backing companies developing AI-powered threat detection, automated security operations, and technologies intended to protect AI applications themselves.

Viasat: $450 Million U.S. Space Force Contract For Golden Dome Space Data Network Backbone Development
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:35 PM
Viasat: $450 Million U.S. Space Force Contract For Golden Dome Space Data Network Backbone Development
Viasat, a Carlsbad, California-based provider of satellite communications and secure networking technologies, has received an indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract with a ceiling of $450 million from the U.S. Space Force’s Space Systems Command (SSC). The award will support the development, deployment, sustainment, and operation of the Space Data Network Backbone (SDN-B) mission operations center, a critical component of the military’s efforts to establish resilient space-based communications infrastructure supporting Golden Dome for America and Joint Force operations.
The contract includes an initial $115 million task order to support development and scaling of the mission operations center and associated network operations capabilities.
The $450 million represents the maximum value available under the IDIQ contract rather than a guaranteed payment to Viasat. Additional work will depend on future task orders and government requirements.
The award positions Viasat as a network and mission systems integration partner supporting the Space Force’s efforts to establish a more interconnected and resilient military space architecture.
The SDN-B initiative is designed to provide high-capacity, low-latency data transport across multiple satellite networks and orbital environments.
Its architecture will support communications requirements for the U.S. Space Force, Golden Dome for America, and military operations conducted by the Joint Force worldwide.
Supporting The Golden Dome Space Data Network Backbone
The Space Data Network Backbone is a multi-vendor data transport architecture designed to connect and manage communications capabilities across participating space and ground systems.
The network is intended to provide resilient connectivity for military operations that depend on timely access to information collected and transmitted through space-based infrastructure.
Rather than relying on a single satellite operator or communications architecture, SDN-B is designed to integrate multiple providers and network elements.
This approach supports the Space Force’s broader objective of developing open architectures that can incorporate commercial technologies and adapt to changing mission requirements.
Viasat will focus on the mission operations center responsible for supporting network management and integration under government direction.
The center is intended to provide a coordinated view of participating SDN-B network elements, allowing operators to monitor connectivity, network performance, and operational status.
The infrastructure will also support government-directed prioritization of communications resources based on military mission requirements.
$115 Million Initial Task Order
The initial $115 million task order will fund work associated with establishing and scaling the SDN-B mission operations center and its network operations capabilities.
Viasat will apply its experience operating secure satellite communications networks to support the development of an enterprise-level operational infrastructure.
The company’s responsibilities include systems engineering, network integration, operational support, and sustainment activities.
The mission operations center will provide tools to manage participating connectivity services and support a common operational picture of the network.
These capabilities are intended to help military operators understand the status and performance of the communications infrastructure supporting their missions.
The contract also provides a framework for future engineering, operational, and sustainment work as the SDN-B architecture develops.
Additional task orders may support evolving requirements involving network availability, cybersecurity, and resilience.
Systems Engineering And Multi-Orbit Integration
A major component of Viasat’s responsibilities involves systems engineering and integration across space-to-ground communications interfaces.
The company will support the integration of multi-orbit connectivity services, helping participating satellite systems operate within a coordinated network architecture.
Multi-orbit communications can involve satellites operating at different altitudes, each with distinct characteristics involving coverage, latency, and available capacity.
Integrating these services can provide military communications planners with greater flexibility and resilience.
Viasat will also help establish enterprise network operations infrastructure to support the management of data transport services.
These capabilities will operate according to government-directed mission priorities.
The objective is to create an integrated operational environment capable of coordinating communications resources across multiple providers.
Common Operational Picture And Cybersecurity
The mission operations center will support a common operational picture that provides information about network health, status, and performance.
This capability is intended to help operators monitor network conditions and maintain awareness of participating SDN-B elements.
A coordinated operational view can support decisions about communications availability and the allocation of network resources.
Viasat’s responsibilities also include life-cycle engineering and sustainment support.
These activities will be performed according to government requirements and applicable future task orders.
The sustainment effort will address evolving needs involving network availability, operational resilience, and cybersecurity.
Because military communications infrastructure supports mission-critical information exchange, the ability to maintain secure and reliable connectivity is a central objective of the program.

The news: Quantum computing software company Q-CTRL has raised USD290 million ($415 million) at a valuation above USD1 billion in a series C round led by Salesforce Ventures.
The context: Q-CTRL’s products help make quantum computing useful by correcting errors and improving performance. It also builds Ironstone Opal, a quantum positioning system that enables geolocation without the need for GPS. Customers include Lockheed Martin, Airbus and IBM.
The round required two expansions to meet the level of investor demand. Among the new investors is the federal government’s National Reconstruction Fund, which has tipped in $70 million.
Other new investors include Affinity Partners, AMD Ventures, EDGE Group, MPower Partners and SPARX Asset Management.
Returning investors include Alpha Edison, Alumni Ventures, Bullhound Capital, DCVC, In-Q-Tel, Lockheed Martin Ventures, Main Sequence, Ridgeline, Salesforce Ventures, Salus Ventures and Square Peg.
What they said: “The investor syndicate we’ve assembled showcases the strength of our technology, revenue growth, and strategic alignment with some of the most important sectors today, from AI to aviation,” Q-CTRL CEO and founder Michael Biercuk said.
Salesforce Ventures partner Robert Keith said: “The hard problem in quantum is not building the machine, it is getting useful output from it. Q-CTRL solves that with AI-powered control software, and the proof is already public: a materials simulation on IBM hardware that any developer can now call directly from the IBM Quantum Platform, and the first quantum navigation system qualified for safety of flight.”
“That software layer will decide whether quantum shows up in enterprise data centers this decade, and it is why Salesforce Ventures led this round,” Keith said.
The sources: Q-CTRL media release , NRF media release

Science Corporation Raises $400M Series D to Expand PRIMA Access
Published
November 17, 2026
By
Evan Mercer, AI Startups & Venture Capital AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
Key Points Science's $400 million Series D funds European expansion of PRIMA while US approval…
View more
Science's $400 million Series D funds European expansion of PRIMA while US approval remains pending.
PRIMA is CE marked in the EU but still requires FDA Humanitarian Device Exemption review before US sale.
The biohybrid neural-interface program remains research-stage with therapeutic uses still undefined.
Science Corporation announced on November 17, 2026 that it raised a $400 million Series D to expand availability of its PRIMA retinal implant in Europe, prepare for a US launch, and increase investment in its biohybrid neural-interface program.
Khosla Ventures, the Ackman Oxman Institute, Tenet Healthcare, 885 Capital, Y Combinator and PLC Neurotech participated, among other investors. The round brings total capital raised since Science’s founding in 2021 to more than $900 million. The company will also expand its research, manufacturing and operational infrastructure.
PRIMA’s Commercial and Regulatory Path
PRIMA is a retinal implant being studied for geographic atrophy caused by dry age-related macular degeneration. Science describes it as the first brain-computer interface CE marked in the European Union to restore form vision—the ability to read letters, numbers and words—for patients blinded by certain types of late-stage macular degeneration. It is registered for supply in the United Kingdom and is not approved or available for sale in any other country.
The implant contains 378 light-powered pixels that convert light from the system’s glasses into signals that stimulate retinal cells. The glasses combine a front-facing camera with an eye-facing projector that shines light precisely onto the implant. The design is intended to replicate the function of light-sensitive cells that have been lost.
At 12 months, 80% of patients in the PRIMA clinical study showed clinically meaningful improvement in visual acuity, and 84% reported reading letters, numbers and words at home with the system, according to Science’s product page. The reported efficacy results include the use of digital zoom and contrast.
In a July 22, 2026 announcement , Science said PRIMA had received two FDA Humanitarian Use Device designations. The program provides expedited review for devices treating rare diseases or conditions, but designation is not marketing approval: PRIMA must still be reviewed and approved through a Humanitarian Device Exemption. One designation covers blindness in both eyes caused by an advanced subset of geographic atrophy, without vision loss from other eye diseases; the other covers vision loss from Stargardt disease, a rare inherited retinal disease. The US approval process remains underway.
Biohybrid Neural-Interface Research
Science’s biohybrid architecture takes a different approach from the retinal implant: it anchors hundreds of thousands of engineered neurons to a device and uses their projections to form connections with neurons in the brain. MicroLEDs stimulate the embedded neurons, which are modified through optogenetics so they can be activated by light, while electrodes record their activity. Science says the architecture can provide orders of magnitude more bandwidth than current devices while avoiding the damage and limitations associated with inserting wires into the brain.
The company describes language and communication, motor control, and learning and reasoning after brain injuries as potential research applications for the technology.
The financing therefore supports two distinct stages of development: commercial expansion of a retinal implant still seeking US approval, and continued development of a separate neural-interface architecture whose therapeutic uses remain research objectives.

candidates.text:
Zilch: £395 Million Debt Facilities Expand Consumer Lending Capacity
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 4:33 PM
Zilch: £395 Million Debt Facilities Expand Consumer Lending Capacity
Zilch has increased its securitization and corporate debt facilities by £165 million, bringing total commitments to £395 million as the payments company expands its product offering. Deutsche Bank led the latest financing, with participation from two major credit funds. The facilities will enable Zilch to originate up to £6 billion in lending annually.
The additional capacity supports customer growth and demand for products including Pay Monthly, launched in August 2026. That offering allows qualifying customers to spread purchases over three, six or 12 months.
Zilch is targeting a broader range of spending needs, including larger purchases such as holidays, household appliances and insurance premiums.
Average annual spending per active customer has reached £2,500, while the company’s gross merchandise value run rate has exceeded £3.5 billion.
The financing follows Zilch’s announcement that it surpassed a $300 million annual run rate and recorded two consecutive quarters of adjusted profit before tax in its 2027 financial year.
The company also plans to move into a new London headquarters in spring 2027, more than doubling its office capacity.
Founded in 2018, Zilch combines debit, credit, installments, earned wage access, credit-building features, offers and rewards within its payments platform.
The expanded funding facilities provide more lending capacity as that product mix develops. Management identified access to efficient funding as important to supporting higher transaction volumes and continued growth.
Chief Financial Officer Hugh Courtney said the financing reflects funders’ confidence in Zilch’s underwriting and ability to scale profitably in the United Kingdom.
The company’s strategy is to serve more customer payment needs through the same platform, strengthening engagement as users move between everyday spending and larger purchases.
KEY QUOTES:
“As we continue to grow at significant scale, having access to efficient funding is a key parameter for success. These expanded facilities give us greater capacity to support our customers where they need us, capturing more of the transactions that matter to customers day to day and providing the most rewarding ways to pay. By serving a broader range of customer needs, we can continue building a highly engaged customer relationship and delivering the value, flexibility and features that our customers really want.”
Philip Belamant, CEO And Co-Founder Of Zilch
“We are proud of our close partnerships with our funders, led by Deutsche Bank, who continue to support our growth as we scale the business profitably in the UK. The upsizing of the facilities represents a strong endorsement of our underwriting capabilities, product market fit and ability to continue scaling at pace.”
Hugh Courtney, Chief Financial Officer Of Zilch

candidates.text:
LPL Financial Brings In $390 Million Firm Contour Wealth Management
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 4:36 PM
LPL Financial Brings In $390 Million Firm Contour Wealth Management
LPL Financial has added Contour Wealth Management, a Pennsylvania-based financial advisory practice serving approximately $390 million in client assets, to its broker-dealer and registered investment advisory platforms. Financial advisor Joe Borgese, a certified financial planner, joins LPL from Cetera alongside a team focused on comprehensive financial planning and multigenerational client relationships.
Contour Wealth Management is based in Boyertown, Pennsylvania, outside Philadelphia.
The firm serves individuals and families, including educators, healthcare professionals, business owners, and clients across multiple generations.
Its planning approach emphasizes developing long-term relationships and adapting financial strategies as clients’ needs evolve.
Borgese began his career in financial services in 1990, initially working in banking before moving into other areas of the industry.
Over more than three decades, he has developed a practice centered on investment planning, retirement strategies, and broader financial guidance.
Contour Wealth Management works with some families across three generations, helping clients address financial needs ranging from retirement planning to college savings.
The practice begins each client engagement by establishing an understanding of the client’s goals, expectations, and personal circumstances.
Advisors then develop financial plans intended to adapt to changes involving careers, families, retirement, and other life events.
The firm’s services include financial planning, investment planning, and tax preparation, supported by working relationships with outside professionals.
The practice is supported by an experienced team that coordinates client relationships and ongoing financial planning needs.
Lindsey Borgese, also a certified financial planner, helps manage the office.
The team includes Diana C. Dugan, an enrolled agent, alongside Brian Christman, Cheryl Dietz, and Karen Walla.
Their responsibilities support client service, administration, and coordination across the firm’s financial planning activities.
Reasons For Joining LPL Financial
Contour Wealth Management selected LPL Financial based on its technology infrastructure, operational support, and advisor-focused service model.
The practice also identified potential cost efficiencies for clients as an important consideration.
LPL provides brokerage, advisory, technology, and practice management services to independent financial advisors and financial institutions.
Its infrastructure is designed to allow advisors to operate their businesses while accessing a broader range of investment products and operational resources.
For Contour Wealth Management, the transition provides access to additional technology and support capabilities while preserving its relationship-driven planning approach.
Borgese believes these resources will help the practice operate more efficiently and continue delivering personalized financial guidance.
The move also reflects the broader appeal of independent advisory platforms that allow practices to maintain their identity while benefiting from the resources of larger financial services organizations.
Financial advisors increasingly evaluate technology, compliance assistance, service capabilities, and operating costs when selecting affiliation partners.
LPL has been expanding its platform through the recruitment of independent advisors and advisory teams.
The company supports more than 32,000 financial advisors and the wealth management practices of approximately 1,100 financial institutions.
Its platform services and custodies approximately $2.6 trillion in brokerage and advisory assets on behalf of approximately eight million Americans.
LPL offers multiple advisor affiliation models, allowing practices to select structures aligned with their business needs.
Contour Wealth Management’s addition increases LPL’s presence in Pennsylvania while bringing an established practice with approximately $390 million in client assets.
The relationship will allow Borgese and his team to continue serving clients while using LPL’s technology, operating infrastructure, and advisor support resources.
KEY QUOTES:
“Our clients’ lives don’t move in a straight line, and their financial plans shouldn’t be static either. We start by understanding what they want their life to look like, then build a plan around those goals and continue adapting it as life changes. Our team has known many of these families for years, and in some cases across generations. That familiarity allows us to be there for the next decision, the next transition and the next step in their journey.”
Joe Borgese, Financial Advisor At Contour Wealth Management
“The biggest consideration for me was what this move could mean for our clients. LPL’s combination of technology, operational support and the team-based approach to supporting advisors gives us an opportunity to work more efficiently. Just as important, we believe this move can help us deliver value to clients while allowing our team to stay focused on the relationships we’ve built.”
Joe Borgese, Financial Advisor At Contour Wealth Management
“Contour Wealth Management, LLC has built a deeply personal practice around continuity, comprehensive planning and relationships that extend across generations. Joe and his team understand that every family’s path is different, and they have created an experience designed to evolve alongside clients through each stage of life. We’re pleased to welcome Contour Wealth Management, LLC to LPL and look forward to supporting the team with the technology, resources and operational scale to preserve those trusted relationships while building for the future.”
Marc Cohen, Chief Growth Officer At LPL Financial

candidates.title: Exus Closes $345 Million Financing Led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives
candidates.snippet: Exus Closes $345 Million Financing Led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives Hoodline
candidates.text:
Source: Nikki / Wikimedia Commons
Exus Renewables North America said Thursday it closed $345 million in senior secured holding company financing led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, money the company says will go toward construction and new U.S. wind, solar and battery projects.
The check is another in a run of company financings and project deals, not a map of which turbines or panels get the cash. Exus framed the close against rising U.S. electricity demand and described itself as an independent owner, developer and operator of utility-scale renewable energy and storage.
What the Money Is For
Exus said the financing will support construction costs and development across its growing U.S. portfolio of wind, solar and battery storage assets. The announcement does not name the projects that will draw on the facility or split the dollars among those three technologies.
President and CEO Jim Spencer said the financing lets the company keep its momentum going. He also said Goldman Sachs Alternatives' support reflects confidence in Exus and gives it flexibility to build projects and bring generation online, including work already underway and a deeper pipeline.
Vikas Agrawal, managing director and co-head of Energy Transition Climate Credit at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, said Exus has a strong platform for developing and operating utility-scale renewable projects. "We're pleased to support its continued investment in new energy infrastructure," he said, tying that support to growing U.S. electricity demand.
A Larger Company-Reported Book
Exus reported more than 800 megawatts operating or under construction and a total portfolio exceeding 6 gigawatts. Those are company figures, not an outside audit of nameplate capacity.
The comparison that is on the record is Exus' own July 22, 2025 financing announcement. Then, the company reported more than 5 gigawatts in its total portfolio and 764 megawatts operating or under construction, alongside $308.2 million in financing for the 185-megawatt Zia Solar portfolio in New Mexico and the 169-megawatt Keystone wind portfolio in Pennsylvania.
From that July 2025 snapshot to Thursday's release, the company-reported operating-or-under-construction figure moved from 764 megawatts to more than 800, and the total portfolio from over 5 gigawatts to more than 6. Exus also said it is expanding its operational footprint to meet growing national energy needs, with work that includes developing, repowering and managing renewable assets.
Separate Deals, Not One Stack
This holding-company financing sits beside other Exus transactions that the available reporting treats as separate. pv magazine USA reported in January that Exus had closed a $400 million senior secured corporate credit facility tied to a 4.5-gigawatt pipeline. Nothing in the Thursday announcement establishes whether that facility is still outstanding or how it relates to the $345 million.
Project-level money has also moved on its own track. On Sept. 22, Exus said it had completed the Highland North and Cambria wind repower projects in Cambria County, Pennsylvania, and that construction was financed through roughly $356 million led by KeyBanc Capital Markets. A week later, on Sept. 29, Exus and ibV Energy Partners announced that Exus had acquired four solar projects totaling 715 megawatts-peak.
Those deals show a company adding and rebuilding capacity in named places — Cambria County wind, a New Mexico solar book, Pennsylvania wind — while Thursday's $345 million is described only at the holding-company level.
Demand, Offices and the Close
Exus put the financing in a market it describes as tight on power. In the Cambria County release, the company said demand for clean power from data centers and other large energy users keeps climbing across that region. Nationally, a Jan. 13 Energy Information Administration release forecast the strongest four-year growth in U.S. electricity demand since 2000, fueled by data centers, and said solar would supply the largest increase in power generation, up a forecast 21% in both 2026 and 2027 after almost 70 gigawatts of new capacity. That is a forecast, not a reading of what Exus will actually build.
The company said it has more than 110 employees operating from offices in Pittsburgh, New York, Albuquerque and Connecticut. PEI Global Partners was financial advisor to Exus. Latham & Watkins LLP was legal counsel to Exus, and Vinson & Elkins LLP was legal counsel to Goldman Sachs Alternatives.
What Thursday actually puts on the table is $345 million of senior secured holding-company financing, led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, for construction costs and new wind, solar and storage development — with the project list still unstated.

Renewables
Exus Renewables North America Closes $345 Million in Financing to Support New Projects
Press Release
Monday, November 16, 2026
SHARE:
Exus Renewables North America, an independent owner, developer, and operator of utility-scale renewable energy and energy storage projects, has announced the closing of $345 million in senior secured holding company financing led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives. The financing will support construction costs and the development of new projects across Exus’ growing U.S. portfolio of wind, solar and battery storage assets.
The financing announced November 12 builds on an active year for Exus , including the closing of a $400 million senior secured corporate credit facility in December and approximately $356 million in project-level construction financing for its Highland North and Cambria wind projects in Pennsylvania in July . With more than 800 MW operating or under construction and a total portfolio exceeding 6 GW, Exus continues to advance its project pipeline amid rising U.S. electricity demand.
“We have projects moving forward and a deep pipeline behind them, and this financing lets us keep that momentum going,” said Jim Spencer, president and CEO of Exus Renewables North America. “The support from Goldman Sachs Alternatives reflects confidence in our team and our projects, and gives us the flexibility to keep building and bring new generation online where it’s needed.”
“Exus has established a strong platform for developing and operating utility-scale renewable energy projects,” said Vikas Agrawal, managing director and co-head of Energy Transition Climate Credit at Goldman Sachs Alternatives. “We’re pleased to support its continued investment in new energy infrastructure as electricity demand grows across the United States.”
PEI Global Partners served as financial advisor to Exus on the transaction. Latham & Watkins LLP served as legal counsel to Exus, while Vinson & Elkins LLP served as legal counsel to Goldman Sachs Alternatives.
—This content was contributed by the communications team for Exus Renewables North America .

candidates.snippet: Path Robotics raises $300M at $2.45B valuation to scale physical AI for manufacturing Ohio Tech News
candidates.text:
Startups + VC
Path Robotics raises $300M at $2.45B valuation to scale physical AI for manufacturing
Annual recurring revenue grew 17-fold over 18 months as the Columbus startup added industrial deployments. Customers include HII, Lockheed Martin and Saronic, while a $600 million performance-based shipbuilding agreement and plans to reach 400 employees by year-end underscore its growth.
Ohio Tech News
10 Nov 2026
— 3 min read
Share
Path Robotics co-founders and brothers Andy and Alex Lonsberry (Photo: Path Robotics)
Columbus-based Path Robotics has raised $300 million in Series E financing at a $2.45 billion post-money valuation to expand its robotic welding business and bring its artificial intelligence technology to more manufacturing tasks.
AI-focused growth equity firm Georgian led the round, announced Nov. 10, with participation from existing investors including Drive Capital. The financing brings Path’s total funding to more than $610 million since its founding in 2018, according to the company. Georgian partner Emily Walsh will join its board of directors.
The investment follows rapid commercial growth. Path said annual recurring revenue increased 17-fold over the past 18 months as it expanded deployments among industrial customers across North America.
The new capital will support additional deployments, development of new robotic platforms, and increased investment in computing resources and AI model training. In a LinkedIn post , CEO and co-founder Andy Lonsberry said Path plans to begin expanding its technology beyond welding into other production-line tasks in 2027.
“Our goal isn't to automate one step, but to automate the entire factory,” Lonsberry said in the announcement.
Scaling across shipbuilding and heavy industry
Path’s expansion targets a production challenge: manufacturers with demand for more products but limited capacity to build them.
The company develops physical AI—technology that enables robots to perceive their surroundings and adapt their actions to changing conditions. Its initial focus has been welding, where variations in parts and joints can make conventional, preprogrammed automation difficult to deploy.
Path said its customers include HII, Lockheed Martin and Saronic, along with manufacturers such as EK Machine, Millerbernd Manufacturing Company, TransAmerican Power Products and TYCROP. Its target industries include shipbuilding and defense, heavy equipment, and energy infrastructure.
Earlier this year, Path announced a $600 million performance-based production agreement with HII to accelerate deployment of its technology across U.S. Navy shipbuilding programs. That agreement is separate from the equity financing announced Nov. 10.
To support growing demand, Path said its workforce has increased 97% year over year, with plans to reach 400 employees by the end of 2026.
Taking its AI beyond welding
At the center of Path’s technology is Obsidian, a physical AI welding model that uses real-world production data to help robots identify weld joints, plan and execute welds, and adapt to changing conditions, according to the company.
Path recently introduced Rove, a mobile welding system that pairs Obsidian with a four-legged robot. The system is designed to bring welding capabilities directly to a part rather than requiring the work to take place inside a stationary robotic cell.
The funding will help Path extend its technology to additional robotic platforms and manufacturing applications.
Walsh said Path’s growing base of production data could help strengthen its technology as deployments expand, “The team has built a strong foundation in welding, and we see enormous potential for Path Robotics to extend that intelligence to new manufacturing applications and industries."
Other participants in the financing included existing investors Addition, IronArc Ventures, Tiger Global, and Yamaha Motor Ventures and its affiliates, along with D. E. Shaw Ventures and NAVER Ventures.
From an Ohio garage to the factory floor
For Lonsberry, the production problem has roots in his family’s Ohio manufacturing experience.
In his LinkedIn post, he said he learned to weld at age 8 in the family garage. His father later turned that garage into a manufacturing company in Warren, where Lonsberry saw firsthand the challenges of building a U.S. manufacturing business.
Before starting Path, Lonsberry said he and fellow co-founder and brother Alex Lonsberry spoke with more than 100 U.S. manufacturers. They repeatedly heard the same concern: backlogs were growing, but production was not.
“The challenge wasn't product demand. It was production,” he wrote.

candidates.title: Welding AI Maker Path Robotics Raises $300M Series E With NAVER Ventures
candidates.snippet: Welding AI Maker Path Robotics Raises $300M Series E With NAVER Ventures Wowtale
candidates.text:
Skilled welders are hard to find, and shipyards and heavy-equipment plants are sitting on full order books. Traditional industrial robots do not help much here. They follow pre-programmed paths, which makes them a poor fit for welds that differ slightly from one part to the next. Path Robotics , a Columbus, Ohio-based startup, is betting that a robot that can see and decide for itself can fill that gap. On Nov. 10, the company announced a $300 million Series E at a $2.45 billion post-money valuation.
Georgian , an AI-focused growth equity firm, led the round. NAVER Ventures and D. E. Shaw Ventures joined as new investors, and existing backers Addition, Drive Capital, IronArc Ventures, Tiger Global, and Yamaha Motor Ventures also took part. Georgian partner Emily Walsh will join Path’s board.
Giving the robot eyes and judgment
A conventional welding robot has to be taught its path step by step, and a part that sits slightly out of place can ruin the weld. Path’s physical AI welding model, Obsidian, takes that teaching out of the loop. The robot finds the weld joint on its own, plans the sequence and path, welds, and adjusts when conditions change mid-job. The model learns from real-world welding data. For a factory, that means variable welds without reprogramming the robot each time.
The company recently added Rove, a mobile welding system that puts Obsidian on a quadruped robot. Instead of bringing the part to a welding cell, the robot walks to the part. Path says it shows the same model can run on different robot bodies.
ARR up 17x in 18 months, led by shipbuilding and defense
Path says its annual recurring revenue grew 17-fold over the past 18 months, though it did not disclose a dollar figure. The growth has come from shipbuilding and defense, heavy equipment, and energy infrastructure. Customers include HII, the largest U.S. shipbuilder, Lockheed Martin, and the maritime defense company Saronic , along with mid-sized manufacturers such as EK Machine, Millerbernd Manufacturing, TransAmerican Power Products, and TYCROP. Earlier this year, Path announced a $600 million performance-based production agreement with HII to deploy physical AI across U.S. Navy shipbuilding programs. Headcount has grown 97% over the past year, and the company plans to reach 400 employees by year-end.
CEO and co-founder Andy Lonsberry said Path started with welding because it is one of the hardest jobs on the factory floor to automate. “Our goal isn’t to automate one step, but to automate the entire factory,” he said. Founded in 2018, Path has now raised more than $610 million. The new money will go toward scaling the welding business, expanding to tasks before and after welding and to new robot form factors, and training AI models.
Georgian pointed to Path’s proprietary models and its growing base of production data, which it said improves the system with every deployment. Lockheed Martin Ventures called the investment an important milestone for strengthening the U.S. defense industrial base.
Competition: welding specialists and general-purpose robot AI
A handful of newer companies are going after the same problem. Korea’s RB-Ware makes a no-code welding robot and has installed more than 250 units in 16 countries, and NeoArcRobotics is building cutting and welding robots for Korean shipyards. Augmentus raised $11 million to scale physical AI for robotic welding, and China’s LE Robotics raised tens of millions of yuan in a Series A+ round in February. None has raised anything close to Path’s total.
Others are chasing general-purpose robot intelligence rather than one task. Skild AI and Physical Intelligence are building foundation models meant to run on any robot, and defense manufacturer Hadrian raised $1.37 billion in a Series D in August to rebuild U.S. manufacturing capacity. Where those companies bet on a universal model or on the factory itself, Path is trying to perfect the hardest single process first and then extend to the steps around it.

candidates.snippet: Palantir Alumni’s Onodrim Raises $300 Million to Buy Up Europe’s Defense Suppliers www.trendingtopics.eu
candidates.text:
DefenseTech
Palantir Alumni’s Onodrim Raises $300 Million to Buy Up Europe’s Defense Suppliers
Jakob Steinschaden , co-produced by AI 09. November 2026, 09:06
Onodrim Industries raised $300 million in a Series A round. © Fred Hayes / Getty Images for Onodrim Industries
Set Trending Topics as a preferred source on Google.
Europe has a new defense unicorn, and it doesn’t build a single drone itself: Onodrim Industries, based in Amsterdam, has closed a $300 million Series A round. The company is now valued at $1.3 billion. Founded by former Palantir employees, it plans to use the money to take majority stakes in established suppliers to the defense, aerospace and manufacturing industries.
The Year’s Largest Series A
The round was led by Lux Capital, an early backer of Anduril, according to the company’s press release . New and existing investors including General Catalyst, Lakestar, Altimeter, Strike Capital, 137 Ventures, 8090 and Expeditions also took part. Onodrim says it is the largest European Series A of 2026. The company raised more than $45 million earlier this year.
The round ended up considerably larger than first planned. In late September, Bloomberg reported that Onodrim was seeking about 200 million euros at a $1 billion valuation.
Buy, Digitize, Scale
The business model looks more like private equity than a typical start-up. Onodrim plans to invest in manufacturers whose products have both civilian and military uses and that sit in the defense industry’s supply chains, where bottlenecks are currently common. The acquired companies are to receive long-term capital along with software and Onodrim’s own engineering teams, who will digitize production and develop new products so the companies can take on larger defense contracts.
Europe has many outstanding companies, but they often lack the resources to grow as fast as is now needed, said Aistis Šimaitis, Onodrim’s co-founder and chief executive. The company plans to announce its first acquisitions in the coming months. Its co-founder Alex Blessing is directly inviting owners of defense, aerospace and industrial businesses to get in touch.
Palantir DNA and an Office in Munich
Mr. Šimaitis previously advised the Lithuanian government, held a senior technology role at Palantir Technologies and earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford. Alexander Blessing, the chief technology officer, studied at Stanford and Cambridge and worked at Palantir as a forward deployed engineer, embedded directly with customers. The founding team also includes Christian Garrett, a partner at 137 Ventures. In addition to Amsterdam, London and Vilnius, Onodrim is now opening offices in Munich and Turin.
Investors are betting on the model. Europe needs a stronger industrial foundation to meet the security challenges ahead, said Brandon Reeves, a partner at Lux Capital. Jeannette zu Fürstenberg, president of General Catalyst, sees Onodrim as redefining the industrial conglomerate: Europe’s established manufacturers already have the expertise, customers and trust, she said, but they lack cutting-edge technology.
The Competition
Onodrim is entering a booming market. European defense tech companies are raising billions, led by Munich-based Helsing, which recently raised $1.8 billion at an $18 billion valuation , and Quantum Systems. Buying established manufacturers is not a new recipe either: Helsing has already acquired the Bavarian aircraft maker Grob Aircraft . But while most start-ups develop their own software, drones or systems, Onodrim is betting entirely on acquisitions in a fragmented supplier market where lead times are often measured in years.
Winning the Trust of Defense Ministries
Whether the bet pays off remains to be seen. According to The Financial Times, the open questions are whether venture capital can consolidate the supplier base quickly enough and whether defense ministries will trust a company founded only about a year ago. Defense contracts have historically gone to the large established prime contractors. On top of that, Onodrim has yet to complete a single acquisition. Its $1.3 billion valuation therefore rests mainly on its team, its investors and its promise to buy quickly in a capital-hungry market.
