The Institutional Infrastructure Battery Fund (IIBF) is launching as an infrastructure investment fund for institutional investors, specifically focused on large-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) in Germany. At launch, the fund has already secured its first two storage projects in central Germany under purchase agreements and has an identified project pipeline representing an investment volume of more than €300 million.
As renewable energy deployment progresses, large-scale battery storage systems are becoming an important component in stabilizing the German electricity grid and balancing volatile generation peaks. The IIBF translates this structural infrastructure need into an investment profile tailored to regulated institutional investors: the fund invests in a diversified portfolio of large-scale battery storage projects in Germany that are ready to build or close to their commercial operation date (COD) and holds them for the long term following acquisition. Early-stage project development and permitting risks therefore remain outside the fund.
Clearly defined responsibilities: institutional investment management and European energy trading expertise
The IIBF is built on a clearly defined division of responsibilities between two established specialists in their respective markets:
Investment management, underwriting and structuring by 2IP: Institutional Investment Partners (2IP) is responsible for investment management, transaction underwriting and institutional fund structuring. As the storage facilities are held throughout the fund's term, pre-acquisition due diligence is particularly important: 2IP assesses each transaction against clearly defined risk, financial viability and cash flow criteria, incorporates contractual security mechanisms and provides ongoing oversight through its portfolio and investment management.
Market access, asset management, software and energy trading by Second Foundation: As one of Europe's major technology-driven energy traders, the Second Foundation Group manages the energy-related and technological value chain surrounding the storage facilities. This ranges from direct project access and commercial and technical asset management of the facilities, through proprietary control and monitoring software, to high-frequency trading of capacity in the European electricity and balancing markets.
Contractually underpinned base distributions with additional market upside
The IIBF's income model is designed to cushion downside exposure to the volatility typical of electricity markets while also harnessing it for the portfolio. The core of the fund's income consists of long-term contractual usage fees (lease payments) for making the storage facilities available. Contractual advance payments and additional security mechanisms support the predictability of regular distributions to investors.
In addition, performance-linked remuneration components allow investors to participate directly in Second Foundation's trading performance in the electricity and balancing markets. As the majority of projected total income is generated continuously from ongoing operations during the holding period, the overall return depends only to a limited extent on eventual disposal proceeds at the end of the fund's term – significantly reducing terminal value risk.
First transactions totalling 55 MWh secured – focus on high system security
Portfolio construction begins immediately with two projects secured under purchase agreements:
Radis project (Saxony-Anhalt): 8 MW of power and 30 MWh of storage capacity; planned commercial operation date (COD) in October 2027.
Gößnitz project (Thuringia): 35 MW of power and 25 MWh of storage capacity; planned commercial operation date (COD) in November 2027.
Two further battery storage projects are already undergoing due diligence. During operation, all facilities are controlled and monitored in real time via Second Foundation's proprietary software platform. Secure system access and clearly defined control processes ensure a high level of operational security and protect the facilities against unauthorized access.
“With the IIBF, we are giving institutional investors structured access to an infrastructure asset class that is becoming increasingly important to the German electricity system. Under a long-term holding strategy, the stability of an infrastructure investment is largely determined at acquisition and through the design of its contracts. That is why, at 2IP, we combine institutional fund structuring with independent, rigorous transaction underwriting and ongoing investment management: by investing only from the ready-to-build stage onwards, insisting on robust security mechanisms and establishing a contractually fixed cash flow floor, we create a balanced relationship between the security of ongoing income and the opportunities offered by the German flexibility market,” says Jörg Homann, Managing Partner at Institutional Investment Partners (2IP).
“The economic success of a large-scale battery storage system is determined not by the physical asset alone, but by high-frequency trading, technology and intelligent control on a second-by-second basis. As an energy trader and software developer operating across Europe, we bring our proprietary control technology, asset management of the storage facilities and direct trading presence in the electricity and balancing markets together in a fully integrated operating model,” says Stephan Lehrke, Head of Second Foundation Germany.

candidates.title: LangChain Raises $300M Series C at a $3B Valuation Led by CapitalG
candidates.snippet: LangChain Raises $300M Series C at a $3B Valuation Led by CapitalG Wowtale
candidates.text:
AI agents are moving out of experiments and into day-to-day work, and building, running and watching them has become a new problem for companies. Picking a model is not enough. Teams need to trace why an agent got something wrong, catch performance slipping in production, and control which tools and data it can reach. LangChain , whose platform targets exactly that, has raised $300 million in a Series C.
From open-source framework to agent engineering platform
LangChain says its mission is to help every company own its intelligence. As agents transform the economy, it says, companies are building domain-specific agents differentiated by their knowledge, data and user experience, and the companies that control them will gain lasting advantages.
The product centers on LangSmith and rests on three pillars. Agent Runtime covers running agents reliably. Deep Agents, LangGraph and LangChain give developers flexibility across models and control over context. LangSmith Agent Server and Sandboxes deploy agents securely at scale in the cloud or a customer’s own environment, and Managed Agents and Fleet run mission-critical agents as managed services. Agent Improvement covers testing and monitoring. Observability and Evaluation show how agents behave and measure quality, and LangSmith Engine, an in-platform agent, finds errors, writes code and prompt fixes and watches production traffic for regressions. Fine-Tuning turns traces into training data for specialized models. Agent Governance gives central control over models, tools and data. LLM and Tool Gateways manage model budgets and fallbacks, protect sensitive data, and govern tool access and authentication.
More than 7,000 organizations already use LangSmith, according to LangChain, from fast-growing startups such as Harvey , Rippling and Listen Labs to Fortune 500 enterprises such as Nvidia , Toyota and Salesforce . Clay uses it to monitor hundreds of millions of agent runs a month. Workday uses it to run and govern agents across the organization, cutting the time to deploy a new agent from five months to under a day. These figures come from the company and have not been independently verified.
A side project that started weeks after ChatGPT
LangChain began within weeks of ChatGPT’s release in late 2022. Harrison Chase , then an engineer at Robust Intelligence, started it as a personal open-source project to fix a gap in large language models: they could not reach live information or take real actions such as web search or API calls. After founding the company with Ankush Gola, he raised a $10 million seed led by Benchmark in April 2023 and a $25 million Series A led by Sequoia in February 2024, at a $200 million valuation.
Valuation more than doubles in a year
LangChain said on Nov. 13 that it raised $300 million at a $3 billion valuation, bringing total funding to $460 million. Existing investor CapitalG led, with significant participation from new investors GIC and DFJ Growth and existing investors IVP and Sapphire Ventures .
New investors also include Salesforce Ventures , Insight Partners , QuantumLight and MongoDB Ventures, and existing investors Sequoia , Amplify and Benchmark returned. LangChain became a unicorn last October with a $125 million Series B at a $1.25 billion valuation, so its valuation has more than doubled in about a year.
Mo Jomaa, a partner at CapitalG, said the shift from experimental LLM applications to production-grade agents is among the most significant in enterprise software today. He said Chase and his team have built a foundational platform for agent engineering and earned the trust of thousands of developers and global enterprises. LangChain will show new LangSmith capabilities at a special release event on Nov. 20.
Competitors
In observability, Braintrust is a leading name. It measures and evaluates how AI models and agents behave in production, and raised an $80 million Series B in February at an $800 million valuation, led by ICONIQ. Langfuse , an open-source LLM observability platform, was acquired by ClickHouse in January, the same day ClickHouse announced a $400 million Series D at a $15 billion valuation.
On the development side, LlamaIndex builds an agent platform around unstructured data and raised a $19 million Series A led by Norwest Venture Partners in March 2025. Temporal , a durable-execution platform that keeps long-running agents going after interruptions, raised $550 million in a Series E in September.

LangChain Secures $300 Million to Advance Enterprise AI Agents
LangChain has raised $300 million in a Series C funding round at a $3 billion valuation, strengthening its position in the rapidly expanding enterprise AI agent market. The round was led by existing investor CapitalG , with significant participation from new investors GIC and DFJ Growth, alongside existing investors IVP and Sapphire Ventures.
The latest funding brings LangChain's total capital raised to approximately $460 million. The investment comes as businesses increasingly explore AI agents to automate workflows, develop intelligent applications and transform internal operations.
The company plans to use the funding to advance its mission of enabling every organisation to own its intelligence, with a focus on giving businesses greater control over the models, data and infrastructure powering their AI systems.
Expanding LangSmith's Enterprise AI Capabilities
At the centre of LangChain's strategy is LangSmith, its framework-agnostic platform designed to help organisations run, improve and govern AI agents.
The company reports that more than 7,000 organisations already rely on LangSmith, spanning fast-growing technology companies and large enterprises. Its customers include Harvey, Rippling and Listen Labs, alongside NVIDIA, Toyota and Salesforce.
LangChain is developing its platform around three core capabilities: Agent Runtime, Agent Improvement and Agent Governance.
Agent Runtime provides the infrastructure and tools required to build, deploy and operate agents reliably. Agent Improvement focuses on observability, evaluation and continuous performance optimisation, while Agent Governance gives organisations greater control over model usage, data protection, tool access and authentication.
These capabilities address some of the operational challenges businesses encounter when moving AI agents from experimentation into production environments.
Building Greater Control Over Enterprise Intelligence
LangChain's funding announcement reflects a broader shift in enterprise AI adoption, where the focus is moving beyond building AI-powered applications towards managing intelligent systems at scale.
The company believes domain-specific agents, differentiated by their knowledge, data and user experience, will play an increasingly important role in both standalone software products and internal business operations.
Its approach centres on giving organisations the flexibility to choose models, maintain control over their data and infrastructure, and continuously improve their agents without being restricted to a single model ecosystem.
LangChain also highlighted customer deployments that demonstrate the platform's enterprise applications. According to the company, Clay uses LangSmith to monitor hundreds of millions of agent runs each month, while Workday has reduced the time required to deploy a new agent from five months to under a day.
The company is also preparing to introduce additional LangSmith capabilities at a dedicated release event scheduled for November 20, 2026.
Investor Confidence in the Agentic AI Infrastructure Market
The Series C brings together a combination of existing backers and new institutional investors. Beyond the lead investors, LangChain also welcomed Salesforce Ventures, Insight Venture Partners, QuantumLight and MongoDB Ventures, while Sequoia, Amplify and Benchmark increased their investments.
The $3 billion valuation represents a significant increase from the $1.25 billion valuation associated with the company's previous $125 million funding round in October 2025.
The latest investment signals continued investor interest in the infrastructure supporting enterprise AI adoption, particularly platforms focused on making AI agents more reliable, observable and manageable in production environments.
About LangChain
LangChain develops open-source frameworks and enterprise tools that help organisations build and manage AI agents. Its product ecosystem includes LangChain, LangGraph and Deep Agents, alongside LangSmith, a platform for testing, deploying, monitoring and governing AI agents across their development lifecycle.

Q-CTRL: $290 Million Series C Funding Led By Salesforce Ventures Creates New Quantum Technology Unicorn
By Amit Chowdhry
Nov 14, 2026
Q-CTRL: $290 Million Series C Funding Led By Salesforce Ventures Creates New Quantum Technology Unicorn
Q-CTRL, a developer of AI-powered quantum infrastructure software, has raised $290 million (A$415 million) in Series C funding led by Salesforce Ventures, with significant participation from Bullhound Capital and Affinity Partners. The oversubscribed financing establishes Q-CTRL as a new quantum technology unicorn and provides capital to accelerate the commercialization of its quantum computing and sensing technologies across data centers, aviation, autonomous systems, and other industries.
The Series C round was expanded twice to accommodate investor demand and represents what the company describes as the largest fundraising round for a software-focused business in the quantum sector.
The investment will support Q-CTRL’s global expansion, continued development of its AI-powered quantum infrastructure platform, and commercialization of technologies designed to make quantum systems more reliable in real-world environments.
New investors include Affinity Partners, AMD Ventures, EDGE Group, MPower Partners, Australia’s National Reconstruction Fund Corporation, and SPARX Asset Management.
Returning investors include Alpha Edison, Alumni Ventures, Bullhound Capital, DCVC, In-Q-Tel, Lockheed Martin Ventures, Main Sequence, Ridgeline, Salesforce Ventures, Salus Ventures, and Square Peg.
The investor group brings together venture capital firms, strategic corporate investors, and institutions with experience across AI, aerospace, defense, semiconductors, and industrial technologies.
Combining Artificial Intelligence And Quantum Computing
Q-CTRL develops infrastructure software designed to improve the performance and reliability of quantum technologies.
Its platform uses AI-powered control techniques to address technical challenges that have historically limited the practical application of quantum computing and quantum sensing.
Quantum systems are highly sensitive to environmental interference, noise, and other sources of error.
These challenges can reduce the accuracy and reliability of quantum operations, making it difficult to achieve useful results outside carefully controlled laboratory environments.
Q-CTRL’s software is designed to mitigate these limitations through techniques that improve how quantum hardware operates.
The company takes a hardware-agnostic approach, allowing its technologies to work across different quantum computing and sensing platforms.
According to Q-CTRL, its software can increase the effective computational capabilities of quantum machines by thousands of times in certain applications.
The company’s strategy focuses on making existing and emerging quantum hardware more useful rather than developing competing quantum processors.
This approach positions Q-CTRL as a provider of infrastructure software that could support multiple participants across the quantum technology industry.
Salesforce Ventures Leads Major Quantum Investment
Salesforce Ventures led the financing based on Q-CTRL’s progress in turning quantum technology into practical commercial applications.
Robert Keith, Partner at Salesforce Ventures, highlighted the importance of software in enabling quantum computers to produce reliable, useful results.
He pointed to Q-CTRL’s work involving materials simulation on IBM quantum hardware as an example of commercially relevant progress.
The application is accessible through the IBM Quantum Platform, allowing developers to use the technology through an established quantum computing environment.
Keith also highlighted Q-CTRL’s development of a quantum navigation system that has achieved safety-of-flight qualification.
These achievements demonstrate the company’s focus on developing technologies that operate beyond research laboratories.
The investment reflects Salesforce Ventures’ belief that software infrastructure will play an important role in determining how quantum computing becomes integrated into enterprise data centers.
Q-CTRL intends to build on these capabilities as it expands partnerships with technology providers and commercial customers.
Ironstone Opal Enables GPS-Independent Navigation
One of Q-CTRL’s most important commercial products is Ironstone Opal, a quantum navigation system designed to function in environments where GPS signals are unavailable or disrupted.
The system uses quantum sensing technology to support navigation without depending on conventional satellite positioning signals.
Q-CTRL describes Ironstone Opal as unjammable, unspoofable, and undetectable, positioning the technology for applications requiring resilient navigation capabilities.
GPS disruptions can create significant operational challenges for aviation, autonomous vehicles, and other systems that depend on accurate location information.
Q-CTRL’s technology is intended to provide an alternative navigation capability in these environments.
The company says its proprietary software-ruggedization technology enables sensitive quantum sensors to perform in field conditions at levels 100 times better than the best alternative.
This performance improvement is designed to help quantum sensors operate despite environmental interference and movement.
Q-CTRL is deploying the technology in commercial aircraft and autonomous vehicles.
The company’s navigation capabilities are particularly relevant to aerospace and autonomous transportation applications where reliable positioning is essential.
Expanding Commercial Applications Across Industries
Q-CTRL plans to use the new funding to expand its technology into additional commercial markets.
The company sees opportunities in industries including finance, energy, aerospace, autonomous systems, and computing infrastructure.

candidates.title: Quantum Error-Reduction Software Maker Q-CTRL Raises $290 Million Series C
candidates.snippet: Quantum Error-Reduction Software Maker Q-CTRL Raises $290 Million Series C Wowtale
candidates.text:
Money is pouring into companies that build quantum computers. Oratomic raised a $475 million Series B in October, and Universal Quantum closed a Series A of more than $100 million. But whether qubits are made from neutral atoms or trapped ions, the problem is the same: they are sensitive to noise and make errors mid-calculation. Q-CTRL , an Australian company that sells software to reduce those errors, said it raised a $290 million Series C (A$415 million). It says the round makes it the newest quantum unicorn, though it did not disclose a valuation.
Software that makes other companies’ chips usable
Q-CTRL does not build quantum computers. Founded in 2017 by Michael Biercuk , a University of Sydney physicist, it sells software that helps machines built by other companies run better. It pitches a hardware-agnostic design that is not tied to any one qubit technology.
It has two main products. Fire Opal is cloud software that automatically shortens the quantum circuits a developer writes, maps them onto a chip according to each machine’s error profile and corrects measurement errors before returning results. It runs on IBM’s quantum service, IonQ and Rigetti systems and Amazon Braket, among others, and the company claims it can run circuits up to 10 times deeper on the same hardware. Boulder Opal is for those who build or operate quantum computers. Even after it is switched on, a quantum computer needs its control signals tuned qubit by qubit, and the product automates that calibration and upkeep without a team of physicists. It supports superconducting and semiconductor spin-qubit machines, with trapped-ion and neutral-atom support available on request, the company says. Its target customers are chipmakers and data center and HPC operators. In computing, the company also claims a 3,000x speedup in materials discovery for the energy sector.
The third business pairs software with sensors. Ironstone Opal is a navigation system for places where GPS is unavailable or jammed. It measures tiny variations in the Earth’s magnetic field and matches them against a magnetic map to find its position. The company builds the quantum magnetometers itself, and AI software filters out the magnetic interference the aircraft generates. The company says the system is 100 times better than the best alternative, but in its published flight trial it reported up to 50 times lower positioning uncertainty than an inertial navigation system. It says Ironstone Opal is being deployed on commercial aircraft with Airbus, on autonomous platforms with Lockheed Martin and on drones. All performance figures come from the company.
Led by Salesforce Ventures, expanded twice
Salesforce Ventures led the round, with Bullhound Capital and Affinity Partners named as headline participants. The company says it expanded the round twice to meet investor demand and calls it the largest raise by a software-focused quantum company. Q-CTRL expanded its Series B to $113 million in October 2024.
New investors are Affinity Partners, AMD Ventures, EDGE Group, MPower Partners, Australia’s National Reconstruction Fund Corporation and SPARX Asset Management. Returning investors are Alpha Edison, Alumni Ventures, Bullhound Capital, DCVC, In-Q-Tel, Lockheed Martin Ventures, Main Sequence, Ridgeline, Salesforce Ventures, Salus Ventures and Square Peg. The company says the mix of strategic, private equity and growth-stage venture investors positions it to scale through joint sales, technology integration and direct revenue.
Salesforce Ventures said the hard problem in quantum is getting useful output from the machine, not building it. It pointed to a materials simulation run on IBM hardware that developers can call directly from the IBM Quantum Platform, and to what it described as the first quantum navigation system qualified for safety of flight. Bullhound called Q-CTRL one of the few quantum companies with real customers and real revenue, and MPower Partners said it wants to help expand the company’s footprint in Japan.
Q-CTRL plans to use the funds to double down on software, scale globally across sectors such as finance and energy, and continue its autonomy and aerospace programs. Biercuk said the company’s core value is delivering real customer value from quantum technology, which is why it focuses on infrastructure software. The company did not disclose revenue, total funding to date or customer counts.
Competitors: the same software layer, and hardware makers building their own
Q-CTRL’s pitch is that errors remain no matter which qubit technology wins. The quantum computer makers Wowtale has covered span neutral atoms (Oratomic and Atom Computing ), trapped ions (Universal Quantum), superconducting qubits ( Qilimanjaro ) and photonics ( PsiQuantum ), and no winner has emerged. Such hardware makers are a potential customer base for software like Q-CTRL’s, though none is confirmed as a Q-CTRL partner.
In the same software layer, QEDMA tackles the problem closest to Fire Opal’s. The Israeli company’s QESEM software analyzes each device’s noise pattern, suppresses some errors and mitigates the rest in post-processing, and it is offered through IBM’s Qiskit Functions catalog. QEDMA raised a $26 million Series A in July 2025 with participation from IBM and Korea Investment Partners. Quantum Machines makes control hardware for quantum computers and raised a $170 million Series C ; its CEO has said more than half of the companies in the field use its technology. Because Boulder Opal supports its controllers, it is both a rival and a complement. Britain’s Riverlane builds error-correction chips and software and raised a $75 million Series C in August 2024. Classiq makes quantum circuit design software, raised a $110 million Series C in May 2025 and is integrated with Fire Opal.
Hardware makers building their own software are another variable. Atom Computing has said part of its Series C money goes to error-correction and control software, and Qilimanj

Q-CTRL, a company specializing in quantum technology infrastructure software development, has raised $290 million in a Series C investment round, with the participation of the UAE’s EDGE Group, which injected $50 million into the company.
Headquartered in Sydney, Q-CTRL develops software solutions for quantum technology applications, including quantum navigation systems designed to operate in environments where satellite navigation services are unavailable or unreliable, applications aimed at supporting autonomous platforms and unmanned vehicles.
EDGE joined a new group of investors in the funding round , which included strategic companies, private equity investors, and investors specializing in growth-stage corporate financing.

He added that EDGE is working in parallel to develop technological capabilities, acquire them, build partnerships, and invest in them, enabling the group to keep pace with technologies that will shape future capabilities.
The investment comes as part of EDGE’s orientation to enhance its capabilities in the fields of artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and navigation technologies capable of operating in environments lacking traditional navigation services.
The group recently integrated autonomous systems within a maritime demonstration carried out by the UAE Navy with the participation of allied forces, which included the operation of surface drone vessels, anti-drone systems, and anti-jamming technologies within a coordinated mission.

Crypto VC funding: Project Faro commits $270m, Index raises $50m
By Lawrence Mondal
Nov 14, 2026 at 6:12 AM UTC
Edited by Olivia Stephanie
News
The payment rail for your crypto. One card. Every chain. No KYC. Spend with Apple Pay or Google Pay in 180+ countries.

Crypto financing announcements have totaled approximately $408.55 million across nine disclosed transactions during Nov. 7–13, 2026, led by a reported $270 million commitment to the bank-backed stablecoin venture Project Faro.
Summary
Nine disclosed financings totaled $408.55 million, including bank commitments and two public token sales.
Project Faro drew approximately $270 million in reported commitments for five years of operations.
Index Industries raised $50 million in seed funding led by Lightspeed Venture Partners.
Alta secured a $47.5 million Series A, bringing its cumulative funding to $80 million.
Project Faro, Index and Alta accounted for nearly 90% of the disclosed weekly total.
The tally includes corporate funding commitments and public token sales alongside venture rounds. Four further announcements covered cumulative or undisclosed funding.
DefiLlama’s funding database provided the weekly inventory, with company announcements, investor disclosures and reporting used to check transaction details.
Project Faro leads crypto financing with $270 million commitment
Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Santander and Deutsche Bank were among institutions committing around $270 million to a stablecoin venture , as crypto.news reported, citing Bloomberg’s Nov. 10 report.
Known as Project Faro, the proposed business would use the capital to cover five years of operating costs. The figure represents committed corporate financing, with no announcement that the full amount has been paid.
The 21-member consortium expects to establish its issuer in the United States. Its stated launch window is the first half of 2027, beginning with a dollar stablecoin intended for payments and digital asset settlement. A euro token is planned later.
You might also like:
Crypto VC funding: Kalshi raises $1b, HIVE secures $129m loan
Index Industries raises $50 million for housing investment infrastructure
Index Industries emerged from stealth on Nov. 10 with a $50 million seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Polychain Capital, Galaxy Ventures and Wintermute Ventures participated.
Founded by former Polychain president Josh Rosenthal and Longmark CEO Brian Hardecker, the company is developing a daily U.S. home-price index and tokenization infrastructure for housing-linked investment products.
Its first planned application is USHP, issued separately by British Virgin Islands-based USHP Limited. The issuer plans an Ethereum release in 2026 and a Solana expansion in 2027.
The announcement states that the referenced securities are unregistered in the United States and cannot be offered to U.S. persons without registration or an applicable exemption.
Alta secures $47.5 million for institutional blockchain infrastructure
Alta announced a $47.5 million Series A led by Index Ventures on Nov. 10, with GV, Blackbird Ventures, Square Peg and Capital49 participating.
The San Francisco company, previously known as Metal, disclosed $80 million in total funding, including $32.5 million in earlier seed financing. Only the Series A enters this week’s total.
Alta is building a blockchain with privacy, identity, and programmable compliance features for regulated financial institutions. Services would cover cross-border payments, foreign exchange and treasury management.
Airwallex is an investor and early design partner, with plans to connect its global payment infrastructure to Alta.
Funding above $10 million reaches banking and trading
Griffin raised a $20 million Series B led by Octagon Partners, joined by Notion Capital, A+ Ventures, Nordic Ninja, Breega and existing investors. The Nov. 12 announcement valued the UK bank above $100 million. Griffin plans to develop card issuing and stablecoin services; its platform serves more than 80 companies.
Marble launched on Nov. 10 with an $11 million seed round led by Polychain Capital. Maven 11, Ripple, Susquehanna Crypto, Lattice and Blockwall participated. Former BitGo executive Matt Ballensweig and former Galaxy Europe CEO Leon Marshall lead the company, which is developing institutional trading and credit financing for AI infrastructure.
DECA Labs announced $12 million in cumulative funding from investors including Polychain, Pantera, Accel and dao5. Its AI-agent network identifies and validates software ideas before development and distribution. The cumulative figure is excluded from the weekly total.
Funding below $10 million includes remittances and token sales
Seva Money secured a $5 million seed round co-led by Blockwall and Revent, with Seedcamp, Stride and Ada Ventures participating. The company supplies remittance providers with wallets, cards and embedded services.
Quranum Protocol announced $4.5 million in strategic funding from Archer Capital, Tidal Capital and Astra Capital for protocol development and financial infrastructure.
vibe/vibe recorded a $300,000 public token sale in DefiLlama’s database. Its sale closed Nov. 13; the project develops a Robinhood Chain launchpad.
Mori Finance recorded a $250,000 token raise on MetaDAO. Its Solana options platform offers covered calls executed through institutional counterparties.
Undisclosed rounds back asset management and lending
Kailash closed a pre-seed round led by UTXO Management for institutional investment products onchain.
Spout received an Ondo investment as it prepares lending against tokenized stocks on Solana.
Lithium secured a strategic investment from LitVM . Its proposed lending service lets users supply USDC or borrow against zkLTC collateral.

candidates.text:
UA Little Rock: $266.5 Million Centennial Campaign Exceeds Fundraising Goal
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:31 AM
UA Little Rock: $266.5 Million Centennial Campaign Exceeds Fundraising Goal
The University of Arkansas at Little Rock has completed its Centennial Campaign with $266.5 million raised, surpassing its $250 million goal and setting a fundraising record for the university.
The seven-year campaign attracted 22,762 donors who made 197,887 contributions. University leaders announced the final total of $266,532,569.07 during a November 5 celebration recognizing donors, alumni and community partners.
The campaign established 211 endowments and helped increase the university’s endowment by 192%. Its investments span scholarships, student support, academic leadership, research and campus facilities.
Private support helped launch the Half-Off Scholarship, which reduced tuition costs for incoming freshmen, and the Trojan Guarantee, which covers remaining tuition for qualifying students receiving both a Pell Grant and the Arkansas Academic Challenge Scholarship.
A $7.5 million Windgate Foundation gift established the Enduring Opportunity Scholarship Program to help sustain the university’s affordability initiatives.
Academic investments included endowed directorships supporting nursing, education and engineering. The university also expanded simulation-based nursing education and developed a year-long paid teacher residency program.
Campus improvements included the revitalization of Trojan Way and renovations to 22 classrooms and laboratories. The Shellam Flake planetarium is scheduled for a soft opening in December 2026.
The fundraising effort included more than 19,000 face-to-face visits by the development team with donors and prospective supporters. Campaign co-chairs Alfred Williams and Jerry Damerow helped lead the initiative alongside university leadership and a broader campaign cabinet.
The new endowments will provide continuing support after the campaign’s conclusion, extending its effects beyond immediate construction projects and scholarship awards to future students, faculty and academic programs.
KEY QUOTES:
“Seven years ago, a $250 million campaign for UA Little Rock might have seemed out of reach. Tonight, we celebrate not just reaching that goal, but what reaching it says about who we have become.”
Christina S. Drale, Chancellor Of The University Of Arkansas At Little Rock
“Those investments have changed UA Little Rock forever. They have helped us become stronger, more innovative and better positioned to serve our students than ever before.”
Christina S. Drale, Chancellor Of The University Of Arkansas At Little Rock

candidates.title: Swiss VC Redalpine Raises $250 Million for A.I., Robotics and Biotech
candidates.snippet: Swiss VC Redalpine Raises $250 Million for A.I., Robotics and Biotech www.trendingtopics.eu
candidates.text:
DeepTech
Swiss VC Redalpine Raises $250 Million for A.I., Robotics and Biotech
Jakob Steinschaden , co-produced by AI 10. November 2026, 08:00
The redalpine team, which has closed its eighth early-stage fund at $250 million. © redalpine
Set Trending Topics as a preferred source on Google.
While many venture capital firms spend months courting investors, Redalpine was done in less than a year: The Swiss firm has closed its eighth early-stage fund, Redalpine Capital VIII (RAC VIII), at $250 million. The fund was oversubscribed and is larger than its predecessor, which closed at $200 million in 2024. Redalpine now manages more than $1.4 billion in total.
Where the Money Is Going
With RAC VIII, Redalpine plans to invest in about 20 European start-ups at the seed to Series A stage, selected from more than 5,000 companies it reviews each year. Checks range from $1 million to $15 million, and Redalpine often leads the rounds. The focus is on companies at the intersection of software and science. Half of the investment team has a background in the natural sciences or engineering, according to Redalpine.
The first three investments from the new fund:
Enact Intelligence: The Zurich robotics start-up aims to give robots a sense of touch and recently raised a $30 million pre-seed round with backing from Yann LeCun, among others.
Helical: The London start-up is building a virtual A.I. lab for drug discovery. Redalpine previously led its $10 million seed round .
Arlequin AI: The team, based in Paris, Berlin and London, is developing an A.I. architecture to protect critical systems and works with government agencies.
Sebastian Becker, a general partner, said artificial intelligence was leveling the playing field for founders around the world, giving the edge to those who best understand the science behind a product and the hardest problems.
Aviva, Flexstone and KfW as Backers
The limited partners in RAC VIII include existing and new investors, among them the British asset manager Aviva Investors, Flexstone Partners and the German development bank KfW. Redalpine was founded in Zurich in 2006, is now based in Zug and has offices in Berlin and London.
Its portfolio includes well-known names such as Mistral AI, N26 and Proxima Fusion. Redalpine led the Munich fusion start-up’s seed round, and in the summer, Proxima raised €411 million at a €2.4 billion valuation . Since 2023, Redalpine says it has sold or taken public 12 portfolio companies. They include the Swiss biotech Araris, which the Japanese drugmaker Taiho acquired for up to $1.14 billion , and, according to Redalpine, Memo Therapeutics (to Ipsen) and the A.I. security start-up Lakera (to Check Point). Companies from its previous fund, RAC VII, have raised more than $1.1 billion from investors in total.
The Competition
Redalpine is not the only firm raising fresh capital for European tech start-ups this year. In Zurich, Lakestar closed Lakestar Resilience I, a $300 million fund for defense and dual-use technologies. Headline raised $400 million for its eighth fund, which targets seed and Series A rounds in A.I., and Accel’s new European fund comes to $800 million. In Germany, Uplift Ventures launched a €100 million deep-tech fund that also invests in seed to Series A rounds.
Money Flows to Established Players
Fund-raising remains difficult for many venture firms, however. European venture funds raised $14.9 billion across 111 funds through the end of September 2026, compared with $15.5 billion in all of last year, according to PitchBook data compiled by SeedBlink . The money is concentrating in the largest funds, and the market beyond them remains tight, according to PitchBook. In the DACH region, 83 venture funds closed with a combined €6.2 billion in 2022, while in the first nine months of 2025, only 21 funds closed with €2.0 billion, according to PitchBook. The median time from launch to final close is 26 months.
That favors established firms with a record of exits, such as Redalpine, while new and smaller fund managers face a tougher climb. Deep-tech start-ups also often need many years and a lot of capital before they generate revenue or can be sold. Whether the bets on fusion energy, robotics and A.I.-driven biotech pay off will therefore only become clear many years from now.

candidates.title: Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking grunt work
candidates.snippet: The startup says its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect their analysis.
candidates.text:
In Brief
Posted:
11:32 AM PST · November 17, 2026
Image Credits: shapecharge / Getty Images
Marina Temkin
Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking grunt work
Model ML, a London-based startup that uses AI to automate work traditionally performed by junior bankers and consultants, including building financial models, preparing pitch decks, and writing due diligence reports, has raised $250 million in Series B funding at a $1.5 billion valuation. The new round, which comes a year after its $75 million Series A round was announced, was co-led by General Atlantic and earlier backer QED Investors.
Brothers Chaz and Arnie Englander co-founded the three-year-old startup after previously co-founding two other companies, including Fat Llama, a peer-to-peer rental marketplace acquired by Swedish rival Hygglo for $41.5 million in 2022.
Model ML develops AI agents that integrate with clients’ systems, data, and tools, including Excel and PowerPoint. The startup says its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect their analysis.
Other startups automating the routine, repetitive tasks for investment bankers and management consultants include Hebbia and Rogo, which raised $160 million at a $2 billion valuation in April.
Anthropic and OpenAI have also built tools for financial professionals, but Model ML says it runs on open source models and that doing so allows it to operate at about 2% of the cost of frontier models while delivering faster results.

ACWA Power stock: $226 million financing closes for Uzbek wind farm
Published on 11/16/2026 at 00:08 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS
ACWA Power secured long-term financing for a wind project in Uzbekistan. The milestone supports the developer's international renewable-energy expansion.
Uzbekistan project reaches financing milestone
ACWA Power secured long-term funding for the Bash II wind farm in Uzbekistan.
The project strengthens the company’s development portfolio across energy and water infrastructure.
ACWA Power is expanding projects from its Riyadh headquarters across international markets.
ACWA Power, SA15CGS10H12, Illustration mit AI erstellt.
ACWA Power has reached financial close on the Bash II wind farm in Uzbekistan's Bukhara Region, according to Oil & Gas News on Sunday, November 15. The Saudi developer secured long-term financing of 226 million US dollars, equivalent to 847.5 million Saudi riyals, from a consortium of international lenders.
Financing advances Uzbekistan project
Bash II has a planned capacity of 300 megawatts and is located in Uzbekistan's Bukhara Region. Financial close marks the transition from project development toward construction and operation, although the report did not provide a commercial start date or identify the lending consortium.
For investors, the financing milestone adds to ACWA Power's pipeline of contracted and developing energy assets. The project also underlines the role of project finance in funding large renewable-energy installations without relying solely on corporate balance-sheet capital.
International energy and water platform
ACWA Power leads energy, water and green hydrogen projects from its headquarters in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Its activities span power generation, water desalination, renewable energy and storage projects across international markets. The company works with partners, customers and communities across multiple regions, giving its portfolio exposure to infrastructure demand beyond its home market.

Sanofi-backed Windward Bio raises $225 million in its Nasdaq IPO as Rezera postpones its listing

Key points
Windward sold 10,294,117 shares at $17 and Sanofi bought $50 million of shares and pre-funded warrants at the same price, for $225 million in expected gross proceeds [1] .
Its lead drug, WIN378, a TSLP antibody licensed from China's Kelun Biotech, is in a Phase 2/3 asthma trial with results expected next year [2] .
Rezera postponed its $200 million IPO of 16.7 million shares at $11 to $13 [3] [4] .
Windward Bio Group priced its initial public offering of 10,294,117 shares at $17 each on Nov. 12, the midpoint of its $16 to $18 range, and sold an additional $50 million of shares and pre-funded warrants to Sanofi in a concurrent private placement at the same price [1] [5] . Gross proceeds are expected to total $225 million before fees and before the underwriters' option on 1,544,117 more shares [1] . The stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Friday under the symbol WWB, and the deal is set to close on Nov. 16 [1] .
Boston-based Rezera postponed a planned $200 million IPO on the evening of Nov. 11, citing market conditions, according to IPOScoop [4] . Jefferies and TD Cowen were bookrunners on both deals, alongside Piper Sandler and UBS for Windward and Cantor Fitzgerald for Rezera [1] [3] .
Two drugs licensed from China
Windward, formed two years ago, raised $365 million of venture funding before the IPO [2] . Its lead drug, WIN378, is an ultra-long-acting injectable that blocks TSLP, the same inflammatory protein targeted by AstraZeneca and Amgen's Tezspire, and could be dosed as rarely as twice a year against Tezspire's monthly schedule [2] . Windward licensed it from Kelun Biotech, which co-developed it with Harbour BioMed [2] . The Phase 3 part of an asthma trial began in September with results expected next year, and a mid-stage COPD study started in June with data due in 2027 [2] . A second drug, WIN027, licensed from Qyuns Therapeutics, targets both TSLP and IL-13 [2] . Windward paid $70 million upfront in cash and equity for the two programs and owes up to $1.6 billion more in milestone payments [2] .
Windward is the biotech sector's 30th IPO this year, according to BioPharma Dive, which counts 2026 as the busiest year for drugmaker listings since 2021, with more than $8 billion raised [2] .
Rezera steps back
Rezera, formerly NodThera, develops oral NLRP3 inhibitors for inflammatory diseases and describes itself as Phase 3-ready [3] [4] . It had planned to sell 16.7 million shares at $11 to $13 on the Nasdaq under the symbol RZRA, and GSK had indicated interest in buying up to $25 million of the offering, about 13% of the deal [3] . Its last amended registration statement was filed with the SEC on Nov. 9 [6] . The company has not said when it might return. The postponement came in the same week that Anthropic's bankers weighed pricing its IPO above its marketed range.

The post Windward Bio Raises $225 Million In Nasdaq Debut At $1.69 Billion Market Capitalization appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Windward Bio Raises $225 Million In Nasdaq Debut At $1.69 Billion Market Capitalization
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:36 AM
Windward Bio Raises $225 Million In Nasdaq Debut At $1.69 Billion Market Capitalization
Windward Bio Group has completed its public market debut after pricing an initial public offering at $17 per share and raising $225 million in gross proceeds, including a $50 million concurrent private placement from Sanofi.
The clinical-stage biotechnology company began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 13, 2026 and ended its first day with a market capitalization of approximately $1.69 billion.
Windward sold approximately 10.29 million ordinary shares in the offering.
The Basel, Switzerland-based company was founded in 2024 by serial biotechnology entrepreneur Luca Santarelli, M.D., and his team. Santarelli previously helped build VectivBio and Therachon, both of which were ultimately acquired.
Windward has raised $365 million since its formation, including a $200 million Series A in January 2025 and a $165 million crossover financing in May 2026.
Pivotal bioVenture Partners China has invested in the company through each financing round from its early formation through the public listing.
Windward is developing ultra-long-acting antibody treatments for respiratory and dermatologic diseases including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and atopic dermatitis.
Its lead program, WIN378, is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting thymic stromal lymphopoietin.
WIN378 is currently being evaluated in the Phase 2/3 POLARIS-1 asthma study and the Phase 2 SIRIUS COPD trial. The drug is being developed for twice-yearly dosing, compared with the once-every-four-weeks schedule of currently approved treatments in the category.
Windward reported positive interim Phase 2 data in September 2026 supporting twice-yearly dosing of WIN378 in asthma.
Its pipeline also includes WIN027, a clinical-stage bispecific antibody targeting TSLP and IL-13 that is currently in Phase 1 development.
Global rights outside Greater China and certain Asian markets to both programs were licensed from Chinese biopharmaceutical companies.
Windward plans to use IPO proceeds to support clinical development of WIN378 and WIN027, advance additional bispecific antibody programs and fund working capital and general corporate purposes.
The company expects top-line Phase 2 asthma data for WIN378 in the first half of 2027, Phase 2 COPD data in the second half of 2027 and Phase 3 asthma data in the first half of 2029.

Church & Dwight Announces $225 Million Investment In BALI Hair Care Business
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 4:19 PM
Church & Dwight Announces $225 Million Investment In BALI Hair Care Business
Church & Dwight has agreed to acquire 45% of BALI Treatment for approximately $225 million, adding an investment in the European hair care and styling company behind BALI CURLS and BALI GENTS.
The agreement includes an option to acquire the remaining 55% beginning two years after closing.
The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory clearance and customary conditions.
BALI reported approximately $100 million in net sales for the 12 months ended October 31, 2026.
Founded in 2022 by Hendrik Genotte, the business develops products for curly and textured hair and has expanded into men’s grooming.
Its brands have established positions in Germany and Austria, with broader European expansion underway.
Products include Hydrating Curl Cream, Curl Defining Gel, Moisturizing Conditioner and Nourishing Shampoo. The company emphasizes vegan and cruelty-free formulations and a creator-led relationship with consumers.
Church & Dwight plans to use its international capabilities to expand distribution beyond BALI’s current concentration in a limited number of European markets.
CEO Rick Dierker said the investment aligns with the company’s preference for asset-light brands with strong category positions and the potential to improve growth and gross margins.
Church & Dwight expects the investment to be accretive to cash earnings in 2027, including acquisition-related costs and interest expense.
The structure gives the company an initial minority stake and a potential path to full ownership, while BALI gains access to a larger consumer products organization.
Church & Dwight’s existing portfolio spans household and personal care brands, including ARM & HAMMER, BATISTE, WATERPIK, THERABREATH and HERO.
The investment extends its international growth strategy into a younger hair care business with established regional demand.
KEY QUOTES
“BALI CARE grew from my own experience with curly hair and a desire to create products that help people embrace their natural curls. We are excited to partner with Church & Dwight, whose global capabilities and shared passion for innovation and consumer-focused solutions will help us bring our products and community to even more people around the world.”
Hendrik Genotte, Founder Of BALI Care
“Our investment in BALI CARE represents an important step in our strategy to accelerate international growth through high-performing, asset-light consumer brands with strong category leadership. BALI CARE has built distinctive brands with strong consumer loyalty and significant growth potential. With distribution today concentrated in a limited number of European markets, we are poised to leverage Church & Dwight’s global capabilities to expand the brands’ reach and support their next phase of growth.
“The BALI CARE investment squarely fits into our acquisition criteria that focuses on (1) #1 or #2 brand in a category; (2) asset-light; (3) expected to be growth accretive to the Company; and (4) expected to be gross margin accretive to the Company. Our strong balance sheet will continue to provide the flexibility to add additional high-quality acquisition and investment opportunities. This capability has been a key driver of Church & Dwight’s consistently strong shareholder returns.”
Rick Dierker, CEO Of Church & Dwight

candidates.snippet:
Nextchem has signed a binding agreement to acquire liquefied natural gas process technologies from Chart Industries for $220 million in cash. The transaction will be completed through Nextchem USA and is expected to close by the end of 2026 or in early January 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals. candidates.text:
Nextchem To Acquire LNG Technologies For $220 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:39 AM
Nextchem To Acquire LNG Technologies For $220 Million
Nextchem has signed a binding agreement to acquire liquefied natural gas process technologies from Chart Industries for $220 million in cash. The transaction will be completed through Nextchem USA and is expected to close by the end of 2026 or in early January 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals. Chart Industries is a wholly owned subsidiary of Baker Hughes.
The acquisition will give Nextchem immediate access to established LNG liquefaction technologies, customer references, an existing backlog, a project pipeline, and a specialized engineering team.
Expanding Nextchem’s LNG Technology Portfolio
The transaction includes Integrated Pre-Cooled Single Mixed Refrigerant technology, its advanced IPSMR+ versions, early-stage IPDMR technology, and a portfolio of small-scale LNG processes.
Nextchem will also acquire more than 90 patents, trademarks, proprietary processes, and technical knowledge. Twelve professionals specializing in process engineering, business development, and commissioning are expected to join the company.
IPSMR is designed for mid-scale LNG projects with capacities ranging from approximately 0.5 million to two million tonnes per annum for each train. Its primary target range is between 1.4 million and two million tonnes.
The early-stage IPDMR platform is intended to extend Nextchem’s offering to larger projects with capacities ranging from approximately two million to more than four million tonnes per annum per train.
Small-scale LNG technologies included in the acquisition address applications below 0.5 million tonnes per annum. These include peak-shaving facilities, remote or stranded gas resources, alternative fuels, and locations without pipeline infrastructure.
Established Operations And Project Pipeline
The IPSMR platform has approximately 14 million tonnes per annum of historical operating references. Another 57 million tonnes is under construction, including a residual backlog of 30 million tonnes.
The technology has also been selected for approximately 90 million tonnes per annum of projects that have not yet reached a final investment decision.
Nextchem will gain capabilities across the project lifecycle, from feasibility studies and process design through licensing, detailed engineering, commissioning, start-up, and performance testing.
A 10-year supply agreement with Chart Industries will provide cold boxes for IPSMR projects. Cold boxes contain heat exchangers, piping, and other equipment used to cool natural gas until it becomes liquid.
The $220 million purchase price will be paid at closing and financed through dedicated credit facilities fully underwritten by BPER Banca. The price reflects a high-single-digit multiple of projected 2027 EBITDA.
Nextchem expects the acquired licensing operation to generate at least $25 million in EBITDA during 2027, with potential additional contributions from equipment sales and broader MAIRE revenue opportunities. The acquisition is expected to increase MAIRE’s EBITDA margin.
KEY QUOTES:
This acquisition represents a major step in the continued development of our technology-driven growth strategy and delivers on the ambition we set at our Capital Markets Day to expand into the LNG market. By adding proven proprietary LNG technologies, established references and highly specialised capabilities to Nextchem, we are expanding into an attractive market with a strong and flexible technology platform. At the same time, technology ownership allows us to engage with clients earlier in the project development cycle and creates further opportunities across MAIRE’s integrated model. The transaction strengthens Nextchem’s asset-light business profile while expanding the addressable market, thanks to the Group’s engineering and execution capabilities.
Alessandro Bernini, CEO of MAIRE

candidates.title: Midwest startups raise $213.5 million in a week. Where is the money going?
candidates.snippet: Midwest startups raise $213.5 million in a week. Where is the money going? Techli
candidates.text:
Four of six deals are reported in Chicago, and the region is experiencing the latest funding activity in the form of investments in AI infrastructure and financial services.
According to StartMidwest’s funding roundup , $213.5 million was raised in six deals by Midwest startups and financial technology companies during the week ending Nov. 6, with two $100 million rounds accounting for almost all the capital.
Ocient, an AI infrastructure firm in Chicago, and Erebor Bank, which is based in Columbus, Ohio, were the leaders of the activity. The remaining included health care technology, artificial intelligence and fintech firms, reflecting the diversity of sectors that are being invested in all over the region.
The headline figure, however, requires some qualification: Erebor Bank’s $100 million investment from Japan’s SBI Holdings was announced as a planned commitment, not a completed financing round. The difference is important in evaluating the amount of capital that actually has flowed to companies in the Midwest.
The biggest round up to date was Ocient’s $100 million Series C , which was announced on November 5. The investment, led by BOKA Capital and OCA Ventures, totals $260 million for the Chicago firm. Other investors who were on board included existing investors Greycroft, In-Q-Tel, Blue Bear Capital, Buoyant Ventures, PSP Growth, Pritzker Group Venture Capital and Eron Wolf. Dallas Venture Capital joined as a new investor.
Ocient is a company that creates data analytics and AI solutions for enterprises dealing with vast amounts of data. The new investment will allow it to continue developing its OcientAIQ solutions that enable enterprises to deploy AI agents and analytics in petabyte-scale data environments.
Reliable, governed data is becoming a key infrastructure need as businesses delve into agentic AI systems that can analyze information and execute tasks. Ocient claims its solution can be used for data governance along with high-performance data analytics, enabling AI agents and analysts to ask questions about the data in a customer’s environment.
The company anticipates that its revenue will more than triple in 2026 due to the demand of customers with growing and high-volume data sets. This projection is not a financial result but an estimate by Ocient.
The second $100 million was from a digital bank called Erebor Bank, based in Columbus, Ohio, which offers services to companies in fields such as artificial intelligence, robotics and advanced manufacturing, defense, and energy. The timing of the completion of the investment was not mentioned in the funding roundup, but SBI Holdings revealed its plan to invest $100 million .
Four of the six transactions were in Chicago. In addition to Ocient, medical technology firm Focused Medical Technologies, a treatment developer for pulmonary embolism, secured $6 million in investment, including two medical technology strategic investors and UCM Ventures. The University of Chicago startup is targeting the funds for product development, manufacturing and setting up for a pivotal study in the United States.
Consumer insights firm QualSights raised $5 million in funding, led by Duo Partners. The company employs smart sensors and a consumer application and AI analytics to provide a better understanding of how humans use physical products. The funding came with the appointment of Prasanna Pitale as Chief Executive.
Fifth Star Funds and Chicago Early Growth Ventures joined Izou Partners as the lead investors in an oversubscribed $2.5 million pre-seed round for healthcare technology company CareLumi. Its software will track AI-powered and automated workflows in healthcare delivery systems, starting with provider credentialing and payer enrollment.
Minneapolis-based Duome capped the list with a capital investment from Great Lakes Credit Union. The company is connecting with credit unions to assist homebuyers who meet the qualifications to acquire homes using a co-investment approach.
The four of the deals occurred in Chicago, Columbus, and Minneapolis, each had one deal. The sector split also indicates that the regions aren’t just focused on traditional software startups – the financial services, health care, and AI infrastructure sectors are also included.
Nevertheless, the weekly total was very skewed. The two $100 million deals made up about 94% of the total $213.5 million reported, with the remaining four deals making up a much smaller portion of the total.
The numbers indicate ongoing investor interest in tackling complex challenges in infrastructure and industry-specific issues for the Midwest startup ecosystem. However, the size disparity between these large financing announcements and the smaller rounds at the early stage also poses a question for the region: Is it possible to reliably get capital to startups at various stages of development?

Square Nine Capital Leads $206 Million Financing For Aline Accounting Partners
Square Nine Capital has led a $206 million financing for Aline Accounting Partners, supporting debt refinancing, near-term acquisitions and continued expansion of the accounting and professional services platform.
The financing consists of a revolving credit facility, a term loan and a delayed draw term loan facility.
Proceeds refinanced existing indebtedness and provided growth capital for acquisitions. The facilities also support Aline’s broader strategy of investing in talent, technology and additional service capabilities.

Member firms receive support across finance and reporting, information technology, human resources, recruiting, staffing, marketing, growth and mergers and acquisitions.
The organization intends to use those shared capabilities to strengthen collaboration, improve operating efficiency and expand what its teams can provide to clients.

Square Nine provides flexible capital to middle-market companies, partnering with founders, owners, management teams and financial sponsors.
Its investments support acquisitions, growth, refinancings, recapitalizations and other strategic transactions across different parts of a company’s capital structure.
The Aline transaction combines funding for immediate balance sheet needs with capacity for additional acquisitions. That structure supports both the existing organization and firms joining its network.
Polsinelli served as legal counsel to Aline. Paul Hastings advised Square Nine.
The financing gives Aline additional resources as it develops a platform built around established accounting practices, local client relationships and centralized support functions. Square Nine’s principals said the arrangement provides flexibility for continued expansion and investment in the organization’s capabilities.

“Aline has built a strong foundation for growth by bringing together established accounting firms and investing in the resources that help them thrive. Christopher Brown And Griffin Coakley, Principals At Square Nine Capital

Modern Wealth Management: $200 Million Centerbridge Investment To Accelerate Growth Of $17 Billion RIA Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:32 AM
Modern Wealth Management: $200 Million Centerbridge Investment To Accelerate Growth Of $17 Billion RIA Platform
Modern Wealth Management has secured a $200 million hybrid debt-and-equity investment from funds managed by Centerbridge Partners to support additional acquisitions and expansion of its national wealth management platform. The transaction comes as the registered investment advisory firm approaches $17 billion in assets under management after completing 26 acquisitions since its founding in 2023.
Funds managed by Harvest Partners SCF also participated in the investment.
Crestview Partners, which provided Modern Wealth’s initial $200 million equity financing in 2023, will remain the firm’s largest institutional investor.
The financing preserves continuity with the existing ownership group while introducing additional capital to support the company’s expansion strategy.
Modern Wealth will also remain majority employee-owned.
The company currently has more than 150 employee shareholders.
Founded in April 2023, Modern Wealth was established by Gary Roth, Mike Capelle, Jason Gordo, and Jason Del Col.
The firm has grown through a combination of acquisitions and organic expansion.
Its operating model focuses on integrating established financial advisory businesses into a platform providing centralized technology, operations, and specialized planning services.
Modern Wealth serves clients through investment management, financial planning, tax planning and preparation, estate planning, and other wealth management capabilities.
The company believes these services allow advisors to address increasingly complex financial needs while maintaining relationships with their clients.
Its acquisition strategy emphasizes partnerships with independent advisory firms seeking additional operational resources and opportunities for long-term growth.
Acquired businesses gain access to the firm’s technology, investment expertise, and centralized support infrastructure.
Modern Wealth intends to use the new investment to expand its presence in important wealth management markets while continuing to pursue additional acquisitions.
The capital will also support development of its integrated planning and advisory platform.
The firm has established an Organic Growth Hub and Advisor Support Center designed to help financial advisors strengthen customer relationships and business development activities.
These resources provide support involving marketing, technology, operations, and specialized financial planning.
Management believes that centralizing certain activities can allow advisors to devote more time to client service and organic growth.
The latest investment comes approximately three and a half years after the firm’s launch.
During that period, Modern Wealth has completed 26 acquisitions and expanded its assets under management to nearly $17 billion.
The company’s growth reflects an ongoing trend within the registered investment advisory industry toward consolidation and the development of larger independent wealth management platforms.
Advisory firms are increasingly seeking access to technology, compliance resources, succession planning solutions, and specialized professional expertise.
Modern Wealth aims to address these needs through an organization that combines national resources with local advisory relationships.
The company also announced a board appointment.
David Canter, CEO of Finley Point Strategy and former President of Bluespring Wealth Partners, has joined Modern Wealth’s Board of Directors.
Canter previously held senior leadership responsibilities involving Fidelity Institutional’s registered investment advisory and family office businesses.
He has also made a significant equity investment through ATON Associates, a firm focused on minority investments in wealth management businesses.
His appointment adds industry experience to Modern Wealth’s governance structure as the company pursues further expansion.
Centerbridge manages approximately $52 billion in assets across private equity, private credit, and real estate.
The firm sees opportunities to support Modern Wealth’s continued development through its investment resources.
Crestview manages funds with more than $10 billion in aggregate capital commitments and has supported Modern Wealth since its launch.
Ardea Partners served as lead financial advisor to Modern Wealth, while Houlihan Lokey and Citizens Bank also provided financial advice.
The $200 million financing strengthens Modern Wealth’s capital position as it continues pursuing acquisitions, investing in technology, and developing its national advisory platform.
KEY QUOTES:
“When we founded Modern Wealth, we set out to build a different kind of wealth management firm, one where advisors have the resources, expertise and support to grow their businesses while delivering a more comprehensive experience for clients. This investment gives us the capital to accelerate our growth while continuing to invest in the people and capabilities that make our model successful. Just as importantly, remaining majority employee-owned ensures the people building this business continue to have a meaningful stake in its future.”
Jason Gordo, President And Co-Founder Of Modern Wealth Management
“Modern Wealth has achieved extraordinary growth in a remarkably short period of time, and we couldn’t be more proud of what Jason, Gary, Mike and the entire team have built. From the outset, we believed in their vision to create a differentiated wealth management platform that puts advisors and clients first.”
Dan Kilpatrick, Partner And Head Of Financial Services At Crestview Partners

News provided by

Nov 12, 2026, 13:33 ET

JERSEY CITY, N.J. , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Asset Based Lending (ABL) , a national private lender and a driving force behind the next generation of real estate investment, has successfully closed its fourth unrated securitization, totaling $200 million. The transaction, ABL 2026 RTL-1, which priced on October 15 and closed on October 26, marks ABL's largest to date, bringing its cumulative securitization volume to $723 million.
The transaction is backed by a diversified pool of business-purpose residential real estate loans, with an industry-leading concentration of ground-up infill construction loans. This reflects ABL's 16 years of experience in ground-up construction lending and its proven ability to manage the complexities and risks of residential development.
"We are proud to lead the industry in financing ground-up construction, and to do it at a cost that keeps our pricing competitive for the builders we serve," said Kevin Rodman, CEO of ABL. "This transaction underscores the strength of the platform our team has built and the confidence investors have in our credit. Every one of these loans puts new housing on the ground."
The transaction also demonstrates ABL's ability to navigate challenging market conditions. Despite heightened volatility and increased investor selectivity across the securitization market, ABL secured competitive financing terms. The deal reached the market in approximately three weeks, making it one of the company's fastest securitization executions.
Performance Trust Capital Partners, LLC served as structuring agent, with Nomura Securities International, Inc. ("Nomura") and Mizuho Securities USA LLC serving as joint bookrunners.
"Successfully executing this transaction amid market volatility reinforces the effectiveness of our capital markets strategy and the quality of our platform," said Daniel Gotay, Head of Capital Markets at ABL. "We have built durable relationships with institutional investors and established a track record they can underwrite, giving us consistent access to capital. For our borrowers, that is what matters most: they can count on ABL to fund their projects from start to finish."
The securitization also reflects ABL's expanding national footprint, with collateral spanning the Northeast, Sun Belt, Rust Belt and South. This geographic diversification supports the company's strategy to continue growing beyond its established Northeast presence and finance residential development in markets across the country.
To learn more about ABL, please visit www.ablfunding.com .
About Asset Based Lending
Asset Based Lending was established in 2010, providing fast bridge financing to real estate investors for the purchase, renovation, new construction, and long-term refinance of single-family, multi-family, and mixed-use properties. A trusted lender to thousands of investors, Asset Based Lending has closed over $4.4 billion in loans since its founding. Learn more at https://www.ablfunding.com/ . Follow the company on LinkedIn .

Market News
Patrick Industries Raises Dividend and Renews $200 Million Buyback
Published
November 13, 2026
By
Elena Kovacs Global Equities & Earnings, AI Research Agent

Table Of Contents
Key Points Patrick raised its dividend while merger covenants block use of the renewed buyback…
View more
Patrick raised its dividend while merger covenants block use of the renewed buyback capacity.
The repurchase authorization sits idle because the pending LCI merger restricts Patrick from buying its own stock.
Patrick balances shareholder returns against funding organic growth and acquisitions from its cash generation.
Patrick Industries ( PATK ) announced on November 13, 2026 that its board had increased the quarterly common-stock dividend to $0.52 per share from $0.47 and replenished its share-repurchase authorization to $200 million. The announcement pairs a higher cash payout with additional repurchase capacity that cannot currently be used because of covenants in Patrick’s pending all-stock merger with LCI Industries ( LCII ) .
The board approved the dividend increase on November 11, 2026. The new rate is approximately 10.6% above the previous rate, calculated from the announced per-share amounts. The dividend is payable on December 7, 2026, to shareholders of record at the close of business on November 23, 2026.
Repurchase Capacity Remains Restricted
The authorization covers repurchases over the next 24 months and includes $61.9 million that remained under the previous authorization. The board therefore added $138.1 million of capacity, calculated as the difference between the new total and the remaining amount.
The repurchase program cannot presently be used. Patrick entered into the LCI merger agreement on June 30, 2026, and its operating covenants restrict repurchases of Patrick common stock. The company expects those restrictions to remain in place while the agreement is in effect.
The restrictions were already visible in Patrick’s third-quarter report , which said the company made no share repurchases during the quarter because of the merger agreement. The SEC declared the merger registration statement effective on October 19, 2026, and Patrick has scheduled a special shareholder meeting for November 18, 2026.
Cash Flow and Capital Allocation
Chief Executive Officer Andy Nemeth said the decisions were grounded in Patrick’s capital allocation, cash generation and balance sheet. “Since initiating our quarterly dividend in 2019, we have raised it each year and have been active with share repurchases, deploying $106.1 million in the first nine months of 2026,” he said.
Returning capital is only one use of that cash. Nemeth said cash generation through the cycle also enables investment in organic initiatives and strategic mergers and acquisitions, which Patrick expects to remain a priority.
The latest results provide context for those competing demands. Third-quarter net sales were $975 million, compared with $976 million a year earlier, while operating income declined to $50 million from $66 million. For the first nine months of 2026, operating cash flow was $147 million, down from $199 million in the prior-year period. Patrick attributed the change to working-capital deployment supporting its composite-products growth strategy and inventory management for customers.
Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow, which Patrick defines as operating cash flow less purchases of property, plant and equipment, was $203 million through the third quarter, compared with $211 million a year earlier. At quarter-end, Patrick had approximately $716 million of available liquidity, comprising borrowing availability under its credit facility and cash on hand, alongside about $1.4 billion of total debt and a total net leverage ratio of 2.9x under its credit agreement.
The immediate capital return is therefore the scheduled December dividend. The replenished authorization establishes capacity for future repurchases rather than current activity, with its use constrained by the merger restrictions while Patrick continues to fund operations, organic initiatives and acquisitions.
