candidates.text:
Serena Williams And Beth Ferreira Unveil $200 Million VC Strategy Through Starfire Ventures
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 8:56 PM
Serena Williams And Beth Ferreira Unveil $200 Million VC Strategy Through Starfire Ventures
Serena Williams and Beth Ferreira have launched Starfire Ventures, an early-stage venture capital firm that plans to attract $200 million in capital for investments in technology-enabled and AI-native companies.
The New York-based firm will primarily invest in seed through Series A rounds, with selective participation in later-stage opportunities. Its target areas include vertical AI, business-to-business technology, and consumer businesses addressing significant but underserved needs.
Starfire’s investment strategy centers on companies that can expand access to health and wellness, education and knowledge, financial management, and consumer experiences. The firm is also interested in infrastructure that improves affordability and access, particularly in industries with more than $1 trillion of potential market value.
Within the experience economy, Starfire plans to evaluate new retail models, stadium technologies, entertainment platforms, interactive products, and other tools that increase access to or improve live and real-world experiences.
The new firm builds on an investment partnership between Williams and Ferreira that began in 2015. Their first collaboration involved a seed investment in online education company MasterClass.
They subsequently invested together in companies including pet food brand Ollie and meal delivery company Daily Harvest. Ollie was acquired by Agrolimen in 2026, while Chobani acquired Daily Harvest in 2025.
Ferreira later became an adviser to Serena Ventures when Williams launched the investment platform. She joined Serena Ventures as a general partner in 2024.
Starfire represents the next stage of the platform Williams established through Serena Ventures, which raised an inaugural $111 million fund in 2022. The new organization combines Williams and Ferreira’s more than 30 years of collective investment experience.
The pair have deployed hundreds of millions of venture capital dollars across their careers. Starfire is intended to pair that investment background with operating expertise, corporate relationships, and an international network that can help portfolio companies develop beyond their initial financing rounds.
The firm said it will evaluate not only the attractiveness of a company’s idea but also the commitment and capabilities of the founding team. This approach reflects Williams and Ferreira’s experience investing across multiple market cycles, when changes in financing conditions placed different demands on company leaders.
Starfire also plans to support founders beyond the initial capital investment. Potential assistance could include access to commercial partners, strategic guidance, hiring networks, brand development, follow-on financing relationships, and international connections.
The firm’s stated focus on critical and underserved problems suggests that it will look for businesses able to pair substantial commercial opportunities with broader access or participation. Examples could include technology that lowers costs, reaches overlooked customers, or creates new ways for people to use essential services.
Williams and Ferreira are also positioning Starfire as an enduring investment institution rather than a platform dependent entirely on its founders’ public profiles. Williams said the firm is being designed to continue beyond its current leadership and create additional opportunities for people to participate in the ownership of growing businesses.
The launch comes as AI is changing the types of companies venture investors evaluate and the ways new businesses develop products. Starfire’s inclusion of both AI-native and broadly technology-enabled companies gives it the flexibility to consider startups built entirely around AI as well as businesses using technology to modernize established industries.
Its planned stage focus will allow the firm to begin working with founders during formative periods when companies are establishing their products, hiring initial teams, developing go-to-market strategies, and identifying product-market fit.
Selective later-stage investments may give Starfire opportunities to support existing portfolio companies through subsequent rounds or participate in businesses with a clear strategic fit.
By combining the history of Serena Ventures with Ferreira and Williams’ decade-long investing relationship, Starfire enters the market as a new brand with an established record of company building, venture deployment, and founder support.
KEY QUOTES:
“Founders are looking for investors who understand their business and can be active partners as they build. Having invested through multiple market cycles, we’ve learned to look beyond a compelling idea to the conviction of the team behind it, and beyond that, we bring the operational expertise and reach to take that new generation of companies to their next stage.”
Beth Ferreira, Co-Founder and General Partner of Starfire Ventures
“With Starfire Ventures, we are building an investment platform designed to live beyond us. We’re continuing to back founders solving critical problems at their breakthrough moments, while broadening access to capital and creating opportunities for more people to participate in the ownership and growth of transformative businesses.”
Serena Williams, Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Starfire Ventures

Attorney General Mike Hilgers announces $183.5 Million multistate settlement with Rent-to-Own finance company Acima Digital, LLC
Courtesy Photo
November 15th, 2026 | Nebraska Attorney General’s Office
Lincoln – Attorney General Mike Hilgers announced a $183.5 million multistate settlement with Acima Digital, LLC, and its parent company, Acima Holdings, LLC. The settlement includes $43 million in consumer restitution, $10.5 million to participating states, and $130 million in lease balance reductions. Nebraska will receive more than $292,608.42 in restitution and $593,465.05 in lease forgiveness for Nebraska consumers.
Acima, a rent-to-own financing company that partners with Nebraska retailers, was accused of misleading consumers about the terms and costs of its rental-purchase agreements. Forty-three states alleged that Acima advertised 90-day payoff programs without clearly disclosing that consumers were automatically placed in 12-month agreements and could end up paying twice the advertised cash price. The company also allegedly misrepresented its services as traditional credit, marked up merchandise prices, and made it difficult for consumers to return merchandise and end agreements.
Under the settlement, Acima must improve retail partner training, provide clearer advertising and contract disclosures, stop marking up merchandise prices, allow consumers to return merchandise without obstruction, and properly address delivery, damage, and repair issues. The company also cannot report rental-purchase agreements to the three major credit bureaus for five years.
Consumers eligible for restitution or lease forgiveness do not need to take action. The settlement administrator will contact consumers receiving restitution, while Acima will notify those eligible for lease forgiveness.

candidates.title: AG ANNOUNCES $183.5 MILLION SETTLEMENT
candidates.snippet: AG ANNOUNCES $183.5 MILLION SETTLEMENT DoingItLocal
candidates.text:
ATTORNEY GENERAL TONG ANNOUNCES $183.5 MILLION MULTISTATE SETTLEMENT WITH RENT-TO-OWN COMPANY ACIMA DIGITAL
(Hartford, CT) — Attorney General William Tong today announced a $183.5 million multistate settlement with Acima Digital, LLC and its parent company, Acima Holdings, LLC, resolving allegations that the rent-to-own finance company misled consumers about its agreements and deceptively marked up prices.
The settlement consists of $43 million in consumer restitution, $130 million in lease balance reductions, and a $10.5 million payment to the states. Connecticut consumers will receive $2,441,257 in lease forgiveness, in addition to the $246,090.70 payment to the state.
Consumers who are eligible to obtain restitution or lease forgiveness pursuant to this settlement do not need to take any action. Consumers eligible to receive restitution will be contacted by the settlement administrator, Rust Consulting. Consumers who are eligible to receive lease forgiveness will be contacted by Acima.
Acima partners with retailers to offer financing to consumers via rental-purchase agreements. The settlement resolves allegations that Acima deceptively advertised its rental-purchase agreements in manner that misled consumers about the nature and cost of its rental-purchase agreements and deceptively marked up the cash price of the merchandise being rented, amongst other deceptive acts and practices with respect to the consummation and servicing of its rental-purchase agreements and its debt collection and credit reporting practices.
“Acima lured and locked consumers into overpriced rent-to-own deals by obscuring key information, including the length of these agreements, the total cost, and options for termination. They took advantage of families struggling to afford basic needs, and we are making them pay. Our settlement sends millions of dollars back to consumers and forces strict reforms to ensure fair and honest practices going forward,” said Attorney General Tong.
The multistate coalition of 43 states alleged that Acima marketed its rental-purchase agreements as 90-day pay off programs without disclosing that consumers were automatically defaulted into the maximum 12-month term whereby consumers could pay approximately two times the cash price advertised by Acima’s retail partner. Acima also advertised its rental-purchase product using terms like “credit,” which often misled consumers into believing that they were obtaining traditional financing. Acima’s process for electronically executing rental-purchase agreements also obscured the terms of the transaction, further compounding consumer confusion. Additionally, Acima obstructed consumers’ ability to terminate their rental-purchase agreements without penalty by returning their merchandise to Acima.
Under the settlement, Acima has agreed to injunctive terms to address these practices, including to:
• Conduct robust training of its retail partners;
• Refrain from making certain representations in its advertising unless other material information is clearly and conspicuously disclosed;
• Refrain from obscuring the material terms and conditions of its rental-purchase agreements during Acima’s electronic signature process;
• Refrain from marking up the cash price from that of Acima’s retail partners;
• Refrain from obstructing consumers’ ability to terminate their rental-purchase agreements by returning the merchandise to Acima;
• Refrain from reporting rental-purchase agreements to the big three credit reporting agencies for a period of five years; and
• Properly handle late deliveries, merchandise damaged at the time of delivery, and adhere to legal obligations to make repairs to merchandise during the course of the lease.
The state attorneys general that joined Attorney General Tong in today’s settlement are Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, Minnesota, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Nevada, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, Wisconsin, and Wyoming.
Assistant Attorneys General Joseph Gasser and Addison Keilty and Deputy Associate Attorney General Michael Wertheimer, Chief of the Consumer Protection Section assisted the Attorney General in this matter.

African startups raise $183 million in October
By AfricanManager

African startups raised a total of $183 million in October 2026 through 34 funding deals worth at least $100,000 each, according to the monthly report published on November 5 by investment tracking platform Africa: The Big Deal.
The amount represents a 24% decline compared with September and stands 29% below the average monthly funding of $259 million recorded over the past 12 months.
The slowdown was even more pronounced year-on-year. Funding fell by 58% from the $435 million raised by African startups in October 2025. The number of announced transactions also declined, with 34 deals recorded in October, against a monthly average of 43 over the past year.
Equity financing accounts for 60% of October funding
Equity investments dominated fundraising activity, accounting for $110 million, or 60% of the total raised during the month.
Debt financing amounted to $71 million, representing 39% of total funding, while grants accounted for approximately $2 million.
The two largest transactions each reached $40 million and were concluded outside Africa’s four leading startup funding markets: Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa.
In Morocco, health tech company ABA Life secured a $40 million investment agreement with pan-African investment fund Admaius Capital Partners.
Founded in 2021, the company develops solutions combining artificial intelligence, medical technologies, telemedicine and connected healthcare infrastructure. The funding will support its artificial intelligence programme for healthcare systems and facilitate its international expansion.
In Tanzania, agritech platform East Africa Foods raised nearly $40 million to expand its processing, storage and logistics capabilities, as well as its digital tools.
The company works with more than 28,000 small-scale farmers and supplies over 10,000 urban retailers. It plans to use the financing to expand into additional East African markets.
Nigeria leads African startup funding
Nigeria topped the continental ranking in October, with nine startups raising a combined $42 million, primarily through debt financing in the energy and mobility sectors.
Morocco and Tanzania followed with $40 million each, largely driven by the two major transactions involving ABA Life and East Africa Foods.
Egypt ranked fourth with $19 million, followed by Senegal with $13 million.
A notable shift in funding distribution was also recorded. Startups based in Africa’s four largest funding markets attracted just 46% of total capital raised in October, their lowest monthly share since November 2022.
Nevertheless, these four markets still accounted for 26 of the 34 startups that announced funding rounds of at least `$100,000 during the month.
Climate technology companies were another major beneficiary, attracting 55% of the funding announced in October.
African startups raise $2.4 billion in first 10 months
Between January and October 2026, African startups raised a cumulative $2.4 billion, down 12% from the $2.7 billion recorded during the same period in 2025.
However, the figures reveal contrasting trends between financing instruments. Equity funding increased by 5% year-on-year to $1.6 billion, while debt financing dropped by 33% to $740 million, compared with $1.1 billion a year earlier.
The number of funded startups also declined. A total of 343 companies announced funding rounds of at least $100,000 during the first 10 months of 2026, against 438 in the corresponding period of 2025, representing a 22% decrease.
The number of identified active investors fell by 16%, from 442 to more than 370.
With only two months remaining in the year, African startups would need to raise an additional $814 million in November and December to match the $3.2 billion secured in 2025, a target that Africa: The Big Deal considers unlikely.
Equity financing, however, could exceed its 2025 level. An additional $338 million would be sufficient to surpass the $1.9 billion raised through equity investments last year.

Crypto venture funding has reached $181 million in November, with Index Industries securing the week's largest deal through a $50 million seed round. API, payments and artificial intelligence led investment focus.
November funding so far totals $181 million across 21 rounds.
The latest monthly tally covers November through November 15.
October closed with $1.85 billion raised across 52 rounds, compared with $680.50 million across 53 rounds in September.
November 9 Seva Money raised $5 million in a seed round led by Blockwall and Revent, with other investors participating. Lithium recorded a strategic investment from LitVM with the amount undisclosed. River One recorded an M&A transaction involving Securitize, also with the amount undisclosed.
November 10 Index Industries raised $50 million in a seed round led by Lightspeed, alongside other investors. Alta secured $47.50 million in a Series A led by Index Ventures, with other participants. Marble raised $11 million in a seed round led by Polychain Capital, alongside other investors.
November 12 Griffin raised $20 million in a Series B led by Octagon Partners, with other investors participating. Kailash recorded a pre-seed round led by UTXO Management with the amount undisclosed. Spout Finance received a strategic investment from Ondo Finance with the amount undisclosed.
November 13 DI recorded funding from OKX Ventures and other investors. The amount and stage were undisclosed.
Over the latest 30 days, the investment activity index fell 35.0% from the previous month. Round counts declined while total funding increased.
The period recorded 57 investment rounds, down 19.7% month over month. Total funding rose 91.2% to $2.32 billion.
The average round size was in the $3 million to $10 million range. Strategic investment was the most active funding stage, while API was the leading investment focus.

candidates.title: Toronto’s Blue J raises $176-million to expand AI offerings to tax professionals
candidates.snippet: Toronto’s Blue J raises $176-million to expand AI offerings to tax professionals The Globe and Mail
candidates.text:
Comments
Share
Save for later
Please log in to bookmark this story. Log In Create an account
Rapidly growing Toronto AI software company Blue J Legal Inc. has secured a nine-figure financing for the second straight year as it prepares to offer agentic products to its clientele of tax specialists.
The University of Toronto spinout led by tax law professor Benjamin Alarie has raised a US$176-million financing led by Baltimore-based JMI Equity. U.S. financiers Oak HC/FT and Sapphire Ventures, which co-led a US$122-million investment into Blue J last year, are participating, as well as past backer Intrepid Growth Partners, a Canadian AI-focused investor. The deal, set to be announced Tuesday, values Blue J at US$700-million.
Nearly US$100-million will go to buy shares from employees and early investors. Blue J plans to use its $80-million in proceeds to commercialize its nascent agent product and expand in the U.K. – its third market after the U.S. and Canada – and globally.
Blue J’s main clients are tax accountants, though it also sells to tax lawyers, making it one of several companies bringing AI-driven products to law firms to hasten the automation of often tedious, time-consuming work .
Mr. Alarie, a past associate dean of U of T’s faculty of law, founded Blue J in 2015 with fellow professors Albert Yoon and Anthony Niblett. They worked to develop AI software that would help lawyers and accountants speed up the process of researching complex taxation matters, powered by predictive analytics software. Blue J raised venture capital and generated modest sales.
Then in late 2022 OpenAI launched ChatGPT, the AI chatbot that answered text questions in seconds. Mr. Alarie realized Blue J could fold generative AI capabilities into its product to answer far more tax-research questions. “The technology wasn’t really there to allow us to create a system that could answer any arbitrary tax research question – until we saw the promise of LLMs,” he said.
Blue J rebuilt its product incorporating OpenAI’s large language models, relaunching it in mid-2023. The updated version produced answers in about 90 seconds, but they were wrong about half of the time, a by-product of the quirky tendency of LLMs to generate incorrect information.
The Toronto company set about refining its product, in part by licensing data from Tax Notes, a leading publisher of tax views and commentary, and benefiting from improvements to successive releases of LLMs. Many of its answers come from content licensed by several tax data and information providers, some in exclusive deals.
By the end of 2024, Blue J could produce answers within 10 seconds that were 95-per-cent-plus accurate and its users could have technical back-and-forth conversations about complex tax matters with the program. Some companies found users could save two hours a week each using Blue J, whose individual plans start at US$1,498 a year.
Mr. Alarie said error rates have come down by about 80 per cent this year as measured by “down votes” from users in response to its generated answers, which now occur 0.05 per cent of the time. “We can now confidently deliver an answer to just about any tax research question,” Mr. Alarie said.
Blue J’s increasing speed and accuracy spurred interest, and the number of client firms mushroomed from less than 100 three years ago to more than 1,000 at the end of 2024 and 4,000 a year later. It now serves more than 6,500 firms. Blue J’s annual recurring revenue has expanded by 165 per cent since its last financing in August 2025 and is now in the mid-eight-figure range.
JMI principal Jack Duane said his firm tracked Blue J for years, and received “resounding positive sentiment” when it spoke to its customers, “not just around Blue J’s technology and research platform but also around the company and team. What came through clearly is they are a trusted AI vendor in a space where trust is of the utmost performance.”
Asked of the competitive risk, including the threat that the LLM giants themselves will move into the space, Mr. Duane responded that Blue J’s offering is “extremely hard to replicate” due to its access to proprietary data “and most importantly, their unique domain expertise.”
JMI is one of the most successful foreign investors in the Canadian tech sector. Its portfolio here includes stakes in Clio, Pointclickcare, Jane, Safe Software and Benevity.
Blue J is close to launching its agentic offerings, which will expand its utility beyond simply generating tax answers to clients. Its new workflow product will also enable them to automatically draft other work using its answers, including memos and notices of assessment. “Blue J will be increasingly capable of assisting with just about any of those advisory workflows for which research is an essential input,” Mr. Alarie said.
With reports from Joe Castaldo

November 13, 2026
|
by

|

Windward Bio has raised $175 million in its US initial public offering, adding to a growing pipeline of healthcare and biotechnology companies tapping public markets as listings in other sectors face pressure from economic uncertainty.
The Basel, Switzerland-based drug developer sold approximately 10.3 million shares at $17 each, within its marketed range of $16 to $18. Its shares are scheduled to begin trading on Friday on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol WWB.
The offering gives Windward fresh capital to advance its experimental antibody medicines for serious respiratory and dermatological diseases, with its lead programme targeting conditions that affect millions of patients worldwide. The company is backed by Novo Holdings, alongside other healthcare investors, and has attracted a $50 million commitment from French pharmaceutical group Sanofi.

Sanofi agreed to purchase $50 million in shares and pre-funded warrants through a private placement, providing Windward with an additional source of institutional backing as it enters the public market. The investment also gives the pharmaceutical group exposure to a biotechnology company developing treatments in areas where demand for new therapies remains significant.
Windward’s lead candidate, WIN378, is being developed for asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or COPD. The antibody is designed to block a protein involved in airway inflammation, an approach intended to address an underlying biological mechanism contributing to both conditions.
The programme will be central to the company’s development strategy as it moves into the public market. However, WIN378 remains an experimental medicine, and its commercial prospects will depend on clinical results, regulatory approvals and its ability to demonstrate meaningful benefits over existing treatments.
Led by founder and chief executive Luca Santarelli, Windward has raised $310 million in equity financing from Novo Holdings and other healthcare investors, including OrbiMed, Blue Owl and RTW Investments.
Santarelli has previously built biotechnology businesses that attracted substantial acquisition interest from larger pharmaceutical companies. VectivBio, one of his earlier ventures, was acquired by Ironwood Pharmaceuticals for $1.2 billion in 2023. Pfizer acquired another company he was associated with, Therachon, in 2019 for $810 million.
That history provides Windward with a management team familiar with biotechnology development and the commercial pressures facing companies seeking to bring new medicines to market. However, previous acquisitions do not guarantee that its current drug candidates will achieve similar outcomes.
The company’s IPO also underscores the importance of specialist healthcare investors in financing drug development. Biotechnology companies often require substantial capital over several years before generating commercial revenue, as clinical trials, regulatory submissions, and manufacturing preparations result in costs well ahead of product launches.
Public listings can provide access to a broader pool of capital, but they also expose early-stage drug developers to market volatility and greater scrutiny of clinical progress. For Windward, the challenge will be to use its new funding to advance its pipeline while showing that its scientific approach can translate into viable treatments.
Windward’s listing comes during a period of renewed activity among healthcare and biotechnology companies seeking to enter US public markets. The sector has accounted for a series of listings this autumn, even as macroeconomic headwinds have weakened IPO activity in other industries.
The contrast indicates that investor appetite for new listings remains selective rather than broadly restored. Companies with specialized healthcare programmes and established institutional backing have found opportunities to raise capital, while uncertainty over economic conditions and market valuations continues to weigh on other potential issuers.
For biotechnology businesses, the appeal of public markets is closely tied to the need for long-term financing. Unlike companies with established cash-generating operations, drug developers must often fund research and clinical trials before they can establish whether a candidate has commercial potential. A successful IPO can extend their financial runway and support development milestones that may improve their prospects of securing partnerships or attracting acquisition interest.
Still, investors face considerable risks. Drug candidates can fail in clinical trials, regulatory authorities can request additional evidence, and even approved treatments may struggle to gain market share. These make Windward’s valuation depend not only on its scientific programmes but also on the pace and quality of clinical data it produces.
Jefferies, TD Cowen, Piper Sandler and UBS Investment Bank are underwriting the offering.
Another Swiss healthcare-related company, dental firm vVardis, is also expected to go public on Friday. Its planned listing alongside Windward would add to the week’s activity and provide another indication of investor demand for companies operating in specialized healthcare markets.

Marrow Therapeutics Launches With $173 Million For Bone Marrow-Targeted Medicines
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:22 AM
Marrow Therapeutics Launches With $173 Million For Bone Marrow-Targeted Medicines
Marrow Therapeutics has launched with $173 million in combined Series A and Series B funding to develop genetic medicines for severe blood and bone marrow disorders.
The company’s $53 million Series A round was co-led by Scion Life Sciences and venBio. OrbiMed led a subsequent $120 million Series B financing.
All Series A investors participated in the Series B alongside RTW Investments, Surveyor Capital, Opaleye, NEXTBio Capital, Affinity Advisors, KKR, Spruce Street Capital, and Columbia Threadneedle Investments.
Scion Life Sciences founded Marrow Therapeutics, which is headquartered in Watertown, Massachusetts.
Developing A Bone Marrow-Targeting Platform
Marrow is developing engineered antibodies that target the transferrin receptor, also known as TfR1, in bone marrow.
The company’s Transferrin Antibody Bioconjugate platform is designed to deliver therapeutic payloads directly to bone marrow cells. Marrow plans to use this approach across multiple hematologic and bone marrow diseases.
Transferrin receptors help cells acquire iron and are present on multiple cell types. Developing medicines that engage the receptor requires controlling where therapeutic material is delivered and minimizing unintended effects in other tissues.
Marrow’s platform is intended to use engineered antibodies to reach bone marrow while avoiding off-target effects. The company is particularly focused on addressing the risk of anemia that has limited some earlier approaches involving TfR1.
Marrow believes its in vivo delivery strategy could overcome limitations associated with existing genetic medicines, including safety concerns, complex manufacturing, and restricted patient access.
These potential advantages have not yet been established in human clinical trials. The company’s programs remain in preclinical development.
Lead Program Targets Two Blood Disorders
Marrow’s lead candidate, MAR-101, is being developed for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia.
The program is currently undergoing studies required to support an investigational new drug application.
MAR-101 is designed to decrease BCL11A and reactivate the production of fetal hemoglobin. BCL11A is a regulator involved in the transition from fetal to adult hemoglobin after birth.
Increasing fetal hemoglobin has become a validated therapeutic strategy for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia. Fetal hemoglobin can reduce the effects of abnormal adult hemoglobin associated with these diseases.
Marrow intends to use one therapeutic approach for both conditions. The company refers to this strategy as a “pipeline in a product” because a single candidate could provide evidence supporting the delivery platform across more than one disease.
The program’s safety, durability, appropriate dose, and effectiveness will need to be evaluated through clinical studies.
Marrow is also developing additional programs for other blood and bone marrow disorders. The company has not disclosed detailed timelines or targets for those candidates.
Leadership With Transferrin Receptor Experience
Romesh Subramanian is leading Marrow as president and chief executive officer.
Tim Weeden has joined the company as chief scientific officer. His experience includes transferrin receptor biology, antibody development, and nucleic acid medicines.
John Najim is serving as chief operating officer and chief technology officer. His responsibilities include chemistry, manufacturing and controls, technical development, and business operations.
Gavriel Mullokandov is a founder and vice president of corporate development. He will support advancement of Marrow’s programs and broader platform.
The company’s leadership team has experience with earlier TfR1-based technologies that have entered clinical development. Marrow plans to apply lessons from those first-generation platforms to bone marrow delivery.
Adding Scientific And Industry Advisors
Art Levin has joined Marrow’s board of directors. Levin was the founding chief scientific officer of Avidity Biosciences and has experience developing genetic medicines.
Stuart Orkin has joined the company’s scientific advisory board. He is the David G. Nathan Distinguished Professor of Pediatrics at Harvard Medical School and an investigator at Boston Children’s Hospital through the Howard Hughes Medical Institute.
Orkin’s research has contributed to scientific understanding of fetal hemoglobin regulation and blood disorders.
The board and scientific advisory appointments give Marrow additional experience in genetic medicine, hematology, and drug development as MAR-101 moves toward a potential clinical study.
The $173 million in financing will support the lead program, development of the Transferrin Antibody Bioconjugate platform, and advancement of additional candidates.
Marrow expects to move its programs toward the clinic during the coming year, although the timing will depend on preclinical results, manufacturing work, and regulatory review.

“We’re at a pivotal moment in genetic medicine and its application in severe blood disorders – the field has validated key targets and shown that genetic approaches can work, but we need to solve the safety and accessibility challenges to truly transform patient outcomes. By precisely targeting the bone marrow, we’re able to deliver the potential of genetic medicines and provide sustained benefit, while simultaneously avoiding the risks that have constrained earlier approaches. Ondas Posts Record $167.5 Million Q3 Revenue, Raises 2026 Outlook
1 min read
ONDS
Ondas reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $167.5 million, up 100% sequentially and more than 16-fold year over year. Gross profit was $36.5 million, with a GAAP gross margin of 21.8%, while net loss was $64.7 million. The company raised its 2026 revenue target to at least $550 million and initiated a 2027 target of at least $1.1 billion.
Financial Highlights
Revenue was $167.5 million, compared with $10.1 million in Q3 2025 and $83.8 million in Q2 2026; pro forma organic revenue grew 64% year over year.
Gross profit was $36.5 million, compared with $2.6 million a year earlier. GAAP gross margin was 21.8%, and adjusted gross profit and adjusted gross margin were $58.3 million and 34.8%, respectively.
Operating loss was $189.5 million, compared with $15.5 million in Q3 2025.
Net loss was $64.7 million, compared with $7.5 million in Q3 2025. Diluted loss per share was $0.10.
Adjusted EBITDA loss was $59.7 million, compared with $8.1 million in Q3 2025. Ondas expects operating-platform Adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q4 2026 and company-wide profitability by Q3 2027.
Business Highlights
Formed Ondas Sentinel, combining DZYNE Technologies and World View under unified leadership to advance U.S. defense programs and the development, production, and deployment of defense technologies.
Established Regna AI to develop sovereign AI applications for defense and national security customers, using NVIDIA Nemotron models and Palantir platforms.
Expanded its land-systems portfolio and capabilities through acquisitions spanning unmanned ground vehicles, precision strike, sensing, connectivity, and navigation. The company also plans to acquire Stemme to strengthen production capacity for the ULTRA aircraft.
Advanced customer programs and product deployments, including counter-drone protection at major sports venues, a U.S. Army follow-on task order, the Digital Bat program, and the first flight of Blitz Block 3. Ondas also opened a training, testing, and flight-operations hub in Springfield, Ohio.

candidates.title: Before Trump Eased Nvidia Chip Exports to China, He Bought $160 Million in Stock, Raising Conflict-of-Interest Questions
candidates.snippet: Before Trump Eased Nvidia Chip Exports to China, He Bought $160 Million in Stock, Raising Conflict-of-Interest Questions BigGo Finance
candidates.text:
Before Trump Eased Nvidia Chip Exports to China, He Bought $160 Million in Stock, Raising Conflict-of-Interest Questions
Add preferred source
1
U.S. President Donald Trump has been revealed to have purchased $1 million to $5 million worth of Nvidia stock (approximately NT$33 million to NT$160 million) just before rescinding the Biden administration's AI chip export controls, and to have made at least three additional purchases of $250,000 to $500,000 each after opening H200 chip sales to China. An anti-corruption organization is questioning the intersection of policy shifts and personal financial interests. The controversy deepened after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid suspicions of involvement with an alleged Chinese spy. Democrats have launched an investigation, leaving Nvidia's China business prospects facing dual policy and political uncertainties.
Key Elements
Donald Trump Nvidia Jensen Huang Alice Huang DeKleptocracy U.S. Department of Commerce H200 chips AI Diffusion Framework Megaspeed The Guardian Council on Foreign Relations
U.S. President Donald Trump has been revealed to have made large purchases of Nvidia stock on the eve of rescinding the previous administration's AI chip export controls, triggering strong questions about the intersection of policy and personal financial interests. According to an analysis by anti-corruption organization DeKleptocracy of Trump's public financial disclosure filings, Trump purchased $1 million to $5 million worth of Nvidia shares (approximately NT$33 million to NT$160 million) just days before scrapping the Biden administration's "Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion" in May of last year.
The policy had originally established tiered management of AI chip exports based on each country's diplomatic and security relationship with the United States, with allies such as South Korea placed in a relatively permissive category, while China, Russia, and North Korea faced the strictest export blockades. The core purpose of the Biden administration's framework was to slow China's acquisition of advanced computing power and thereby its ability to build up its own AI capabilities. The Trump administration decided to scrap the entire framework on the grounds that it hindered American corporate innovation, imposed unnecessary regulatory burdens, and effectively relegated dozens of countries to "second-tier" status in a way that could damage diplomatic relations.
The timing overlap makes this transaction particularly sensitive. Had the framework actually taken effect, Nvidia's shipments to China—a market that once contributed about a quarter of its sales—would have been significantly constrained. After Trump announced the rescission of the controls, Nvidia's stock price promptly rose. The disclosure filings also show that Trump simultaneously purchased shares in tech giants including Apple, Meta, and Microsoft, rather than betting solely on Nvidia.
The controversy does not end there. In December 2025, Trump further announced that Nvidia would be allowed to sell H200 chips to approved customers in China, and the U.S. Department of Commerce formally granted approval in January 2026. The H200 was one of Nvidia's most advanced products at the time, with experts estimating its performance at roughly six times that of the chips China could obtain at the time. Disclosure filings show that after the export-opening announcement, Trump made at least three more Nvidia stock purchases, each in the range of $250,001 to $500,000 (approximately NT$16 million). Counting all records since taking office, the related trades have reached dozens.
DeKleptocracy stated bluntly that while the United States is still debating whether a suspected Chinese spy manipulated White House policy to profit an AI company, it must equally confront whether Trump's financial interests prompted him to hand the AI industry's critical technology to China.
At the center of the storm is Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. According to The Guardian, Huang had an extramarital affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who is alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence. This relationship enabled Megaspeed, Alice Huang's Singapore-based cloud computing company, to obtain billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia chips at a time when other operators could scarcely secure supply. Jensen Huang has announced his resignation following the exposure of the affair.
Jensen Huang has long been regarded as a close ally of Trump, and the two have met multiple times. Nvidia also donated $25 million (approximately NT$820 million) in October 2025 to support the construction of the Trump White House ballroom project, with Huang stating at the time that he was pleased to participate.
The Council on Foreign Relations has warned that allowing the H200 could substantially boost the computing capacity of China's AI factories, effectively adding fuel to the fire for America's primary competitor.
Political pursuit has already begun. It is understood that U.S. Democrats have initiated proceedings to investigate the political-business relationship between Trump and Jensen Huang, as well as the decision-making process behind the easing of semiconductor export controls.
The significance of this episode for the market goes beyond a single stock-disclosure controversy. Nvidia's China business prospects are now tied simultaneously to national security reviews and the White House occupant's personal financial records. Any advancement of congressional investigations or convening of hearings could reignite market concerns about the flip-flopping of export policy. For investors, whether H200 exports to China can proceed smoothly and whether the channel through which Megaspeed obtained chips will be pursued are two key indicators for gauging the visibility of Nvidia's China revenue.

candidates.text:
Boyuan Capital Closes RMB 1.1 Billion ($155 Million) Industrial AI Fund
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:03 AM
Boyuan Capital Closes RMB 1.1 Billion ($155 Million) Industrial AI Fund
Boyuan Capital has completed the final close of its second fund with approximately RMB 1.1 billion ($155 million) in capital commitments.
Fund II will invest in industrial artificial intelligence, embodied intelligence, advanced manufacturing, and the international expansion of Chinese industrial companies.
The fund’s limited partners include national funds of funds, social-security funds, industrial groups, financial institutions, and local government-guided funds.
German outdoor power-equipment manufacturer STIHL also participated in the fund, expanding Boyuan Capital’s international industrial and corporate network.
The U.S. dollar amount is an approximate conversion and may vary with exchange rates.
Expanding Boyuan’s Industrial Investment Strategy
Boyuan is Bosch Group’s only market-oriented investment platform. The firm combines financial investment with access to Bosch’s engineering knowledge, value chain, industrial applications, customers, and international operations.
Fund II builds on Boyuan’s earlier investment activity across automotive technology, new energy, and intelligent manufacturing.
The new vehicle will focus more directly on applying AI within industrial environments. Boyuan is targeting technologies that can move beyond laboratory demonstrations and operate at commercial scale in manufacturing, robotics, automotive, energy, and other physical industries.
The firm plans to evaluate whether a company’s technology can solve identifiable industrial problems, be integrated into existing production environments, and generate products or services that can be delivered consistently at scale.
Boyuan will also examine whether portfolio companies can use China’s engineering and manufacturing capabilities to compete in international markets.
Creating Companies Through Industrial Partnerships
Fund II’s strategy includes creating new businesses through carve-outs and joint incubation projects connected to Bosch and other industrial partners.
A carve-out can transform a technology, operating unit, or internal project into an independent company. Joint incubation allows Boyuan to combine the technical capabilities of an established industrial group with a new management team and outside capital.
This approach is intended to give young companies access to real industrial environments earlier in their development. It may also help them validate products with potential customers before investing in broader commercialization.
Boyuan plans to identify technologies within Bosch’s value chain that could become independent businesses. The firm will also pursue joint ventures with other manufacturers and technology partners.
Seven Initial Portfolio Companies
Fund II has already invested in seven companies.
The portfolio includes Bowintec, which was jointly incubated by Boyuan and Galbot, and Weifu Smart Sensing, a company created with Weifu High-Tech and Bosch.
Boyuan has also invested in robotics companies Linkhou Robotics and Inspire Robots. These investments reflect the fund’s focus on embodied intelligence, where AI systems interact with physical environments through robots, sensors, and automated equipment.
Another portfolio company, X-Motors, is pursuing international expansion beginning in Indonesia. Its strategy illustrates Boyuan’s effort to help Chinese advanced manufacturing companies establish operations and customer relationships outside their domestic market.
The fund intends to continue investing across industrial AI, robotics, sensing technology, automotive systems, and other areas where software, hardware, and manufacturing capabilities intersect.
Supporting Commercialization And Global Expansion
Boyuan plans to provide more than financial capital through its OpenBosch and Bo-ignition programs.
These initiatives connect portfolio companies with engineering expertise, industrial customers, real-world applications, and international networks.
The firm can help companies evaluate whether a technology works within an operating factory, vehicle, energy system, or other industrial setting. It can also support product validation, customer introductions, and the development of commercial operations.
For companies seeking international growth, Boyuan intends to provide connections to overseas industrial partners and markets. This assistance could include identifying local customers, adapting products to regulatory requirements, and establishing business operations outside China.
The participation of STIHL adds another international industrial organization to the fund’s network. Boyuan expects relationships with global manufacturers to support technical collaboration and potential commercialization opportunities for its portfolio companies.
Fund II’s strategy reflects the growing effort to apply generative AI, machine learning, robotics, and intelligent sensing to physical industries. Boyuan’s investment approach will emphasize whether these technologies can produce measurable operational and commercial results.
KEY QUOTES:
“Artificial intelligence is becoming a major force shaping the future of industry. However, technologies can only create lasting value when they are applied in industrial settings and solve real-world problems.”
Hongquan Jiang, Managing Partner and Chairman of Boyuan Capital
“We look further: Can its technology be deployed in real industrial environments? Can it deliver products and solutions at scale? And can the company bring China’s engineering and manufacturing capabilities to global markets?”
Michael Zhu, Managing Partner and Chief Executive Officer of Boyuan Capital

candidates.text:
MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:44 AM
MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
MaxCyte has agreed to acquire Akron BioProducts from affiliates of Arcline Investment Management for $151.8 million. The transaction is expected to close before the end of 2026, subject to customary conditions.
Akron Bio supplies Good Manufacturing Practice-grade reagents and ancillary materials used across cell therapy manufacturing. Its products include cytokines, growth factors, human plasma-derived materials, specialty media, and other consumables.
The acquisition will expand MaxCyte beyond its historical focus on nonviral cell engineering. Akron’s products are used in both viral and nonviral workflows at stages ranging from cell expansion through cryopreservation.
The combined company’s technologies are incorporated into five commercially approved therapies and support more than 100 clinical programs. Both businesses maintain drug master files referenced in customers’ regulatory submissions, creating long-term connections to validated manufacturing processes.
Akron is expected to produce approximately $28 million in 2026 revenue and between $7 million and $8 million of EBITDA. MaxCyte expects the acquisition to nearly double its revenue base, increase recurring consumables revenue, and accelerate its path toward profitability.
The companies have limited customer overlap despite serving similar biopharmaceutical markets. MaxCyte therefore expects to use its commercial infrastructure to introduce Akron products to additional customers and pursue cross-selling opportunities.
The buyer projects that Akron’s positive cash flow will help reduce the combined company’s annual cash burn to less than $10 million in 2027. MaxCyte expects to hold approximately $40 million to $45 million of cash when the transaction closes.
The consideration consists of $105 million in cash, subject to adjustments, 20,639,733 MaxCyte shares valued at approximately $26.8 million, and $20 million of guaranteed deferred payments. The deferred amount will be paid in two $10 million installments in January 2028 and January 2029.
MaxCyte has also secured a credit facility of up to $75 million from MidCap Financial, consisting of a $55 million term loan and a $20 million revolver. It plans to draw $20 million from the term loan and $2 million from the revolver at closing.
Akron will continue operating under its existing brand, with its management team and employees remaining part of the combined organization.
KEY QUOTES
“The acquisition of Akron marks an exciting new chapter for MaxCyte. This acquisition represents a significant step forward for us, expanding our presence across the viral and non-viral cell therapy development and manufacturing workflow, while projecting to nearly double our revenue base and accelerate our path to profitability. From day one, Akron provides us with an established portfolio of clinical and commercial programs supported by Akron’s DMFs and reagents. By bringing together two highly complementary businesses, we are diversifying our revenue base, increasing our mix of recurring revenue and expanding our exposure to the growth of commercially approved cell therapies, positioning MaxCyte for more durable near- and long-term growth. Like MaxCyte, Akron has become a trusted supplier to leading biopharma companies by delivering differentiated, high-quality products and best-in-class service. Akron is a market leader in the mission-critical consumables required for cell therapy manufacturing, including cytokines, growth factors, human plasma-derived products and media. We are excited to work alongside the talented Akron team as we bring together two companies to deepen customer relationships and better support cell therapy developers from development through commercialization.”
Maher Masoud, President and CEO of MaxCyte
“We are tremendously excited by the opportunity to join these two world-class organizations, leveraging our collective experience and expertise to support our partners as they bring transformative therapies to patients around the world. At Akron, we have always believed in earning our partners’ trust through consistent execution, uncompromising quality, and a deep commitment to the patients they serve. As part of MaxCyte, we remain committed to delivering the quality, reliability, and innovation our partners have come to expect.”
Ezequiel Zylberberg, COO of Akron Bio
“Akron Bio’s success reflects the dedication of its team, and we believe MaxCyte is the best partner to drive continued growth and expand its impact on patients. Our decision to accept MaxCyte shares as part of the consideration reflects our confidence in the combined company’s long-term value and allows us to participate in its future success.”
Arcline Investment Management

Round led by Highland Europe, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management's 1GT and Axon Partners Group, and with participation from existing and new investors.
BARCELONA, Spain , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stark Future, the Barcelona company behind the world's best-selling enduro motorcycle, today announced the close of a financing round with a total transaction value in excess of €150 million, the largest investment ever made in a European electric motorcycle company. The round values Stark Future at €1.2 billion pre-money, making it Europe's first electric motorcycle company valued above €1 billion. The round was led by Highland Europe, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management's 1GT climate private equity strategy and Spain-based international investment firm Axon Partners Group, with participation from existing shareholders and friends and family. The round was oversubscribed and exceeded the initial target, prompting the Company to keep the door open for a second closing to accommodate additional strategic partners, including Lombard Odier among others.
Continue Reading
Anton Wass - CEO and Founder of Stark Future
Stark Future HQ - Barcelona
Stark VARG SM_Lineup
Anton Wass, Production line Barcelona HQ
Founded in 2020 on an uncompromising belief that electric motorcycles should not just be the green alternative, but the better machine, Stark Future builds bikes designed to beat the best combustion competitors in every category they enter. Today, the VARG platform, spanning motocross, enduro and supermoto, is designed, engineered and built in-house at the Company's 20,000 m² facility on the outskirts of Barcelona. The new capital will fund global expansion and the development of new electric platforms.
In just three years of sales, Stark has gone from challenger to category leader. The VARG is now the best-selling enduro motorcycle on the planet, outselling every combustion competitor. Within its first year, Stark took around 50% of the enduro market in Germany and the top spot in France and Italy, while the United States has grown to be its largest market by volume. From a standing start, Stark has taken around 5% of the €3 billion global off-road motorcycle market from combustion in three years. The new capital is aimed at repeating that, and more, by entering new motorcycle categories, in a much larger €90 billion addressable motorcycle market. Few hardware companies grow this fast. Fewer do it profitably.
Anton Wass, Founder and CEO of Stark Future, says: "Six years ago, Stark was an unwavering belief that electric could be the better machine, not the compromise. Today it's the largest investment ever made in a European electric motorcycle company. We turned the industry on its head once with the VARG, taking 5% of a €3 billion market from combustion in three years. This gives us the resources to do it again, and more, in a €90 billion market. While others in this industry have run out of road, we've grown, turned profitable, and brought Highland Europe and world-renowned institutional investors on board, and we have kept the door open in the second closing for a few more who share the same ambition. None of it would have happened without the riders who chose a VARG before the world's biggest investors did, and the dealers who put it on their floors. Thank you for making this dream real. We're not here to take part in the future of motorcycling. We're here to lead it."
Tony Zappalà, Partner at Highland Europe, added: "Since selling its first bike just three years ago, Stark Future has become the go-to name in performance off-road motorcycling. It has built that traction in the most technical and unforgiving segment of the market. Once we met with Anton and the team, we caught the fever of the company's guiding principle: to build the best bike with no compromises. Motorbikes are the last major vehicle category to meaningfully undergo electrification. Many have tried, but no one has matched Stark's success. We believe it will be the company that leads the transition with best-in-class performance."
Vikram Raju, Head of Climate Private Equity Investing at Morgan Stanley Investment Management and 1GT, said: "The most compelling climate solutions are often those that do not ask their customers to compromise. Stark Future is a powerful example of that, combining a relentless focus on engineering excellence with electric motorcycles built to compete on performance first. At 1GT, we back ambitious founders and teams whose products and solutions have the potential to create meaningful real-world impact and advance the transition to a lower-carbon economy. Stark Future Closes Financing Round in Excess of €150 Million in Total Transactional Value as Its Electric Motorcycles Overtake Combustion on the World Stage
November 16, 2026
Motor Sports NewsWire
Motorcycle , Powersports
0
Round led by Highland Europe, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s 1GT and Axon Partners Group, and with participation from existing and new investors.
BARCELONA, SPAIN – November 16, 2026 – ( Motor Sports NewsWire ) – Stark Future, the Barcelona company behind the world’s best-selling enduro motorcycle, today announced the close of a financing round with a total transaction value in excess of €150 million, the largest investment ever made in a European electric motorcycle company. The round values Stark Future at €1.2 billion pre-money, making it Europe’s first electric motorcycle company valued above €1 billion. The round was led by Highland Europe, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s 1GT climate private equity strategy and Spain-based international investment firm Axon Partners Group, with participation from existing shareholders and friends and family. The round was oversubscribed and exceeded the initial target, prompting the Company to keep the door open for a second closing to accommodate additional strategic partners, including Lombard Odier among others.
Founded in 2020 on an uncompromising belief that electric motorcycles should not just be the green alternative, but the better machine, Stark Future builds bikes designed to beat the best combustion competitors in every category they enter. Today, the VARG platform, spanning motocross, enduro and supermoto, is designed, engineered and built in-house at the Company’s 20,000 m² facility on the outskirts of Barcelona. The new capital will fund global expansion and the development of new electric platforms.
In just three years of sales, Stark has gone from challenger to category leader. The VARG is now the best-selling enduro motorcycle on the planet, outselling every combustion competitor. Within its first year, Stark took around 50% of the enduro market in Germany and the top spot in France and Italy, while the United States has grown to be its largest market by volume. From a standing start, Stark has taken around 5% of the €3 billion global off-road motorcycle market from combustion in three years. The new capital is aimed at repeating that, and more, by entering new motorcycle categories, in a much larger €90 billion addressable motorcycle market. Few hardware companies grow this fast. Fewer do it profitably.
Anton Wass, Founder and CEO of Stark Future, says: “Six years ago, Stark was an unwavering belief that electric could be the better machine, not the compromise. Today it’s the largest investment ever made in a European electric motorcycle company. We turned the industry on its head once with the VARG, taking 5% of a €3 billion market from combustion in three years. This gives us the resources to do it again, and more, in a €90 billion market. While others in this industry have run out of road, we’ve grown, turned profitable, and brought Highland Europe and world-renowned institutional investors on board, and we have kept the door open in the second closing for a few more who share the same ambition. None of it would have happened without the riders who chose a VARG before the world’s biggest investors did, and the dealers who put it on their floors. Thank you for making this dream real. We’re not here to take part in the future of motorcycling. We’re here to lead it.”
Tony Zappalà, Partner at Highland Europe, added: “Since selling its first bike just three years ago, Stark Future has become the go-to name in performance off-road motorcycling. It has built that traction in the most technical and unforgiving segment of the market. Once we met with Anton and the team, we caught the fever of the company’s guiding principle: to build the best bike with no compromises. Motorbikes are the last major vehicle category to meaningfully undergo electrification. Many have tried, but no one has matched Stark’s success. We believe it will be the company that leads the transition with best-in-class performance.”
Vikram Raju, Head of Climate Private Equity Investing at Morgan Stanley Investment Management and 1GT, said: “The most compelling climate solutions are often those that do not ask their customers to compromise. Stark Future is a powerful example of that, combining a relentless focus on engineering excellence with electric motorcycles built to compete on performance first. At 1GT, we back ambitious founders and teams whose products and solutions have the potential to create meaningful real-world impact and advance the transition to a lower-carbon economy. We are excited to support the company’s next phase of growth and look forward to bringing the resources and global capabilities of Morgan Stanley to the partnership as Stark continues to scale internationally.”
Alfonso de León, Managing Partner at Axon Partners Group , said: “Stark is the rare technology and performance company that grows like a tech business and earns like an industrial one. As a Spanish-based investment firm, Axon is proud to invest alongside Highland, 1GT, and a group of world-class investors to support a Spanish company leading a global category. This is just the beginning of what Stark will become.”
Stifel served as the lead financial adviser to Stark Future for this transaction. Investec-led financing recapitalizes operating assets and funds new construction projects
BOSTON , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Calibrant Energy, a leading provider of on-site energy solutions, today announced the close of a $145 million debt facility led by Investec for solar and battery storage projects across multiple U.S. power markets. The portfolio includes a 120 megawatt-hour (MWh) battery energy storage system (BESS) serving a hyperscale data center customer in PJM. Citi , Liberty Bank, and Siemens Financial Services also participated in the facility.
Data center operators are looking for ways to get online faster as PJM and federal regulators work through how large power users connect to the grid. Calibrant's engineered BESS solutions give energy-intensive facilities greater control over how and when they draw power. This flexibility supports faster interconnection timelines and reduces the need for costly grid infrastructure upgrades that would otherwise be passed on to other ratepayers.
"Data center operators are choosing on-site energy storage because it is a fast, reliable, and effective way to get online and operate as responsible grid citizens," said Phil Martin, CEO of Calibrant Energy. "With this financial close and site mobilization for a hyperscale data center, Calibrant continues to demonstrate that large-load flexibility is not just possible but a commercial reality today."
Calibrant's turnkey, zero-capex solutions unlock the path to reliable power that the world's largest power users need to grow their businesses.
"Investec is proud to support Calibrant and Macquarie on this transaction," said Fred Petit, Co-Head of Energy & Infrastructure North America at Investec. "We value the opportunity to partner with experienced investors and operators, and to provide financing that advances the energy transition and the critical infrastructure needed to meet growing power demand across the U.S."
Calibrant Energy now has more than 5.9 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage capacity in operation, in construction, or under exclusive development agreements, including additional sites with the same hyperscale customer. This growth reflects rising demand from large power users for on-site energy solutions that accelerate speed to power while easing strain on the grid. It also reflects customers' preference for a trusted, experienced partner that can develop, own, and operate these solutions and deliver the power outcomes their business plans depend on.
About Calibrant Energy : Calibrant Energy is a leading provider of on-site energy solutions for large power users. Calibrant's turnkey, zero-capex solutions unlock the paths to power that the world's largest power users need to grow their businesses, while enabling a more reliable, affordable, and sustainable power grid. As the trusted on-site energy partner to many of the world's largest enterprises, Calibrant has more than 2.2 GW / 5.9 GWh of projects in operation, construction, or under exclusive development agreements. Calibrant is backed by Macquarie Asset Management. Learn more at www.calibrantenergy.com

Investec plc is a FTSE 100 listed company which holds the majority of Investec Group's non-Southern African businesses under a dual listed company structure. IBP partners with private, institutional and corporate clients, offering banking and investment services in the UK, Europe and certain other countries.
IBP also offers wealth management services through its strategic combination with Rathbones Group. IBP has operated in the UK since 1992. As part of the Investec Group, IBP is a purpose-driven organisation, dedicated to its core purpose of creating enduring worth. This means we will always strive to create long-term value for all stakeholders and contribute meaningfully to people, communities and the planet. candidates.title: Vumedi Raises $140M Series B, Oakland Health Tech
candidates.snippet: Vumedi Raises $140M Series B, Oakland Health Tech Hoodline
candidates.text:
555 12th St. — Oakland Street Scene
Google Street View
An Oakland health-tech company has raised $140 million in a new funding round. Vumedi, which builds an AI-powered learning platform for physicians, has raised $140 million in Series B funding, with plans to pour the money into talent, research and development, product development and outreach as it expands its clinical learning tools.
The investment came from Oak HC/FT, according to FinSMEs , which reported the round. Vumedi is led by founder and CEO Roman Giverts, and the company describes its platform as a tool that connects clinicians with specialists and peers so they can learn procedures, evaluate treatments and navigate complex cases, the outlet reports.
What the Platform Actually Does
At the center of Vumedi's pitch is scale paired with AI. The platform uses artificial intelligence to turn more than 100,000 physician-led videos and nearly 5,000 podcast episodes, spanning more than 21 medical specialties, into what the company calls an on-demand clinical resource, per the same report. Rather than leaving clinicians to sift through hours of footage, the system synthesizes multiple expert perspectives and links directly to time-stamped segments within videos.
The company says its platform now serves more than 150,000 NPI-verified clinicians and generated over 56 million minutes of learning over the past 12 months. Back in a 2018 interview, Giverts described Vumedi's mission as helping physicians make the best care decisions through what he called unbiased video education in an interview with MPO-mag.com . That same article reported the platform then had roughly 250,000 physician users and 20,000 videos contributed by more than 5,000 healthcare organizations and professionals, including partnerships with 150 hospitals and conferences such as Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic and Johns Hopkins.
Funding Figures Don't All Line Up
Not every account of Vumedi's fundraising history tells the same story. A snippet from 01net referenced a $104 million investment from Oak HC/FT, though it's unclear from that report whether it describes the same financing as the newly reported $140 million round or a separate transaction. Separately, CB Insights lists Vumedi's most recent funding round as a $79.98 million Series B dated May 22, 2025, and puts the company's total raised at $82.08 million across four rounds. The available reporting does not reconcile these differing figures with the $140 million sum reported this week.
Part of a Broader AI Health-Tech Wave
Vumedi's raise lands amid a broader uptick in digital-health investment. Companies in the sector raised $7.4 billion in the first half of 2026, up roughly $1 billion from the same period in 2025, according to Fierce Healthcare . The outlet counted 244 completed deals in that window, with $4.2 billion invested in the first quarter and $3.2 billion in the second.
A notable share of that capital came in the form of megadeals. Nineteen companies raised 20 financings of at least $100 million in the first half of 2026, representing 45 percent of all capital invested, Fierce Healthcare reported, citing deals that included AI radiology company Aidoc's $150 million raise. Clinical-reference platform OpenEvidence, a comparable player in physician-facing AI tools, announced its own $210 million Series B at a $3.5 billion valuation in mid-2025, co-led by Google Ventures and Kleiner Perkins with Sequoia Capital, Coatue, Conviction and Thrive also participating, according to a release distributed via PR Newswire . That company said it planned to use its funding to expand strategic content partnerships feeding its medical knowledge library, a goal that echoes Vumedi's own stated plans to grow its content, features and formats.
For now, Vumedi's leadership has framed the new capital as fuel for expansion rather than a pivot. The company's stated plans, per FinSMEs, center on investing in people and product to expand its AI-driven video and podcast library.

candidates.text:
Zacua Ventures Raises $135 Million to Invest in AI, Robotics and Industrial Technology
Published on: 11 November، 2026
Zacua Ventures
Zacua Ventures closes its $135 million Fund II to back Physical AI, construction robotics, industrial technology, energy, manufacturing and infrastructure startups.
The next major opportunity in artificial intelligence may not be confined to software applications or foundation models.
Increasingly, investors are looking toward technologies that can transform the physical economy, from construction sites and cement factories to energy networks, manufacturing facilities and data centers.
Zacua Ventures is positioning itself at the center of this shift, closing its second fund at $135 million to expand investments beyond construction technology into a broader range of Physical Industries, including robotics, manufacturing, energy, mining and critical infrastructure.
$135 Million to Back Technologies Building the Physical Economy
Zacua Ventures closed Fund II at $135 million, more than doubling its $56 million debut fund and exceeding its fundraising target by 35%.
The raise reflects growing investor interest in technology applied to capital-intensive industries that have historically attracted less venture capital than software and digital platforms.
The firm’s investment thesis is built around a simple premise: construction, energy, manufacturing and mining are not merely facing productivity challenges.
They need fundamental operational transformation through AI, robotics, data and advanced technologies.
AI Is Moving From Digital Applications to Physical Industries
Zacua’s strategy extends beyond conventional AI tools, targeting companies that deploy technology directly into industrial and field operations.
Its investments include autonomous construction robots, AI platforms that identify project risks before construction begins, and technologies designed to reduce emissions from cement production.
These businesses are becoming increasingly relevant as industries face labor shortages, aging workforces, complex operational processes and growing demand for AI infrastructure.
The opportunity is not simply to automate existing workflows, but to redesign how physical industries operate.
Why Venture Capital Is Turning Toward Physical Industries
Construction, energy, manufacturing and mining represent enormous markets with persistent productivity gaps and substantial infrastructure requirements.
McKinsey estimates that global infrastructure investment needs will reach $106 trillion through 2040, while Gartner projects data-center power demand could reach 290 gigawatts by 2030.
These requirements create opportunities for startups developing technologies that improve industrial productivity, reduce operating costs and reshape supply chains.
However, investing in physical industries is fundamentally different from funding software companies. Technologies must be tested in real operating environments, integrated into existing equipment and workflows, and demonstrate measurable economic value before they can scale.
From Construction Robotics to Low-Carbon Cement
Zacua’s early Fund II investments illustrate the breadth of its strategy.
Origin Robotics develops autonomous robots capable of finishing interior walls, while CURA Climate is working to electrify cement production and reduce emissions by up to 85% through its pilot technology.
Neuron Factory applies AI to preconstruction planning, using a proprietary knowledge graph to identify risks and coordinate project decisions.
These companies highlight an important investment principle: the value of industrial technology depends not only on innovation, but also on its ability to solve expensive operational problems in markets where implementation can be challenging.
Corporate Networks Give Zacua a Commercialization Advantage
Zacua is backed by more than 30 corporate and institutional investors across over 20 countries, including Volvo Group Venture Capital, Holcim Maqer Ventures, Hilti Venture, Trimble Ventures and Dubai Future District Fund.
The network provides startups with access to industrial customers, strategic partners and real-world operating environments.
This support can help founders overcome one of the most difficult barriers in industrial technology: moving from a promising prototype to commercially deployed solutions at scale.
The Real Investment Opportunity Is Industrial Productivity
Zacua Ventures represents a growing venture-capital thesis that treats technology as a tool for rebuilding the physical economy rather than simply creating another generation of digital applications.
As AI investment expands into construction, energy, manufacturing and mining, startups capable of delivering measurable productivity improvements could become major beneficiaries of the next investment cycle.
The challenge remains execution.
Industrial startups must demonstrate economic value, secure customer adoption and manage complex deployment requirements before their technologies can generate sustainable returns.
For venture capital, the opportunity may be substantial—but the winners will be those that turn advanced technology into measurable improvements in the real world.

candidates.text:
Zacua Ventures raises $135 million to invest in robotics, physical AI and industrial technology
November 15, 2026 by Sam Francis
Venture capital firm Zacua Ventures has closed its second investment fund at $135 million, more than doubling the size of its original $56 million fund as it expands its focus on robotics, physical AI and technologies for industrial applications.
The San Francisco-based firm says Fund II was 35 percent oversubscribed, attracting commitments from more than 30 corporate and institutional investors across over 20 countries.
Originally focused on construction technology, Zacua is broadening its investment strategy to include manufacturing, energy, mining, infrastructure and other sectors it collectively describes as the “Physical Industries”.
The firm believes these sectors offer substantial opportunities for technologies that combine robotics, artificial intelligence and software with practical industrial expertise.
Vivin Hegde, founding partner at Zacua Ventures, says: “The industries that underpin modern life are entering a forced transformation cycle. Housing is out of reach. Energy grids are under pressure. Workforces are aging out. The AI infrastructure buildout is placing even greater demands on the industries already struggling to keep pace.
“These are not isolated problems; they’re converging across the Physical Industries, a category venture capital has largely overlooked. We built Zacua in construction because we saw these challenges firsthand. Fund II takes what we learned there and applies it to the broader physical world.”
Building on construction robotics investments
Zacua has already invested in 34 early-stage companies across 11 markets, with several investments demonstrating its interest in industrial automation.
Among its portfolio companies is Gravis Robotics, an ETH Zurich spinout developing physical AI for autonomous construction equipment. The company raised $200 million in Series A funding from SoftBank earlier this year, reaching a reported valuation of $1 billion.
Another investment is Origin Robotics, whose OG1 robot autonomously finishes interior walls. The company emerged from stealth with $20 million in seed and Series A financing, with Zacua leading the latter round.
Other investments include Flexnode, which develops modular data centers, and CURA Climate, which is working on technologies to reduce emissions from cement production.
Zacua’s first exit came earlier this year when construction risk-management software company Document Crunch was acquired by Trimble.
Expanding industrial investment
Fund II’s investors include Volvo Group Venture Capital, Holcim Maqer Ventures, Hilti Venture, Trimble Ventures, Acciona, DPR Construction, Mortenson and Dubai Future District Fund.
The firm says its corporate investor network provides portfolio companies with access to industrial customers, technical expertise and opportunities to test emerging technologies in operational environments.
Juan Nieto, founding partner at Zacua Ventures, says: “Fund I proved that our model works in one of the most complex and consequential industries in the world.
“Fund II allows us to take that same playbook much further. We are not changing what we do. We are applying the same early-stage conviction, founder-first philosophy and industry network across the broader Physical Industries.”
Zacua has already begun investing from Fund II, with robotics, industrial AI and infrastructure technologies expected to remain central to its strategy.
