candidates.snippet: South African fintech Yoco secures $100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital Advisors Innovation Village
candidates.text:
Yoco Founders
South African fintech Yoco secures $100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital Advisors
0
By
Tapiwa Matthew Mutisi
on
November 9, 2026
Africa , Fintech , Funding , Investments , SMEs , Startups
Yoco Technologies , the South African fintech company backed by global private equity firm TPG Inc., has secured a $100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital Advisors LLC (VPC), a U.S.-based alternative investment manager with approximately $3.6 billion in assets under management.
The funding represents a significant milestone for Yoco as it continues expanding its financial services ecosystem for small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) across South Africa.
Funding to Expand Merchant Financing
According to reports, Yoco plans to use the new credit facility to strengthen and expand financing opportunities available to its growing network of merchants.
The company has evolved beyond its origins as a point-of-sale (POS) payments provider and now offers a broader suite of digital commerce solutions designed to help small businesses accept payments, manage operations, and access working capital.
The $100 million facility will enable Yoco to extend additional funding to merchants that use its platform, helping business owners access capital needed to purchase inventory, invest in growth, manage cash flow, or navigate seasonal fluctuations.
Access to affordable financing remains one of the biggest challenges facing SMEs in South Africa, making merchant-lending solutions an increasingly important area of growth for fintech companies.
Yoco’s Evolution Into a Full-Service Fintech Platform
Founded in 2015, Yoco initially built its reputation by providing simple card payment devices and digital payment solutions to small businesses that were often underserved by traditional banks.
Over time, the company expanded its offering to include:
Payment acceptance solutions
Point-of-sale systems
Business management tools
Online payment services
Merchant cash advances and financing products
Digital commerce solutions
Today, Yoco serves hundreds of thousands of merchants across South Africa, ranging from informal traders and restaurants to retail stores and service-based businesses.
The company’s technology-driven approach enables it to analyse transaction histories and business performance data, allowing it to offer financing products tailored to merchants’ actual business activity rather than relying solely on traditional credit assessments.
Strategic Backing From TPG
Yoco has attracted significant investor interest in recent years, including backing from TPG Inc. , one of the world’s largest private equity and alternative asset management firms. The involvement of TPG has provided Yoco with additional capital and strategic support as it expands its footprint within South Africa’s rapidly growing digital payments market.
The latest facility from Victory Park Capital further strengthens Yoco’s ability to scale its lending operations without diluting existing shareholders, as debt financing allows the company to access growth capital while maintaining ownership structures.
Victory Park Capital’s Growing Fintech Portfolio
Victory Park Capital has become an active investor in financial technology and alternative lending businesses globally.
The firm specializes in providing flexible capital solutions to companies operating in sectors such as:
Financial services
Fintech
Consumer lending
Asset-backed finance
Small business financing
Its financing structures are often designed to help high-growth companies scale lending activities and reach underserved customer segments. The partnership with Yoco aligns with VPC’s broader strategy of supporting technology-enabled financial services platforms that increase financial inclusion and improve access to capital.
Boosting Financial Inclusion for South African SMEs
The new funding arrives at a time when digital financial services are playing an increasingly important role in South Africa’s small-business sector. Many entrepreneurs continue to face difficulties accessing traditional bank financing due to limited collateral, insufficient credit history, or lengthy approval processes.
By leveraging merchant transaction data and digital payment records, fintech companies such as Yoco are helping to bridge this gap and provide businesses with faster, more accessible funding options. The $100 million facility is expected to strengthen Yoco’s ability to meet growing demand for working-capital solutions among its merchant base while supporting broader efforts to improve financial inclusion for South Africa’s SME sector.
Outlook
The agreement with Victory Park Capital marks another major step in Yoco’s transformation from a payments provider into a comprehensive financial platform for small businesses. With access to $100 million in additional capital, the company is well positioned to expand its merchant financing operations, deepen customer relationships, and support the growth of thousands of South African businesses.
As fintech-driven lending continues to gain momentum across Africa, Yoco’s latest funding deal underscores investor confidence in digital financial services and the critical role they play in helping small businesses access the capital needed to grow and thrive.

candidates.text:
Rox Raises $100 Million Series B at $1.3 Billion Valuation to Grow Revenue for the Global 2000
News provided by
Rox
Nov 11, 2026, 08:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rox, which researches and develops the world's best revenue agent for the Global 2000, today announced a $100 million Series B financing at a $1.3 billion valuation.
The round is co-led by General Catalyst and March Capital, with existing investors Sequoia Capital and Factory doubling down on their investment, alongside new investors including Databricks Ventures and Prosperity7 Ventures.
In its first year in market, Rox has grown annual recurring revenue by more than 10x and is now deployed by leading public and private enterprises in non-tech industries including IT services, energy, commodities, medical technology, industrial manufacturing and automotive.
Rox is seeing more than 700% net revenue retention across enterprise customers, and some are seeing ~25x return on investment within 90 days.
The financing follows Rox's $50 million seed and Series A announced in November 2024. Zach Frankel, an early investor in Ramp, Cognition and Applied Compute, is also an early backer of Rox.
Built for the sellers who drive revenue
Enterprise sales follows a power law: the top 15% of reps bring in roughly 90% of revenue. However, the average rep spends 40% of their time on administrative work, according to Salesforce. Rox was built to raise the ceiling for those teams.
The Rox agent helps automate pipeline generation, deal execution, and upsells, so reps can better manage complex accounts and build relationships.
Agents doing real commercial work
Rox is a vertically integrated, enterprise-ready AI system built on each customer's individual data warehouse. The results are already changing sales economics:
For a global IT services firm, Rox delivered $330M in qualified pipeline in eight weeks. Reps also handed off pursuit prep to Rox and got 1,000 hours back for selling.
For a global medical technology company, Rox has identified $200M+ of new funding opportunities at medical facilities that the team is actively pursuing. Despite multi-year sales cycles for some opportunities, Rox has already helped the team close $24M in revenue in just five months.
For a leading global engineering and professional services firm, Rox identified over $310M in potential opportunities, spanning signal-qualified leads and estimated net-new pipeline from previously missed public-sector bids.
For a market-leading DevSecOps platform, Rox doubled outbound volume. Rox has transformed them into an agent-driven org and delivered millions of dollars of pipeline.
For a leading payroll provider, Rox opens up an entirely new source of growth: autonomously finding and engaging 4M prospects the sales team couldn't economically reach, and turning them into meetings at just 20% of the cost of traditional outreach.
For a global industrial software company, Rox doubled sales team capacity and delivered 50+ meetings in just six weeks.
For a large German engineering and technology company, Rox delivered 24.3x ROI in 90 days by automating sales work the business had never been able to do before, from always-on pipeline tracking to personalized outreach at scale.
Revenue is the next frontier for AI agents and one of the hardest. Unlike code, where an agent can test its work immediately, sales outcomes take weeks or months to materialize. Rox is solving that with custom models and original research, including launching a revenue-agent benchmark to measure performance on real-world revenue tasks. Rox recently cut outbound prospecting pricing by 50%, driven by research-led improvements.
"Rox is the product I wish I had," said Ishan Mukherjee, Co-founder and CEO of Rox. "We built Rox for the Global 2000 because that is where the problem is the hardest and the stakes are the highest. Our own go-to-market runs entirely on Rox, with no other tools, and our customers are already generating hundreds of millions of dollars of pipeline at a fraction of the traditional cost. This round lets us go further in our ultimate goal of growing the world's revenue."
Rox will use the capital to advance its AI research, custom models and evaluation infrastructure, and expand its work with large enterprises across healthcare, industrial, financial services, energy and technology. Rox was named a Visionary in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Revenue Action Orchestration and a Major Player in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for Worldwide Unified Revenue Orchestration Platforms.
INVESTOR QUOTES
Konstantine Buhler, Partner, Sequoia Capital
"Rox is a clear example of the real ROI of AI, delivering measurable results for Global 2000 sales teams and CROs in under a quarter. We backed Ishan and his team early because of their deep expertise in enterprise sales and their proven ability to drive meaningful pipeline impact. Rox will become synonymous with revenue, and we are proud to be investors in their vision."
Marc Bhargava, Managing Director, General Catalyst
"Ishan is as obsessed with revenue as other founders are with rockets, and that has pulled the strongest applied-AI team we have seen in this category. For the first time, boards are telling revenue leaders to try something new rather than renew the incumbent. There is a long graveyard of companies that said they'd take on Salesforce. The difference now is that the old systems were never built for agents, and boards are finally willing to start fresh. Rox is winning those conversations. That's why we doubled down."
Sumant Mandal, Co-Founder and Managing Partner, March Capital
"We're thrilled to partner with Ishan and the Rox team as they build a generational platform for revenue teams. Their rare combination of deep technical talent and real domain expertise shows up in the product, and it came through clearly in our conversations with delighted Global 2000 customers across industries."
Prosperit

Published on: 13 November، 2026
Rox
Rox, the AI startup developing autonomous agents for enterprise sales, has raised $100 million in Series B funding at a $1.3 billion valuation,
Rox, the AI startup developing autonomous agents for enterprise sales, has raised $100 million in Series B funding at a $1.3 billion valuation, with participation from Prosperity7 Ventures, the venture capital arm of Saudi Aramco.
The round was co-led by General Catalyst and March Capital, with existing investors Sequoia Capital and Factory participating alongside new investors, including Databricks Ventures.
From Customer Data to AI-Powered Sales Execution
Rox develops AI revenue agents designed to help large enterprises identify commercial opportunities, generate sales pipelines and automate customer-facing workflows.
Its platform supports tasks ranging from prospect research and lead qualification to personalized outreach, meeting scheduling, deal management and account expansion.
The agents operate within companies’ existing systems and leverage enterprise customer data to support sales execution.
Rather than simply generating recommendations or content, Rox aims to enable AI agents to take action across revenue workflows and deliver measurable commercial outcomes.
ARR Grew More Than 10x in Its First Year
Rox said its annual recurring revenue (ARR) grew more than tenfold in its first year in the market, as the platform expanded across enterprise customers in technology, energy, industrial and financial services sectors.
Its customer base includes companies such as Groq, Ramp and Puma Energy. Rox also reported net revenue retention exceeding 700% among enterprise customers, reflecting significant expansion in revenue from existing accounts.
The company is positioning its platform around measurable business impact, including pipeline generation, customer engagement and sales productivity.
Funding to Accelerate AI Research and Enterprise Expansion
Rox plans to use the new capital to advance AI research, develop custom models and strengthen its evaluation infrastructure for real-world revenue tasks.
The company also intends to expand its enterprise customer base across healthcare, industrial manufacturing, financial services, energy and technology.
Why AI Revenue Agents Are Attracting Investors
The funding highlights a broader shift in enterprise AI, from tools that generate content or assist employees to agents capable of executing complex workflows and connecting data with business actions.
Sales is emerging as a major application area because it involves extensive customer data, repetitive administrative tasks and multiple interconnected processes, from prospecting to account management.
However, the long-term opportunity for Rox will depend on its ability to demonstrate sustainable customer returns, scale enterprise deployments and compete with established customer relationship management platforms.
The investment underscores growing venture capital interest in AI agents that can deliver measurable operational and commercial outcomes, positioning autonomous enterprise workflows as a major frontier in AI adoption.

candidates.text:
Stage 2 Capital: $100 Million Fund Close Expands Early-Stage B2B AI Investing
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 5:02 PM
Stage 2 Capital: $100 Million Fund Close Expands Early-Stage B2B AI Investing
Stage 2 Capital has closed $100 million across Venture Fund IV and Catalyst IV, expanding its investment capacity for early-stage business-to-business AI companies while introducing an AI agent to help founders access its operator network.
Venture Fund IV will make investments of $2 million to $5 million in companies from seed through Series A. Catalyst IV will invest $200,000 in pre-seed businesses, often participating in their first institutional financing.
Both funds combine capital with support from experienced go-to-market executives. Stage 2 uses a pod model that pairs a venture investment partner with a partner whose background is in operating go-to-market functions.
The firm’s limited partner network includes more than 1,000 leaders with experience across sales, marketing, customer success, revenue operations, partnerships and forward-deployed engineering. Network members come from companies including Anthropic, OpenAI, Databricks, Lovable, SpaceX and ElevenLabs.
Stage 2’s new MCP agent is designed to connect portfolio founders with relevant expertise and relationships in that network. The firm says the agent will help identify operators who have recently addressed problems similar to those facing a portfolio company.
The system draws on the firm’s Science of Scaling framework, developed by Co-Founder and Managing Partner Mark Roberge. That framework helps companies assess when they are ready to scale and how quickly to grow.
The fund close follows four portfolio transactions: Salesforce’s acquisition of Momentum, Mainsail’s acquisition of Steelhead, Avalara’s acquisition of Versori and PSG’s majority investment in Order.co.
Stage 2 has already begun deploying the new funds, backing businesses including Letter.ai, Qualitate and Axle. The firm led Letter.ai’s $10.6 million Series A, which was followed four months later by a $40 million Series B led by Battery Ventures.
KEY QUOTES
“We started Stage 2 Capital because early-stage founders need more than capital. They need investors who can help them navigate their operational challenges. No firm solved this well for go-to-market.”
“That’s been true since day one, and these latest funds demonstrate the success of the model. We’ll always be in the room with our founders. Now, with AI, we can more easily surface the collective expertise, experience, and connections across our LP network, connecting founders with the right people and insights at the moment they need them”
Jay Po, Co-Founder And Managing Partner Of Stage 2 Capital
“We see founders make the same two mistakes over and over. Some scale too slowly and miss their window. Others scale before they’re ready and put the entire business at risk. We have well-established ways to measure revenue, but very little discipline around deciding when a company is actually ready to scale or how fast it should grow. Too often, boards rely on a playbook that worked for another company ten years ago, without considering whether it makes sense for the business in front of them. We want to help founders and investors make those decisions based on evidence rather than assumptions.”
Mark Roberge, Co-Founder And Managing Partner Of Stage 2 Capital
“Stage 2 was with us from our Series A on, as an extension of our team. They helped us pressure-test when we truly had product-market fit and how fast to scale from there. And every GTM problem we hit after that, they found the person who had already solved that exact problem at our stage. They introduced us to customers we couldn’t have reached on our own, and connected us with experienced operators who changed our trajectory.”
Ashley Wilson, Co-Founder Of Momentum

candidates.text:
Databento Raises $100 Million Series C at $1.1 Billion Valuation
News provided by
Databento Inc.
Nov 12, 2026, 08:57 ET
Share this article
Share this article
SALT LAKE CITY , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Databento, the market data platform for modern finance, today announced a $100 million Series C financing at a $1.1 billion valuation. The round was led by Fifth Down Capital, an early investor in Databento, with participation from nearly all of the company's existing investors, including NEA, DRW Venture Capital, Tribe Capital, and Hedosophia.
The announcement follows Databento's $97 million Series B earlier this year. Since closing its previous round, the company has more than doubled its revenue while remaining profitable.
Databento serves leading quantitative trading firms, brokerages, asset managers, commodities firms, and digital asset companies. The company has also established a strong presence in artificial intelligence, having signed enterprise contracts with five of the six leading frontier AI labs.
Databento had 39 employees when it closed its Series C, reaching a $1.1 billion valuation with a fraction of the headcount of traditional market data providers.
"In this AI era, we're seeing remarkably small teams build billion-dollar companies, but that level of efficiency is unprecedented in the market data industry," said Christina Qi, co-founder and CEO of Databento. "Until now, reaching this milestone required hundreds of employees given the sheer scale of physical infrastructure involved. I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished, and we'll continue to prioritize exceptional talent as we grow."
"Fifth Down first invested in Databento pre-revenue, as we recognized early on that the company had an opportunity to challenge the established model for delivering financial market data," said Andrew Spellman, founder and CEO of Fifth Down Capital. "Our confidence has only grown as Databento's traction and execution have demonstrated it can serve demanding institutional customers, sustain rapid growth, and build a profitable business. Databento's performance has reinforced our original thesis and strengthened our conviction in the company. We are thankful to Christina and Luca for the opportunity to increase our investment and involvement by leading the Series C financing."
The round also included a strategic investment from Fitch Ventures, bringing the perspective of a leading financial information provider with deep expertise in credit ratings, financial data, and market insights.
"Financial data is becoming increasingly API-driven and machine-consumed, creating an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how institutions and other market participants access it," said Gabby Munoz, Global Head of M&A and Venture Investments at Fitch Group. "Databento has built differentiated infrastructure at the source and paired it with a modern, self-service model that makes institutional-grade market data available on demand. We're excited to back the team as they scale a platform we believe will help shape how market data is captured, delivered, and consumed."
The new funding will support Databento's continued investment in its market data infrastructure and expansion into additional asset classes.
About Databento
Databento is the market data platform for modern finance. The company provides real-time and historical data across futures, options, equities, and indices through a unified API. By owning the entire stack from source to delivery, Databento is the first platform of its kind to combine the performance and reliability demanded by the world's leading trading firms with a dramatically simpler developer experience. To learn more about Databento, visit databento.com .
About Fifth Down Capital
Founded in 2014, Fifth Down Capital is a network-based investment firm that invests in private companies and funds. Fifth Down currently manages over 70 investment vehicles and has a full-time team of 30 professionals. For more information, visit fifthdown.com .

candidates.text:
Focus Financial Partners: Acquisition Of ML Management Partners Expands Entertainment Industry Business Management Services
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:53 AM
Focus Financial Partners: Acquisition Of ML Management Partners Expands Entertainment Industry Business Management Services
Focus Financial Partners, a financial services firm providing wealth management, family office, and business management services, has acquired ML Management Partners (MLM), a New York City-based business management firm specializing in serving entertainment industry professionals and high-net-worth individuals. The transaction closed on November 1, 2026, and strengthens Focus’s business management platform with additional expertise serving clients in television, film, and related creative industries.
Founded in 1988 by Mark Landesman, ML Management Partners provides business management and family office services to entertainment professionals, including actors, comedians, directors, producers, writers, industry executives, and other creative professionals.
The firm maintains offices in New York City and Los Angeles.
The acquisition expands Focus’s portfolio of specialized business management firms and provides MLM with access to additional resources and infrastructure.
Focus reported more than $550 billion in collectively advised assets as of June 30, 2026.
Expanding Focus’s Entertainment Industry Capabilities
The acquisition strengthens Focus Financial Partners’ presence in a specialized segment of the financial services industry.
Business management firms serving entertainment professionals often provide services tailored to clients with complex financial affairs and careers involving multiple income sources.
These clients may include performers, producers, directors, writers, and executives working across television, film, and other entertainment businesses.
ML Management Partners has developed its business around these relationships over nearly four decades.
The firm’s experience extends beyond traditional entertainment industry clients to include family office services for high-net-worth individuals.
Focus believes the acquisition supports its broader strategy of building a platform that combines specialized financial expertise with extensive operational resources.
The company has continued investing in businesses that complement its wealth management and family office services.
MLM adds an established client base and experienced leadership team to that platform.
ML Management Partners’ Nearly Four-Decade History
ML Management Partners was founded in 1988 by Mark Landesman.
The business initially focused primarily on serving comedians before expanding its services across the broader entertainment industry.
Today, MLM works with professionals both in front of and behind the camera, including talent, executives, producers, directors, and writers.
Its client base also includes individuals and businesses with specialized financial management requirements.
The firm operates from New York City with a second office in Los Angeles, providing a presence in two important centers of the U.S. entertainment industry.
Landesman has emphasized the importance of maintaining long-term relationships and personalized services for the firm’s clients.
He described the acquisition as an opportunity to preserve MLM’s established approach while accessing the broader resources of Focus.
The partnership is intended to allow MLM to continue serving its existing clients while developing additional capabilities.
Focus Builds Its Business Management Platform
Focus Financial Partners operates a financial services platform combining wealth management, business management, and family office capabilities.
Its strategy emphasizes providing specialized services through experienced professionals supported by broader institutional resources.
The acquisition of ML Management Partners reflects Focus’s continued investment in the business management industry.
Travis Danysh, Chief Strategy Officer at Focus, highlighted the quality and growth of the company’s existing business management portfolio.
He described the addition of MLM as an important step in the evolution of Focus’s business management strategy.
The transaction also reflects the company’s emphasis on investing in specialized talent and service offerings.
Focus expects to work with MLM’s team to expand the business and serve additional clients.
Access To Broader Resources And Infrastructure
Joining Focus provides ML Management Partners with access to resources associated with a larger financial services organization.
These capabilities are intended to support continued business development and service delivery.
For MLM, the transaction provides a way to pursue growth while maintaining its focus on clients with specialized financial needs.
The firm’s leadership sees opportunities to enhance its existing services through Focus’s broader platform.
For Focus, the acquisition adds a business with established relationships in the entertainment industry and experience serving high-net-worth clients.
The combination brings together MLM’s specialized knowledge with Focus’s financial services infrastructure.
Supporting Long-Term Business Management Growth
Focus Financial Partners serves individuals, families, and institutions through integrated financial services.

SA’s Yoco secures $100m credit facility to scale merchant cash advances
0
By
Tom Jackson
on
November 16, 2026
News , Southern Africa
South African fintech company Yoco has secured a US$100 million credit facility from US investment firm Victory Park Capital to expand its merchant cash advance operation.
Yoco builds tools and services to help small businesses accept card payments in-store and online, access loans, and manage their day to day activities. The startup has advanced more than ZAR6.5 billion (US$395 million) to over 40,000 merchants since 2018, working with specialist credit providers.
The company, which secured US$83 million in Series C funding back in 2021, has now secured a US$100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital, which will allow it to scale its cash advance operations, and gain greater control over the pricing and risk of its merchant loans.
The aim is to use the transaction data generated by merchants using Yoco’s card machines and online payment tools to assess businesses that traditional lenders may struggle to evaluate, helping the company turn its payments relationship with more than 200,000 businesses into a larger cash advance operation.
“We have spent a decade building an operating system that runs a merchant’s whole business, payments, point of sale, and now the decisions in between. Financing was the one layer we didn’t fully control. This facility changes that,” said Yoco CEO Carsten Holtkemeyer.
Victory Park Capital brings experience in private credit and asset-backed finance to the arrangement, having invested more than US$12 billion across 260 investments since 2007. Senior partner Jason Brown, said Yoco had demonstrated a track record of supporting small and independent businesses.
“We’re supportive of Yoco’s mission to expand access to flexible financing solutions for South African entrepreneurs,” he said.

candidates.text:
Seawolf Therapeutics: $100 Million Funding And Up To $1.2 Billion Sanofi Partnership To Advance DNA Medicines
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:32 AM
Seawolf Therapeutics: $100 Million Funding And Up To $1.2 Billion Sanofi Partnership To Advance DNA Medicines
Seawolf Therapeutics, a San Diego-based biotechnology company developing DNA-based medicines, has emerged from stealth with $100 million in funding and announced a multi-target research collaboration with Sanofi worth up to $1.2 billion in potential milestone payments, plus royalties. The company is developing a lipid nanoparticle-based DNA delivery platform designed to enable sustained production of therapeutic proteins inside patients’ cells.
Seawolf’s financing includes seed and Series A investments backed by Versant Ventures, MPM BioImpact, Novartis Venture Fund, Eli Lilly, CRISPR Therapeutics, Sixty Degree Capital, Alexandria Venture Investments, and Pathway to Cures, the philanthropic venture arm of the National Bleeding Disorders Foundation.
Versant Ventures led the seed financing, while the Series A included Versant, MPM BioImpact, and Novartis Venture Fund.
The capital will support advancement of Seawolf’s proprietary therapeutic pipeline, including a lead program targeting metabolic diseases.
Developing The TRIDENT DNA Delivery Platform
Seawolf’s technology platform, called TRIDENT, stands for Targeted RNA-Induced DNA Expression via Nuclear Translocation.
The system uses lipid nanoparticles to transport DNA into cells and facilitate access to the nucleus, where genetic information can support production of therapeutic proteins.
Lipid nanoparticles are also used in certain RNA-based medicines, but RNA therapies can face limitations involving how long protein expression lasts.
Seawolf is developing a different approach intended to provide more durable protein production by delivering DNA-based payloads.
TRIDENT combines a proprietary lipid nanoparticle, DNA encoding a therapeutic protein, and an auxiliary factor that helps facilitate nuclear entry.
The company says its technology has demonstrated sustained protein expression above therapeutic levels in nonhuman primate studies at doses reported to be safe and well tolerated.
The company has also generated preclinical proof-of-concept results in animal models involving metabolic and rare diseases.
These findings remain preclinical and will require further evaluation before therapeutic benefits and safety can be established in humans.
A Redosable Approach To DNA Medicines
Seawolf is designing its technology to allow repeat administration when necessary.
The company describes TRIDENT as a nonviral DNA delivery approach that avoids some of the limitations associated with virus-based genetic medicine platforms.
Its goal is to provide durable protein expression while preserving the ability to adjust or supplement dosing.
The technology could support several therapeutic approaches, including replacement of defective genes and systemic production of biologic medicines.
Seawolf believes this flexibility may allow the platform to address multiple disease categories.
Sanofi Collaboration Includes Up To $1.2 Billion In Milestones
Alongside its funding announcement, Seawolf disclosed a multi-target research collaboration and exclusive license agreement with Sanofi.
The partnership will focus on developing undisclosed therapies for bleeding disorders and additional indications.
The agreement includes up to $1.2 billion in research, development, and commercialization milestone payments, along with tiered royalties on sales of any resulting products.
The milestone total represents potential future consideration contingent on the progress of the collaboration, rather than funding already received.
The agreement provides Seawolf with a major pharmaceutical partner as it advances its delivery technology.
Supporting The Next Stage Of Development
Seawolf President and CEO Elizabeth Alcamo said the funding and Sanofi partnership position the company to advance its lead program in metabolic diseases while developing therapies addressing additional unmet medical needs.
Versant Managing Director Tom Woiwode, who chairs Seawolf’s board, highlighted the potential of DNA delivery to support long-lasting production of therapeutic proteins.
With $100 million in funding and a pharmaceutical collaboration carrying substantial potential milestones, Seawolf is preparing to move its DNA delivery platform toward further therapeutic development.
KEY QUOTES
“Seawolf is charting a new course in patient care through LNP-based DNA medicines. With a strong syndicate of investors and our collaboration with Sanofi, we are well-positioned to execute on our next stage of growth, which will include advancing our lead program for metabolic diseases and collaborating with Sanofi in its mission to develop therapies for patient unmet needs.”
Dr. Elizabeth Alcamo, President And CEO Of Seawolf Therapeutics
“Nucleic acid-based therapies have advanced dramatically over the past decade. The Seawolf team is now delivering on the promise of using DNA to drive robust and long-term expression of therapeutic proteins directly from the patient’s own cells. I look forward to seeing this groundbreaking technology transform treatment options for patients.”
Dr. Tom Woiwode, Managing Director At Versant Ventures And Chairman Of Seawolf Therapeutics

PHOENIX , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Trinity Capital Inc. (NYSE: TRIN ), a leading alternative asset manager, today announced the commitment of $100 million in debt financing to Phononic, a North Carolina-based company developing solid-state cooling solutions for AI data centers. The financing will support accelerated growth and manufacturing capacity expansion to meet increasing customer demand.
Phononic's proprietary Thermal Control Systems™ provide software-defined cooling for AI infrastructure by combining high-performance thermoelectric devices with intelligent controls. Compact, solid-state devices and an integrated software control layer deliver precision cooling at the point of need for critical components, including GPUs, high-bandwidth memory, networking silicon, and the optical transceivers that connect them. Phononic's Thermal Fabric™ software layer monitors conditions throughout the data center and dynamically adjusts thermal control in real time as AI workloads change. Together, these solutions are designed to unlock greater AI infrastructure performance, optimize compute and facility capacity, and reduce energy and water consumption.
"As AI hardware continues to evolve, we believe precise, real-time cooling at the chip level is becoming increasingly important," said Phil Gager, Senior Managing Director of Tech Lending at Trinity Capital. "Phononic has built the thermoelectric technology and software to address that need, and we're pleased to back their team as demand for their solutions continues to build."
Phononic enters its next phase of growth as a profitable company backed by leading venture and growth-equity investors. With demand accelerating across AI infrastructure, the company is expanding manufacturing capacity to meet growing customer requirements and scale delivery of its intelligent thermal control solutions.
"AI infrastructure is advancing at an unprecedented pace, and cooling has become a critical bottleneck to growth, limiting both facility capacity and compute and optical performance. Our customers are demanding disruptive thermal control solutions that can overcome these limitations at scale," said Dr. Tony Atti, CEO and Founder of Phononic. "Our partnership with Trinity Capital enables us to accelerate manufacturing capacity expansion to meet that demand and support the next wave of growth across AI infrastructure."
About Trinity Capital Inc.
Trinity Capital Inc. (NYSE: TRIN ) is an alternative asset manager that seeks to deliver consistent returns for investors through access to private credit markets. Trinity Capital sources and structures investments in well-capitalized growth-oriented companies across five distinct lending verticals: Tech Lending, Equipment Finance, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Sponsor Finance, and Asset Based Lending. As a long-term, trusted partner for innovative companies seeking tailored debt solutions, Trinity Capital has deployed more than $6.8 billion across over 511 investments since inception in 2008 (as of September 30, 2026). Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, Trinity Capital's dedicated team is strategically located across the United States and Europe. For more information on Trinity Capital, please visit trinitycapital.com and stay connected to the latest activity via LinkedIn .
About Phononic
Phononic is a leader in software-defined thermal control for AI infrastructure, combining breakthrough solid-state cooling technology with intelligent hardware and software to unlock greater performance, efficiency, and reliability. Deployed across major U.S. hyperscalers, Phononic's solutions deliver precision thermal control at the source for optical connectivity, GPUs, high-bandwidth memory, and other critical AI components. Through its Thermal Control Systems™ and Thermal Fabric™ intelligence layer, Phononic enables real-time, workload-responsive thermal optimization that helps mitigate throttling, improve energy efficiency, and maximize AI infrastructure performance. For more information, visit www.phononic.com .

candidates.title: Adaspace Hong Kong IPO Raises $95.6 Million for AI Satellites
candidates.snippet: Adaspace Hong Kong IPO Raises $95.6 Million for AI Satellites iNews Zoombangla
candidates.text:
Adaspace Technology raised HK$750 million ($95.6 million) in a Hong Kong initial public offering, and its shares moved higher by the midday break after opening below the offer price. The debut puts a listed supplier of AI-powered satellites and satellite-data services on the market as the company seeks funding for research, production and facilities.
Reuters reported that the shares opened at HK$24.44, 1.8% below the HK$24.90 offer price, and were last at HK$24.60 in its morning report. Bamboo Works later reported a rise to HK$25.26 by the midday break, 1.45% above the offer price. Those are snapshots from different points in Friday’s session; neither is a closing price.
The Chengdu-based company sold 30.12 million shares at HK$24.90 each, the bottom of its marketed range of HK$24.90 to HK$33.20, Reuters reported. The wire also said the retail tranche was subscribed 3.43 times and the international offering was covered 1.79 times. Those figures describe separate parts of the offering and should not be combined as one subscription measure.
Reuters describes Adaspace as a maker of AI-powered satellites that also provides satellite-data services. The Hong Kong exchange’s November 12 global-offering announcement identifies Adaspace Technology and refers investors to the company’s November 5 prospectus. The filing is the primary record for the offering; Reuters and Bamboo Works provide independent reports on the first trading session.
Bamboo Works reported net proceeds of HK$652 million ($83.6 million). It said the company plans to use 35.6% of that amount to strengthen research and development, 24.4% to build a center in Shenzhen, 20% for strategic investments and acquisitions, and 10% to repay bank loans. These are the allocations listed in the report; they do not account for every part of the proceeds.
The same report gave a snapshot of the company’s recent finances. Adaspace recorded first-half 2026 revenue of 226 million yuan ($33.9 million), down 6.3% from a year earlier. Its net loss narrowed 21.5% to 150 million yuan. The revenue decline and narrower loss are separate measures, so the loss reduction does not mean revenue grew.
For the Adaspace Hong Kong IPO, the distinction between the amount raised and the net proceeds matters: Reuters reported the HK$750 million raise, while Bamboo Works cited HK$652 million in net proceeds. The reports also show a share price that first fell below the offer price and later moved above it by midday, without establishing the final close.
The debut marks the start of public trading for the company’s shares, while the planned research, production and Shenzhen spending remain future uses of the funds. The available reports do not establish how quickly those investments will translate into additional satellites, data services or revenue. They document the offering terms, early trading and the company’s stated financial results, leaving later operating performance to subsequent disclosures.

By Amit Chowdhry

LibertyStream Advances Up To $95 Million Financing And Signs New Lithium Sales Agreement
LibertyStream Infrastructure Partners has extended its financing exclusivity period with Endurance Finance Partners through January 15, 2027 as the companies continue working toward a proposed financing package of up to $95 million.
Endurance is acting as arranger for the financing framework, which is intended to support LibertyStream’s Freedom 1, Freedom 2 and potentially additional lithium production sites.
The original non-binding financing term sheet was announced on September 3, 2026.
All other terms remain unchanged.
LibertyStream said the additional exclusivity period will allow definitive financing documentation to be coordinated with its broader capital plan.
The proposed financing remains subject to due diligence, investment and credit approvals, definitive agreements, required corporate and regulatory approvals and other customary conditions.
Future project sites would require separate approvals.
The company also disclosed a new commercial agreement supporting its planned lithium production.
On November 4, 2026, LibertyStream entered into a sales contract with a major international cathode manufacturer supplying the U.S. market.
The agreement covers 500 tonnes of lithium carbonate in 2027 and up to an additional 17,000 tonnes between 2028 and 2031.
The 2028 through 2031 volumes remain subject to execution of a long-term supply agreement.
LibertyStream previously entered into a separate offtake agreement in July 2026 with a U.S. industrial customer for 600 tonnes of lithium carbonate annually over five years.
The company is developing technology designed to produce lithium carbonate from oilfield brine.
Its strategy involves deploying proprietary direct lithium extraction technology into existing oil and gas infrastructure, an approach intended to lower capital costs and reduce project development risk.
LibertyStream is working to develop Freedom 1 and Freedom 2 as it seeks to become an early commercial-scale North American producer of lithium carbonate from oilfield brines.
The proposed Endurance financing could provide capital to advance those projects, although LibertyStream said there is no assurance that definitive financing agreements or its proposed Nasdaq listing will be completed.

Remedy Robotics, a San Francisco medtech treating stroke patients remotely, and cofounded by Perth-born doctor David Bell, has raised US$62 million (A$92m) in a Series B, backed by a range of Australian venture funds.
US venture firm DCVC led the round, with existing backers Blackbird, Tony Fadell’s Build Collective, Divergent Capital and KdT Ventures chipping in alongside the the University of California’s investment office, Skip Capital and super fund Hostplus as new investors.
Remedy previously raised US$35 million across its Seed and Series A rounds.
The fresh capital is for a clinical trial across the University of California’s network by a surgical robot designed to let specialists treat stroke patients hundreds of kilometres away. The medtech is seeking US Food and Drug Administration approval for procedures on the blood vessels supplying the brain. It also plans to place prototype robots with clinical partners, including the Australian Stroke Alliance.
Bell spent eight years in medicine, including cardiac surgery and air retrieval, before studying at Stanford, where he met his cofounder and CTO Jake Sganga. In 2021, the pair lined a garage in Venice Beach with lead, bought a second-hand X-ray machine and had a colleague in Berkeley operate their prototype remotely.
“This funding will allow our world-leading hardware, software, and machine learning teams to progress the N1 system towards clinical trials and potential FDA approval, while also developing additional features including full autonomy,” Sganga said.

Israeli-American cybersecurity startup Daylight has raised $80 million in a Series B funding round that brings the total raised by the company to $120 million.
The investment round was led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives’ Growth Equity, with additional support from Okta Ventures, Bain Capital, Craft Ventures, Vintage Partners, and Maple Capital.
Founded in 2024, with headquarters in New York and Tel Aviv, Daylight has built Aura, an AI-native platform that hunts for, analyzes, and contains cyber threats in real time.
Combining AI automation with human expertise, the platform continuously builds, runs, and customizes agents that handle day-to-day operations based on customers’ workflows, risks, and priorities.
Daylight provides these capabilities as part of a flexible service model. Customers can select the service to be fully managed, co-managed, or supported by forward-deployed engineers.
As AI agents handle routine operations, customers can use Aura to investigate their security environments, access security data, and manage security operations.

“As these agents become more capable, they’ll fundamentally change how threats are detected, investigated, and contained, with expert security engineers implementing, governing, and continuously improving their operations,” Daylight co-founder and CEO Hagai Shapira said.
“At Daylight, we’re already bringing this vision to life through an agent-native model that combines the speed and scale of AI with the judgment and oversight of human experts. We’re building the foundation for a new era of security operations,” Shapira added.
The company plans to use the fresh funding to accelerate its platform’s development, expand its security and technology teams, grow its presence in the US, and enter new markets in the EMEA and APAC regions.

candidates.snippet: As AI Threats Surge, Daylight Raises $80M Led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives The Globe and Mail
candidates.text:
NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 10, 2026 / Daylight, which combines AI agents with human security experts to detect, investigate, and respond to cyber threats, today announced an $80 million Series B led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, with existing investors Bain Capital, Craft Ventures, Vintage Partners, and Maple Capital. The round brings Daylight's total funding to $120 million. Daylight's revenue has surged more than 40x over the past year, fueled by rapidly growing demand from Fortune 500 enterprises and leading AI-native companies. Its customer base includes Lovable, LastPass, Rogo, dLocal, and Miro.
October's wave of cyber incidents, dubbed "Black October," stretched incident response teams already under pressure from increasingly complex security threats. As organizations turn to AI to help manage these mounting demands, the technology isn't necessarily easing the burden. A July 2026 ISC2 survey found that 65% of cybersecurity professionals using AI now spend more time determining whether to trust its recommendations than they did a year ago, while 63% spend more time verifying its outputs.
The challenge goes beyond AI adoption. Companies also struggle to find security services that fit their specific needs. Traditional managed security providers offer rigid, one-size-fits-all services, while standalone AI tools often leave companies managing yet another system. Some organizations want to outsource security operations entirely, while others have internal teams and want to retain control over their detections and processes. As a result, enterprises are left piecing together multiple vendors for detection and response, threat hunting, phishing, data protection, and security data management.
Daylight brings these capabilities together through a flexible service model that combines AI automation with some of the world's top security engineering talent, expertise that most companies struggle to recruit and retain. Its AI-native platform and security engineers continuously build, run, and customize AI agents to each customer's systems, workflows, risks, and priorities. The agents handle day-to-day security operations, while engineers focus on decisions requiring human judgment. Customers can choose how the service is delivered, whether fully managed, co-managed alongside their internal teams, or supported by forward-deployed engineers.
Daylight detects threats in seconds and responds to and contains them within minutes, up to 10 times faster than traditional managed security providers. Customers can run leaner security teams without sacrificing the expertise needed to protect their businesses, as AI agents take on routine operations and experienced security engineers handle complex decisions. Through Aura, Daylight's AI-native platform, customers can also investigate their security environment using natural language, access their security data in a centralized data lake, and manage their security operations from one place.
Daylight's coverage also extends to the AI platforms enterprises use themselves, protecting against AI-native risks like prompt injection, risky MCPs, and unusual AI-driven activity. Those detections run through Daylight's full MDR workflow, where AI activity is investigated alongside identity, endpoint, cloud, SaaS, and business context. The capability is already in use by enterprise customers, including Miro.
"The future of security operations won't be defined by how many people a company can deploy, but by how effectively AI agents can take on increasingly complex security work," said Hagai Shapira, co-founder and CEO of Daylight . "As these agents become more capable, they'll fundamentally change how threats are detected, investigated, and contained, with expert security engineers implementing, governing, and continuously improving their operations. At Daylight, we're already bringing this vision to life through an agent-native model that combines the speed and scale of AI with the judgment and oversight of human experts. We're building the foundation for a new era of security operations."
"Cybersecurity remains a top priority for enterprises of all sizes, and we see a significant opportunity for agentic technologies to transform how security outcomes are delivered," said Irit Kahan, Managing Director and Global Head of Cyber Security Investing within Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives. "By scaling human expertise with agentic technology, Daylight has the potential to enable organizations to respond at machine speed, with greater accuracy and at scale."
George Foster, Investor within Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives added, "Daylight continues to drive innovation in this space, scaling high-level security expertise through the use of agentic technology. We believe this combination positions the company to have the potential to become a leader in the next-generation of cybersecurity."
Daylight was founded by Hagai Shapira and Eldad Rudich, who first met while serving in an elite Israeli military intelligence unit. Shapira was an early product leader at cybersecurity unicorn Torq, where he worked closely with enterprise security teams, while Rudich was Torq's first employee and VP of R&D, building its core platform and engineering organization from the ground up. candidates.text:
Project Omega Raises $80 Million To Develop Nuclear Fuel Recycling Infrastructure
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 11:10 PM
Project Omega Raises $80 Million To Develop Nuclear Fuel Recycling Infrastructure
Project Omega has raised $80 million in Series A financing to develop nuclear fuel recycling infrastructure and long-duration power products. B Capital led the round, with participation from noa VC, 645 Ventures, and other investors focused on nuclear technology and national security. Existing investors Starship Ventures, Mantis Ventures, Decisive Point, Virta Ventures, Pace Ventures, Essential Capital, and Washington Harbour Partners also participated.
B Capital General Partner Jeff Johnson will join Project Omega’s board of directors.
The company is developing a non-aqueous pyroprocessing platform intended to recover useful materials from spent nuclear fuel. Its technology targets isotopes that can be used in long-duration power systems, reactor feedstock, and commercial, scientific, and medical applications.
Project Omega said the process does not separate pure plutonium and could reduce nuclear-waste volume by up to 90%.
Its initial products include radiovoltaic systems that convert the natural decay of radioisotopes directly into electricity. Potential applications include sensors, autonomous systems, communications infrastructure, spacecraft, undersea platforms, and equipment deployed in areas where battery replacement is difficult.
Project Omega has worked with Idaho National Laboratory through the ARPA-E CURIE program and demonstrated stable electrical current from strontium-90 at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory. It has also developed radioisotope power systems through DARPA’s Rads to Watts program.
The financing will support a pilot facility for isotope recovery and feedstock production, construction of a nuclear fuel recycling facility, and further development and manufacturing of the company’s X Series expeditionary power systems.
Project Omega has offices in Newport, Rhode Island, and Hailey, Idaho, along with a laboratory in Fall River, Massachusetts.
KEY QUOTES:
America’s growing demand for reliable power is colliding with a nuclear fuel cycle that remains dependent on foreign supply and leaves enormous value stranded in used fuel. Project Omega’s technology has the potential to create multiple revenue streams from a largely untapped domestic resource, spanning long-duration power, reactor feedstock and strategic isotopes. We’re excited to support Staff Sheehan and his highly experienced team as they scale this platform and unlock economic potential across the nuclear value chain.
Jeff Johnson, General Partner and Global Head of Energy at B Capital
The country’s nuclear renaissance will not happen without the fuel. We have a domestic source for this, nearly 100,000 metric tons of used nuclear fuel, which is one of America’s largest untapped energy resources. We are building a vertically integrated strategy around an abundant domestic feedstock, with a non-aqueous recycling process that recovers useful isotopes, and products with clear strategic demand. That combination creates the potential for an entirely new nuclear innovation economy.
Stafford Sheehan, Founder and CEO of Project Omega
Project Omega has progressed well beyond a compelling scientific idea. The company is building the fuel-cycle infrastructure needed to support America’s growing nuclear industrial base and help power the country’s next era of innovation.
Howard Morgan, Co-Founder, Chair and General Partner at B Capital

Alta: $80 Million In Total Funding Advances Institutional Blockchain Infrastructure
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 6:38 PM
Alta: $80 Million In Total Funding Advances Institutional Blockchain Infrastructure
Alta has raised $80 million in total funding, including a $47.5 million Series A led by Index Ventures, to develop blockchain infrastructure designed for regulated financial institutions. GV, Blackbird Ventures, Square Peg and Capital 49 participated in the Series A. The total also includes $32.5 million in previous seed financing.
Alta is building infrastructure that allows financial assets and products to move globally and programmatically, with privacy, compliance, identity and authorization controls incorporated into the blockchain itself.
Its architecture uses recursive zero-knowledge cryptography to verify that transactions meet required rules while keeping balances, transaction details, identities and compliance policies private. The company intends the system to support activity across assets, blockchain networks and jurisdictions.
Airwallex has selected Alta as a technology partner, connecting its global payments infrastructure with Alta’s blockchain. The collaboration will support stablecoin pay-ins and payouts, alongside connectivity to local fiat payment networks across 200 countries and 90 currencies.
Alta positions its infrastructure as a neutral foundation that banks, payment providers and other financial institutions can use to develop services.
Its first product will focus on corporate liquidity management. Built around tokenized assets, the offering is intended to enable just-in-time funding, improve foreign exchange efficiency and reduce the cash businesses keep in prefunded accounts.
The product will also allow businesses to move into and out of yield-bearing tokenized assets, helping them earn interest on capital that would otherwise remain idle. Alta cited an estimated $4 trillion held in prefunded accounts globally as evidence of the opportunity to improve capital efficiency.
The company’s founders include CEO Loong Wang, President Catherine Porter and Airwallex Co-Founder and CEO Jack Zhang. They identified institutional controls and connectivity as requirements for expanding blockchain-based finance, including transactions initiated by AI agents.
Alta will use the funding to continue developing its blockchain, expand institutional partnerships and global financial connectivity, and grow its engineering and compliance teams.

candidates.snippet: Enza Capital is raising up to $80 Million to bet on African AI Startups Innovation Village
candidates.text:
Enza Capital is raising up to $80 Million to bet on African AI Startups
0
By
Smart Megwai
on
November 11, 2026
Africa , Business , Funding , Investments , Startups
Enza Capital has secured a first close of $21 million for its third fund, Enza Capital III LP, which it will dedicate entirely to artificial-intelligence startups across Africa.
The pan-African venture firm, which has offices in Nairobi, Johannesburg and Cairo, is targeting $60 million for the fund with a hard cap of $80 million, and expects a final close in about a year, the firm said in an emailed statement .
The fund’s entire thesis rests on a gap. African AI, by the report’s account, attracts relatively little venture capital despite growing interest in its potential. Investors deployed about $46.8 million into African AI startups through 2026, the report says, concentrated mostly in fintech and risk-intelligence companies and modest next to AI investment in other regions.
A Briter Bridges report cited in the report found that 30% of surveyed African AI companies are entirely bootstrapped, with funding clustered among more established players; some founders say investors’ preference for proven traction makes it harder for early-stage AI companies to raise money at all.
Enza Capital is betting that the gap in African AI funding is a market failure to be exploited, not a verdict on the sector’s potential.
Enza Capital’s existing investments span SeamlessHR, Money254, Sendy, Gigmile and Peach Payments, giving a sense of the firm’s range before this fund narrows its focus specifically to AI.
That earlier spread, across HR tech, personal finance, logistics and payments, suggests Enza Capital III LP will be looking for AI applied across similarly varied sectors rather than betting narrowly on one vertical.
What to watch
The first thing to consider is the pace over the next 12 months. To move from a target of $21 million to a goal of $60 million, and even aiming for a hard cap of $80 million, it will be essential to convince limited partners that the funding gap in African AI is investable rather than simply an indicator that the market has already assessed the associated risks.
The second point to consider is whether the fund’s eventual portfolio will focus primarily on fintech and risk-intelligence companies, which have already attracted most of the continent’s AI capital, or if it will genuinely explore newer categories that the report indicates are currently underfunded and lacking institutional investment.

Energy Transition / Private Equity & Venture Capital
Course Corrected Raises €80 Million to Back European Energy and Resource Transition Startups
Kenny Fisher
November 12, 2026
Venture capital investor Course Corrected announced today that it has raised €80 million (USD$89 million) at the final close of its second fund, focused on investing in early-stage European technology companies across the energy and resource transition.
Founded in 2021 by Christine Ahlstrand, Kerstin Cooley and Katja Bergman, Stockholm-based Course Corrected invests in early-stage technology companies developing solutions to enable industries to become more energy, resource and cost efficient. Fund II builds on the firm’s first fund, which focused entirely on climate tech.
According to the firm, Fund II will invest in 20 – 30 companies across key themes including energy systems, industrial optimization and automation, electrification and resource-smart solutions, focusing on scalable businesses whose products advance the energy and resource transition.
Kerstin Cooley, founding partner at Course Corrected, said:
“We invest to generate strong financial returns. Impact is how we get there: by backing juggernauts that solve real problems, scale commercially, and transform industries for the better.”
Fund II invests only in European companies. Course Corrected noted that the fund’s close amidst a need for Europe to channel more of its savings into European businesses, noting that only a small fraction of pension and insurance assets are allocated to venture capital, and that more than half of EU venture funds’ investments are directed to startups outside of the EU.
Christine Ahlstrand, founding partner at Course Corrected, said:
“Europe has the research, the technology, the founders and the markets. But who will own the next generation of industry if we do not finance the companies building it?”
To date, Fund II has made seven investments, including Tavion, Renasens, eComID and Skye.
Investors in the fund include the European Investment Fund (EIF), which committed €35 million, Swedish state-owned venture capital investor Saminvest, pension investors SEB Life & Pension and SEB-Stiftelsen, a Swedish foundation and private investors.
Pontus Bergekrans, CIO at SEB Life & Pension AB, said:
“We believe Europe has the talent and innovation needed to lead the energy transition. Course Corrected combines a strong team, a focused strategy and access to companies addressing some of the region’s most important challenges.”

Indian FinTechs raised USD 76 million across six equity funding rounds in October 2026, according to data collated by Tracxn.
The month witnessed funding activity across healthcare and insurance technology, investment and trading platforms, blockchain-based financial infrastructure, lending and debt resolution, and cross-border payments .
The largest deal of the month came from Even, a healthcare platform offering managed care services, doctor consultations and health insurance solutions, which raised USD 50 million in a Series B round from Khosla Ventures and Alpha Wave Global.
This was followed by StockGro, a stock market advisory and research platform, which raised USD 10 million in a Series B round from Aart Corporate Advisors.
Advt
Another notable transaction was Fission Labs , a financial technology company building blockchain-based infrastructure for tokenised investment funds, which raised USD 10 million in a Series A round. The round saw participation from Pantera Capital, Circle, Borderless Capital, New Form Capital, gCC, Manhattan Venture Partners, Reflexive Capital and Lattice, along with angel investors Ari Rubenstein and Anthony Scaramucci.
Together, the three largest transactions accounted for USD 70 million, or nearly 92 per cent of the total funding raised during October.
Among the other deals during the month:
Tradl, an artificial intelligence-powered trading platform, raised USD 4 million in a seed funding round from Stellaris Venture Partners.
CredFix, a financial technology platform connecting lenders and borrowers, particularly those facing financial distress, raised USD 2 million in a seed round from Stargazer Growth and Tanglin Venture Partners.
Saber, a provider of stablecoin-powered cross-border payment infrastructure, also raised an undisclosed amount in a seed funding round from Tether and Titan.
Funding activity in October was lower than the previous month, with total funding declining to USD 76 million across six deals, compared with USD 111 million across 10 deals in September 2026.

candidates.snippet: China Physical AI Roundup: UniX AI Raises $75M Pre-A, Plus TensorWorld, UBTech Order and Huawei CloudRobo AI Insider
candidates.text:
Physical AI · Humanoids
China Physical AI Roundup: UniX AI Raises $75M Pre-A, Plus TensorWorld, UBTech Order and Huawei CloudRobo
By Greg Bock · 17 November 2026 · 5 min read
Insider Brief
Chinese robotics companies attracted new funding and commercial orders across humanoids, robot components and physical AI, led by UniX AI’s 500 million yuan (about $75 million) Pre-A round.
TensorWorld raised more than $100 million across two early funding rounds, while robot-chip developer XiXuan Chuangzhi secured 500 million yuan (about $75 million) at a 4 billion yuan post-money valuation.
UBTech secured an order for 400 humanoid robots, Huawei Cloud released an open-source robot world model, and TARS and Robotera reported industrial and logistics deployments.
China ‘s robotics companies continue drawing fresh investment in humanoids , robot chips and training models, led by UniX AI’s 500 million yuan (about $75 million) Pre-A round. Other developments include a 400-unit UBTech humanoid order, Hesai’s third-quarter results and Huawei Cloud’s release of an open-source robot world model .
UniX AI
UniX AI , which makes wheeled humanoid robots for security, hotels and retail, has raised 500 million yuan (about $75 million) in a Pre-A round, Science and Technology Daily reported , citing the Suzhou company. Existing investors Xienuo and Yonghua added to their stakes. New backers include Greenland Group, a customer that joined as a strategic investor, along with Keli Sensing, HUST Ventures and others. UniX said it ships more than 100 robots a month, with peak monthly output above 300, and has batch orders from property groups, Certis and Inspur. Proceeds will fund algorithm research, product updates and wider use in property management, hotels and retail.
TensorWorld
TensorWorld, which was founded in July and is building physics-based foundation models that predict how objects move and interact, has raised more than $100 million across an angel round and an angel-plus round, according to a Starlink Capital post published by 36Kr . Cathay Capital and HongShan co-led the angel round, with IDG Capital, CDH VGC, Starlink Capital and Ant Group participating. Ant Group, Heyu Capital and Meituan Strategic co-led the later round.
XiXuan Chuangzhi
XiXuan Chuangzhi, a robot-chip company set up in May by UBTech, MetaX and Fenglong, closed a 500 million yuan (about $75 million) angel round at a 4 billion yuan (about $600 million) post-money valuation, China Securities Journal reported , citing a UBTech WeChat post. GGV Capital and Matrix Partners China co-led the round. Funds will go to chip and platform research, a software toolchain, hiring and joint testing with robot makers. XiXuan plans a development platform in 2027 and its first system-on-chip in 2028. MetaX is a listed chip designer.
UBTech
UBTech signed an agreement for Yongda Auto to buy 400 of its U1 Pro ultra-bionic humanoids, with delivery planned this year, NBD reported . NBD said it was UBTech’s first disclosed large order for that line. The robots will be used for product demonstrations, sales and customer service, and the partners plan a Shanghai showroom. The contract value was undisclosed. UBTech also signed a pact with Tianyi Telecom Terminal, a China Telecom unit, setting a three-year goal of more than 1 million home-companion robots and 100,000 ultra-bionic or wheeled humanoid terminals, IT Home reported . Those figures are market targets, not a firm purchase order.
Hesai
Hesai reported third-quarter revenue of 1.07 billion yuan ($159.3 million), up 34.3% from a year earlier, and net income of 80.8 million yuan ($12.1 million), its sixth straight profitable quarter on a GAAP basis, according to the company . It shipped 23,405 robotic actuation modules, up 97% from the second quarter, and 91,618 robotics lidar units, up 51.1%. Hesai (HSAI) also said cumulative actuation shipments reached 35,295.
Huawei Cloud
Huawei Cloud released CloudRobo-WM1.2, an open-source robot world model trained on its Ascend chips, at an online event . The company said the model uses a DualAct design that generates robot actions directly from the world model and ranked first on the RoboTwin 2.0 and LiberoPro 2.0 benchmarks, Sina Tech reported . Huawei said it is also releasing the training framework and recommended methods for running the software on Ascend systems.
Huawei Cloud indicated 80% of Chinese embodied-AI companies use Ascend Cloud, and that its CloudRobo platform has more than 16,500 developers and 230 companies and universities, CLS reported . CLS said partners include JAKA, Spirit AI, Galaxea, Youibot and Realman. Huawei Cloud also said a street-sweeping robot developed with Fulongma is on pre-sale ahead of a Shanghai launch in December. The price and specifications were undisclosed.
TARS
TARS said Aptiv expects to finish deploying 100 A-Series industrial robots by year-end, with the first units already running on an Aptiv factory line, according to a company release . The partners have a longer goal of 1,000 units. TARS also signed an agreement with Changzhou wire-harness maker Aibog to put hundreds of industrial robots on Aibog’s lines in batches for harness assembly, Yangtse Evening News reported . Timetables and financial terms for the Aibog work were undisclosed.
Robotera
Robotera ’s humanoids are sorting parcels for China Post at 11 sites in eight Guangdong cities, with an average feeding rate of more than 1,500 items an hour, Chaoqi reported . The report did not give a unit count for those sites. It also said Robotera has deployed 45 robots at China Post’s Hangzhou mail center.
Other Funding
Bluepoint Touch , which makes force and torque sensors for robots, closed a Series D3 of several hundred million yuan, according to PEdaily . The exact amount was undisclosed. Fourteen investors joined the round, including Hongtai Fund and Hony Capital. AgiBot and Galbot are both customers and shareholders. PEdaily said the company has raised more than 1 billion y

November 11, 2026
Staff
Solar , Storage
Renewable energy project developer Green Genius has completed a €65 million (~$72.5 million) green bond issue to refinance existing subordinated construction loans. The bonds have a four-year maturity and carry a floating interest rate based on the three-month Euro Interbank Offered Rate (EURIBOR) plus 8% annually. They are expected to be admitted to trading on the Sustainable Bond List of Nasdaq Stockholm.
FluoRok, a U.K.-based company developing materials for applications including lithium-ion battery electrolytes , has raised $30 million in an oversubscribed Series A funding round to scale its manufacturing platform and expand fluorochemical production. Orano Venture Fund and Supernova Invest led the funding round, with participation from Bidra Innovation Ventures.
RadianX, a perovskite solar module manufacturer formerly known as California Perovskite Technology, has raised $9 million in combined venture and project financing to scale production of its certified perovskite solar modules. SOSV and Twynam co-led the seed funding round, with participation from One Small Planet, Sahsen Ventures, Avila VC, California Innovation Fund, quantumEDGE, Riceberg Ventures, and Alumni Ventures.
ARRAY Technologies, a provider of solar tracking technology, fixed-tilt products, and foundation solutions, and Shoals Technologies Group , a provider of electrical balance-of-system solutions for utility-scale solar and battery storage, have entered into a definitive agreement for a stock-for-stock merger. Under the merger agreement, ARRAY will be the legal acquirer and corporate parent of the combined company, and Shoals shareholders will receive 1.6931 ARRAY shares for each Shoals share they own.
SOLV Energy, a company that provides construction, operation, and maintenance services for large-scale solar and battery storage projects, has acquired Texas-based ASB Energy Services, a contractor specializing in substation foundations, civil construction, and battery energy storage infrastructure, for approximately $45 million. The transaction comprises $36 million in cash and $9 million in shares of SOLV Energy’s Class A common stock, excluding customary closing adjustments.

candidates.title: UTEP raises record $70 million; city of El Paso adopts new plan to improve parks
candidates.snippet: UTEP raises record $70 million; city of El Paso adopts new plan to improve parks El Paso Matters
candidates.text:
Sign up for essential news about El Paso. Delivered to your inbox — completely free.
This is your weekly news roundup, which takes a quick look at some developments in government, politics, education, environment and other topics across El Paso.
Record Number of Donors Gave UTEP Historic $70 Million in Fiscal Year 2026
The University of Texas at El Paso reported a record $70 million in philanthropic support during the 2025-26 fiscal year that ended Aug. 31. UTEP officials said the money would be used to support initiatives that benefit students, faculty and aspects of campus life.
The university’s previous record was $50.5 million in fiscal year 2024. The institution also reported that the 6,703 donors were the most in school history. UTEP recorded 6,428 donors in fiscal year 2024-25.
Among the major donations during 2026 fiscal year were the record $30 million from UTEP alumnus Miguel A. “Mike” Loya in February for engineering scholarships, $5 million from Tawney, Acosta and Chaparro, and $5 million from the Paul L. Foster Family Foundation in a matching gift for the planned UTEP law school, and $1.5 million from University Medical Center and $1.1 million from the Hospitals of Providence and Tenet Healthcare Foundation to enhance healthcare education.
There also were donations to the Athletics Department of $2.5 million from Paul L. Foster and Alejandra de la Vega Foster, and $1 million each from Frank and Shirley Sloan and Bob McFadden.
The university said in a news release that the money raised would go toward athletics, student scholarships, campus enhancements, faculty recruitment and retention, academic and research initiatives and other strategic priorities.
UTEP President Heather Wilson said the historic level of philanthropy reflected the confidence of supporters to the university’s mission.
“Their generosity is an investment in our students and our academic excellence,” Wilson said in the release. “We couldn’t do nearly as much without them.”
Lifeguards surveill the pool at the Westside Natatorium, April 30, 2026. (Corrie Boudreaux/El Paso Matters)
City Adopts New Parks Master Plan With Focus on Existing Facilities
The City Council on Monday adopted its new 10-year Parks and Recreation Master Plan that aims to improve existing parks and facilities, rather than create new ones.

Sign up
The plan works as a guide for the city to make improvements to existing parks and facilities through the next 10 years. The city owns and operates 291 parks, 30 miles of trails, 23 recreation and sports centers, 10 senior centers and 15 aquatic facilities.
Some potential improvements include adding lighting, shade and playground amenities while facility repairs, renovations and reconstruction are planned.
RELATED: El Paso pays millions more for city pools despite rising revenue
Facilities that were recommended for replacement or reconstruction included the Grandview Pool, Nations Tobin Pool, Leona Ford Washington Recreation
Center and the South El Paso Senior Center.
Facilities that need heavy renovation and expansion included the Armijo Aquatic Center, Don Haskins Recreation Center, Delta Aquatic Center, Hawkins Aquatic Center, Officer David Ortiz Recreation Center, Nations Tobin Sports Center and the Marty Robbins Aquatic Center.
The plan, conducted by Halff Associates, only identified costs of about $15.3 million for repairs and improvements – not including expansions, major renovations or replacements or any new facilities. It did not estimate costs for those big-ticket items. The plan also doesn’t give specific funding sources, but suggested options such as using the city’s general fund, bonds, community partnerships, sponsorships, grants or user fees.
The city hired the Richardson, Texas-based firm for $580,000 in August 2025 to develop the new master plan. The firm also conducted the 2014 study that led to the 2015 master plan under which the city developed the water parks, spray parks and two Olympic-sized competitive swimming pools or natatoriums. Those projects were largely funded through the voter-approved 2012 quality of life bond and certificates of obligation – a form of debt that doesn’t require voter approval.
A $12.2 million plan to expand the Texas Tech Health El Paso Woody L. Hunt School of Dental Medicine Oral Health Clinic will benefit the community and serve as a recruitment incentive to future students and faculty. (Daniel Perez/El Paso Matters)
