Texas Tech Regents Agree to $12 Million Budget to Expand El Paso Dental Clinic
The Texas Tech University Board of Regents approved Wednesday a budget of $12.2 million for the expansion of the Dental Oral Health Clinic at the Texas Tech Health El Paso during the board’s quarterly meeting in Lubbock.
The agreement calls for local institutional funds to be used for this project, which consists of the renovation of almost 12,000 gross square feet within TTHEP’s Woody L. Hunt School of Dental Medicine Oral Health Clinic, 222 Rick Francis St.
The work includes the conversion of campus support office space into space for clinics, instruction and administration that will support the continued growth of the dental education programs and the need for patient care services.

Israeli Startup Edelbyte Raises $70 Million to Enter Data Infrastructure Market
Founded by four Microsoft veterans, the company is targeting established players including Snowflake and Databricks as AI drives demand for faster, more affordable data analytics
Mandi Kogosowski
|
15/11/2026
Sponsored
Illustration: Kampus Production via pexels.com
Israeli startup Edelbyte has emerged from stealth with $70 million in seed and Series A funding to compete in the data infrastructure market, targeting established providers including Snowflake, Databricks, and ClickHouse.
Founded in 2025 by four former Microsoft engineers, the company is developing a search and analytics platform designed to help enterprises handle growing data volumes and AI-driven workloads without significantly increasing infrastructure costs.
The funding round was led by Sequoia and Quiet Capital, with participation from Greenoaks and Swish Ventures .
Edelbyte's founders – Avner Aharoni, Evgeney Ryzhyk, Alexander Sloutsky, and Yoni Leibowitz – each spent approximately 20 years at Microsoft, where they worked on Kusto, the data engine used across multiple Microsoft products.
The company is addressing a growing challenge for enterprises: AI applications and agents generate increasing numbers of queries across large datasets, putting additional pressure on infrastructure and budgets. Companies often respond by limiting queries, archiving data, or investing in additional capacity.
Edelbyte says its platform can help reduce these costs while supporting higher query volumes. Some customers migrating from existing systems have reportedly been able to run up to ten times more queries within the same budget.
Despite being founded less than two years ago, the company says it already has Fortune 500 customers running petabyte-scale deployments.
Based in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, Edelbyte plans to use the funding to expand its enterprise customer base, international operations, and workforce.

Economy
Elumelu Acquires Additional $70m Seplat Shares, Raises Stake to 22.05%
Published 2 seconds ago
on 17/11/2026
By Adedapo Adesanya
By Adedapo Adesanya
Nigerian businessman, Mr Tony Elumelu, has acquired an additional $70 million stake in Seplat Energy Plc through his energy investment firm, Heirs Energies Limited, increasing its shareholding in the energy firm to 22.05 per cent.
The latest acquisition involved approximately 5.9 million shares, representing about one per cent of Seplat, Bloomberg reported, citing a spokesperson for Heirs Energies.
The transaction marks another increase in Mr Elumelu’s investment in the Nigerian energy company, following a similar acquisition in September and an initial purchase of a 20 per cent slice in December 2025.
In October, Heirs Energies acquired an additional six million shares, representing one per cent of Seplat, for approximately £53.22 million (about N94 billion), raising its shareholding to 21.07 per cent at the time.
The initial acquisition involved about 120.4 million shares purchased from French energy company Maurel & Prom for about $500 million.
The latest investment comes as Heirs Energies pursues plans to expand its operations and increase its stake in Seplat.
The company’s chief executive, Mr Osa Igiehon, said in an interview last month that increasing its holding in Seplat aligns with its growth strategy, which also includes raising oil production to 100,000 barrels per day by the end of the decade.
Meanwhile, Mr Elumelu is expected to assume the position of Chairman of Seplat on January 1, 2027, succeeding Mr Udoma Udo Udoma, who is due to retire from the organisation’s board on December 31, 2026.

candidates.title: BAE Systems Receives Maximum $62.9 Million DLA Energy Automation Support Contract
candidates.snippet:
BAE Systems Technology Solutions & Services has received a fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract with a maximum value of approximately $62.9 million for global support of energy automation and fuel-storage safety systems.
The post BAE Systems Receives Maximum $62.9 Million DLA Energy Automation Support Contract appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
BAE Systems Receives Maximum $62.9 Million DLA Energy Automation Support Contract
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 10:39 AM
BAE Systems Receives Maximum $62.9 Million DLA Energy Automation Support Contract
BAE Systems Technology Solutions & Services has received a fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract with a maximum value of approximately $62.9 million for global support of energy automation and fuel-storage safety systems.
The Rockville, Maryland-based contractor will provide sustainment for operational technology, automatic tank gauging, independent alarm systems, and overfill-protection equipment.
The Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard are identified as customers under the contract. The broad customer group reflects the use of fuel-management and storage systems throughout military installations and operational locations.
The five-year contract includes no option periods and has a performance completion date of November 9, 2031. Its stated $62.9 million value is the maximum IDIQ ceiling rather than a guaranteed payment to BAE Systems.
The government will issue orders for required products or services over the performance period. The announcement does not identify an initial task order, guaranteed minimum, or specific amount obligated when the IDIQ contract was awarded.
Fiscal 2027 defense working capital funds are identified as the applicable appropriation. Future orders and obligations will depend on customer requirements, available funding, and the contract’s ordering procedures.
The procurement was competitive, with four responses received. The Defense Logistics Agency Contracting Services Office in Columbus, Ohio, is the contracting activity for contract SP4706-27-D-0002.
Automatic tank gauges help monitor fuel levels and related storage conditions. Independent alarms and overfill-protection equipment can reduce the risk of spills, equipment damage, environmental incidents, and operational interruptions.
Operational technology sustainment may include maintenance, technical support, configuration management, repair, replacement, and other services needed to keep these systems functioning. The government announcement does not provide a more detailed breakdown of individual tasks.
The contract gives multiple military services and the Coast Guard a common mechanism for obtaining global support. BAE Systems will be eligible to receive orders up to the ceiling during the five-year period, but actual contract revenue will depend on the number and value of orders placed.

candidates.text:
FHLBank Chicago: $62 Million Affordable Housing Grants To Support 1,786 Homes Across Illinois And Wisconsin
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:29 AM
FHLBank Chicago: $62 Million Affordable Housing Grants To Support 1,786 Homes Across Illinois And Wisconsin
The Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago has awarded $62 million through its 2026 Affordable Housing Program General Fund to finance 47 affordable housing projects in Illinois and Wisconsin. The funding will support the acquisition, rehabilitation, and construction of 1,786 affordable housing units across the two states.
The awards include an additional $10 million approved by FHLBank Chicago’s Board of Directors to expand support for affordable housing development.
The grants are intended to address housing affordability challenges as development costs and constrained housing supply continue to affect communities.
FHLBank Chicago operates as a regional member-owned cooperative within the Federal Home Loan Bank System.
Its member institutions include commercial banks, credit unions, insurance companies, savings institutions, and community development financial institutions.
The Affordable Housing Program provides grants to support projects sponsored through participating member institutions.
Applications are submitted by housing developers, government organizations, public housing authorities, tribally designated organizations, and other eligible participants.
The funding helps bridge gaps between the cost of providing affordable housing and the financing available through other sources.
The 2026 awards cover projects involving different housing needs and development approaches.
One recipient is Reclaiming Chicago NFP, which received support for the construction of 24 affordable single-family homes on vacant city-owned lots.
The homes will be developed across four Chicago neighborhoods: Back of the Yards, Roseland, North Lawndale, and Washington Park.
The project is sponsored by First Eagle Bank, a member of FHLBank Chicago.
It is part of an initiative organized by United Power for Action and Justice, a coalition that brings together civic and religious organizations.
Five nonprofit development partners are participating in the effort.
The project is intended to expand opportunities for homeownership while returning vacant properties to productive residential use.
First Eagle Bank has also provided a $1 million interest-free loan to support the development.
The combination of financing and grant support is intended to help move the project toward construction.
Another award will support Milwaukee Development Corporation’s conversion of a former hospital into affordable apartments.
The project will create 124 residences for adults ages 55 and older.
Of those units, 25 will be designated as supportive housing for residents with disabilities.
Jewish Family Services will provide on-site services to eligible residents.
Associated Bank is sponsoring the project through the Affordable Housing Program.
The redevelopment is intended to preserve a historic building while introducing additional affordable housing options for older adults.
Projects like these illustrate the program’s support for both new construction and the reuse of existing properties.
Since the Affordable Housing Program General Fund began in 1989, FHLBank Chicago has allocated more than $630 million in grants through the end of 2025.
These investments have helped provide housing for more than 85,000 households.
The latest $62 million allocation represents another significant commitment to affordable housing development across the bank’s two-state district.
The organization believes the funding will help developers and community partners move projects forward despite rising construction costs and financing challenges.
By supporting 47 projects and 1,786 housing units, FHLBank Chicago aims to expand access to affordable homes while strengthening neighborhoods across Illinois and Wisconsin.
KEY QUOTES:
“Affordable housing remains a pressing need across Illinois and Wisconsin, as rising development costs and limited housing supply continue to challenge communities. By increasing our investment in this year’s AHP General Fund, we’re able to support more affordable housing and help our members and community organizations move critical projects forward.”
Michael Ericson, President And CEO Of FHLBank Chicago
“FHLBank Chicago’s Affordable Housing Program plays an important role in closing financing gaps and making affordable housing projects possible. We’re proud to support Reclaiming Chicago’s efforts to transform vacant lots into affordable homes and create meaningful homeownership opportunities for Chicago families. Beyond sponsoring the AHP grant, First Eagle Bank has also provided a $1 million interest-free loan to help advance this important initiative. We strongly believe in Reclaiming Chicago’s mission, and their efforts to revitalize neighborhoods and expand affordable homeownership have certainly not gone unnoticed.”
Faruk Daudbasic, Senior Vice President Of Commercial Lending And Community Development At First Eagle Bank
“This development will bring much-needed affordable housing to Milwaukee while preserving an important part of the neighborhood’s history. We’re grateful to FHLBank Chicago and Associated Bank for supporting a project that will help older adults live independently with access to the services they need.”
Pat O’Brien, President Of Milwaukee Development Corporation

candidates.text:
Remedy Robotics Raises $62 Million Series B to Bring Life-Saving Cardiovascular Intervention to Patients Everywhere
News provided by
Remedy Robotics, Inc.
Nov 16, 2026, 10:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Funding will support clinical trials, advancement toward FDA approval, and planned commercial deployment of the company's AI-enabled endovascular robotic platform and software suite
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Remedy Robotics, Inc. ("Remedy"), a leading healthcare and physical AI company developing robotic systems for cardiovascular care and endovascular intervention, today announced it has raised $62 million in Series B funding to accelerate its mission of delivering flawless, immediate robotic care to all patients, regardless of location.
The funding will support several major milestones, including a planned pivotal clinical trial in partnership with the University of California and advancement toward FDA approval for neurovascular intervention. Remedy will also deploy prototype N1 Systems across its network of clinical partners, including through its strategic partnerships with SVIN Mission Thrombectomy and the Australian Stroke Alliance, while continuing to advance the system's industry-leading AI capabilities and autonomous functions.
"Endovascular intervention is the gold standard treatment for stroke and many cardiovascular emergencies, yet access remains limited to a small number of hospitals. For these time-critical conditions, that's devastating. Even when specialist intervention is available, treatment is often delayed, and complications are frustratingly common," said Dr. David Bell, CEO and Co-founder of Remedy Robotics . "This funding will allow us to accelerate toward deployment of our N1 System so we can bring quality intervention to patients everywhere, regardless of geography."
DCVC led the Series B, with participation from new investors including UC Investments (the University of California's investment office), Skip Capital, and Hostplus (one of Australia's largest pension funds). Existing investors Build Collective by Tony Fadell, Blackbird, Divergent Capital and KdT Ventures doubled down.
"Remedy Robotics represents a new generation of medical robotics and physical AI companies, focused not only on technical innovation, but on solving real-world challenges," said James Hardiman, General Partner at DCVC . "We believe the company is uniquely positioned to redefine how life-saving intervention is delivered and are thrilled to support them as they advance toward broader clinical and commercial adoption."
Remedy is finalizing development of the N1 System, an AI-enabled robotic platform and software suite that uses machine learning to analyze preoperative imaging, simulate cases in advance, provide real-time 3D-2D image registration and complete entire endovascular procedures robotically. Designed for on-site, remote, or autonomous operation, the system has the potential to dramatically expand access to and improve the quality of specialized neurovascular, coronary, and peripheral vascular care. Remedy now works with more than 100 hospitals worldwide and is among a small group of physical AI companies bringing robotics into real-world clinical use. In October 2025, Remedy announced that it had successfully completed the world's first remote neurointerventional procedures using the N1 System.
"This funding will allow our world-leading hardware, software, and machine learning teams to progress the N1 system towards clinical trials and potential FDA approval, while also developing additional features including full autonomy," said Jake Sganga, CTO and Co-founder of Remedy Robotics . "We are particularly excited to deepen our partnership with the University of California, having worked closely with their clinical experts since 2021, and as we prepare for our planned pivotal clinical trials to be held across the UC network."
"Remedy is building the kind of company we look for at Blackbird: one with world-class technical talent, a massive global problem to solve, and the potential to create an entirely new category," said Michael Tolo, Partner at Blackbird . "We believe Remedy is uniquely positioned to transform how endovascular care is delivered, and we are excited to support the company through its next phase of growth."
Cardiovascular disease, including stroke and heart attack, is the leading cause of death globally—claiming nearly 20 million lives each year—about twice the toll of all cancers. Beyond the human cost, stroke alone carries an annual economic burden of approximately $891 billion worldwide through healthcare costs and lost productivity. Access to endovascular intervention, the most effective treatment for many cardiovascular conditions, remains severely limited because only highly specialized physicians at a small number of hospitals can perform it. Today, just 2.8 percent of eligible stroke patients worldwide have access to endovascular treatment, leaving millions each year with otherwise preventable disability. Because cardiovascular emergencies are so time-critical, patient outcomes vary sharply based on proximity to specialized care, even in countries with well-developed specialist networks, such as the United States. Remedy's technology directly addresses this access gap, delivering expert care for stroke, severe heart attacks, hemorrhagic conditions, and other time-critical cardiovascular emergencies to patients wherever they are.
Remedy aims to elevate the standard of care across the cardiovascular continuum, from diagnosis to discharge and surveillance, with the goal of making flawless, immediate cardiovascular care available to patients everywhere, from San Francisco to rural areas of Arkansas where timely care is out of reach, or to Lagos, Nigeria, where intervention is almost entirely unavailable.
The N1 System is under development and is not currently available for sale or clinical use in any jurisdiction.

Oyster Therapeutics: $60 Million Series A-2 Funding To Advance Alzheimer’s Drug Development And Protein Degradation Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 4:19 AM
Oyster Therapeutics: $60 Million Series A-2 Funding To Advance Alzheimer’s Drug Development And Protein Degradation Platform
Oyster Therapeutics, formerly known as Kesmalea Therapeutics, has raised $60 million in Series A-2 funding to advance its next-generation targeted protein degradation technology for Alzheimer’s disease and other neurodegenerative conditions. The financing will support the development of the company’s lead oral tau degrader toward clinical trials while expanding its proprietary SELFTAC drug discovery platform. The round was led by 4BIO Capital, a London-based venture capital firm specializing in life sciences, with participation from new investors Eli Lilly and Company, CE Ventures, Actium Group, and TOHO Ventures, which is managed by Global Brain.
Existing investors Syncona, Oxford Science Enterprises, Mission BioCapital, and MGB Ventures also participated.
The financing comes as the company rebrands from Kesmalea Therapeutics to Oyster Therapeutics, reflecting its transition toward clinical development and broader ambitions in neuroscience.
Headquartered in London, Oyster is developing medicines based on targeted protein degradation, a therapeutic approach designed to eliminate disease-associated proteins by using the body’s natural cellular protein disposal mechanisms.
Unlike conventional treatments that may inhibit the activity of particular proteins, targeted protein degraders are designed to trigger their removal from cells.
Oyster is initially focusing on neurodegenerative diseases involving abnormal accumulations of the tau protein.
Tau plays an important role in maintaining healthy neuronal structures, but abnormal forms can accumulate and contribute to diseases known as tauopathies.
Alzheimer’s disease is among the best-known conditions associated with pathological tau accumulation.
The company’s lead program is an orally administered, brain-penetrant tau degrader designed to selectively remove harmful forms of tau while preserving healthy tau.
Developing medicines capable of reaching the central nervous system presents considerable challenges because the blood-brain barrier restricts the passage of many therapeutic compounds.
Traditional bifunctional protein degraders can be relatively large molecules, limiting their ability to cross biological membranes and reach brain tissue.
Oyster’s proprietary SELFTAC platform is designed to address this limitation by enabling larger targeted protein degraders to function as smaller molecular components.
The technology uses a reversible linker connecting two molecular structures, commonly called warheads.
One component binds to the targeted protein, while the other recruits the cellular machinery responsible for protein degradation.
The reversible linker enables the components to exist as smaller molecules that can more readily penetrate biological membranes.
The molecules are subsequently designed to self-assemble into a functional bifunctional degrader capable of triggering the removal of the intended protein.
Oyster believes this approach could improve central nervous system penetration while preserving the versatility of conventional targeted protein degradation technology.
The company also expects its smaller molecular designs to support oral administration, potentially making treatments more convenient for patients.
Oral therapies can offer practical advantages for diseases affecting large populations, including simplified administration, room-temperature storage, and potentially lower manufacturing costs.
Beyond its lead tau program, Oyster intends to use SELFTAC as a platform for generating additional targeted protein degrader candidates.
The technology incorporates a modular design that supports high-throughput screening of different molecular combinations.
This approach is intended to accelerate candidate identification while improving the efficiency of drug discovery.
Oyster has also established a sponsored research agreement with Massachusetts General Hospital to strengthen its tau biology research capabilities.
The collaboration will provide access to patient-derived neuronal cell lines and specialized methods for generating and detecting oligomeric tau.
Oligomeric tau refers to aggregated forms of the protein that are considered particularly relevant to neurodegenerative disease processes.
The research will be supervised by Dr. Catarina Silva, an investigator at the Mass General Brigham Neuroscience Institute and Assistant Professor of Neurology at Harvard Medical School.
The collaboration is intended to help Oyster evaluate its therapeutic candidates in biologically relevant systems and strengthen its understanding of disease-associated tau.
The $60 million financing will support continued preclinical development, advancement toward human studies, and further investment in the SELFTAC platform.
Oyster’s strategy reflects increasing interest in therapeutic approaches that directly address proteins implicated in neurodegenerative conditions.
However, the company’s lead program remains investigational, and its safety and effectiveness in patients have not yet been established.
As Oyster advances toward clinical development, the company will seek to demonstrate whether its technology can effectively reach the brain and selectively degrade disease-associated proteins.
The rebranding marks a new phase for the business as it works to translate its protein degradation research into potential treatments for Alzheimer’s and other neurological diseases.

candidates.text:
Eli Radiopharma: Nearly $60 Million Series A Financing To Advance Radiopharmaceutical Pipeline Toward Clinical Development
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:27 AM
Eli Radiopharma: Nearly $60 Million Series A Financing To Advance Radiopharmaceutical Pipeline Toward Clinical Development
Eli Radiopharma has raised nearly $60 million (RMB 400 million) in Series A financing to advance its radiopharmaceutical pipeline toward clinical development. The funding will support preclinical research, regulatory submissions, early-stage clinical studies, and the expansion of the company’s research and development capabilities.
Huagai Capital led the financing round, with Bayland Capital serving as co-lead investor. Additional participants included Boyu Ventures, Delian Capital, InnoPinnacle Fund, Haibang Venture, Bairui Capital, Shenzhen Angel FOF Management, and Grand Flight Investment.
Existing shareholders CSPC & Growth Bio Fund, Huaige Capital, KHK Fund, Longfeng Venture, Hongsheng Capital, Bioclub Fund, and Skyfield Capital also participated in the financing.
Eli Radiopharma plans to allocate the proceeds toward preclinical research, investigational new drug applications, and early-stage clinical development. The company will also strengthen its research platforms, recruit additional talent, expand clinical operations, and pursue business development opportunities.
Founded in 2024, Eli Radiopharma focuses on developing radiopharmaceutical products that combine molecular targeting with radionuclide technology. Its pipeline includes diagnostic and therapeutic candidates designed to address unmet medical needs in oncology and neurological diseases.
The company has advanced multiple programs targeting novel molecular mechanisms through lead discovery, laboratory validation, and animal studies. Several candidates are approaching investigational new drug submissions, representing an important transition from early research toward human clinical testing.
Radiopharmaceuticals combine targeting molecules with radioactive isotopes to identify or treat diseased tissue. Therapeutic radioligands are designed to deliver radiation directly to tumors while limiting exposure to surrounding healthy tissue. Related diagnostic imaging agents can help physicians identify appropriate patients, evaluate disease progression, and monitor treatment responses.
The financing also reflects growing international interest in radiopharmaceutical innovation originating in China. Global pharmaceutical companies have increasingly explored opportunities involving novel molecular targets, therapeutic radionuclides, and expanded clinical applications.
Eli Radiopharma’s investors identified these areas as important drivers of future industry growth, particularly as radiopharmaceutical technologies move into additional cancer indications and other therapeutic applications.
The company’s longer-term strategy includes building a globally competitive pipeline capable of serving patients in international markets, including the U.S. and Europe. Its immediate priorities involve completing preclinical development, meeting regulatory requirements, and advancing differentiated candidates into clinical studies.
The Series A financing provides Eli Radiopharma with additional resources to move its lead programs closer to clinical validation while expanding the infrastructure needed to support a broader radiopharmaceutical development portfolio.
KEY QUOTES
“Moving our pipeline toward the clinic is a critical next step in translating our research into meaningful advances for patients. This financing will support our efforts to advance our lead programs through preclinical development and regulatory milestones.”
Dr. Feng Yu, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Eli Radiopharma

News provided by

Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital co-lead $30 million expansion to scale Kindo's go-to-market operations and accelerate development of its AI agent management platform
LOS ANGELES , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kindo , the run-anywhere AI agent management platform that puts the enterprise in control, today announced a $30 million raise co-led by Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital, bringing total capital raised to $57.6 million. The company grew revenue by approximately 800% year over year in 2026 and will use the financing to expand its go-to-market organization and accelerate development of its enterprise AI Control Center and Deep Hat models and add-ons.
Continue Reading
Meet Kindo video
As autonomous agents spread through the enterprise and their numbers swell into the thousands, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance teams struggle to control risks and costs without a centralized tool that can discover, observe, and control the entire enterprise AI footprint. Every time a company lets an AI agent access data, update a customer record, approve a request, or change a production system, it delegates authority. The same permissions that let an agent get work done can let it expose sensitive data, make changes outside company policy, disrupt a critical workflow, or rack up huge inference costs.
"Agent builders from the AI labs, hyperscalers, and thousands of startups make it easy to deploy powerful agents across the business," said Ron Williams, founder and CEO of Kindo. "What's missing is the tooling that lets an organization centrally control how those agents are built, what data they can reach, where that data can go, and what they cost, while also allowing support teams to reach in and fix an agent at any hour. That gap is why the teams responsible for supporting and controlling Al are rightfully putting the brakes on Al transformation."
Kindo gives organizations control of the AI agents already running across their operations. It starts with discovery, uncovering shadow AI and mapping where agents are in use, then brings their activity, access, costs, and outcomes into one view. The teams that must support and control AI, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance, get a single set of controls: what employees can do with an agent, what an agent can touch, how it behaves around the clock, and what it costs. The result is an AI Operations Center, SOC- and NOC-style monitoring and intervention for AI, where those teams eliminate risk, drive down cost, and make sure AI delivers measurable outcomes.
Implementation is turnkey and is run by the IT operations staff an organization already has. Teams connect the agents, data sources, and AI models already in use, and from that moment everything is discovered, observed, and controlled from one place. Kindo's gateways govern and audit every call an agent makes to connected data, tools, and approved models. Identity controls apply the organization's existing permissions to people and agents alike, with the option to tighten them centrally. For mission-critical agents that need deeper control, Kindo's harness, purpose-built for centralized agent operations, adds around-the-clock monitoring, support, and direct intervention, including the ability to take over an agent when something goes wrong.
Customer Adoption
Kindo runs in production at large and mid-market enterprises in financial services, professional services, healthcare, and aviation/transportation. Global aviation in-flight data provider Aireon's CISO reported in May 2026 that using Kindo for threat hunting and Tier 1 and Tier 2 SOC functions helped the company work faster, get more value from its existing security monitoring infrastructure, and save more than $2 million a year.
Controlling AI Cost
Security and compliance were the first reasons organizations needed control of their agents. Cost is now front and center. AI spend is growing year over year with no end in sight, and it has become a key issue slowing AI programs.
Kindo's AI Control Center gives Finance teams a way in. Every token consumed and every agent run's outcome is recorded, including the failed ones, so costs and return on AI spend roll up by individual, agent, department, and project. Budgets can be set, alerts triggered, and hard spend caps enforced. Finance sees what each agent is trying to do, what it did, and how much it spent doing it, which surfaces the agents that fail often, deliver little, or use models that are overkill for the task.
For agents running in Kindo's harness, the Deep Hat add-ons drive those costs down. Deep Hat Sift learns from an agent's verdicts which events on busy alert and ticket queues it would dismiss; once a person approves the threshold, Sift skips those runs, logs every event it filters, and sends a sample through to measure misses. Deep Hat Tune adapts a smaller, lower-cost model to a specific task, reserving larger models for work that needs them. Deep Hat Shrink runs repeatable workflow steps as code, eliminating the model cost entirely, and still routes exceptions back to the model when needed. Deep Hat Attack gives security teams low-cost, private offensive security testing, reducing frontier cybersecurity model use for day-to-day security work.
TFX Capital and CircleRock Capital participated in the financing, alongside existing investors Drive Capital, Riot Ventures, RRE Ventures, Eniac Ventures, Marlinspike Partners, New Era Ventures, and Sunset Venture. As part of the financing, Andre Fuetsch, managing director at Crosspoint Capital, and Ernie Bio, managing director at Forgepoint Capital, will join Kindo's board of directors.

LanceDB Raises $57.5M Series B to Expand Its Multimodal AI Lakehouse
Published
November 17, 2026
By
Evan Mercer, AI Startups & Venture Capital AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
Key Points LanceDB raised $57.5 million to expand a lakehouse that curates and serves AI training…
View more
LanceDB raised $57.5 million to expand a lakehouse that curates and serves AI training data.
The company reports more than tenfold year-over-year revenue growth since its Series A in June 2025.
LanceDB aims to unify training data, experiments and rollouts so teams stop hand-managing pipelines.
LanceDB announced on November 17, 2026 that it raised $57.5 million in Series B funding to expand its multimodal lakehouse, a platform for organizing and delivering AI training data. The round brings the company’s total funding to $98.5 million.
Bessemer Venture Partners and Innovation Endeavors led the round, with participation from Theory Ventures, Dimension, Swift Ventures, CRV and Y Combinator. LanceDB plans to put the capital toward a broader role across model development, including training-data management, feature engineering, experiment execution and data loading.
Adoption and Technical Scale
LanceDB says researchers can lose weeks or months obtaining and curating training data even though frontier AI advances are measured in days and weeks. Its multimodal lakehouse is intended to close that gap by combining curation, search and retrieval, feature engineering and training for work on frontier models, world models, physical AI and enterprise applications.
The company reports more than tenfold year-over-year revenue growth since its Series A in June 2025. Its open-source library has been downloaded more than 120 million times, representing sixfold growth in total downloads from the same point a year earlier. Customers include Netflix, Microsoft AI, Runway , Luma AI and Midjourney.
The platform is designed to hold multimodal data such as videos, images and sensor data while supporting large-scale retrieval and training. LanceDB says the platform supports more than 130,000 requests per second with latency below 210 milliseconds for 95% of requests, individual tables containing hundreds of petabytes of data or more than 40 billion vectors, and training across 8,000 GPUs in parallel.
Enterprise additions address updates to those tables while they are in use. A durable, memory-accelerated write path handles real-time ingest, distributed indexing scales across large datasets, and managed compaction continuously optimizes tables in the background. LanceDB says managed compaction supports up to 100 billion multimodal rows while multiple researchers concurrently read, write and query the same table.
Customers Describe Changing Training Datasets
Runway CTO Kamil Sindi described how one training example evolves: “A training example at Runway doesn’t stay still. It starts as a video and a prompt, then we add embeddings, resolution and duration metadata, whatever the next experiment needs.” Runway began using the Lance data format in 2024 and later became a LanceDB Enterprise customer. The company now uses Lance and LanceDB Enterprise together so researchers can work through large, changing datasets more quickly.
NVIDIA Cosmos, an open-source user and partner, provides another deployment example. Technical lead Max Li said the team curated roughly one million hours of video with Lance for Cosmos 3, is moving toward training directly from the format, and finds its object-storage-native architecture useful for streaming, filtering and inspecting large datasets as they are revised while supplying data to large GPU clusters.
Microsoft AI data-platform head Suqiang (Jack) Song said his organization uses LanceDB as its training-data layer for billions of rows spanning images and code, with distributed inference jobs reading Lance directly on thousands of nodes; operating within Microsoft’s own tenant and security policy was non-negotiable for production.
Series B Roadmap
LanceDB intends to bring training data, context, logs and rollouts into one system at petabyte scale. Research teams would also be able to run large numbers of AI-agent experiments in parallel without contaminating shared datasets. The work is aimed at the full model-improvement cycle, reducing the manual pipeline oversight and data-loading problems that can slow research.
LanceDB also plans to deepen its feature-engineering tools. A team would define a transformation once, after which the platform would apply it throughout the dataset, backfill existing rows and process new data as it arrives. Further work targets more of the preparation done before training, plus better data loading and caching during training runs.
The Series B pushes LanceDB beyond retrieval into the continuing work of changing datasets, conducting experiments and supplying training jobs. Its next phase will test whether one platform can accommodate both frontier-scale data volumes and the constant, experiment-by-experiment changes described by customers such as Runway.

Systems Planning And Analysis Receives Up To $55.7 Million Navy Trident II Support Order
Systems Planning and Analysis has received a Navy task order valued at up to approximately $55.7 million to support the Trident II Strategic Weapons System.
The Alexandria, Virginia-based company will perform technical assessments and studies, systems engineering and analysis, program integration, and schedule support.
The cost-plus-fixed-fee term task order is identified as N0003027F3024. Its $55.7 million stated value includes optional line items, meaning the full amount depends on whether the Navy exercises those options.
Work is expected to continue through September 30, 2031. Washington, D.C., will account for 60% of performance, while Alexandria will account for 32%.
The remaining work will be distributed among Bangor, Washington; Denver, Colorado; Titusville, Florida; Kings Bay, Georgia; Pittsfield, Massachusetts; Valley Forge, Pennsylvania; Magna, Utah; and Sunnyvale, California. Each location represents 1% of performance.
Initial obligations total approximately $1.7 million. This includes $200,981 in fiscal 2026 research, development, test, and evaluation funding; $150,000 in fiscal 2027 RDT&E funding; and approximately $1.3 million in fiscal 2027 Navy operation and maintenance funding.
The $200,981 fiscal 2026 RDT&E allocation will expire at the end of fiscal 2027. The source announcement does not state that the remaining potential task-order value has been obligated.
The effort also benefits a foreign military sale to the United Kingdom, reflecting the U.K.’s role in the Trident strategic weapons enterprise.
The task order will be issued as a sole-source acquisition under an authority associated with federal small-business research and development programs.
Portfolio Acquisition Executive, Strategic Systems Programs in Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity. Strategic Systems Programs manages the Navy’s sea-based strategic deterrence systems.

candidates.text:
Charta Health: $55 Million Series B To Expand AI Medical Chart Review
By Amit Chowdhry
Nov 11, 2026
Charta Health: $55 Million Series B To Expand AI Medical Chart Review
Charta Health has raised $55 million in Series B funding to expand its artificial intelligence platform for medical chart review and create a common standard of billing accuracy for healthcare providers and insurers. Insight Partners led the round, with participation from existing investors Madrona, Bain Capital Ventures, and South Park Commons, along with QuantumLight.
Charta applies AI to unstructured clinical information, including physician notes, scanned orders, laboratory results, and images. Its technology reviews medical records to determine whether documented care supports the codes used for billing.
The company wants providers and payers to resolve coding discrepancies before a claim is submitted rather than through denials, audits, and appeals. Those administrative processes contribute billions of dollars in costs to the U.S. healthcare system.
Charta for Providers reviews every chart before billing and checks the documentation against official coding guidance, payer rules, and an organization’s clinical protocols. Findings are presented within electronic health record workflows for human approval.
The company says its platform produces consistent double-digit reductions in denial rates. It also gives compliance and medical leadership teams information about documentation gaps, recurring errors, and provider performance.
Charta works with healthcare organizations including American Family Care, Grow Therapy, and Pediatric Associates Family of Companies. It will use the funding to improve the accuracy and intelligence of its provider technology and expand into additional medical specialties.
The financing also supports Charta for Payers, a suite developed with one of the country’s largest health insurers. The offering initially focuses on Medicare Advantage and Affordable Care Act Marketplace plans.
Its six products cover retrospective hierarchical condition category coding, automated second-pass reviews, coder workflows, prospective risk-adjustment intelligence, audit preparation, and quality care-gap detection.
The technology can identify conditions documented but not coded and diagnoses that lack sufficient clinical support. Charta’s longer-term objective is to give providers and insurers a consistent interpretation of the same medical record before reimbursement decisions are made.
KEY QUOTE:
“Healthcare payments depend on the medical chart, and charting errors cause costly problems across the entire process. As payers and providers both adopt AI, we believe the opportunity lies in getting the underlying record, or the ‘ground truth,’ right before a claim is submitted. Charta pairs AI with customer-specific coding expertise and serves both sides of that market. We are excited to partner with Justin, Scott, and the team as they scale.”
Jeff Horing, Co-Founder and Managing Director at Insight Partners

candidates.title: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM
candidates.snippet: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM TechCrunch
candidates.text:
Dreamteam , a startup founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million to challenge Salesforce and HubSpot with its AI-native CRM, betting that AI can finally shake up a market where established players have so far proved difficult to dislodge.
The funding comprises seed and Series A rounds, led by Together Fund and Accel respectively, with participation from Premji Invest. The San Francisco-based startup declined to disclose the size of each round or its valuation.
Traditional CRMs depend on salespeople to manually record customer interactions and keep deal information up to date. That often leaves businesses with incomplete or outdated information. Dreamteam aims to eliminate much of that work by automatically capturing context from sources including emails and customer conversations. It also uses AI agents to handle tasks such as follow-ups, meeting preparation, and pipeline monitoring.
Dreamteam co-founder and CEO Anand Venkatraman (pictured above, right) told TechCrunch that he had repeatedly encountered problems with traditional CRM platforms over more than 25 years in enterprise software, including at Salesforce and Freshworks. Salespeople spent considerable time updating records, yet managers still struggled to get a reliable picture of their business. “In all these years, I have never come across an instance where I could click a button and get a forecast from the CRM,” he said.
That experience led Venkatraman to co-found Dreamteam in 2025 with Senthil Kanthaswamy (pictured above, center), who spent more than nine years at Freshworks, most recently as a product leader at Freshservice, and Ramesh Parthasarathy (pictured above, left), who previously worked on AI and platform engineering at Freshworks.
At the heart of Dreamteam’s CRM is what it calls the Company Brain. This acts as virtual memory, pulling together information from emails, meetings, and other customer interactions to build a shared record of customer relationships. Four built-in AI agents use that information to research prospects, draft follow-up emails, flag potential risks to deals, and configure CRM workflows, with sales teams retaining control over what gets sent to customers.
Dreamteam has signed up more than 100 customers across 13 countries in the three months since it began actively selling its product, with most paying for the service, Venkatraman said. The startup has also replaced established CRM platforms at several businesses, including Salesforce at healthcare company DMS Health and HubSpot at other customers.
The advertising sales team at media streaming company Plex also chose Dreamteam over HubSpot and other AI-native CRM alternatives, Venkatraman told TechCrunch. Plex’s co-founder and chief product officer Scott Olechowski said Dreamteam’s ability to integrate with AI tools already used across the company was a “game changer.”
Replacing established CRM platforms at scale may prove more difficult. In a blog post earlier this year, venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) argued that while AI could transform how businesses manage customer relationships, existing CRMs are likely to remain the systems where customer records are stored, with a new generation of AI-powered tools capturing much of the value by working on top of them.
Venkatraman acknowledged that Salesforce and HubSpot are unlikely to disappear anytime soon, but noted that their entrenched positions do not guarantee they will dominate the next generation of CRM software.
“We see this as an electric-car moment for systems of record,” he said, adding that AI requires a fundamental rethink of how CRMs are built — not simply adding new features to existing platforms.
Kanthaswamy believes startups have a window of two to five years to gain ground before established CRM providers can fully adapt to AI. Rebuilding software around a fundamentally different architecture takes time, he stated, giving newer companies an opportunity to attract customers while incumbents work to overhaul their existing products.
Dreamteam also plans to expand beyond sales into other parts of the customer lifecycle, including onboarding, customer support, and upselling. The startup already has a feature called Magic Apps that allows users to create custom applications and dashboards within the CRM using natural-language instructions, without writing code.
Currently, Dreamteam employs more than 35 people, with its engineering team based in Chennai and its go-to-market operations in the United States. Kanthaswamy said the startup aims to reach eight figures in annual revenue by the end of 2027, though he declined to disclose the startup’s current revenue.

candidates.title: AI-Native CRM Dreamteam Raises $53 Million in Seed and Series A Funding
candidates.snippet: AI-Native CRM Dreamteam Raises $53 Million in Seed and Series A Funding Wowtale
candidates.text:
For more than two decades, CRMs such as Salesforce and HubSpot have depended on salespeople remembering to type in what happened on a call. When they forget, customer context disappears and the pipeline fills with stale data. Dreamteam , an AI-native CRM built on the opposite premise, said it raised $53 million from Accel, Together Fund and Premji Invest. The company described the amount as seed and Series A funding combined and did not disclose a valuation.
A CRM that fills itself from conversations
At the center of Dreamteam is what it calls the Company Brain, a running memory built from customer conversations, emails, meetings and workflows. It pulls out buyer intent, objections, competitor mentions and stakeholder dynamics. The company argues that legacy CRMs, built around structured fields and hand-coded workflows, cannot hold signals like a prospect hesitating on price or a board suddenly scrutinizing costs. It says an account that changes hands carries over the customer’s goals, objections and open commitments.
Four AI teammates work on top of that memory. Rachel is a research assistant that enriches accounts and contacts. Sally, the sales assistant, preps meetings, drafts follow-up emails and manages tasks. Raj is a RevOps partner that monitors the pipeline, flags at-risk deals and improves forecasts. Alex is a CRM administrator that configures the system from plain-language requests. The company says customers do not have to build or train their own agents.
Humans keep control. A person has to approve any outgoing email, teams set pricing rules and approval limits, and users can see where a recommendation came from and correct what the system remembers. Alongside the human interface, Dreamteam offers an API and a Model Context Protocol server so AI agents such as Claude or ChatGPT can reach the CRM. A feature called Magic Apps lets business users build apps and dashboards in natural language.
The company says more than 100 companies in 13 countries use it, and its press release puts the figure at hundreds across AI, online media, healthcare, manufacturing and consulting. Named customers include invideo, Plex and DMS Health. invideo started with a small pilot and expanded to its whole sales team, and Plex’s co-founder and chief product officer called its compatibility with existing AI tools like Claude “a game changer.” Revenue and pricing were not disclosed.
Three former Freshworks executives
The co-founders are former senior executives at Freshworks. CEO Anand Venkatraman leads sales and go-to-market, Ramesh Parthasarathy leads engineering and Senthil Kanthaswamy leads product. The company says they helped scale Freshworks from its early startup days through its IPO and have built AI applications since the GPT-2 era, scaling them to tens of thousands of businesses. When AI reasoning made it possible for software to understand context and carry out work, they decided to rebuild CRM from scratch rather than layer AI onto existing systems. Dreamteam was founded in 2025 and says it is headquartered in Sacramento, California.
Its blog post names Together Fund and Accel as leads, with Premji Invest participating. Together Fund, founded by Freshworks founder Girish Mathrubootham, is Dreamteam’s first institutional investor. Mathrubootham said the cloud wave created a generation of enterprise software leaders 25 years ago and that AI demands software rebuilt from the ground up, with CRM among the largest categories ripe for disruption. Accel partner Shekhar Kirani said each person on a team sees a different version of the customer because no central system holds the information, and that Dreamteam is building that system with AI agents. He said Accel wants to help redefine the $100 billion-plus CRM market. Premji Invest said CRMs must evolve from systems of record into systems of intelligence and action.
Dreamteam says it plans to extend beyond sales into a shared intelligence layer across the customer lifecycle, from acquisition to upsell. It did not say how it will spend the new funding.
Competitors: AI-native CRMs crowd in
Salesforce and HubSpot still dominate the market and are adding their own agent features. Dreamteam’s closest rivals are newer CRMs designed around AI from the start.
Lightfield pivoted from the AI presentation tool Tome and raised a $47 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz. Britain’s Attio raised a $52 million Series B led by GV. Day AI raised a $20 million Series A led by Sequoia in February and made its CRM platform generally available; its founder, Christopher O’Donnell, previously worked at HubSpot. Monaco , started by former Brex chief revenue officer Sam Blond, raised $35 million led by Founders Fund in February. In Europe, Brevo , which combines marketing and sales channels, raised 500 million euros and became a unicorn last December.
Dreamteam pitches two differences. It ships four prebuilt AI teammates covering research, sales, RevOps and admin, so customers do not build agents themselves. And its founders helped grow Freshworks into a public CRM and customer-support software company. But with no valuation, revenue or pricing disclosed, it is hard to tell how this round compares with its rivals’.

Bay Raises $50 Million to Stop AI Agents From Making Dangerous Decisions Inside Companies
Epil Bodra
| November 11 | Business Stories , Funding Feed
Share
Cybersecurity startup Bay has emerged from stealth with $50 million in funding , just nine months after its founding, as businesses face growing security risks from autonomous AI agents operating across corporate systems.
The company, founded in early 2026 by former Israeli intelligence and cybersecurity professionals, has developed technology designed to detect and block potentially harmful actions by AI agents, including those operating with legitimate access permissions.
The funding includes a $37 million Series A led by Battery Ventures , with participation from Micron Ventures, Microsoft’s venture capital arm M12, and Wiz CEO Assaf Rappaport. Bay also disclosed an earlier $13 million seed round backed by YL Ventures and Striker.
Cisco Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel and former Zscaler Chief Strategy Officer Manoj Apte are among the company’s private investors.
Bay was established by CEO Yuval Zacharia, Chief Product Officer Aner Morag , and Vice President of Research and Development Boris Danilovich.
The founders identified a critical security problem after one of their own AI coding agents attempted to expose a cloud environment to the public internet while completing a test.
The agent had not been compromised, nor was it acting under instructions from an attacker. Instead, it was using authorized permissions to accomplish its assigned task, potentially creating a serious security vulnerability in the process.
That experience became the foundation for Bay’s approach to AI security, which focuses on preventing dangerous actions even when an agent is functioning as intended.
Unlike traditional security systems that primarily focus on unauthorized access or malicious activity, Bay examines what an AI agent is attempting to accomplish and whether its actions could violate an organization’s security policies.
Its platform discovers AI agents operating across corporate environments and analyzes their activities within the context of an entire session, including their assigned objectives and previous actions.
Based on that information, the system can approve an action, block it, or refer it for human authorization. Bay says these decisions occur locally within milliseconds, allowing permitted operations to continue without disrupting workflows.
The technology supports AI assistants, coding agents, custom-built agents, and the tools they use across employee devices, cloud infrastructure, and software-as-a-service applications.
Bay also claims its platform can be deployed in under five minutes using existing corporate security infrastructure, without installing additional persistent endpoint agents or network proxies.
The company says its technology is already being used by dozens of enterprise customers across finance, insurance, manufacturing, media, and technology.
Wix, ClickUp, Micron, and Peloton are among its named customers. Micron is also participating in the company’s latest funding round through Micron Ventures.
Zacharia told Calcalist that Bay’s rapid fundraising was supported by early customer demand and revenue growth. She said the company generated millions in revenue during its first quarter of sales, although an exact figure was not disclosed.
“We raised a significant amount of capital, and we did so very quickly. The primary driver was the large number of customers we managed to acquire and the revenue we generated in such a short timeframe, which helped us close the funding round rapidly,” Zacharia said.
The startup currently employs approximately 35 people, primarily in Israel, and plans to expand its product development and engineering operations.
It also intends to strengthen its sales, marketing, and customer-facing teams in the United States and Europe, with Zacharia planning to relocate to the US.
Bay’s leadership brings experience from Israeli military intelligence and major cybersecurity companies.
Zacharia previously served in Unit 8200 before becoming director of research and AI at Hunters. Morag also worked in Unit 8200 and later became vice president of product at Noname Security.
Danilovich previously worked at Preempt Security and subsequently held senior engineering leadership roles at CrowdStrike, where he managed a department of approximately 90 engineers.
With its latest funding, Bay plans to accelerate product development and expand adoption among enterprises deploying autonomous AI systems.
The company’s central challenge is one that traditional access controls alone cannot necessarily resolve: an AI agent may have permission to perform an action, but that does not mean the action is safe.
As organizations give AI systems greater autonomy, Bay is positioning its technology to assess those actions before they create security problems.

Bay Emerges From Stealth With $50M After Fortune 100 Companies Used Its Platform to Triple Autonomous AI Agent Use
By James Dargan · 13 November 2026 · 5 min read
Insider Brief
Bay, an AI security platform for agentic enterprises, has emerged from stealth with $50 million in total funding, including a $37 million Series A led by Battery Ventures and a $13 million seed led by YL Ventures and Striker Venture Partners.
The Tel Aviv-based company evaluates each AI agent action in the context of the full session and decides in milliseconds whether it can proceed, deploying across devices, cloud and SaaS in under five minutes without extra endpoint agents or network proxies.
Founded less than a year ago by Yuval Zacharia, Aner Morag and Boris Danilovich, Bay already counts Micron, Peloton, ClickUp and Wix among its customers and will use the funding to expand its teams in the US and Europe.
PRESS RELEASE —  Bay , the AI security platform building the trust layer for agentic enterprises, has emerged from stealth less than a year after its founding with dozens of enterprise customers, including Micron, Peloton, ClickUp and Wix. Bay addresses a primary barrier to AI adoption by allowing autonomous agents to perform business-critical work safely while enterprises retain control and accountability at scale.
Bay has raised $50 million in total funding. The financing includes a $37 million Series A led by Battery Ventures and a previously undisclosed $13 million seed led by YL Ventures and Striker Venture Partners. Micron Ventures, M12, Microsoft’s Venture Fund and Assaf Rappaport, CEO of Wiz, also participated in the Series A.
“AI is fundamentally changing how enterprises operate, and the ability to deploy autonomous agents safely will become a critical competitive advantage,” said Andrew Byrnes, Director of Venture Capital, Micron. “We’ve seen firsthand how Bay’s technology can help accelerate AI adoption while maintaining the control and accountability required in a large enterprise. We believe that this trust layer will become essential infrastructure for the agentic era.”
Bay grew out of the same problem it now solves for customers. Its founders watched one of their coding agents try to expose a cloud environment to the internet to complete a test. The agent had not been compromised. It used legitimate permissions to pursue a legitimate goal in a dangerous way.
Bay brings AI governance and enforcement across employee devices, cloud infrastructure, and SaaS applications in under 5 minutes, without an additional persistent endpoint agent, kernel driver, or network proxy. It secures the full range of AI that enterprises are deploying through a single platform that covers multiple use cases under one set of policies. Bay combines AI discovery and posture management, session-level observability, and real-time enforcement, and connects to existing security workflows for automated remediation.
“In Bay, we saw a company we felt had a differentiated technical approach that was already winning enterprise customers at an early stage,” said Dharmesh Thakker, General Partner at Battery Ventures. “That combination gave us conviction to lead the round. We believe Bay can become a core control layer for companies putting AI agents to work at scale.”
“We evaluated a crowded field of companies addressing AI agent security, and Bay stood out because it can understand and control individual agent actions, from the endpoint to the cloud, while fitting into infrastructure enterprises already use,” said Yoav Leitersdorf, managing partner at YL Ventures. “We believe Bay can become as fundamental to enterprise AI adoption as the network firewall was to the internet era.”
Bay evaluates each proposed action in the context of the full agent session and decides locally in milliseconds whether it can proceed. Instead of requiring security teams to write and maintain rules for every new agent or tool, Bay learns from the organization’s agent activity and interprets context around each action in real time, distinguishing between activity that looks identical in isolation but carries very different risks. As teams add new agents and workflows, Bay adapts its policies and expands the work agents can safely do on their own. The platform works across the AI models, assistants, and agent frameworks an organization chooses.
“If you’re a security leader at an enterprise today, you’re likely facing one of two realities: either AI agents have already spread across your organization and it’s the Wild West, or your leadership has mandated an enterprise-wide AI rollout by the end of the year to accelerate the business,” said Yuval Zacharia, co-founder and CEO of Bay. “Either way, the challenge is the same: enabling AI adoption at scale without losing control. Bay was built to be the one platform that secures every way the enterprise uses AI, so security becomes the reason AI ships faster, not the reason it stalls.”
Zacharia founded Bay alongside CPO Aner Morag and VP of R&D Boris Danilovich. Zacharia began her career in Israeli intelligence at Unit 8200, where she led a department of 50 people before becoming the first-ever intelligence officer to transition into offensive cybersecurity and was assigned to the unit’s most elite department. Following her military service, she served as Director of Research and AI at Hunters.
Danilovich previously led a department of 90 engineers at CrowdStrike, spearheading one of the most critical components of its endpoint security platform and serving as a key leader of the company’s Israeli R&D center. Morag joined Noname Security as one of its earliest employees, rising to VP of Product and playing a key role in scaling the company.
Bay is available to enterprises today. The company will use the funding to expand its product and engineering teams and grow its sales, marketing, and customer teams in the United States and Europe.

Bay secured $50 million in funding for its enterprise AI agent security platform.

Tel Aviv-based Bay has emerged from stealth with $50 million in funding, comprising a $37 million Series A round led by Battery Ventures and a $13 million seed funding round led by YL Ventures and Striker Venture Partners.

The platform’s Enforcer component evaluates every proposed agent action in milliseconds within the context of the full session. It decides whether to allow, refer to the user, redirect based on policy, or deny the action.
Bay’s embedded AI system, Lighthouse, automatically builds and maintains policies based on the organisation’s activity history. This system protects against dangerous agent activity, whether caused by malicious prompt injection or organic agent purpose drift.
Bay’s CEO and co-founder Yuval Zacharia told SecurityWeek that effortless deployment, immediate time to value, and clear operationalisation were non-negotiable design principles. The company built a flexible, agentless architecture for deployment across an entire fleet in under five minutes.
Its patented technology retrospectively analyses 30 days of historical logs. This allows customers to see Bay’s potential value and complete a proof of value in less than 14 days. The funding will support product development, engineering team expansion, and go-to-market plans in the US and Europe.

Index Industries Raises $50 Million in Funding to Reinvent How the World Invests in Real Estate
News provided by
Index Industries
Nov 10, 2026, 12:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Index Industries is co-founded by Josh Rosenthal, formerly the President of Polychain Capital, joining as CEO, and Brian Hardecker, CEO of Longmark and formerly of Blackstone, joining as Chairman.
The round is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Galaxy Ventures, Polychain Capital, Wintermute Ventures and more.
Index Industries will launch the USHP Index, a proprietary benchmark for U.S. home prices, made investable through USHP, a liquid index product, issued by USHP Limited.
NEW YORK , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Index Industries emerges from stealth with a $50 million seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from Polychain Capital, Galaxy Ventures, Wintermute Ventures, and other institutional investors. The company is building the technology and infrastructure to transform U.S. housing into a broadly investable asset class. Its platform combines a daily-reporting index with tokenization technology and real estate and capital markets services to power third-party housing-linked investment products. USHP , based on Index Industries' U.S. Home Price Index and issued by USHP Limited (BVI), will be the first investment product built on the platform.
U.S. housing is a $55 trillion market, making it one of the largest asset classes in the U.S. Yet despite its scale, broad-based investment exposure to U.S. home prices has remained difficult to access through traditional financial products. Index Industries was founded to close that gap.
Index Industries' first offering will be the U.S. Home Price Index (USHP Index), a proprietary benchmark for U.S. home prices. Calculated daily, it integrates data from the major housing indices into a single national measure, providing a continuous and comprehensive read on home prices. The index is intended to support housing-market research, reporting, and portfolio monitoring and housing-related financial products.
Index Industries is co-founded by Josh Rosenthal, who joins as CEO following his role as President and General Partner of Polychain Capital, and Brian Hardecker, a former Principal at Blackstone and the Founder and CEO of Longmark, a leading residential real estate platform formed in 2021 that has $2 billion in assets under management. Index Industries combines two worlds of expertise to bring breakthrough tokenization technology to new real estate assets.
"Indexing is one of the most important and least celebrated innovations in modern finance. It reduces the expertise and cost barriers to investing in an entire market, which is what U.S. housing needs," said Josh Rosenthal, co-founder & CEO of Index Industries. "I've spent my career looking for industry-shaping financial technology, and Index Industries is exactly that. It has the potential to change how the world sees housing: not just as a roof over your head or something that is out of reach, but as an investable asset class."
"U.S. housing is a massive market. It accounts for roughly a quarter of the aggregate value of the U.S. economy, yet it draws far less attention because there haven't been accessible ways to take a position in it," said Brian Hardecker, co-founder and chairman of Index Industries and CEO of Longmark Group. "Housing is uniquely inflation-protected, uncorrelated to other asset classes, and has arguably been one of the most stable paths to wealth accumulation. It hasn't seen the benefits of financial innovation that other sectors have. That's beginning to change with USHP, and we're proud to play a role."
"Real estate is one of tokenization 's biggest opportunities, but bringing a $55 trillion asset class onchain requires traditional institutional infrastructure no crypto -native team has ever had. That's the gap Index Industries closes. It's rare to see two worlds of expertise converge at this caliber: traditional institutional rigor paired with scalable, secure, compliant technology that will unlock access and liquidity for the world's largest asset class. Index Industries' partnership with Longmark made leading this investment an easy decision for Lightspeed," said Justin Overdorff, Partner at Lightspeed Venture Partners.
Tokenization is a defining innovation in financial markets today, and the world's largest institutions are racing to adopt it. Index Industries applies tokenization to one of the most sought-after asset classes and is designed to create entirely new financial products that unlock access, income, and liquidity at institutional scale.
The USHP Index is expected to launch imminently. USHP Limited plans to release USHP in 2026 on Ethereum and expand to Solana in 2027. For more information, visit indexindustries.com .

Optics11: €50 Million Funding To Expand Underwater Defense And Energy Grid Sensing Technology
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:07 AM
Optics11: €50 Million Funding To Expand Underwater Defense And Energy Grid Sensing Technology
Optics11, an Amsterdam-based deep technology company developing fiber-optic sensing systems for maritime security and energy infrastructure, has secured €50 million in follow-on equity financing. The investment brings the company’s total capital raised over the past 15 months to more than €100 million and will support manufacturing expansion, international growth, and increased deployment of its sensing technologies.
The latest financing was backed by existing institutional investors FORWARD.one, Value Creation Capital, SET Ventures, and JOIN Capital, with all four participating in the new round.
The investment comes as governments, defense organizations, and infrastructure operators seek additional capabilities to protect underwater assets and strengthen electricity networks.
Optics11 develops fiber-optic sensing systems designed to detect underwater activity, identify potential security threats, and monitor conditions within critical energy infrastructure.
The company’s technology originated from research at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, where its underlying photonics and acoustics capabilities were developed before Optics11 was founded in 2011.
Its sensing approach uses light to detect small acoustic signals rather than relying on powered electronics at the measurement location.
This design enables highly sensitive monitoring while remaining passive and resistant to electromagnetic interference.
The technology has applications across maritime surveillance, subsea infrastructure protection, and electrical grid monitoring.
Expanding Maritime Defense Capabilities
Optics11 is developing products intended to strengthen underwater surveillance and anti-submarine warfare capabilities.
Its OptiBarrier system provides persistent seabed sensing designed to detect and classify underwater targets at distances of up to 100 kilometers from the shoreline.
The system is intended to provide ongoing monitoring of sensitive maritime areas and infrastructure.
The company’s OptiArray platform extends its fiber-optic sensing capabilities into a mobile towed array that can be deployed from vessels.
OptiArray supports underwater intelligence gathering, maritime surveillance, and anti-submarine warfare operations.
Earlier in 2026, the Dutch Ministry of Defence selected Optics11’s containerized OptiArray technology for the ASWINABO program, also known as Anti-Submarine Warfare In A Box.
The program aims to provide advanced underwater sensing capabilities through a wider range of maritime platforms.
These include crewed and uncrewed surface vessels, as well as certain civilian ships.
The initiative is intended to improve the Royal Netherlands Navy’s readiness and operational flexibility.
Optics11 considers the selection an important validation of its technology and a potential foundation for additional defense deployments.
The company sees increased interest in maritime sensing systems as European governments reassess their ability to monitor underwater activity and protect critical infrastructure.
Strengthening Electricity Grid Monitoring
Optics11 also applies its sensing technology to electrical infrastructure through its OptiFinder platform.
OptiFinder is designed to detect and locate partial discharge activity within high-voltage electrical equipment.
Partial discharge can be an early indication of insulation degradation and developing faults inside assets such as transformers.
Identifying these conditions before equipment failure can help infrastructure operators plan maintenance and reduce operational disruptions.
OptiFinder uses fiber-optic acoustic sensing to provide information about potential problems within high-voltage assets.
The technology is already deployed in operational environments internationally.
Electricity networks are facing increased pressure from electrification, higher power demand, and the need to improve infrastructure reliability.
Optics11 believes these developments will create additional opportunities for advanced monitoring systems capable of identifying equipment problems at an early stage.
Scaling Manufacturing And International Operations
The company plans to use its new capital to increase manufacturing capacity and expand international operations.
The investment will also support delivery of existing orders and development of relationships with government agencies, industrial companies, and infrastructure operators.
Optics11 reported growing international demand across both maritime security and energy grid applications.
Its expanding order book and commercial pipeline reflect interest in sensing technologies that provide earlier detection and more detailed information than certain conventional approaches.
The company intends to increase its ability to manufacture and deploy systems while continuing product development.
With more than €100 million invested over 15 months, Optics11 is positioning itself to expand its role in protecting maritime and electrical infrastructure.
The financing supports its transition toward broader commercial deployment as demand increases across defense and energy markets.

“This investment is a significant milestone for Optics11 and reflects the growing international demand for technology that can help protect the critical infrastructure our societies depend upon. From ASWINABO to OptiFinder, we are seeing our technology move into real-world deployment, with increasing interest from governments, operators and partners around the world.
