Arcturus Therapeutics Secures $50 Million Meiji Investment At 80% Premium
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 4:20 PM
Arcturus Therapeutics Secures $50 Million Meiji Investment At 80% Premium
Arcturus Therapeutics has expanded its collaboration with Meiji Seika Pharma through a $50 million equity investment, an additional technology license and a proposed pandemic preparedness partnership in Japan.
Meiji will purchase unregistered Arcturus securities at $20.27 per share, an 80% premium under the announced transaction terms. Its investment will represent approximately 7.9% of outstanding shares following the transaction.
The companies also signed an exclusive license covering the application of Arcturus’s ARCT-154 technology in an undisclosed therapeutic area.
Separately, a memorandum of understanding establishes principal terms for a potential collaboration and license agreement involving pandemic preparedness and response in Japan. That arrangement remains subject to a definitive agreement.
Arcturus intends to use the investment to support its cystic fibrosis program and accelerate ARCT-2601, an investigational treatment for ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency.
ARCT-2601 is the first mRNA therapeutic intended to use the company’s LUNAR 2.0 delivery platform. Its development is expected to contribute to clinical evaluation of that next-generation technology.
President and CEO Joseph Payne said the expanded relationship reflects Meiji’s confidence in the company’s capabilities and platform.
Founded in 2013 and based in San Diego, Arcturus develops mRNA medicines focused on liver and respiratory diseases.
Its technologies include lipid-mediated delivery and self-amplifying RNA. The company also developed KOSTAIVE, a self-amplifying mRNA COVID vaccine.
Other collaborations include work with Thermo Fisher Scientific, BARDA and Japanese manufacturing joint venture ARCALIS.
Meiji’s investment adds capital while extending an existing strategic relationship across development, licensing and potential public-health applications.
The company’s pipeline programs remain subject to clinical development, regulatory review and other requirements before potential commercialization.
KEY QUOTES
“We are pleased to expand our relationship with Meiji as we advance innovative mRNA medicines and seek to deliver value to patients. The investment, together with the license agreement and the pandemic preparedness MOU, reflects Meiji’s confidence in our development capabilities and the potential of our technology platform. Alongside our CF program, these proceeds will be used to accelerate development of ARCT-2601 for OTC deficiency, the first mRNA therapeutic to utilize our LUNAR 2.0 delivery platform.”
Joseph Payne, President And CEO Of Arcturus Therapeutics

candidates.title: Alta Raises $47.5 Million for Its Compliance-Focused Blockchain
candidates.snippet: Alta Raises $47.5 Million for Its Compliance-Focused Blockchain BlockTelegraph
candidates.text:
What to know
Alta announced a $47.5 million Series A led by Index Ventures.
The company is developing a blockchain with compliance features for banks and large businesses.
Airwallex is both an early backer and a channel encouraging customers to use Alta for crypto transactions.
Alta has raised $47.5 million in a Series A round to build a compliance-focused blockchain for banks and large companies. Index Ventures led the round, which Alta announced Tuesday, according to Fortune’s report .
The company is developing its own blockchain with a compliance layer that lets customers ensure processed transactions follow rules and regulations around the world. Alta is pitching the system to financial firms and large companies seeking faster money transfers with crypto.
Why Alta Is Building a Compliance-Focused Blockchain
Financial firms already have a choice of networks, including Ethereum, Solana and Avalanche. Alta chief executive Loong Wang told Fortune he believes blockchain is the best technology for transferring money, but said existing options lack privacy and compliance tools designed for banks and other large financial players. Glass office tower viewed from below beneath clouds.
Wang said Alta’s features include a tool that prevents people from sending funds at random to addresses on its blockchain. The feature addresses a practice known as an airdrop, which can require wallet holders to accept funds whether they want them or not.
“We often say we wouldn’t have built an L-1 if we didn’t have to,” Wang told Fortune. His comments describe the company’s rationale for creating another network despite the many Layer 1 blockchains already available.
Airwallex Provides a Distribution Connection
Alta previously raised $32.5 million in seed funding, backed primarily by Airwallex, the Australian fintech company competing with Stripe and others in global payments. Alta has 25 employees and offices in San Francisco and Melbourne.
Fortune reported that Wang has a personal connection with Airwallex chief executive Jack Zhang. Zhang had been skeptical of crypto, but recently acknowledged the inherent value of stablecoins for cheap and efficient money transfers.
Airwallex is also serving as a distribution channel, encouraging its global customer network to use Alta’s platform for crypto transactions. The relationship comes as Airwallex rivals build crypto infrastructure too, including Stripe and its Tempo blockchain.
“With the rise of agentic banking and programmable payments, stablecoins are becoming an important vector for settlement,” Zhang said in a statement announcing Alta’s funding round.
Investors Join Alta’s Series A
GV (Google Ventures), Blackbird Ventures, Square Peg and Capital49 also participated in the Series A. Capital49 is a venture firm established by Airwallex’s cofounders. The company did not disclose its valuation in the round.
Alta was previously known as Metal and recently rebranded. Wang founded an earlier crypto startup that he sold in 2021, then pivoted to a second startup using quantum computing to aid drug discovery before returning to crypto technology to found Alta with Catherine Porter, a former Meta executive.
The round places Alta among companies building transaction infrastructure for institutional crypto use. Banks are also exploring stablecoin settlement and digital asset infrastructure, including efforts discussed at MERGE Madrid 2026 . Other coverage has examined how banks put deposits on blockchain and plans for a shared banking network . Those initiatives provide context for the institutional market Alta is pursuing, while the company’s stated next step is to attract banks and large companies to its own network.
Frequently asked questions
How much did Alta raise in its Series A?
Alta announced a $47.5 million Series A round led by Index Ventures.
What is Alta building?
Alta is building its own blockchain with a compliance layer intended for banks and large companies. The company says its tools address privacy and compliance needs.
What does Alta's compliance layer do?
The layer lets customers ensure transactions they process are consistent with rules and regulations around the world, according to the source.
How is Airwallex connected to Alta?
Airwallex primarily backed Alta’s $32.5 million seed round and is encouraging customers in its global network to use Alta’s platform for crypto transactions.

Funding
Mosaic Raises $47M Seed to Develop Spatial Intelligence for Surgery
Published
November 10, 2026
By
Nova Jain, AI Entrepreneurship & Founders AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
Mosaic Intelligence Labs announced on November 10, 2026 that it had emerged from stealth with $47 million in seed funding to develop sensing-enabled spatial intelligence and robotic systems for surgery, initially focusing on procedures performed through the vascular system.
The San Francisco company named 8VC, Fundomo, Lingotto Innovation and Obvious Ventures among its backers. Chief executive Ileana Pirozzi and chief technology officer Alison “Ali” Kight Mackanic founded Mosaic after meeting during their doctoral studies at Stanford. Their work alongside clinicians exposed how difficult, less-invasive procedures often remain tied to knowledge held by individual operators.
“We kept returning to one question: what would it take to scale the knowledge of the very best surgeons?” Pirozzi said. “We believe that starts with making our machines aware, and turning surgical repetition into experience we can learn from.”
Starting With Endovascular Procedures
Mosaic’s initial target is endovascular care. In these procedures, physicians thread flexible wires and catheters through blood vessels to reach treatment sites. Mosaic describes blood vessels as routes to virtually every organ, yet operators have no direct line of sight inside them. They use live X-ray imaging, preoperative scans and the feel of the instruments to work out where they are and what lies ahead.
The company identifies radiation exposure and outcomes that vary with operator experience as limitations of that workflow. Interpreting the available signals can take years of practice, and much of the resulting knowledge is difficult to record or hand down. The result is a mismatch: surgical access has become less invasive, while navigation still depends heavily on the perception and judgment of the person holding the instrument.
For context, Mosaic’s website compares open surgery’s 20–30 cm incision and keyhole surgery’s 1–2 cm ports with endovascular surgery’s 2 mm needle puncture, and lists stopping strokes, clearing blocked coronary arteries, repairing aneurysms and restoring blood flow to limbs among current applications. That range helps explain why Mosaic is treating vascular navigation as a reusable capability across multiple procedures.
Giving Surgical Instruments a Learning Loop
The technical design begins by instrumenting the point where surgical tools meet anatomy. Mosaic intends to combine those sensor readings with computation that reconstructs the vascular environment from within, maintaining a three-dimensional picture of anatomy and instrument position as it changes. A robotic interface would support precise instrument control.
The learning architecture would record the environment, instrument movement and physician actions as synchronized streams. Physical models would then help the system relate what it senses to what happens when it moves. The release connects this approach to the robotics concept of a world model: a representation of an environment that helps a machine predict how its actions will change that environment.
All of these capabilities remain development goals; the announcement supplies no patient-outcome findings or clinical-performance results. The nearer objective is to assist physicians’ perception and control, while the recorded procedures are intended to become a source of cumulative learning for machines over time.
Recruiting and Longer-Term Treatment Goals
Mosaic is recruiting engineers, physicians and creatives in San Francisco. Open roles cover hardware engineering, sensing, perception, machine learning and clinical engineering, matching a technical effort that spans physical instruments, software, robotics and clinical practice.
Mosaic’s longer-term goal is to widen the treatments delivered through these vascular routes. The company says catheters can deliver drugs, energy, biologics and other therapies directly to a target site, and that more reliable navigation could expand both the range of treatments delivered through blood vessels and the settings in which clinicians can offer them.
Mosaic’s near-term product challenge and longer-term data ambition are linked: dependable navigation must work in individual procedures before those procedures can provide a useful foundation for cumulative machine learning.

Insider Brief
San Francisco startup Mount Thor raised $45 million in seed and Series A equity funding to expand cloud infrastructure providing on-demand access to Apple’s macOS operating system and silicon for AI development.
CRV and Conviction co-led the Series A, while Chad Byers and Offline Ventures co-led the seed round, with additional non-dilutive financing secured for hardware purchases.
Mount Thor plans to expand computing capacity and develop infrastructure for AI agent training, software testing, long-running autonomous tasks and inference using open-source models optimized for Apple silicon.
San Francisco startup Mount Thor has raised $45 million in seed and Series A equity funding to expand cloud infrastructure that gives AI developers on-demand access to Apple’s macOS operating system and silicon.
According to the company , CRV and Conviction co-led the Series A, while Chad Byers and Offline Ventures co-led the seed round. Other investors included CSC Leasing, Enea Capital, Long Journey Ventures and Upper90 , along with individuals associated with Cognition, Core Automation, Daytona, Meta, OpenAI, Together AI and Vercel. The company also secured an undisclosed amount of non-dilutive capital to purchase hardware.
Founded in 2026, Mount Thor develops and operates data center systems built around Apple hardware, providing computing resources for AI research, software development and running AI models.
The financing will support additional computing capacity and hiring, particularly as the company develops infrastructure for running open-source AI models on Apple silicon.
Building Infrastructure for AI Agents
Mount Thor is focused on developers of AI agents that use computers to perform tasks, including those requiring software available only on macOS, by building and managing rack-scale systems of Apple hardware to allow customers to access computing environments remotely rather than maintain their own equipment.
“Making Apple’s operating system and silicon available at datacenter-scale is a massive untapped opportunity in AI infrastructure,” said Peter Voell, Founder and CEO of Mount Thor. “Decades of investment in accessibility and human-computer interaction make macOS the best place for agents to work and for humans to hold them accountable. And with chips like the M5 Ultra, Apple silicon is becoming a high performance, more power- and cost- efficient platform for production inference.”
Mount Thor identified several uses for the infrastructure:
AI research: Creating reinforcement learning environments for computer-use models.
Agent testing: Providing secure macOS environments for developing and evaluating AI agents.
Long-running operations: Supporting agents that operate for weeks across a user’s devices using the same Apple identity.
Software development: Building, testing and simulating applications for Apple devices.
AI inference: Running open-source models optimized for Apple silicon.
Mount Thor reported deploying its first data center in less than six months and plans to increase capacity as demand grows. Its team includes people who previously developed infrastructure at Cerebras, CoreWeave, Fluidstack, Nebius, OpenAI and xAI.

The round brings Numa's total funding to $96 million. It caps a year in which Numa tripled in size, tripled its annual recurring revenue and became the AI system GM, FordDirect, BMW and Stellantis each put in front of their dealerships.
Numa has already won the hardest part of the dealership: the customer conversation. The system has handled more than 1 billion calls, texts and chats and booked more than 4 million appointments. Dealerships that run on Numa stay and grow with it. Net revenue retention has risen over the past year, and more dealerships are moving to longer agreements.
For decades, dealership software was built one task at a time. Each system kept its own record of what happened, and none of them acted on what the customer just said. The first wave of AI did not change that. It answered faster, then handed the work back to people to chase by hand.
Numa does not hand the work back. It knows not just who the customer is but what they need, and it acts on it: booking the visit, finding the right car, routing the call or flagging the customer about to leave.
"In two years, every general manager will have an AI COO," said Tasso Roumeliotis, founder and CEO of Numa. "At more than 1,500 dealerships, they already do, and it is Numa. It knows every conversation in the store, sees what needs attention and runs the work that follows. That is not another dashboard or another point tool. It is an operating system. The DMS was built to record the dealership. It was never built to run it. Numa was, and this round puts more engineers to accelerate it."

In sales, Numa for Sales, launched this month, as the first agent with Inventory Fluency. It knows every new and used vehicle on the lot down to the trim, features and miles, learns each buyer's situation and gets them in the car that fits best, even when the one they called about has sold. Every qualified lead lands in the dealership's CRM with the full conversation, so the salesperson who picks it up already knows the buyer.
On every line into the store, Operator, launched in September, is the first Precision Routing system for dealerships. It answers first, understands why each customer is calling and puts them in the right hands with that reason carried through. When the phone rings, everyone at the dealership knows the call is for them. Operator continues to climb above 95% with calls going to the right destination.
LiveCSI™ reads customer interactions as they happen and flags the ones putting satisfaction at risk while there is still time to fix them, instead of waiting for a survey to report what went wrong. In 90 days, it analyzed 50 million interactions.
Every dealership on Numa now has over 25+ natural voices to choose from, with regional accents, a new Spanish voice, sharper recognition of vehicle makes, models and VINs, and adjustable speaking speed. The voice on the line sounds like someone who works at the dealership. It comes at no added cost, with nothing for the store to set up.
Three of the largest automakers in North America have each chosen Numa. GM named Numa an iMR Approved Turnkey Vendor, and more than 240 GM dealerships run on Numa today. In those stores, reply times have dropped from 23 hours to 24 minutes, each store saves about $11,000 a month, and 86% of customers flagged as heat cases return for service within six months. FordDirect selected Numa as its strategic AI vendor, making Numa available to more than 3,000 Ford and Lincoln dealerships. Numa is also approved on Stellantis' MarketCenter, opening access to more than 2,600 dealerships in the U.S. and 440 in Canada.
The operating system for the dealership is not on its way. It is already running.

candidates.text:
TKTMJ Wins $42.4 Million Army Corps Construction Contract In Louisiana
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 10:46 AM
TKTMJ Wins $42.4 Million Army Corps Construction Contract In Louisiana
TKTMJ has received a $42.4 million Army contract for construction and site work in Metairie, Louisiana. The Natchitoches, Louisiana-based small business will provide construction access to the work site, demolition, clearing and grubbing, excavation, embankment placement, geotextile and stone installation, and turf establishment and maintenance.
The firm-fixed-price contract was competitively procured through an internet solicitation. The government received four bids.
Work will be performed in Metairie and is expected to be completed by November 15, 2027. The contract is identified as W912P8-27-C-A003.
The full $42.4 million contract amount was obligated when the award was made using fiscal 2027 civil expenses funding.
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers’ New Orleans District is the contracting activity. The district oversees flood-risk management, navigation, coastal restoration, environmental, and other civil works projects throughout southern Louisiana.
Although the announcement does not name the specific project, the listed activities indicate a substantial civil construction effort involving preparation, earthwork, ground reinforcement, stone placement, and final site stabilization.
Construction access work will allow personnel and equipment to reach the active site. Demolition, clearing, and grubbing will remove existing structures, vegetation, debris, and other obstructions before excavation begins.
Excavation and embankment placement will reshape the site in accordance with the project design. Geotextiles can separate, reinforce, filter, or stabilize soil layers, while stone is commonly used for drainage, erosion control, structural support, or surface protection.
Turf establishment and maintenance will stabilize completed areas and restore ground cover after major construction activity.
The firm-fixed-price structure establishes an agreed amount for the defined scope, placing much of the performance-cost risk on TKTMJ unless the government authorizes changes.
Because the Army Corps obligated the entire amount at award, the $42.4 million represents a funded contract rather than an ordering ceiling or value dependent on unexercised options.

NEW YORK, NY – WEBWIRE – Tuesday, November 10, 2026
Garage Founders: Alaz Sengul (CTO) and Martin Hunt (CEO)
Garage , the leading AI-powered marketplace for America�s essential equipment, today announced $41 million in Series B funding led by Invus Opportunities, along with Infinity Ventures, Initialized Capital, Y Combinator, Benchstrength, and FJ Labs. The Problem: A Trillion-Dollar Heavy Duty Equipment Market Still Running Offline
Despite representing a $1 trillion market, the process of buying and selling heavy duty assets remains fragmented, opaque, and largely offline. Local governments and essential service providers still rely on labor intensive and archaic means to manage the procurement and disposition of their most essential assets. By streamlining every step of the transaction, the platform connects local communities directly to a national market, transforming a complex, months-long process into a modern, transparent digital experience.

Equipment Warranties: Reduces buyer risk by offering comprehensive warranties on pre-owned assets.
Nationwide Market Access: Breaks down local geographic constraints by connecting municipalities to a vetted, 50-state network, with the average transaction traveling more than 1400 miles.
Integrated Financing: Custom-built financing designed specifically to navigate local government budgets, compliance standards, and municipal purchasing requirements.
Delivering Unprecedented Value to Taxpayers
Garage is currently serving over 1000 communities in all 50 states, as well as Canada. By facilitating a more efficient secondary market, Garage has saved municipalities an estimated $100M+ by facilitating the capture of higher surplus asset recovery values and assisting with the procurement of pre-owned assets to enhance fleets with limited budgets. Today a new fire truck can cost as much as $2 million while on Garage communities can acquire a high-quality used truck for approximately $150,000, a more than 90% cost reduction.

South Charleston, WV: Garage helped a community of 13,000 recoup more than $1.2 million to reinvest in their community, including cancer screenings for firefighters.

Burlington, VT: Historically sent surplus equipment to local auctions, selling for little more than scrap value. In less than a month on Garage, they sold two fire engines that brought in an extra $80k not previously in the budget.

candidates.snippet:
The British Business Bank has committed an additional £40 million to Harwood Private Capital to increase the availability of flexible financing for smaller and lower-middle-market businesses across the United Kingdom.
The post British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:09 PM
British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund
The British Business Bank has committed an additional £40 million to Harwood Private Capital to increase the availability of flexible financing for smaller and lower-middle-market businesses across the United Kingdom.
The investment supports the first closing of Harwood Private Capital UK Fund II. Commitments to the fund and its related co-investment vehicles now total approximately £120 million.
Harwood will use the capital to provide debt financing for privately held companies pursuing organic expansion, acquisitions, and shareholder transitions. The strategy gives business owners an alternative to conventional bank lending or a complete sale through an M&A transaction.
The commitment increases the British Business Bank’s total investment with Harwood to £75 million. The government-owned development bank previously committed £35 million to the manager’s inaugural HPC UK SME Fund in 2020.
Harwood specializes in flexible private-credit solutions for lower-middle-market companies. Its target borrowers include founder- and family-owned businesses that need additional growth capital but want to preserve ownership and strategic control.
The inaugural fund invested across digital technology, clean-energy supply chains, manufacturing, tourism, and other sectors. One portfolio example is Western Marinas, a Welsh marina operator that used Harwood financing to restore facilities in Wales and southwest England.
That investment supported local jobs and family-operated businesses while attracting visitors and economic activity to surrounding coastal communities. It demonstrates how private credit can finance physical assets and regional companies that may not fit the standardized requirements of traditional lenders.
The British Business Bank’s mandate is to improve access to capital for smaller companies and address financing gaps that can limit growth, productivity, and job creation. In its 2025-2026 financial year, the bank supported £9.4 billion of financing for approximately 38,000 businesses.
That total included £1.3 billion of public funding, £4.3 billion of private capital attracted through the bank’s programs, and £3.7 billion of guaranteed lending. Around 30,000 recipients had not previously received support through the institution.
Harwood Private Capital UK Fund II is intended to extend this impact by supplying customized debt structures for companies whose requirements may not be served adequately by banks or private equity investors.
KEY QUOTES:
“Many smaller businesses continue to face challenges accessing the flexible growth capital they need to scale, invest and realise their ambitions. Harwood has developed a strong track record of providing tailored financing solutions to UK SMEs, particularly those that have not been backed by private equity. Our commitment will help increase the availability of growth capital for businesses, support economic growth and create jobs throughout the UK.”
Adam Kelly, Managing Director of Debt and Regional Funds at the British Business Bank
“The British Business Bank has backed Harwood Private Capital since our first fund, and this renewed commitment reflects the strength of that partnership. Founder and family-owned businesses are the backbone of the UK economy, yet many are still underserved by traditional lenders whilst wishing to maintain ownership control. The £120m of committed capital allows us to keep providing the flexible, partnership capital these businesses need to grow, make acquisitions and manage ownership transitions on their own terms.”
Haseeb Aziz, Managing Partner at Harwood Private Capital

Promise Robotics Raises $40 Million CAD Series B to Scale the Production Infrastructure Powering Homebuilding
News provided by
Promise Robotics
Nov 17, 2026, 09:05 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Round led by White Star Capital follows a multi-year agreement with America's largest homebuilder and the launch of Promise's first U.S. facility in Phoenix.
PHOENIX , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Promise Robotics , the company bringing Physical AI to homebuilding, today announced the close of a $40 million CAD Series B funding round led by White Star Capital to expand the production infrastructure needed to scale homebuilding. The round also included participation from Horizons Ventures, Radical Ventures, Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSP Investments).
Homebuilders are under increasing pressure to expand housing production, but scaling through traditional construction methods alone is constrained by skilled labor availability and the complexity of adding production capacity market by market. Promise Robotics addresses that constraint by giving builders access to automated production capacity without requiring them to develop and operate factories themselves. The funding round will support the continued expansion of that production network across North America.
This announcement comes just weeks after Promise Robotics expanded its U.S. production network and signed a multi-year commercial agreement with D.R. Horton, America's largest homebuilder by volume. As the first major U.S. homebuilder to leverage Promise Robotics' Factory-as-a-Service® (FaaS) platform, D.R. Horton's adoption underscores growing demand for scalable, technology-driven homebuilding solutions. With production already live in Calgary and Nisku, Canada, more than 2,500 housing units under contract across three markets, and its first U.S. facility planned for Phoenix, the company is demonstrating the momentum and operating scale this new investment will help accelerate.
FaaS gives a broad range of homebuilders across geographies access to an integrated production platform that takes existing home designs and translates them into a coordinated production process spanning robotic manufacturing, factory operations, and onsite installation. Through FaaS, builders can access automated production capacity without developing and operating their own factories, helping them improve cycle times, increase capacity, and scale more predictably across communities and markets.
"Homebuilding can't scale on trade labor alone, and builders shouldn't have to become manufacturers to grow. We're building the production infrastructure the industry can scale on; a network of intelligent factories that get better with every home it helps build. This round lets us extend that network across North America," said Ramtin Attar, CEO and co-founder of Promise Robotics.
"From our very first conversations with the Promise Robotics team, it was clear nobody is building what they're building. Home construction is a massive industry that needs a new way to keep up with demand, and Promise is delivering it, giving builders automated production as a service through its technology, factories, and a business model designed to scale. Just as impressive is how well this team executes across builders, projects, and markets, with their recent multi-year agreement with D.R. Horton a powerful proof point. We're thrilled to partner with Promise as it builds what we believe can become the defining platform in its category, with a production network that grows more valuable and harder to replicate as it scales," said Sanjay Zimmermann, General Partner at White Star Capital.
Promise Robotics has taken a measured, capital-efficient approach to growth. Over the past six years, the company has strategically invested in building its proprietary technology platform, validating its business model, and achieving critical operational milestones while steadily expanding its production network into new markets, including its recent entry into Phoenix, AZ.
As housing shortages continue to impact communities across North America, Promise Robotics' automation and AI-driven manufacturing will play a critical role in increasing housing production while improving efficiency, quality and predictability throughout the construction process.

About Promise Robotics
Promise Robotics is building the production infrastructure homebuilding scales on. Its Physical AI platform turns a builder's existing designs into robotic production plans and delivers precision structural components from a growing network of intelligent factories. Through Factory-as-a-Service®, builders access production capacity as a service, paying for output rather than factories. Promise has live production in Calgary and Nisku, Alberta, and opens its first U.S. facility in Phoenix in 2027. Investors include Horizons Ventures, Radical Ventures, White Star Capital and PSP Investments. For more information, please visit www.PromiseRobotics.com .

candidates.text:
Star Holdings: Q3 Revenue Reaches $39.9 Million As Net Loss Widens To $45.1 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:50 AM
Star Holdings: Q3 Revenue Reaches $39.9 Million As Net Loss Widens To $45.1 Million
Star Holdings reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $39.9 million, up from $28.1 million a year earlier, as land development activity increased. The real estate-focused company nevertheless recorded a net loss of $45.1 million, compared with net income of $274,000 in the third quarter of 2025.
Operating lease income was $1.7 million, compared with $1.8 million a year earlier. Interest income and other operating sources contributed to the quarter, while land development revenue increased to $21 million from $1.7 million. The company recognized revenue from the sale of a land parcel during the period, with related development cost of sales reducing the transaction’s contribution.
The loss allocable to common shareholders was $45.1 million, or $3.74 per share, compared with income allocable to common shareholders of $1.8 million, or $0.14 per share, in the prior-year quarter. Results reflected the timing of property transactions, carrying costs, interest expense, and changes in the value or performance of Star’s remaining assets and investments.
For the first nine months of 2026, total revenue was $80.2 million, compared with $84.8 million a year earlier. The nine-month net loss narrowed to $18.1 million from $47.5 million, while the loss allocable to common shareholders improved to $13.9 million from $45.1 million.
Star Holdings was created to hold and realize value from a portfolio of legacy real estate assets and other investments. Its results can vary significantly between periods because land sales, loan repayments, hotel activity, and asset dispositions do not occur on a uniform schedule. Third-quarter revenue growth therefore showed progress in monetizing property, but the substantial reported loss demonstrated the continuing costs and valuation effects associated with managing the portfolio. Future performance will depend heavily on the timing and economics of additional asset sales, development activity, and resolution of remaining obligations.

candidates.title: JPYC Raises $38M in Extended Series B To Grow Yen Stablecoin Adoption
candidates.snippet: JPYC Raises $38M in Extended Series B To Grow Yen Stablecoin Adoption CoinMarketCap
candidates.text:
Japan's registered yen stablecoin issuer JPYC Inc has secured a total of 6 billion yen ($38 million) in an extended Series B funding round, drawing in a major domestic logistics firm as it moves to expand its footprint in the country's growing digital payments market.
The latest injection came from AZ-COM Maruwa, a Tokyo-listed logistics company, which committed 1 billion yen ($6.3 million) to the round. Earlier in the Series B, Metaplanet Ventures had invested 400 million yen ($2.53 million) in March.
Logistics Firm Plans Stablecoin Payroll Use
AZ-COM Maruwa, which counts Amazon Japan among its clients, said it plans to use JPYC to pay fees and salaries to roughly 2,300 business partners and individual contractors. The company reportedly sees the speed of yen-denominated stablecoin transfers as a practical solution for attracting business partners and managing driver shortages brought on by an aging workforce and stricter overtime rules. Nikkei reported the firm's plans last month.
JPYC said the round's proceeds will fund expansion of its financial and Web3 ecosystem and accelerate adoption of its yen-pegged stablecoin. The company launched last October as Japan's first registered stablecoin under the country's updated payment services rules, and has since begun piloting payments at a location of Lawson, Japan's third-largest convenience store chain.
Related Article: JPYC Stablecoin Set for 1st Large-Scale Corporate Use in Japan Logistics Deal
Traditional Banks Join Japan's Stablecoin Race
Japanese authorities have signaled support for broader stablecoin adoption, and established financial institutions have responded. SBI Group launched JPYSC in June as the country’s first trust bank-backed yen stablecoin. Three of Japan's largest banks, MUFG, SMBC, and Mizuho, are working together on a jointly issued stablecoin of their own.
AZ-COM Maruwa's investment stands out as a sign that industrial companies outside the financial sector are beginning to see yen stablecoins as practical infrastructure for supply chain payments and contractor settlement, rather than purely as a bet on digital assets.

candidates.title: Graphon Labs Raises $35M Series A to Give AI Agents Long-Term Memory
candidates.snippet: Graphon Labs Raises $35M Series A to Give AI Agents Long-Term Memory Wowtale
candidates.text:
AI models keep getting smarter, yet they still struggle to understand the videos, documents and conversations people have accumulated. A startup building memory infrastructure that preserves the structure of that data has now raised a Series A.
Graphon Labs announced a $35 million Series A on Nov. 10. RRE Ventures led the round, and according to the press release, HP, Energy Impact Partners, Hitachi Ventures and Gaia VC participated. It comes six months after the company’s seed round and brings total funding to $43.3 million. Graphon plans to use the money to expand its infrastructure for developers and enterprise customers, then extend from the cloud and on-premises deployments to consumer devices.
The seed round drew some attention in Korea. According to May reports from The Next Web and SiliconAngle, Novera Ventures led the $8.3 million seed, with Perplexity Fund, Hitachi Ventures, Gaia Ventures, Samsung Next and GS Futures also participating. The Next Web reported that GS Group is an early customer, using the technology for convenience-store traffic analysis and safety monitoring on construction sites.
The problem Graphon targets is that AI “memory” today is mostly storage. Fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) have been used to bring company knowledge into models, but when documents are cut into pieces and searched as vectors, sentences with nearly identical words and opposite meanings, such as “refund allowed” and “refund not allowed,” can land close together. A rule may be found while the fragment holding its exception is missed. The company likens it to tearing a book apart page by page, crumpling the pages and trying to find them again.
Its answer is to keep the structure. Graphon reads mixed data such as video, images, spreadsheets, recordings and markdown files and builds a detailed graph without deciding in advance which relationships will matter. It then uses a compressed representation of that graph, the “graphon,” to guide where to search. According to press reports, the graphon is a mathematical concept formalized around 2008 by UC Berkeley professors Jennifer Chayes and Christian Borgs, among others, and the two serve as technical advisers.
Developers use it much like S3: put files in a bucket and Graphon builds the structure. The website lists four APIs, Storage, Search, Answer and Research. Products are split into Graphon Enterprise, Graphon Developer and Graphon On-Device Memory for phones, laptops, cameras and wearables, and enterprise customers can choose hosted, customer-managed VPC or on-premises deployment.
The performance figures are the company’s own. Graphon says it scored 93.9% accuracy on the LoCoMo conversational memory benchmark while using 58% fewer tokens than loading the full conversation, and 90.2% accuracy with 95% token savings on ConvoMem. On ATM-Bench, which spans video, audio and text, it reported 81.7%, 5.0 percentage points ahead of the next entry on the public leaderboard. None of these numbers has been independently verified.
Disclosed customers include the San Francisco 49ers and Hitachi Rail. The 49ers are weighing it for finding sponsorship opportunities and supporting staff work, while Hitachi Rail is evaluating its potential to surface contextual knowledge in industrial settings and improve AI reasoning. RRE Ventures’ Raju Rishi pointed to the fact that models can reason and agents can act, yet neither improves without accumulating knowledge, as the reason for investing.
The company is led by CEO Arbaaz Khan , who said in the company blog that working as an applied scientist on an Amazon customer service team made him feel the gap between a plausible answer and a correct one. He founded the company with Clark, with whom he had researched graph-based techniques since their PhD days to help robots remember where they had been and explore unfamiliar environments. May reports named Clark Zhang as chief technology officer and Deepak Mishra as chief operating officer. The company says its team includes engineers and researchers from Amazon, Meta, Google, Apple and NVIDIA.
Several startups are already competing in the agent memory layer. Mem0 lets developers add persistent memory to AI with a few lines of code and has raised $24 million across its seed and Series A. Supermemory , founded by a 19-year-old, raised a $3 million seed for a memory engine that analyzes documents, chats and emails. Memories.ai focuses on video memory, processing up to 10 million hours of footage, and raised an $8 million seed with Samsung Next participating. Letta , backed by Felicis, is also named as a rival. While those companies lean toward particular kinds of data such as conversation logs or video, Graphon pitches weaving video, documents and spreadsheets into a single graph.

candidates.text:
Coframe: $35 Million Funding To Expand Autonomous AI Website And Advertising Optimization Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 3:28 PM
Coframe: $35 Million Funding To Expand Autonomous AI Website And Advertising Optimization Platform
Coframe, an artificial intelligence company developing self-optimizing digital experiences, has raised $35 million in total funding, including a $25 million Series A round co-led by Khosla Ventures and Hanabi Capital. The investment will support development of the company’s autonomous AI platform, which continuously generates, tests, and improves websites, landing pages, and advertising campaigns. The financing also included participation from executives and technology leaders associated with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind.
Coframe is developing what founder and CEO Josh Payne describes as the “living internet,” a model in which websites and other digital interfaces adapt continuously based on user interactions and business objectives.
Traditional websites generally display predetermined content and require development teams to make changes through scheduled design, engineering, and marketing projects.
Coframe’s platform is designed to automate much of that process by generating new content and design variations, testing their performance, and deploying improvements.
The company uses a specialized transformer model trained on user behavior alongside a team of AI agents responsible for different aspects of the optimization process.
Those agents perform functions resembling a strategist, designer, software engineer, quality assurance specialist, and data scientist.
Together, they can generate and evaluate hundreds of website or advertising variations within minutes.
The technology analyzes how visitors interact with digital experiences and uses those results to improve future versions.
Coframe says the platform can personalize content for different visitors while continuously adjusting interfaces to support conversion and engagement objectives.
The company reports that its technology has generated more than $300 million in incremental revenue for customers.
Its customer base includes Dropbox, Boston Consulting Group, Block, Backcountry, Sur La Table, and other businesses.
According to Coframe, customers have experienced conversion rate increases of 158% at Dropbox, 410% at Replit, and 60% at Cash App.
The company also reported that a Fortune 500 customer achieved a 70% increase in conversion within 30 days of signing its contract.
Across its customer base, Coframe says conversion rates have improved by more than 20% on average.
These performance figures are company-reported results and may vary across different implementations and customer environments.
At Dropbox, Coframe said an experiment that previously required approximately four weeks of engineering, design, and quality assurance work was created and deployed in 30 minutes.
The platform has also reported a 39% experiment success rate across thousands of tested variations.
Coframe says this represents more than three times the industry average, while customers have increased their experimentation frequency by tenfold or more.
Beyond website and advertising optimization, Coframe is developing capabilities for applications, email, and other digital experiences.
The company is also preparing for an internet in which AI agents increasingly perform research, product comparisons, and purchases on behalf of users.
Coframe announced a collaboration with OpenAI involving its ChatGPT advertising offering.
The collaboration is intended to help customers optimize advertisements and landing pages as a connected experience.
It builds on an earlier partnership focused on training a specialized model to generate brand-aligned code and creative assets.
Coframe is also incorporating AI agent considerations into the websites it builds.
Payne founded Coframe in 2023 after studying Mathematics and Computer Science at Stanford University.
He previously co-founded Autograph with Tom Brady, a business that reached a valuation exceeding $2 billion.
Payne also developed GPT-Migrate, an early autonomous coding agent.
Coframe has expanded its leadership through acquisitions of companies founded by two former Optimizely executives.
Bo Mohazzabi now serves as Vice President of Go-to-Market, while Steven Ebin is General Manager of Revenue Optimization.
The new financing will support Coframe’s efforts to develop more sophisticated AI systems for digital experience creation and optimization.
By combining autonomous software development, design, analytics, and personalization, Coframe aims to reduce the time required to improve digital experiences while helping businesses increase conversion rates and revenue.
KEY QUOTES:
“We’re building an internet that improves itself. A digital experience should understand what it is trying to accomplish, adapt to the person interacting with it and learn from every result. Instead of waiting months for the next redesign, companies should have websites and applications that get better every day.”
Josh Payne, Founder And CEO Of Coframe
“For decades, the web has been frozen in place, showing every visitor essentially the same page. Coframe is building the living internet, where two people can visit the same website and have completely different experiences, personalized to who they are and what they need. These interfaces continuously learn and improve themselves. This is a huge leap beyond traditional A/B testing and the next iteration of the internet.”
Vinod Khosla, Founder Of Khosla Ventures
“The way most companies build and manage their user interfaces today is wrong, and in a year or two it will be obvious why that is. User interfaces should improve themselves, and be personalized to every user.”
Pavlo Razumovskyi, Co-Founder And Vice President Of Engineering At Coframe

Connie Health: $35 Million Credit Facility From Rivonia Road Capital Expandable To $100 Million For Medicare Brokerage Growth
Connie Health, a technology-enabled Medicare insurance brokerage, has secured a $35 million asset-backed revolving credit facility from Rivonia Road Capital, with the potential to expand the financing commitment to $100 million. The facility will support the Boston-based company’s national expansion through organic growth and acquisitions as it increases the reach of its AI-powered insurance distribution platform.
The financing is backed by Connie Health’s existing Medicare insurance book of business and is designed to provide scalable capital for expanding its network of licensed insurance agents.
Connie plans to use the facility to support the origination of new insurance policies and strategic acquisitions of businesses that complement its existing operations.
The arrangement represents an additional source of financing beyond the approximately $85 million in equity capital Connie has raised since its founding.
The company’s most recent equity financing was a Series B round completed in early 2025 and led by HealthQuest Capital, with participation from Khosla Ventures, aMoon, and Pitango.
Expanding A Technology-Enabled Medicare Brokerage
Founded in 2019 by Oded Eran, David Luna, and Michael Scopa, Connie Health operates an insurance brokerage focused on helping Medicare beneficiaries evaluate and enroll in appropriate coverage.
The company’s offerings include Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement, and Medicare Prescription Drug Plans.
Connie combines a network of hundreds of local licensed insurance agents with a centralized technology platform designed to manage insurance distribution and customer service operations.
Under its operating model, customers are connected with a dedicated local agent who can help explain available coverage options, assist with enrollment, and provide support after a policy becomes effective.
The company believes maintaining these personal relationships can help beneficiaries navigate the complexity of Medicare coverage.
Its technology platform supports agents by automating and centralizing administrative activities.
These include lead generation, compliance management, back-office operations, and post-enrollment servicing.
By handling these functions through a common technology infrastructure, Connie aims to allow agents to spend more time assisting customers.
The platform incorporates AI capabilities intended to improve efficiency across insurance distribution and servicing.
The combination of local agent relationships and centralized technology is central to Connie’s growth strategy.
Using Asset-Backed Financing To Support Expansion
The $35 million facility provides Connie with access to revolving capital supported by its existing Medicare business.
Asset-backed revolving credit facilities allow eligible companies to borrow against specified assets or contractual cash flows, subject to applicable financing terms.
For insurance distribution businesses, existing policy portfolios and associated economic interests can provide a basis for structured lending arrangements.
Connie plans to use the facility to support the acquisition of new customers and expand its business through acquisitions.
The potential increase to $100 million provides room for additional borrowing capacity as the company’s financing needs evolve, although expansion is not automatic.
Management views acquisitions as an important component of its national growth strategy.
The company intends to combine acquired operations with its existing technology platform and service infrastructure.
Its goal is to expand the number of beneficiaries served while maintaining personal relationships between customers and their insurance agents.
Connie’s leadership emphasized that customer retention is an important characteristic of its business model.
The company believes its focus on long-term agent relationships supports ongoing engagement and service quality.

Rivonia Road Capital is a Los Angeles-based private capital manager focused on asset-backed financing for nonbank financial services businesses.
Founded in 2017, the firm provides customized financing solutions to specialty lenders, financial technology companies, and other businesses operating across consumer, commercial, and real estate finance.
Its investment strategy combines institutional lending experience with expertise in financing businesses whose assets or cash flows require specialized structures.
The transaction with Connie expands Rivonia’s exposure to insurance distribution.
Rivonia believes Connie’s combination of local insurance expertise and centralized technology creates opportunities for continued growth.
The capital manager also highlighted Connie’s leadership experience and approach to managing acquisitions.
For Connie, the financing provides another tool for executing its expansion plans while continuing to invest in its agent network and technology infrastructure.
The company intends to maintain its focus on personalized Medicare guidance as its operations expand nationally.
With $35 million in committed asset-backed financing and the potential for capacity to increase to $100 million, Connie Health is strengthening its financial resources for organic policy growth and strategic acquisitions.

candidates.snippet: Orakl Oncology Raises $34M Series A to Expand AI Cancer Drug Prediction Unite.AI
candidates.text:
Funding
Orakl Oncology Raises $34M Series A to Expand AI Cancer Drug Prediction
Published
November 12, 2026
By
Evan Mercer, AI Startups & Venture Capital AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
Norrsken VC announced on November 12, 2026 that it co-led Orakl Oncology’s oversubscribed $34 million Series A alongside Singular, bringing the AI drug-development company’s total funding to $50 million.
Orakl plans to expand its dataset and AI research team, increase data generation fivefold and move beyond colorectal and pancreatic cancers into lung and gastric cancers. The proceeds are also intended to establish US and UK teams, deploy predictions across more than 10 drug programs and discover and validate drug co-targets from patient biology and experimental screens.
New investors InfraVia, Serena, the Patient Autonome Fund managed by Bpifrance, teampact.ventures and Plug and Play joined the round, alongside existing backers Verve Ventures, Speedinvest and HCVC.
Patient-Derived Data and AI
Founded in 2023 as a spin-out of Gustave Roussy, Orakl grows patient-derived tumor organoids, which are laboratory models of individual patients’ cancers, and screens them against drugs. Its platform overview describes results enriched with genomic, transcriptomic and phenotypic data and anchored to longitudinal clinical histories, creating a multimodal dataset for its predictive systems.
Orakl’s biopharma products are divided between O-Predict and O-Target. O-Predict is designed to anticipate trial endpoints including tumor response, progression-free survival and overall survival, identify biomarkers that distinguish likely responders, assess drug combinations and compare benefit-risk profiles. O-Target focuses on therapeutic-target discovery.
Norrsken calls the resulting patient cohorts virtual cancer patients . The drug-response measurements must be generated through patient samples, laboratory infrastructure and hospital partnerships rather than assembled from existing databases. Every experiment adds proprietary data connecting patient biology, clinical information and observed drug responses.
What the SCOPE Preprint Shows
Orakl reports 90% accuracy for prospective predictions of individual patient responses across more than 30 clinical trials. A separate April 2026 preprint co-authored by Orakl staff provides detailed arm-level results for SCOPE, the Screening-to-Clinical Outcome Prediction Engine. It is marked as early-stage research that may not yet have been peer reviewed.
SCOPE was trained on 54 treatment lines from 52 patients with metastatic colorectal or pancreatic cancer, using matched clinical data and organoid screens covering nine compounds. To predict trial outcomes, it generated synthetic patient profiles from published eligibility criteria and matched them to a biobank of 81 patient-derived organoid lines.
External validation covered 32 arms from 23 published trials. The authors report an R² of 0.85 and a mean absolute error of 0.82 months for predicted median progression-free survival, the time patients live without disease progression. For objective response rate—the share of patients with a measured tumor response—R² was 0.71 and mean absolute error was 7.3 percentage points. Combining organoid and clinical data significantly outperformed either data type alone.
SCOPE also selected the superior treatment arm in seven of eight head-to-head comparisons. The preprint describes a prospective application to daraxonrasib before Phase III data became available, in which the platform predicted superiority over standard chemotherapy in KRAS-mutant metastatic pancreatic cancer.
Commercial Pipeline and Expansion
Just over a year after commercial launch, Norrsken reports that 18 of the world’s 20 largest pharmaceutical companies are in Orakl’s commercial pipeline. The figure covers pipeline participation rather than signed customers; the first pharmaceutical engagements have become multi-year collaborations. More than 15 additional cancer centers across Europe, North America and Asia are in contract negotiations.
Orakl has more than 40 employees, 30% of whom hold PhDs. Its co-founders are CEO Fanny Jaulin, CTO Gustave Ronteix and COO Diane-Laure Pagès, whose backgrounds span cancer biology, AI, data science, oncology and hospital partnerships.
The next phase will test whether Orakl can extend that patient-derived data model into additional cancers while converting its broad pharmaceutical pipeline into more multi-year drug-development collaborations.

candidates.text:
Orakl Oncology: $34 Million Series A Funding Co-Led By Norrsken VC And Singular To Expand AI-Powered Cancer Drug Discovery
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:56 AM
Orakl Oncology: $34 Million Series A Funding Co-Led By Norrsken VC And Singular To Expand AI-Powered Cancer Drug Discovery
Orakl Oncology, an artificial intelligence-driven biotechnology company developing technologies to improve the prediction of cancer drug responses, has raised $34 million in Series A funding co-led by Norrsken VC and Singular. The financing will support the company’s continued expansion, international hospital partnerships, and development of its AI platform, which combines patient-derived tumor samples, clinical information, and experimental biological data to advance oncology drug research.
The financing was announced by Diane-Laure Pagès, Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer of Orakl Oncology, who highlighted the company’s growing network of cancer research partners and expansion plans. The company was founded in 2023 by Pagès, Fanny Jaulin, Ph.D., and Gustave Ronteix.
Orakl originated at Gustave Roussy, the French cancer research and treatment institution where Pagès completed her doctoral studies.
Since its founding, the company has expanded from three co-founders to a team of more than 40 scientists, engineers, AI researchers, and business professionals.
Approximately 30% of its employees hold doctoral degrees.
Orakl plans to establish additional teams in the United States and United Kingdom as it expands its international research and commercial operations.
Building AI Models Around Patient-Derived Cancer Biology
Orakl Oncology is developing an AI platform designed to improve the predictability of responses to cancer treatments.
A central component of its strategy involves generating and analyzing biological information derived from patient tumors.
Cancer treatment responses can vary significantly between patients, even when they have cancers classified within the same disease category.
These differences create challenges for pharmaceutical researchers seeking to identify which experimental medicines are most likely to demonstrate beneficial effects.
Orakl is addressing this problem by combining AI with experimentally generated biological data and associated clinical information.
The company believes training AI systems on information closely connected to actual patient biology can support more relevant drug development research.
Its technology is intended to help researchers understand relationships between tumor characteristics and responses to potential treatments.
Rather than relying exclusively on publicly available datasets, Orakl is building proprietary biological information through its research infrastructure and hospital collaborations.
This approach is designed to provide a foundation for developing AI models focused on oncology drug response prediction.
Expanding International Hospital Partnerships
Orakl has established a network of hospital partnerships supporting access to patient tumor samples and related clinical information.
The company signed five hospital partnerships during 2026.
It also expects more than 15 additional cancer centers across Europe, North America, and Asia to join its network.
These relationships are an important component of Orakl’s approach to developing its AI platform.
Participating hospitals provide research-ready tumor samples and clinical information that can be analyzed alongside laboratory-generated data.
The company says its research infrastructure can generate up to 200 gigabytes of information per patient across seven matched data modalities.
Combining multiple types of biological and clinical information can help researchers investigate relationships that may not be apparent from individual datasets.
Orakl believes its international hospital network provides access to a broader range of cancer biology and research material.
The company also sees the combination of hospital relationships, laboratory infrastructure, proprietary datasets, and AI technology as an important differentiator.
Combining Laboratory Research And Artificial Intelligence
Orakl’s platform brings together experimental biology and computational analysis.
Laboratory research provides biological observations that can be used to investigate how tumors respond to different treatment approaches.
AI systems can analyze information from these experiments alongside associated clinical and patient-derived data.
The objective is to identify patterns that could help researchers better understand drug responses and prioritize further investigation.
This approach may be useful in earlier stages of oncology drug development, when researchers are evaluating potential treatments and identifying promising therapeutic candidates.
However, Orakl’s technology remains focused on drug development research rather than providing individualized clinical treatment recommendations.
In a response to a question on LinkedIn, Pagès clarified that the company’s technology is not yet ready to be used in the clinic for individual patients.
She indicated that its current applications are focused on earlier stages of drug development.
That distinction is important because research tools designed to improve drug discovery require additional validation before they can be used to guide individual patient care.
Growing From Three Founders To More Than 40 Employees
Orakl has expanded its organization significantly since launching in 2023.
The company began with three co-founders and now employs more than 40 people across scientific and business functions.
Its workforce includes biologists, software engineers, AI researchers, and other specialists.
Approximately 30% of employees have Ph.D. qualifications, reflecting the company’s emphasis on scientific research.
Pagès highlighted the contributions of the company’s employees in reaching its latest financing milestone.
Orakl intends to continue recruiting as it expands its operatio

candidates.text:
Southland Holdings: $34 Million Tunnel Project And New Data Center Contracts Awarded
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 8:55 PM
Southland Holdings: $34 Million Tunnel Project And New Data Center Contracts Awarded
Southland Holdings has secured a $34 million tunnel construction project in the Southwest along with additional contracts supporting data center construction in the Mid-Atlantic and Southwest. The awards expand activity across the company’s civil infrastructure business as demand continues for specialized construction services supporting transportation and digital infrastructure.
Two Southland subsidiaries within its Civil segment will perform the newly awarded work.
Southland Contracting received the $34 million tunnel project, which includes the design and installation of approximately 5,800 linear feet of liner-plate crossings.
The project scope also includes associated shafts, shoring, and grouting work.
The award adds to Southland’s tunnel construction operations, which form part of its broader infrastructure services business.
Separately, Oscar Renda Contracting secured a master service agreement to provide labor and equipment at a data center site in the Mid-Atlantic.
The subsidiary also received two contracts, including another master service agreement, for work at a data center location in the Southwest.
The data center agreements will provide construction-related labor and equipment services as directed by the customer.
Southland has not disclosed a final contract value for the data center work. The amount will depend on the actual quantities of services and equipment required during project execution.
The company also clarified that the data center agreements are project-specific and are not recurring contracts.
The awards provide Southland with additional exposure to the data center construction market, where infrastructure development requires specialized construction capabilities and supporting services.
Data centers depend on extensive physical infrastructure, including power systems, cooling equipment, utility connections, and supporting facilities. Construction activity in the sector creates opportunities for contractors involved in site preparation, civil engineering, and related infrastructure work.
Southland operates across several infrastructure markets, including bridges, tunneling, transportation, communications, marine construction, steel structures, water and wastewater treatment, and water pipelines.
Its subsidiaries provide specialized construction services for public and private sector projects throughout North America and internationally.
The company traces its roots to 1900 and is headquartered in Grapevine, Texas.
The latest awards reinforce the company’s participation in two infrastructure markets receiving substantial investment: underground transportation and utility infrastructure, and data center development.
The $34 million tunnel project provides a defined contract value, while the additional data center agreements create opportunities for further project revenue based on customer-directed work.
Southland did not provide project completion schedules or anticipated revenue recognition timelines for the new awards.

candidates.text:
Zus Health: $33 Million Series B To Expand Connected Healthcare And AI Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 12:46 PM
Zus Health: $33 Million Series B To Expand Connected Healthcare And AI Platform
Zus Health has raised $33 million in Series B funding to expand its intelligent patient record platform, national healthcare data network, and artificial intelligence-powered clinical workflows. Drive Capital led the round, with participation from Sanofi Ventures, HealthX Ventures, Alumni Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, F-Prime, Maverick Ventures, and JAZZ Venture Partners. The financing brings the company’s total capital raised to more than $100 million.
Founded in 2021, Zus is developing infrastructure that combines fragmented clinical information into a continuously updated patient record. Its technology is designed to give healthcare providers and applications access to more complete and actionable patient information without requiring each organization to build its own connectivity network.
The Zus Aggregated Profile creates a longitudinal patient record from information across electronic health record networks, pharmacies, laboratories, care-event notifications, and other clinical sources. An intelligence layer uses AI to organize that information and make it available through clinical and administrative workflows.
Zus supports pre-visit preparation, care transitions, risk adjustment, quality-gap closure, and population health management. Its Generated Patient Summaries transform fragmented records into concise information that clinicians and care teams can use during treatment.
The company’s national network supported more than 110 million transactions during August. Its AI-native clinical platform generated 39 million evidence citations during 2026 through the announcement date.
Zus also applied to become a Qualified Health Information Network under the Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement. Its candidacy and HITRUST certification support its effort to participate in secure nationwide health information exchange.
The funding will be used to improve clinical intelligence, expand national data connectivity, increase record freshness, and support additional workflows across value-based and specialty care.
KEY QUOTES:
“The story of electronic medical records doesn’t end with the silos we have today. We’ve spent decades digitizing healthcare, but the information still doesn’t move with the patient. We’re building a networked medical record that changes that—connecting information across the healthcare system and making it available to the people and applications that need it. And now, with AI, we have an extraordinary opportunity to build workflows that actually make delivering care easier, faster, and more effective.”
Jonathan Bush, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Zus Health
“We believe healthcare is entering a new era in which AI can fundamentally change how care is delivered, but that transformation depends on having reliable, connected patient information. Zus has built the foundation to address that challenge at scale. Its combination of technology, market opportunity, and leadership gives us conviction in the company’s ability to help shape the next generation of healthcare.”
Molly Bonakdarpour, General Partner at Drive Capital

The latest funding brings Zus Health's total capital raised to more than $100 million. The company will use the investment to advance its intelligent patient record platform, expand its nationwide healthcare data network and develop AI-powered clinical workflows.
Zus Health, the health technology company founded by Jonathan Bush, has raised $33 million in Series B funding to expand its healthcare data infrastructure and develop AI-powered clinical workflows. The round was led by Drive Capital, with participation from Sanofi Ventures, HealthX Ventures, Alumni Ventures and existing investors Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), F-Prime, Maverick Ventures and JAZZ Venture Partners.
The latest funding brings Zus Health's total capital raised to more than $100 million. The company will use the investment to advance its intelligent patient record platform, expand its nationwide healthcare data network and develop AI-powered clinical workflows.
Founded in 2021, Zus Health has built an API-first, FHIR-native medical record platform designed to consolidate fragmented patient information into a continuously updated longitudinal health record. Its platform connects data from EHR networks, pharmacies, laboratories, care event notifications and other clinical sources, making patient information accessible through APIs, standalone applications, embedded components and direct EHR integrations.
The company's Zus Aggregated Profile (ZAP) combines fragmented clinical information into a unified patient record, supported by AI-powered clinical intelligence. The platform is designed to help healthcare organizations access a more complete view of patients without building their own data connectivity infrastructure.
According to Bush, the company has developed its platform in three layers: a nationwide patient record, a data network that continuously feeds information into the record, and AI-enabled workflows that automate care-related tasks.
"Electronic health record systems (EHRs) succeeded at digitizing healthcare but failed to make patient information portable across organizations," Bush, founder and CEO of Zus Health, told Fierce Healthcare.
The company currently works with value-based care organizations, digital health companies, provider organizations, and diagnostics and precision medicine companies. Its solutions support pre-visit preparation, transitions of care, risk adjustment, quality gap closure and population health management.
Zus reported that its nationwide network supported more than 110 million networked transactions in August, while its AI-native clinical platform generated 39 million evidence citations year-to-date across its solutions.
The company is also seeing growth in specialty care, particularly oncology, where patient records are often distributed across multiple providers. Its aggregated patient data is being used to support treatment eligibility reviews, clinical trial criteria assessments and genetic testing, reducing the manual effort involved in reviewing fragmented records.
"We believe healthcare is entering a new era in which AI can fundamentally change how care is delivered, but that transformation depends on having reliable, connected patient information," said Molly Bonakdarpour, general partner at Drive Capital, in a statement.
With the new funding, Zus plans to expand its data network connectivity and AI-powered clinical intelligence capabilities. It also aims to develop additional workflows for population health and care management, value-based care and specialty care.

candidates.text:
Cloud Security
Dreeze Emerges From Stealth With $33M to Rebuild Cloud Apps After Cyberattacks
Created by Zerto and Kashya veterans, the startup has launched a platform designed to recover whole cloud applications.
By
SecurityWeek News
|
November 11, 2026 (6:16 AM ET)
Flipboard
Reddit
Whatsapp
Whatsapp
Email
Cloud application recovery startup Dreeze announced on Tuesday that it raised $33 million in a seed funding round as it emerged from stealth mode with a platform built to bring back whole cloud applications instead of only the data behind them.
The round was led by Norwest and Bessemer Venture Partners, with Claltech also investing.
Dreeze , whose staff is split between Israel and the United States, said the money will go toward product development, bigger sales and marketing teams, and getting its platform into more enterprises.
The company was formed in 2025 by Avi Raichel and brothers Ziv and Oded Kedem. The three previously worked together at Zerto, which HPE acquired , and Kashya.
Dreeze’s argument is that getting data back after an incident is not the same as getting an application running again. A cyberattack or a mistake by an AI agent can leave an organization with its data intact but without the configurations, secrets, infrastructure and connections the application needs.
Its platform, named Application Revival, scans the customer’s cloud environment on an ongoing basis, works out which resources and dependencies belong to which application, and generates a recovery plan from the live environment. Backups of data and configurations are stored with those recovery plans in an immutable, isolated vault under the customer’s control.
Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.
In a recovery scenario, Application Revival automatically reconstructs the application as a whole. Customers can also run recovery tests in an isolated account, with no impact on production.
“Companies have spent years getting better at backing up data, but getting the data back doesn’t mean the business is back,” said Ziv Kedem, the company’s CEO. “With cyber threats increasing and AI introducing new risks, enterprises need to assume that critical applications will go down.”
“We started Dreeze because recovery needs to go further. Our goal is to make Application Revival the new standard, so companies know they have a proven path to bring their applications back when something goes wrong,” he added.
The AWS version of the platform is generally available. Support for Microsoft Azure is in early access, with general availability expected in early 2027.
