candidates.title: With $23M in funding, Luminal is the latest startup to put Nvidia's CUDA moat in its crosshairs
candidates.snippet: With $23M in funding, Luminal is the latest startup to put Nvidia's CUDA moat in its crosshairs SiliconANGLE
candidates.text:
UPDATED 10:00 EST / NOVEMBER 12 2026
INFRA
With $23M in funding, Luminal is the latest startup to put Nvidia’s CUDA moat in its crosshairs
by Mike Wheatley
Luminal AI Inc. has outlined a plan to tear down Nvidia Corp.’s formidable software moat in the artificial intelligence chip industry after raising $23 million in early-stage funding.
Today’s Series A round was led by Standard Capital and saw participation from existing investors such as Y Combinator, SagaVC, Liquid 2 and Felicis, bringing Luminal’s total amount raised to date to more than $28 million. It comes about a year after the startup raised $5.3 million in seed funding.
Everybody knows about Nvidia these days. The chipmaker has ridden the generative AI wave to a staggering $5 trillion market valuation, surpassing rivals such as Apple Inc., Alphabet Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. to become the most valuable publicly traded company in the world. But anyone who assumes that it’s solely Nvidia’s graphics processing units that set it apart would be mistaken, for the real reason for its dominance of the AI computing industry is not just silicon, but software.
For almost two decades, Nvidia’s proprietary Compute Unified Device Architecture or CUDA software framework has been the real differentiator, serving as a virtually impenetrable barrier that prevents rivals such as Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Google LLC and Amazon Web Services Inc. from stripping away its market lead. Though those rivals have developed some very powerful GPUs and custom application-specific integrated circuits for running AI workloads at lower costs than Nvidia’s hardware, they haven’t been able to match the scale of Nvidia’s software ecosystem.
Virtually every major AI framework, including TensorFlow and PyTorch, has been built natively on Nvidia’s CUDA software, enabling developers to run their AI models on Nvidia’s GPUs without any modifications. But to run their models on alternative chips, developers need to rewrite much of the underlying code, which is challenging and time-consuming work. That’s why the vast majority of AI workloads still run on Nvidia’s chips.
Many developers don’t want to be paying the exorbitant fees needed to rent Nvidia’s GPUs or purchase them outright, but they also don’t want to spend months at a time fine-tuning their codebases to get their AI models to run optimally on alternative hardware, and it’s this challenge that Luminal intends to solve for them.
The startup’s solution is a two-pronged architecture platform that consists of its proprietary search compiler and a fully managed inference cloud that combine to eliminate the hassles of bringing AI workloads onto different chips.
Co-founder and Chief Executive Joe Fioti told SiliconANGLE that the compiler works by systematically exploring different ways of running neural networks on the target chip in order to come up with the most optimal path. It benchmarks each variation until it finds the best possible solution, and then it automatically generates the code developers need.
Once the code is ready, it caches the implementation so it can be reused across recurring inference workloads. In this way, it allows developers to run their AI applications across heterogeneous chip architectures with minimal fuss, Fioti said.
“We started out building in the open on GitHub as AI adoption took off, and quickly saw how much demand there was for a more efficient way to run AI models across different hardware,” Fioti said of the company’s origins.
Luminal’s compiler and inference cloud are designed primarily for running high-throughput, continuous-uptime AI applications that demand massively scalable inference. Think applications such as AI coding tools, automated image generation engines, AI video generators and real-time voice agents.
“The cost of running AI shouldn’t limit who gets to build it,” Fioti said. “We’re building the infrastructure to make high-performance inference more accessible, giving developers more choice beyond Nvidia’s ecosystem without forcing them to compromise on speed or cost.”
Luminal launched its compiler and public cloud-based inference infrastructure just four months ago and adoption is growing rapidly. It’s already processing more than 45 trillion tokens per month – a number that’s roughly equivalent to 10% of the total tokens consumed so far by Together AI Inc., an $8 billion-valued infrastructure unicorn that has been serving the market for more than four years already. The startup has established a strong partnership with AWS, and runs a significant amount of its workloads on that company’s Tranium processors.
Going forward, Luminal’s plans include expanding its engineering team, scaling its go-to-market operations and optimizing its compiler and inference infrastructure to support more chip hardware and AI models.
Standard Capital’s Dalton Caldwell said he’s betting on Luminal because AI inference is the fastest-growing market in the world. “We backed it because of its deep technical expertise and its demonstrated proof that it can squeeze fantastic performance out of heterogeneous hardware,” he said. “Luminal’s ability to get the most out of GPUs that have already been purchased … is incredibly high leverage.”
Though Luminal has had a promising start, it’s certainly not the only company trying to break Nvidia’s CUDA stranglehold on the AI industry. Both Google and AWS have their own things going on, notably launching alternative AI frameworks to PyTorch that make it easier for developers to create AI models and applications that can run on their native processors.
Luminal also faces competition from startups such as Spectral Compute Ltd. , which offers a programming toolkit and compiler that enables CUDA-based code to run natively on any AI-accelerated chip. There are also open-source efforts such as the UXL Foundation’s OneAPI , which converts CUDA code into software that can easily run on any silicon.

Melbourne adtech Vudoo has raised $22 million in a Series B as it looks to scale in the US
The round was led by US fund Blue Sky Capital, supported by several existing family office investors.
The funds will go on expanding its overseas sales operations and developing its commerce technology.
Vudoo has hired two executives to lead its North American push as it looks to get more retailers selling directly through ads and videos.
Vudoo was founded in 2017 by Nick Morgan and Andrew Spalding, who conceived the interactive videos idea while chatting in a Singapore bar. One of its earliest checkouts appeared in a 2022 Vogue Australia campaign with News Corp Australia for Moët & Chandon. Viewers watching model Victoria Lee put together a birthday celebration could buy a personalised bottle of champagne inside the video, then continue watching

The post Hardwick Tactical Receives Maximum $20.2 Million DLA Air Force Jacket Contract appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Hardwick Tactical Receives Maximum $20.2 Million DLA Air Force Jacket Contract
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:04 AM
Hardwick Tactical Receives Maximum $20.2 Million DLA Air Force Jacket Contract
Hardwick Tactical has received a fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract with a maximum value of approximately $20.2 million to produce flame-resistant intermediate-weather jackets for the Air Force.
The Mayaguez, Puerto Rico-based small business will manufacture intermediate weather outer-layer jackets in sage and operational camouflage pattern configurations.
The five-year contract includes no option periods. Its ordering period will conclude on November 11, 2031.
The procurement was competitive, with one response received. The Defense Logistics Agency reported the acquisition as competitive despite receiving a single offer.
Funding will come from fiscal 2027 through 2032 defense working capital funds. The announcement does not identify an initial order, obligation, or guaranteed minimum amount.
Accordingly, the approximately $20.2 million represents the contract’s maximum ordering ceiling rather than guaranteed revenue to Hardwick Tactical. Actual payments will depend on the quantities DLA orders during the five-year period.
The Air Force is the military customer identified for the garments. Intermediate-weather outer layers provide protection in cooler or changing conditions while allowing service members to perform operational duties.
The flame-resistant requirement is particularly important for personnel working near aircraft, fuel, machinery, or other environments where exposure to fire or thermal hazards may occur.
Offering the garment in sage and operational camouflage pattern versions allows DLA to support different uniform and mission requirements.
DLA Troop Support in Philadelphia is the contracting activity for contract SPE1C1-27-D-0014. The organization manages military clothing and textile supply chains, including the procurement of uniforms, protective apparel, and related materials.
The IDIQ structure gives the agency flexibility to place orders based on inventory levels, deployment requirements, sizing demand, and other operational needs.
The award adds a long-term Air Force apparel contract to Hardwick Tactical’s production portfolio while preserving its federal designation as a small business.

candidates.text:
WhiteMatter: $20 Million Series A To Expand Enterprise AI Agent Governance
By Amit Chowdhry
Nov 11, 2026
WhiteMatter: $20 Million Series A To Expand Enterprise AI Agent Governance
WhiteMatter has raised $20 million in Series A funding to expand its enterprise platform for governing autonomous artificial intelligence agents, models, tools, and interactions. Blumberg Capital led the round, with participation from existing investors Crew Capital and Sprout & Oak. WhiteMatter previously operated under the name QuilrAI.
The company developed its platform to address security and operational risks created by AI agents that can access sensitive information, generate content, make decisions, interact with software, and create or influence other agents.
WhiteMatter governs AI across endpoints, browsers, software-as-a-service applications, cloud systems, and code. It assesses agents before deployment, applies policies to their actions, monitors outcomes, and manages traffic and spending through a controlled gateway.
Its architecture can deploy a dedicated Guardian agent for every AI agent operating within a customer’s environment. When autonomous systems create additional agents, WhiteMatter can provision corresponding Guardians to extend policy enforcement.
WhiteMatter has more than 2.25 million agents under management and expects that number to exceed 5.5 million by the end of 2026. Its platform has governed 116 billion AI interactions and helped customers avoid more than 11 trillion tokens during the past nine months.
The company tripled its customer base during 2026 and increased revenue fivefold over six months. It reported approximately 200% net revenue retention with no customer churn.
Customers include Sentara Health, Alter Domus, New American Funding, Concentrix, and other large enterprises. WhiteMatter’s policy architecture delivers decisions in 2.24 milliseconds and can process as many as 7,800 actions per minute.
The new capital will support research, product development, go-to-market expansion, and additions to WhiteMatter’s executive team. The company is positioning its technology as an operational and security layer for businesses deploying AI at scale.
KEY QUOTES:
“Despite all the discussion about pausing AI development, enterprises are doing the opposite. AI technology is too powerful, the opportunity is too significant, and the competitive pressure is too real to put it back in the box. Companies that slow down AI adoption risk being overtaken by competitors that move fast, stay secure, and scale AI with confidence, which is exactly why we built WhiteMatter.”
Vidit Arora, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of WhiteMatter
“WhiteMatter is helping us scale that adoption responsibly by providing greater visibility into how AI is being used, protecting sensitive information at the point of use, and guiding our workforce toward appropriate behaviors and tools in real time. We’re not governing AI to slow innovation. We’re creating the trust and guardrails that allow us to innovate responsibly, keep saying yes, and ultimately advance our mission of improving health every day.”
Zishan Siddiqui, Chief Information Security Officer at Sentara Health
“At Alter Domus, we scale practical AI with measured returns: squads of Industrialized Agents in production, and work that used to take a quarter now takes a week. That pace is only responsible if governance keeps up. With WhiteMatter in our cyber defense stack, every agent is governed before it goes live, every tool call is policy-checked at one gateway, and the telemetry shows us where AI actually creates value. Security, adoption, and enterprise value aren’t separate conversations here. They’re one lifecycle, and we can see all of it.”
Demetry Zilberg, Chief Technology Officer of Alter Domus
“Every wave of enterprise computing eventually produced its own security layer, from the network to the cloud to identity. Agents are the next wave and could soon outnumber employees inside enterprises, requiring a governance layer built natively for them. We backed WhiteMatter because its platform approach and Guardian agent model give enterprises the guardrails an autonomous workforce needs, at a scale no human security team could manage manually.”
Pramod Gosavi of Blumberg Capital

candidates.text:
SPARETECH raises $20M Series B to help manufacturers cut industrial spare parts inventory by 60%
USA - English
USA - English
News provided by
SPARETECH
Nov 10, 2026, 10:10 ET
Share this article
Share this article
SPARETECH aims to cut manufacturers' spare parts inventory by 60% within three years with AI that ensures parts are available when they are needed
MUNICH , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SPARETECH, a provider of enterprise AI for spare parts management, today announced it has raised $20 million in Series B funding to help manufacturers cut their spare parts inventory without risking downtime. Blume Equity and Insight Partners co-led the round, with participation from Headline.
Geographic expansion and growth trajectory
Continue Reading
SPARETECH Founders | Dr. Lukas Biedermann & Martin Weber
SPARETECH has established itself in the United States and grown its revenue fivefold since the start of 2024. Over the same period, the company grew its spare parts catalog to more than 40 million verified parts and expanded its network to 15,000 manufacturer and supplier partners. The global rollout of Nestlé, a SPARETECH customer, put 320 plants across 70 countries live in less than a year, further affirming SPARETECH's global enterprise capabilities and speed.
"Every customer we work with wants the same thing: the production line running with less inventory on the shelf. That is the problem we are going to solve with Maintenance teams, and our goal is to cut spare parts inventory by 60% in the next three years, while securing the same uptime."
Martin Weber, CEO and Co-Founder, SPARETECH
Why spare parts stay on the shelf
Spare parts management has long been one of manufacturing's most persistent inefficiencies. A single stockout can halt production and idle an entire line, making plants default to holding extensive spare parts inventories as a safeguard. The result is a substantial amount of capital sitting on the shelf. SPARETECH's 2026 benchmark report puts the average value of spare parts inventory at $169 million per company.
Source: Unlocking cost savings in spare parts management: The 2026 benchmark report on MRO spend, productivity, and working capital , SPARETECH, 2026.
From visibility to availability
Since its founding, SPARETECH has helped customers gain visibility into the parts they hold and standardize their spare parts data, which is the foundation of effective spare parts management. Meaningfully reducing inventory levels, however, requires more than good data. It requires physical action.
SPARETECH is moving the market beyond insights and recommendations toward measurable outcomes: lower inventory with the same uptime. To reach the 60% goal, every maintenance professional needs confidence that the right part will be available when needed, even if it sits on another company's shelf. SPARETECH's AI will secure that availability.
"Every part sitting idle is cash that could be working somewhere else. We are building AI that makes sure the right part is available when a plant needs it and put those idle parts back into circulation, so the money tied up on the shelf can go back to growing the business."
Dr. Lukas Biedermann, COO and Co-Founder, SPARETECH
Why now
Industrial automation keeps expanding, and a single new production line can add thousands of spare parts that someone has to stock. The problem grows with every machine that is installed. With the cost of capital rising, manufacturers can no longer afford to keep that much money sitting on the shelf. At the same time, AI can now secure availability at a scale no team could manage by hand.
"Often building resilience in supply chain ends up in building more inventories for spare parts. A much more suitable way would be a system, which secures better resilience with up to 60% less inventories sitting on the shelves. SPARETECH is exactly doing this. A fascinating opportunity especially for the manufacturing industry."
Joe Kaeser, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Siemens Energy and Daimler Truck
"SPARETECH is exactly the kind of business we back. Idle spare parts are a large, overlooked pool of wasted resources, and putting them back to work gives manufacturers a measurable return and the planet less waste. We are delighted to partner with Martin, Lukas, and the team as they scale."
Michelle Capiod, Co-Founding Partner, Blume Equity
Investing in innovation and expansion
SPARETECH will use the funding to continue building the AI that secures spare part availability for industrial companies and put their surplus parts back into circulation, expand its presence in North America and new regions, and deepen its work with existing customers.
"The next stage of SPARETECH's growth runs through North America. American manufacturers operate large plant networks with a lot of capital tied up in spare parts, and they need a partner built for that scale. Insight has spent decades helping software companies grow in the United States, and we are excited to support Martin, Lukas, and the team as they scale."
Brad Fiedler, Managing Director, Insight Partners
"The digital world is moving into the physical one, and Germany has the industrial substance to lead that shift. SPARETECH is building industrial AI for spare parts management, and it already gives maintenance and procurement teams confidence in uncertain times. This is where industrial AI starts to pay off for global manufacturers."
Christian Miele, General Partner, Headline
Learn more at sparetech.io .
About SPARETECH
SPARETECH's enterprise AI software empowers global manufacturers to reduce their spare parts spend and inventory. Built on verified original manufacturer data, the platform standardizes material master data, right-sizes inventory across plants, and enables sourcing and surplus resale across the network. Maintenance and procurement teams know what they have, get what they need, and sell what they don't.

Danish biotech specialist raises €20 million to accelerate market-ready trait development
Make us your Google favorite
Danish biotechnology company Traitomic has raised €20 million in a Series A round led by Sofinnova Partners. The investor consortium also includes the Export and Investment Fund of Denmark (EIFO), Footprint Firm, Nordic Foodtech VC, PSV Hafnium and SVG Ventures. The round marks Traitomic's first external investment since its spin-out from Carlsberg and follows the development of a growing customer base across multiple industries. The funding will support international expansion and continued development of the company's scientific and commercial capabilities.
The world increasingly depends on improved biological performance to address challenges in food security, resource efficiency and sustainability. Yet translating a biological need into a commercially relevant trait can be slow, fragmented and difficult to scale. Traitomic helps bridge that gap not only by developing market-ready traits, but also supporting customers from initial commercial challenges through to deployment.
© Traitomic (L-R) Toni Wendt, Technology Lead; Jan Gottlieb, Commercial Lead; Gustav Hambraeus, Managing Director
Traitomic's proprietary FIND-IT platform identifies specific genetic variants in conventionally bred populations without gene editing, enabling rapid trait development while maintaining broad regulatory and commercial applicability. Unlike many trait-development approaches that are tailored to specific organism types, the platform can be applied across both plant and microbial systems.
To date, Traitomic has delivered 116 traits to 47 customers across 32 organisms spanning plant breeding and seed; food supply chain and precision nutrition; and biosolutions and industrial biotech. The projects range from improving crop robustness and yield, to developing differentiated food products with enhanced flavour, nutrition or shelf life, and optimising enzymes and strains used in industrial biotechnology. This breadth of applications reflects demand from customers across multiple industries and highlights the significant opportunity to expand trait development across the broader bioeconomy.
© Traitomic
The funding will support Traitomic's international expansion and help the company capture this opportunity across food, agriculture and biosolutions markets. In addition, Traitomic will continue to broaden its integrated offering, enabling closer collaboration with customers from initial biological or commercial challenges through delivery of market-ready traits.
Gustav Hambraeus, CEO and co-founder, Traitomic said: "This investment marks the beginning of Traitomic's next chapter. Over the past years, we have demonstrated that customers across the food value chain are looking for faster routes from biological insight to commercial impact. With the support of our new investors, we can now expand internationally, deepen our collaboration with customers and bring our integrated approach to trait development to many more innovation challenges."
© Traitomic
Michael Krel, Partner, Sofinnova Partners said: "Traitomic has demonstrated something that is rare in biological innovation: the ability to develop commercially relevant traits across a broad range of organisms and applications. Combined with the company's strong customer traction and proven track record, this creates a compelling foundation for future growth. We believe Traitomic is well positioned to become a leading partner for trait development across agriculture, food and industrial biotechnology, and we look forward to supporting the team with both capital and experience as they enter their next phase of international expansion."
Anders Røed, Executive Vice President, Group Strategy and Commercial, Carlsberg said: "Traitomic is an excellent example of how fundamental research can create value far beyond its original field of application. FIND-IT was developed at Carlsberg Research Laboratory to improve barley, and it is now enabling advances in agriculture, food production and industrial biotechnology. I am proud of what the team has achieved and excited to continue supporting the company as it enters this next phase of international growth."

11 Ноя, 2026
Американский стартап привлёк $20 млн на космические аппараты, которые сами собираются на орбите
Новости
Rendezvous Robotics
28 октября стартап Rendezvous Robotics из Голдена в штате Колорадо объявил о посевном раунде на $20 млн. Его возглавили венчурные компании MaC Venture Capital и Toyota Ventures, а средства пойдут на разработку нового поколения аппаратов, лётные демонстрации и расширение команды.
Помимо лидеров, в раунде участвовали фонд University of Michigan Endowment, Astera, Industrious Ventures, Humbition и NextView Ventures. Компанию и дальше поддержали существующие инвесторы Aurelia Foundry, ATX Venture Partners и Mana Ventures.
- Реклама -
Стартап ищет выход из ограничений, которые накладывает запуск. Большинство аппаратов проектируют так, чтобы они поместились в головной обтекатель — защитную оболочку на вершине ракеты, под которой летит груз. Из-за этого ещё до запуска приходится идти на компромиссы в выработке энергии, вычислительных мощностях, размере антенн и теплоотводе, хотя потребность во всём этом растёт.
Гендиректор Джо Лэндон пояснил Payload, что отрасль не хочет аппаратов меньшего размера и меньшей мощности. «Никто не говорит о том, чтобы делать спутники меньше и менее функциональными, — сказал он. — Все хотят больше мощности, больше теплоотвода, более крупные антенны, более чувствительную связь. Но этого не достичь, пока мы не научимся строить прямо в космосе».
Подписывайтесь на Mediasat в Telegram : здесь самые интересные новости из мира технологий
Rendezvous Robotics предлагает другой подход — аппарат из компактных независимых модулей-плиток. Их запускают по отдельности, а на орбите они самостоятельно маневрируют, выравниваются и соединяются в одну конструкцию, которую после запуска можно перестроить под новые задачи. Этот подход вырос из почти десятилетних исследований соосновательницы компании Ариэль Экблау в Массачусетском технологическом институте (MIT) в рамках программы TESSERAE. Ранние поколения TESSERAE уже проверяли на суборбитальной ракете New Shepard компании Blue Origin и во время двух миссий на Международной космической станции (МКС).
Сейчас Rendezvous Robotics разрабатывает новое поколение более крупных независимых модулей, а их движение, выравнивание и сборку проверяет на Земле. Эти испытания продолжат серией параболических полётов в ноябре 2026 года, во время которых самолёт ненадолго создаёт невесомость. В этих полётах испытают электромагнитный привод и движение модулей. Отдельно от них, в декабре на МКС, проведут заключительную демонстрацию TESSERAE пятого поколения — 32 плитки должны автономно собраться в трёхмерную конструкцию.
Демонстрационную миссию на низкой околоземной орбите запланировали не ранее апреля 2028 года. В ней семь независимых модулей должны автономно соединиться в один аппарат, разделиться и снова собраться в иной конфигурации без помощи внешних роботизированных манипуляторов. Компания называет её первой в своём роде и уже зарезервировала место в совместном запуске (rideshare), где модули выведут на орбиту вместе с другими грузами.
Модульность даёт и практическую выгоду. Оператор может менять конфигурацию аппарата, добавлять новые модули или заменять неисправные прямо на орбите, а не строить и запускать новый аппарат. По словам Лэндона, нынешнее обслуживание спутников сводится к продлению срока службы, тогда как система Rendezvous при повреждении может сама изменить свою структуру на лучшую из доступных. Лэндон допускает и создание на орбите склада модулей, который будет выдавать запасные части по требованию.

candidates.text:
Griffin: $20 Million Series B Funding Led By Octagon Partners To Expand Card Issuing And Stablecoin Banking Services
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:49 AM
Griffin: $20 Million Series B Funding Led By Octagon Partners To Expand Card Issuing And Stablecoin Banking Services
Griffin, a United Kingdom-based licensed bank providing embedded banking infrastructure to fintech companies and technology platforms, has raised $20 million in Series B funding led by Octagon Partners. Notion Capital, A+ Ventures, Nordic Ninja, Breega, and other existing investors participated in the round, which values Griffin at more than $100 million.
The financing will support the expansion of Griffin’s banking platform into card issuing and stablecoin-related services while providing capital for continued growth toward profitability.
Griffin operates a regulated banking infrastructure platform that enables businesses to integrate accounts, payments, and compliance capabilities into their products.
The company serves more than 80 businesses, including Uber, Countingup, Anna Money, Yonder, and Prosper.
Its infrastructure supports more than 300,000 underlying retail and business customers and processes nearly 10 million payments annually.
The latest investment comes approximately two years after Griffin began operating as a fully licensed UK bank.
Expanding Into Debit And Credit Card Issuing
Griffin plans to use the Series B financing to introduce card issuing capabilities.
The initial offering will enable customers to launch branded retail and corporate debit cards using Griffin’s banking infrastructure.
This will extend the company’s existing services beyond accounts and payments.
Businesses using Griffin’s platform will be able to combine banking accounts, payment processing, and card products through a single infrastructure provider.
The company also intends to introduce credit card capabilities following the initial debit card launch.
These services are designed for fintech businesses and other technology companies that want to offer financial products without independently developing every component of the underlying banking infrastructure.
Griffin believes adding cards will strengthen its relationships with existing customers while creating opportunities to serve additional businesses.
The expanded platform will provide more options for companies developing financial services embedded within their own applications.
Developing Stablecoin Payment Infrastructure
The second major area of investment involves stablecoin-related banking services.
Griffin plans to develop reserve capabilities for businesses operating in the stablecoin market.
The company also intends to integrate on-chain cross-border payments into its platform.
Stablecoins are digital assets designed to maintain a relatively stable value, often by referencing a conventional currency.
Businesses developing stablecoin-based financial services may require banking relationships, reserve management arrangements, and payment infrastructure.
Griffin’s planned capabilities are intended to support these requirements.
The company’s existing regulated banking operations provide a foundation for developing additional services.
The stablecoin initiatives remain planned product developments rather than capabilities that the announcement identifies as fully launched.
More Than 80 Companies Use Griffin’s Infrastructure
Griffin has expanded its customer base since becoming a fully licensed bank in 2024.
The company initially worked with five businesses testing its systems.
Its platform now supports more than 80 companies offering financial products and services.
These customers include established businesses and fintech platforms across different financial services categories.
Griffin provides clearing and embedded banking capabilities, allowing customers to deliver banking products under their own brands.
The company currently serves more than 300,000 underlying retail and business customers.
Its infrastructure processes nearly 10 million payments each year.
The expansion illustrates increasing adoption of Griffin’s model of combining regulated banking services with technology infrastructure designed for other businesses.
Recurring Revenue Grows 3.2 Times Year Over Year
Griffin reported that recurring revenue increased 3.2 times year over year for its financial year ended September 2026.
The figures are based on unaudited financial accounts and remain subject to change following completion of the company’s statutory audit.
The company was also included in the Sifted 250 ranking of Europe’s fastest-growing startups by revenue.
Additionally, Griffin joined Tech Nation’s Future Fifty 2026 cohort, which recognizes high-growth UK technology businesses.
Octagon Partners highlighted the company’s commercial development and its progress toward achieving double-digit millions of pounds in annual recurring revenue.
The investor also emphasized Griffin’s combination of proprietary technology, AI, and regulated banking infrastructure.
The company operates under the supervision of the Prudential Regulation Authority and Financial Conduct Authority.
Supporting Fintechs Through A Regulated Banking Platform
Griffin’s business model combines banking authorization with technology services designed for fintech companies and platforms.
The company offers services including business accounts, embedded accounts, payments, safeguarding, and compliance-related infrastructure.
These capabilities allow customers to develop financial products while relying on Griffin for regulated banking functions.
Its strategy emphasizes providing a unified infrastructure platform that can support different financial services applications.
By adding card issuing and stablecoin capabilities, Griffin intends to broaden the range of products its customers can offer.
The company also believes the expanded platform will improve its ability to attract additional fintech partners.

Accountable Launches to Give Power to American Taxpayers
News provided by
Accountable
Nov 16, 2026, 09:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Co-founded by Acorns CEO Noah Kerner and Jeff Cruttenden, Accountable raises $20 million to help Americans file their taxes, follow their money, and ultimately decide how it is spent.
NEW YORK , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Accountable, a new consumer tax and civic company, launched its waitlist today with the belief that taxpayers should be treated like investors in the country they fund. Investors expect transparency into how their money is put to work, accountability for how it is managed, and a voice in the decisions that shape where it goes. Taxpayers deserve the same.
Continue Reading
Every year, Americans file more than 160 million federal income tax returns, while individuals— not corporations—account for roughly 85% of federal tax revenue. The average taxpayer spends about 12 hours preparing and completing a return, only to be left with a larger question once it's filed: what did their money actually pay for?
Co-founded by Acorns CEO Noah Kerner and Jeff Cruttenden, Accountable Launches to Give Power to American Taxpayers.
Post this
Accountable's first product, a tax filing platform designed around the needs of the taxpayer, will launch in January 2027 ahead of tax season. With a filer's permission, Accountable retrieves available tax information and documents, prefills their return, and guides them through reviewing and submitting for one flat price of $76, with filing free for anyone experiencing financial hardship. Accountable customers will also receive a personalized taxpayer receipt showing an estimated breakdown of what their taxes fund across federal, state, and local government spending.
"Cumulatively, taxes are the largest check most of us will ever write, and it's ridiculous that we don't even get a receipt," said Noah Kerner, co-founder of Accountable. "Taxpayers deserve a better experience: smart, fast and fair filing, transparency into what we're paying for, and power over where our money goes. After all, it's our money, we fund this country, and we should feel like shareholders in it."
The filing platform is the first step in Accountable's broader vision: help Americans file their taxes, follow their money and, over time, have a greater voice in how it is spent. Accountable is starting with filing because it is the most direct financial interaction most Americans have with government. Each year, Americans are asked to account for every dollar they earn. Accountability should go both ways.
For Kerner, Accountable is a continuation of a career spent giving everyday people more access and agency in complex financial systems. At Acorns, Kerner has helped over 15 million everyday Americans save & invest over $30 billion. At Say, he gave individual investors a voice in the companies they own. At Accountable, he wants to give taxpayers the same voice in the country they fund. The full team behind Accountable comes with a wealth of experience across tax, civic, investing, health, and consumer technology sectors.
"We backed Accountable because we believe the taxpayer is one of the biggest consumer categories still waiting to be reinvented," said Lauren Kolodny, Founding Partner at Acrew Capital . "Noah has spent his career earning the trust of everyday Americans. With Accountable, he's bringing that same consumer-first mindset to one of the most important financial relationships in their lives."
"Americans have more tools than ever to understand where their money goes, except when it goes to the government," said Brent Murri, Partner at M13 . "At M13, we look for founders who transform complex, entrenched systems into experiences that give people greater control. Accountable has the potential to fundamentally change the relationship between Americans and the government they fund."
Accountable has raised $20 million in total funding, including a seed round co-led by Acrew Capital and M13, with participation from Greycroft, Torch Capital, Treasury, 645 Ventures, Eniac Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Tusk Ventures, and angel investors like Josh Wolfe, founder of Lux Capital, and Zach Perret, co-founder of Plaid. The capital will support the buildout of Accountable's filing platform and team ahead of its January launch. Kerner will continue to serve as CEO of Acorns.
Americans can join the waitlist beginning today at AccountableUSA.com .
About Accountable
Accountable is a consumer tax and civic company on a mission to bring Americans closer to America. Its first product, a tax platform designed to give Power to the Taxpayer, launches for the 2027 tax season. Join the waitlist at AccountableUSA.com .

Fresh Off $20M Series A, WhiteMatter Taps Leaders from Proofpoint and Hitachi to Scale Globally
News provided by
WhiteMatter
Nov 17, 2026, 09:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Jasmine Wu joins as Chief Marketing Officer and Anuj Gupta as Managing Director, Asia Pacific & Japan
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Following its $20 million Series A at a $202 million valuation and fivefold revenue growth in six months, WhiteMatter , formerly QuilrAI, today announced two senior hires to accelerate its global expansion. Jasmine Wu, formerly senior marketing executive of Proofpoint and ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok, joins WhiteMatter as Chief Marketing Officer, while Anuj Gupta, former Managing Director of Hitachi Systems India, joins as Managing Director, Asia Pacific & Japan (APJ). They join Chief Revenue Officer Tammy Sexton, who joined in late 2025, as WhiteMatter builds out its leadership team to meet growing global demand for AI agent governance.
Continue Reading
Jasmine Wu joins as Chief Marketing Officer and Anuj Gupta as Managing Director, Asia Pacific & Japan
WhiteMatter was founded by CEO Vidit Arora, a founding member of Securonix who spent more than a decade helping build the security analytics company, leading across product, solution architecture, and global customer experience. He created WhiteMatter to solve a new security challenge: how companies govern AI agents that can make decisions, access systems, and take action on their own. WhiteMatter helps enterprises assess and approve agents before they go live, then continuously control what they can access and do in production. The company has received acquisition offers but is instead focusing on building and scaling the business independently. The new appointments bring the marketing, sales, and leadership needed to support that growth.
"When AI began moving from a tool people use to agents that make autonomous decisions, I watched the traditional security model start to break," said Arora. "I founded WhiteMatter on the belief that companies would need to rethink security and infrastructure for a world built around AI and agents. That world is here. Enterprises are scaling agents now, and they need governance based on how agents actually behave, starting from pre-production blueprints. Jasmine, Anuj, and Tammy have each built and scaled category-defining businesses, and they give us the go-to-market strength to deliver that governance worldwide."
Wu joins from Proofpoint, where she served as Head of Product Marketing and GTM Operations as the company grew from under $1 billion to more than $2 billion in annual recurring revenue. Before that, she was Head of Marketing at ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok. Her career spans 15+ years across security and consumer technology at global scale. At WhiteMatter, she will lead global marketing to establish WhiteMatter as the company defining the agent and AI lifecycle governance category.
"The AI and agent challenge extends far beyond security, yet it has been treated as a security problem for too long," said Wu. "Enterprises are deploying thousands of agents and AI workflows powered by non-deterministic models, but runtime protection alone cannot govern an agent that was never properly assessed before deployment. We believe AI and agent governance must be approached as a lifecycle: from the moment an agent is proposed to every execution in production, with a complete record of the decisions made along the way. This requires a fundamentally different approach, and a company built specifically to deliver it. That company is WhiteMatter. Grey matter is where agents think and act; white matter connects and protects them. We are building that critical layer for the agentic enterprise."
Anuj Gupta's appointment marks WhiteMatter's entry into Asia Pacific and Japan, one of the fastest-moving markets for enterprise AI adoption. He joins from Hitachi Systems India, where as Managing Director and CEO, he helped grow a $10.6 million business into a $425 million industry leader. He was also instrumental in the successful integration of Micro Clinic and its transition into the Hitachi Systems global network, contributing significantly to the organization's growth, operational evolution, and expanded market presence. At WhiteMatter, he will lead APJ market entry and expansion, building a regional ecosystem of partners, enterprise customers, and technology alliances.
"Asia Pacific and Japan represent a significant opportunity for enterprise AI, but adoption has to move hand in hand with governance and accountability," said Gupta. "Enterprises here are deploying agents at the same pace as the US, often with leaner security teams and stricter regulators. A deployment-first approach lets them govern an agent once, before it goes live, instead of chasing every action after. That is how we help organizations embrace AI with confidence, and that is the model we are bringing to APJ."
The two hires join Sexton, who leads WhiteMatter's revenue strategy. She has years of experience selling security at LaunchDarkly, Skyflow, and Sumo Logic, with a track record of scaling sales teams through hypergrowth at venture-backed technology companies.
To learn more about WhiteMatter's leadership team, visit www.whitematter.io/about
About WhiteMatter
WhiteMatter, formerly QuilrAI, is the first agent-native company built to secure and operationalize the agentic enterprise across the entire AI agent lifecycle. Foundation models are non-deterministic, so protecting agents only at runtime leaves every decision to the last millisecond and every alert to the security team. WhiteMatter treats AI security as a deployment problem first: every agent is assessed, governed against policy, and deployed from an approved blueprint before reaching production; while every action is governed before execution and every outcome is measured and validated.

Primordial Labs: $18 Million Series A Funding To Expand AI-Powered Military Command And Control Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:59 AM
Primordial Labs: $18 Million Series A Funding To Expand AI-Powered Military Command And Control Platform
Primordial Labs, a defense technology company developing natural-language command and control software for military systems, has raised $18 million in Series A funding to expand deployment of its Anura platform. The investment will support the company’s engineering and product development operations while accelerating adoption across military vehicles, aircraft, and uncrewed systems. The financing was led by Ballistic Ventures, with participation from existing investors Squadra Ventures and Lockheed Martin Ventures.
Founded in 2021 and headquartered in New Haven, Connecticut, Primordial Labs develops technology that allows military personnel to interact with complex equipment using natural-language instructions.
Its Anura platform functions as a software layer between human operators and the systems they control.
Modern military platforms often incorporate multiple sensors, radios, displays, and autonomous systems, each with separate interfaces.
Operating this equipment can create significant demands on personnel, particularly when crews must coordinate different systems during fast-moving missions.
Anura is designed to simplify these interactions by allowing operators to communicate goals and instructions in natural language.
The system translates those instructions into individual tasks and coordinates their execution across connected equipment.
It also monitors the results and adjusts activities as operational conditions change.
The platform is intended to support human-machine teaming by reducing the number of separate interfaces operators must manage.
Primordial Labs has integrated Anura with more than a dozen crewed and uncrewed platforms across land and air applications.
In October 2026, the company announced a master teaming agreement with General Dynamics Land Systems.
The partnership is intended to bring Anura to ground combat vehicles across the General Dynamics Land Systems portfolio, including the Abrams tank.
The company is also delivering licenses for small uncrewed aircraft systems to U.S. Army and special operations units.
These licenses are available through the Army’s UAS Marketplace.
Two Small Business Innovation Research Phase III awards received in 2026 expand the company’s work into Army rotary-wing aircraft and the U.S. Air Force’s MQ-9 ground control station.
These projects provide opportunities to demonstrate the platform in different operating environments.
Anura’s architecture is designed to integrate with existing equipment rather than requiring military customers to redesign entire systems.
The approach aligns with the Modular Open Systems Approach, which emphasizes interoperability and flexibility across defense platforms.
Primordial believes this design can help military organizations adopt the technology across different equipment manufacturers and operational environments.
The company’s founders bring experience developing autonomous and AI-enabled technologies at Lockheed Martin.
Co-Founder and CEO Lee Ritholtz and Co-Founder and CTO Adrian Pope previously worked at Lockheed Martin’s Skunk Works.
They participated in the development and deployment of small uncrewed aircraft systems and helped establish the Lockheed Martin Artificial Intelligence Center.
Their experience also included autonomous control technologies and human-machine teaming projects.
Primordial’s workforce combines engineering professionals with former special operations personnel.
The company intends to use the financing to expand its engineering, product, and commercial teams while fulfilling existing defense contracts.
Management also sees potential long-term applications outside the military.
Industries including mining, energy, logistics, and public safety increasingly operate autonomous equipment alongside human workers.
These environments may benefit from interfaces that allow personnel to coordinate complex systems through natural-language instructions.
For now, Primordial is concentrating on military deployments, with the $18 million financing supporting broader implementation of Anura across existing and future platforms.
KEY QUOTES:
“Crews on every platform are being asked to employ more capability with fewer people, much faster, and with less time for training. Anura provides humans and machines with a shared understanding of the mission and operating context, making systems easier to field, use, and learn. We’re delivering licenses to the Army and SOCOM today, and this round lets us meet the demand we’re seeing across domains, from ground vehicle crew stations to the cockpit to the dismounted soldier.”
Lee Ritholtz, Co-Founder And CEO Of Primordial Labs
“The military doesn’t need another proprietary interface for every new system. It needs technology that makes existing and future capabilities work together. Primordial’s use of the Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) is particularly compelling because it allows Anura to integrate across sophisticated military platforms without requiring them to be redesigned. Combined with the ability to translate a warfighter’s natural expression of intent into action, this represents a potentially important advance in human-machine teaming.”

Alecto raises $20M seed funding to make UK property law more accessible to consumers with AI
by Kyt Dotson
Alecto Conveyancing Ltd. , a London-based artificial intelligence-native law firm, today announced it raised $20 million in seed funding led by Insight Partners to make the law more accessible to the general public.
Firstminute Capital, Blue Lion Global, Andrena Ventures, FJ Labs, Antiportfolio Ventures, the Rigby Group and Mischon de Reya LLP also joined in the round. Angel investors participating in the round included Octopus Group Chief Executive and founder Simon Rogerson and SwiftKey founder John Reynolds.
Founded in September 2025 by CEO Will Rice (pictured), a serial entrepreneur who previously built fintech mortgage lender Gen H, Alecto’s first service targets the United Kingdom conveyancing market, the legal work required to buy and sell property. Rice drew on his experience building a mortgage company and decided to focus initially on bringing more people into ownership. With that expertise, Alecto aims to use AI to help give everyday people greater access to the law.
Alecto argues that traditional legal services are starved, with too few qualified attorneys and too few hours a day. Billing is based on hours, not outcomes and the service model doesn’t lean toward customers; this leads to unpredictable costs and a process that leaves customers in the dark.
The law firm said it’s using AI and legal experts to explain opaque legal processes in plain language and help clients make informed decisions. The company intends to target the property conveyancing market, which represents almost $3.3 billion in the U.K. alone, and aims to become the number one leader in property legal services by 2027.
“For too long, the legal industry has expected customers to work on its terms; now, AI presents the opportunity to put the consumer in control,” Rice said. “People don’t want to buy a lawyer’s time; they want results. Alecto exists to make the law accessible to everyone, giving control back to the consumer.”
Consumer legal services in the U.K. value growth pushed revenue over £55 billion, around $72.5 billion, in 2026, according to a report from Research and Markets . Business and commercial practices lead with 51% market value, followed by growth in the injury and conveyancing law markets.
“Property is where we prove the model. We’re building the technology and operations to rapidly break into new countries and new areas of law,” Rice added. “Ultimately, access to exceptional legal support should not depend on how much money you have or how confidently you can navigate the system.”

candidates.text:
EagleRock: $15.4 Million Midland Basin Acquisitions And Double Eagle V Agreement Expand Permian Footprint
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 3:45 PM
EagleRock: $15.4 Million Midland Basin Acquisitions And Double Eagle V Agreement Expand Permian Footprint
EagleRock has completed two acquisitions in the Midland Basin for a combined $15.4 million and entered into an agreement with Double Eagle V covering approximately 35,000 additional dedicated acres. The transactions expand EagleRock’s surface land and infrastructure operations in the Permian Basin while increasing its exposure to water management and royalty revenue opportunities.
The additional acreage dedication increases the land dedicated to EagleRock by Double Eagle in the Midland Basin to approximately 105,000 acres.
The new agreement covers approximately 35,000 acres across Midland and Glasscock counties in Texas.
It represents an increase of approximately 50% in Double Eagle’s dedicated acreage within the region.
EagleRock expects the agreement to generate additional royalty revenue without requiring an upfront capital investment.
This structure reflects the company’s capital-light operating model, which uses agreements with energy producers to generate income from the use of surface land and associated infrastructure.
Double Eagle V is an active private operator in the Midland Basin and EagleRock’s largest shareholder.
The additional dedication strengthens the relationship between the two companies and provides EagleRock with exposure to future development activity.
Management expects the agreement to begin making a meaningful revenue contribution in 2027.
Additional growth could follow as Double Eagle advances drilling and completion activities across the dedicated acreage.
Alongside the agreement, EagleRock acquired two properties totaling approximately 2,000 acres.
The acquisitions were completed at an aggregate price of $15.4 million.
EagleRock financed the purchases through cash on hand and borrowings under its existing revolving credit facility.
The company said the assets were purchased at a valuation below 10 times EBITDA.
One property is located directly adjacent to EagleRock’s existing Shallow Valley operations.
The other is adjacent to the newly announced Double Eagle V acreage dedication.
The geographic proximity is intended to support operational coordination and improve the company’s ability to serve customers.
The acquired properties provide additional water supply, storage, and disposal capabilities.
They also include potential opportunities for sand development.
These assets can support oil and gas operators that require water management services and access to infrastructure during drilling and production.
Water handling is a significant operational requirement in the Permian Basin because energy development involves both water consumption and the management of produced water.
Companies providing surface land and related infrastructure can participate in these activities through leases, royalties, and service arrangements.
EagleRock believes the acquisitions will create opportunities to increase revenue while benefiting from shared operating capabilities.
Following the transactions, the company’s Midland Basin portfolio includes approximately 44,000 acres of controlled surface land and approximately 105,000 dedicated acres.
The larger footprint provides additional exposure to energy development across the region.
EagleRock plans to use its existing operations and customer relationships to pursue further opportunities in surface land management and associated infrastructure services.
The acquisitions and acreage agreement reflect its strategy of expanding through complementary properties and capital-efficient commercial arrangements.
KEY QUOTES:
“The Double Eagle V Dedication builds on a relationship that already anchors our Midland Basin position, and it requires no upfront capital from EagleRock. The two acquisitions follow the same approach. They sit next to assets we already have, expand our water supply and storage, and are accretive. Together, these transactions expand our Midland Basin footprint and enhance our ability to serve customers across the region.”
Greg Pipkin, CEO Of EagleRock

CSIRO spinout lands $15 million to make green hydrogen using less power
Hadean grabs $15m to turn factory waste heat into cheaper green hydrogen for steel. Watch this pilot test the hydrogen hype.
Simon Thomsen
Nov 9, 2026
2 min read
Share
0
Prefer Startup Daily
The Hadean Energy team
CSIRO spinout Hadean Energy has secured a $15 million grant from the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) to test whether waste heat from heavy industry can cut the cost of making green hydrogen.
ARENA will fund half the $30 million pilot plant proposed for industrial gas supplier BOC’s Western Port site in Victoria. The plant will produce up to 7kg of hydrogen hourly for a neighbouring steelworks. That’s about 85% of the hydrogen needed for annealing, a heat treatment to prevent the steel’s surface from oxidising.
CSIRO and corporate adviser RFC Ambrian launched Hadean in 2023, with the latter’s fund dropping $1.5 million into its seed round that year.
Based at CSIRO’s Clayton research precinct in Melbourne, Hadean is commercialising a tubular solid oxide electrolyser researchers spent eight years developing. Its ceramic tubes use electricity and heat to split steam into hydrogen and oxygen. Hadean estimates that tapping the heat a factory already generates can reduce electricity use by around 30% compared to conventional electrolysers.
In 2024, a prototype ran for 1,000 hours at BlueScope’s Port Kembla steelworks in NSW. It used less than 36 kilowatt-hours of electricity per kilogram of hydrogen by using steam from the plant. The Victorian pilot will scale the system from about one kilowatt to 200-300kW.

ARENA CEO Darren Miller said green hydrogen has significant potential to reduce emissions from industries that are difficult to electrify.
“This pilot will demonstrate how Hadean’s technology performs in a real-world industrial environment and provide the evidence needed to assess its commercial potential,” he said.
“This could open the door to broader use of green hydrogen in steelmaking and other industrial applications, while helping build Australia’s hydrogen industrial capability.”
Hadean also raised capital from RFC Ambrian, engineering partner Amarna Energy and private investors to cover its share of the initial design and engineering work. Amarna will design the equipment that connects the electrolyser to industrial sites.
The startup expects to raise more capital over the next 12 months for construction costs.

candidates.title: Dallas AI Startup 4Minds Raises $15M Series A at $500M Valuation
candidates.snippet: Dallas AI Startup 4Minds Raises $15M Series A at $500M Valuation Dallas Innovates
candidates.text:
Dallas-based AI startup 4Minds, which emerged from stealth mode in April, is already halfway to unicorn status. The company said today that it has raised a $15 million Series A round at a $500 million post-money valuation.
Investors include Dallas-based Waterwood Capital Group and Lubbock-based Isom Holdings — both led in part by Clayton Isom, whose family founded Wichita Falls-based oil and gas management company Stephens & Johnson in the 1960s — and several family offices with ties to the energy and data center industries.
The startup plans to use the money to expand its sales and marketing teams. It focuses on selling to companies in financial services, banking, insurance, biotech, pharmaceutical and other regulated industries, as well as consumer packaged goods, retail and logistics. It also will add to its product development team.
A new way to automate enterprise AI
At 4Minds, developers created software to help large companies build AI systems that understand their business. The platform automatically pulls data from more than 40 business systems, scrubs it and organizes it into a “knowledge graph” that maps how the data is related. The knowledge graph then continuously trains the AI models on business uses, ensuring information stays current. It all runs inside a company’s own system, so its sensitive data never touches a public AI model.
It’s “the easiest way for any enterprise to build end-to-end automation for AI workloads,” co-founder and CEO Ryan Trimberger told Dallas Innovates.
The 4Minds team sees enormous potential, Trimberger said. Large companies are ramping up spending on AI. Enterprise AI spending in the U.S. reached an annualized run rate of $177 billion in September 2026, up more than fivefold from $33 billion a year earlier, according to a Menlo Ventures report .
Many companies aren’t realizing the returns they’d like from those investments, though. Factors include difficulty scrubbing data for use in an automated AI system, rising costs and data security concerns, Trimberger said. Tackling all those issues at once is 4Minds’ selling point.
“When we initially started, we were focused on making smaller [large language models] really powerful, and the thesis was around cybersecurity,” Trimberger said. “That’s just native to who we are as a business. … We realized very quickly this wasn’t just cybersecurity. This was going to be every business, every domain, every vertical.”
Building in Deep Ellum
Trimberger founded 4Minds in 2024 along with Jerome Naidoo and Jason Nocco. The three founders make up the first three minds in the company’s name. The fourth represents the company’s customers, Trimberger said.
The team stayed small at the outset, focusing exclusively on product development. As recently as February, 4Minds employed just 13 people. Today, its headcount tops 60. Trimberger said he expects that number to approach 100 by early 2027.
He declined to share the startup’s revenue targets but said, “We think we can scale and be in the nine-figure range very quickly.”
The company sells 4Minds on the AWS and Microsoft marketplaces. It’s also part of AWS’ Global Startup Program and the Microsoft for Startups Pegasus Program , and will be featured at this month’s Microsoft Ignite 2026.
Access to strong research universities played a key role in choosing Dallas as the home for 4Minds’ product team, Trimberger said.
The company has recruited several people from the University of North Texas’ data science program and has formed a relationship with Dean Kinshuk, who leads UNT’s newly named Anuradha and Vikas Sinha College of Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics. It maintains similar relationships with the University of Texas at Arlington for machine learning and Southern Methodist University for cybersecurity, Trimberger said.
“We’ve been really, really intentional to try to build an ecosystem for not just hiring but for long-term, private-sector research,” he said. “We consider ourselves an AI lab, and I think a lot of that is just an extension of our higher ed partnerships.”
Its entire product team is based in North Texas, working from an office in Deep Ellum, a location that Trimberger said is a great fit.
“We needed something that was going to be modern, cool and fit what we were building,” he said. “I don’t think there’s really anybody doing this kind of frontier-level tech in DFW, so we need a space to reflect that. We are proud to be in Dallas.”
Why family offices?
Because 4Minds concentrates on the software layer of generative AI, it doesn’t need the large investments required by companies with significant infrastructure buildouts , Trimberger said. This allows what he described as an unconventional approach to fundraising, seeking smaller amounts of money from family offices.
“We’re not building infrastructure like a data center company would, so our operating capital is much lighter,” he said. “So, we’ve decided to forgo the traditional venture capital for our Series A and focus exclusively on Dallas-based family offices. That’s a strategic avenue for us.”
The startup’s investors can be a built-in customer base, as they look not just to invest in AI but to introduce AI to portfolio companies, Trimberger said. The approach also means 4Minds’ investors understand what it takes to operate and scale a business.
“These are people who have already built their own successful businesses,” he said. “They’ve built their own empires, so there is an immediate mutual respect there.”
Waterwood Capital’s developers used 4Minds’ technology for months before the firm invested in the company, Waterwood co-founder Clayton Isom said in a statement. The family office’s other portfolio companies include IronHorse Power Services, Evergreen Power Solutions and FairBill Solutions, all based in Dallas; Weatherford-based 3B Inspection; and The Woodlands-based 3B Surveying.

Clawlab Raises Over $15 Million in Pre-A3 Funding to Bring Smart Knitting Home
News provided by
Clawlab
Nov 12, 2026, 12:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
SHENZHEN, China , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Clawlab, a technology startup developing smart tools for textile creation, has raised more than $15 million in a Pre-A3 funding round led by miHoYo. Vision Plus Capital and Shunwei Capital also increased their investments through super pro rata participation. The round brings Clawlab's total funding to approximately $25 million across four equity rounds. Its shareholder base includes Sequoia China, Shunwei Capital, YM Capital, Vision Plus Capital, and miHoYo, bringing together leading venture capital firms and a strategic corporate investor.
Investors Back Clawlab's Vision for a New Consumer Category
With AI software commanding much of the market's attention, Clawlab's more than $15 million funding round reflects investor interest in a different opportunity: the untapped consumer potential of smart knitting.
The opportunity comes from a gap between rising consumer demand and the tools available to meet it. Interest in personalized, hands-on creation is growing, yet most knitting equipment remains designed for factories and professional users. Pattern development, stitch control, and machine operation still require specialist expertise. The category lacks a desktop device capable of bringing industrial-grade knitting capabilities within reach of individual creators.
Clawlab is addressing that gap with the world's first smart knitting machine designed for home use. It turns an image or idea into a finished knitted item, handling pattern preparation, stitchwork, and repetitive production while leaving the design, colors, and intended use to the user.
That flexibility supports a wide range of applications, from scarves and doll clothes to pet accessories and personalized gifts. A hobby project can also grow into custom work or a small business. Clawlab is set to unveil this smart knitting machine to a global audience at CES 2027.
The Engineering Foundation Behind Clawlab
Bringing professional knitting equipment into the home involves more than reducing its size. The real challenge is translating complex engineering into a product that feels intuitive to everyday users. Clawlab's founder and CEO Wenxin Hu previously worked as a hardware engineer at DJI and Meituan, while most members of the company's core R&D team are also former DJI employees. Together, they bring experience developing consumer-grade smart hardware and other technically complex products.
That background has shaped Clawlab's approach to product development. Rather than simply miniaturizing existing equipment or adding digital features, the company is rethinking the knitting experience across hardware, software, and interaction design around the needs of individual creators. The technology takes on the complexity, while users retain control of the creative process.
The Long-Term Vision in Knitting
Clawlab chose knitting based on a simple premise: textiles meet one of the most basic and enduring needs of everyday life.
"Textiles meet a broad, long-standing need in everyday life. Standardized products are abundant, but consumers' desire for personal style, customization, and emotional expression remains underserved," said Wenxin Hu. "We want to reconnect ideas, design, and production so that people without professional training can create through knitting."
Their longer-term ambition is to make knitting an everyday medium of expression. Smart knitting equipment, design software, and a creator community can help people turn ideas, memories, and care for others into one-of-a-kind pieces they can hold, share, and pass on.
About Clawlab
Clawlab is a technology startup founded in 2023 that develops smart tools for textile creation. It is building the future of knitting through a combination of innovative knitting technologies and a connected maker community. Its mission, "Push knitting forward. Bring more ideas to life," is to develop the tools and technology that help more people turn what they imagine into something they can hold. Clawlab's vision is to make knitting an everyday language for expression, much like words and pictures, through which people can tell their stories, preserve memories, and connect with others. For more information, please visit www.clawlab.com

Radical Ventures and Costanoa double down as Delphina launches the Context Factory, where AI agents build and maintain the business context behind trusted answers
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Delphina , whose Context Factory uses AI agents to build and maintain the business context behind trusted AI analytics, announced $7.5 million in new funding, bringing its total funding to $15 million. The round was co-led by Radical Ventures and Costanoa, with participation from Tenacity Capital joining high-profile angels Fei-Fei Li, Nobel laureate Guido Imbens, and early employees of Anthropic and OpenAI. . Delphina will use the funding to scale the Context Factory and grow its go-to-market and customer engineering teams.
Delphina was built to meet data teams' standards, but business teams now ask 73% of the questions on the platform, and CEOs at more than half of its customers are active users. At Substack, more than 70% of employees use Delphina, including CEO Chris Best. Other customers include LATAM Airlines, Gen Digital, Upstart, Udemy, Medely, Coursera, and BaseCamp Franchising.
"We want to give our people superpowers with AI. Delphina does that for data," said Chris Best, CEO of Substack. "Now our teams get accurate answers in seconds instead of waiting weeks in a queue. It's changed how we make decisions."
AI analytics is only as good as what it knows about the business: which tables are trusted, how metrics are defined, and what experienced analysts know but never wrote down. Most companies build that context by hand, and it goes stale as the business changes. The Context Factory hands that work to agents. They build a working baseline from a company's existing data and documents in hours, find and fix gaps as people ask questions, and route important changes to domain experts for approval.
"At Uber, everyone, including the CEO, was hands-on with data. That direct line to the numbers was a real advantage, but it took an army of data engineers to keep it from collapsing into chaos," said Jeremy Hermann, Delphina's CEO and co-founder. "The Context Factory gives every company that same advantage. Agents do the heavy lifting, and data teams become the knowledge captains who decide how the business sees its numbers."
"Most companies are data-obsessed but struggle to become data-driven," said Duncan Gilchrist, Delphina's President and co-founder. "When everyone can get trusted answers, everyone suddenly has questions. Ops, sales, marketing and finance teams are now the heaviest users of Delphina, and they keep coming back."
Hermann built and led Uber's Michelangelo machine learning platform and co-founded Tecton, which was acquired by Databricks. Gilchrist led global pricing data science at Uber. The Context Factory is available today at delphina.ai .
About Delphina
Delphina gives everyone in a company, from the front line to the CEO, trusted answers from the company's own data. Its Context Factory uses AI agents to build and maintain the business knowledge that enables accurate AI analytics, with experts approving important changes. Delphina is based in San Francisco and backed by Radical Ventures and Costanoa Ventures. Learn more at delphina.ai .

ODAIA Raises Series C to Scale Predictive Commercial Intelligence for Pharma
News provided by
ODAIA
Nov 17, 2026, 09:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Returning investors and strategic investor PHM back
ODAIA's next stage of growth
BOSTON , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ODAIA , an AI company delivering predictive commercial intelligence for pharma, today announced it has closed a US$15 million Series C financing led by Monograph Capital and anchored by strategic investor PHM , the leading health media agency in the U.S., part of Publicis Groupe. Investors from ODAIA's earlier rounds are also returning: BDC Capital , Flint Capital , Innospark Ventures , and Graphite Ventures from its Series A and Threshold Ventures and Wittington Ventures from its Series B. ODAIA will use the capital to grow within the enterprise pharma accounts it already serves and continue innovating its commercial intelligence platform.
Leading biopharmaceutical companies use ODAIA for commercial intelligence and workflow automations for field and marketing teams across many therapeutic areas. ODAIA predicts patient journeys, uncovers missed Rx opportunities, determines which healthcare professionals (HCPs) to prioritize through which channels, and keeps sales and marketing working from one brand strategy.
"Pharma has proven that AI works in commercial. The hard part now is scaling it," said Philip Poulidis , CEO and co-founder of ODAIA. "Most companies can show results on one brand, and every new brand or therapeutic area still costs another team and another build. ODAIA started by helping field teams decide where to focus. Today our platform is the commercial intelligence infrastructure that scales what's working across brand, marketing, and field teams, and across a company's whole portfolio. This round lets us go deeper with the enterprise customers we already serve and, with PHM, bring that infrastructure to more of the industry, faster."
"We have watched the ODAIA team turn predictive AI into decisions that pharma brand and field teams act on every day," said Charles Conn , co-founder and partner at Monograph Capital, which co-led ODAIA's Series B and led this round. "The ODAIA team has a track record of helping large and specialty pharma brands reach the physicians whose patients need their therapies most."
One strategy for brand, field, and marketing
Inside most pharma companies, data sits in many systems owned by separate teams, so brand, marketing, and field each work from a different picture of the same physician. Patients get missed, field and digital effort lands in the wrong places, and nobody can say with confidence what is influencing HCP decisions. ODAIA's commercial intelligence platform provides the foundation underneath. It brings disparate data, field sales activity, and digital engagement into one view of each HCP that brand, marketing, and field teams all work from.
Brand teams codify their strategy once in Brand Strategy Studio , and ODAIA's decision engines turn it into HCP-level choices about who to reach, through which channel, when, and with what message. Extending to a new brand or therapeutic area is a matter of configuration. The platform identifies physicians whose patients are likely to need a therapy, often months before a diagnosis shows up in the data. Field Intelligence delivers prioritized call plans to field teams inside their CRM, and Marketing Intelligence orchestrates individualized HCP journeys across digital and partner channels.
Every ODAIA recommendation comes with the reasoning behind it, so commercial and compliance teams can see why. Commercial leaders ask questions of their data in plain language and get finished analysis in minutes. The platform continuously measures engagement and prescription lift and feeds the results into the next decision, so teams can adjust as markets change.
Alongside the financing, ODAIA signed a commercial Platform Agreement that makes PHM, Publicis Groupe's U.S. health media agency, ODAIA's exclusive agency partner in the U.S.
ODAIA continues to work directly with pharma companies, and its platform works alongside the CRM, in-house analytics models, and data infrastructure each brand already uses. The partnership connects signals across digital media and field sales so clients can coordinate HCP engagement across both.
Founded out of the University of Toronto in 2018, ODAIA is headquartered in Toronto with an office in Boston. To learn more about ODAIA's commercial intelligence platform, visit odaia.ai .

ODAIA is the leading AI company delivering predictive commercial intelligence for pharma. By continuously turning HCP and patient signals into real-time actions, ODAIA enables commercial teams to adapt strategy as markets change and activate updated guidance directly within the systems they already use.
