Investment to Accelerate iCareManager's Mission to be the System of Record for Intellectual and Developmental Disability and Human Services Providers
iCareManager receives growth investment from Five Elms Capital to build a leading AI-native platform for intellectual and developmental disability (IDD) care providers
Funding will modernize the platform, expand AI capabilities, extend go-to-market reach, and grow the senior leadership team
High-quality customer support remains core to the strategy as iCareManager serves a growing provider base
Five Elms brings deep experience scaling vertical AI-native software businesses
COLUMBIA, Md. , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- iCareManager, a leading EHR and care management platform purpose-built for providers supporting people with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD), today announced a strategic growth investment from Five Elms Capital. The partnership will accelerate product innovation, expand AI capabilities, grow the leadership team, and extend iCareManager's reach to more provider organizations across the U.S.
Continue Reading
iCareManager
IDD providers operate in one of healthcare's most complex environments, navigating state-specific Medicaid waivers, service authorizations, billing, EVV, medication management, and compliance amid workforce shortages and financial pressure. Since 2011, iCareManager has simplified these challenges with technology built specifically for the IDD community.
iCareManager is a unified platform that connects clinical care, service delivery, compliance, workforce management, and billing for human services providers. It brings person-centered planning, eMAR, documentation, scheduling, and Medicaid billing into one view, with built-in support for state-specific rules and EVV. White-glove onboarding and ongoing support help providers adopt it with confidence.
"Over the years, we've built iCareManager with a clear purpose: to make technology work better for the people who provide support and care," said Kamal Sheikh, Co-Founder and CEO of iCareManager. "We're now entering a new era where AI will fundamentally change how people work and interact with technology. The next generation of software won't just help people manage their work; it will increasingly work alongside them. Five Elms understands what we've built, the market we serve, and where we want to go. This partnership gives us the resources and expertise to accelerate that vision, continue innovating, and bring more value to the providers who rely on us every day."
With Five Elms Capital's investment, iCareManager plans to advance the modernization of its technology platform while expanding its next generation of AI-enabled capabilities. "So much of a provider's day runs through iCareManager, from support plans and medication administration to compliance and billing, all on a single record," said Zach Gornet, Vice President at Five Elms Capital. "The AI capabilities the team is building will take real administrative weight off direct support professionals so they can spend more time with the people they serve."
Building on its integrated foundation, iCareManager is developing practical, responsible AI tools that simplify documentation, surface relevant information, and support clinical and operational decisions, reducing administrative work so staff can spend more time on quality care.
"20 years inside the daily work of IDD and assisted living providers has given iCareManager a deep understanding of the data and information behind every service delivered, and that is where AI changes everything," said Babar Nawaz, Co-Founder & COO of iCareManager. "AI will never replace the human. It will replace the admin work and the tedious work, so staff can spend their time helping individuals and residents in a much better way. With Five Elms behind us, this is a game-changing moment for iCareManager. We now have the backing to bring better, safer technology and better AI to every provider out there. The next chapter is going to be very exciting, and we are just getting started."
As iCareManager enters its next phase of growth, its mission is unchanged: giving organizations that support people with intellectual and developmental disabilities technology that simplifies operations, strengthens compliance, and frees caregivers to spend more time with the people they serve.
Austin Gideon, Principal at Five Elms Capital, commented on the investment: "Five Elms backs category-defining software built by exceptional teams, and iCareManager is exactly that. The company has become essential for agencies supporting people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. We're proud to partner with the iCareManager team on the next phase of growth."
Vista Point Advisors acted as the exclusive financial advisor to iCareManager.
About iCareManager
iCareManager is a cloud-based EHR and care management platform for IDD, assisted living, and human services providers. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Columbia, Maryland, the platform unifies care planning, documentation, eMAR, incident reporting, staff management, attendance, and billing and claims in a single system, and is extended by AI products that automate documentation, medication safety, care planning, and claims. iCareManager is SOC 2 Type II certified and HIPAA compliant. candidates.text:
CIBC Innovation Banking: Growth Financing To Support PortX’s AI-Native Banking Integration Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:46 AM
CIBC Innovation Banking: Growth Financing To Support PortX’s AI-Native Banking Integration Platform
CIBC Innovation Banking has provided growth capital financing to PortX, a Seattle-based financial technology company developing an AI-native integration platform for community banks and credit unions. The financing will support PortX’s product development and expansion as financial institutions seek more efficient ways to connect banking systems, fintech applications, and payment networks.
PortX provides application programming interface infrastructure designed to connect technologies that financial institutions use to manage accounts, process payments, and access customer information.
Its platform currently connects with more than 30 core banking systems and over 100 fintech applications.
It also supports payment connectivity involving the Automated Clearing House network, the Federal Reserve’s FedNow instant payment system, and wire transfers.
These integrations are intended to help community banks and credit unions modernize operations without replacing their existing core systems.
Smaller financial institutions frequently face challenges when adopting new technology because traditional banking platforms may require customized integrations with outside applications.
Developing and maintaining these connections can require substantial engineering resources, create additional operating expenses, and delay the introduction of new financial products.
PortX aims to address these issues through reusable infrastructure that connects multiple systems through a common integration framework.
The platform is designed to support real-time information exchange, application interoperability, and consistent data access.
PortX has also incorporated governance capabilities intended to support the adoption of AI within regulated financial institutions.
Its infrastructure allows activities to be logged, traced, and tracked, supporting oversight of automated processes and interactions across connected systems.
The company holds SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certifications, reflecting its investment in information security controls and management practices.
PortX believes these capabilities are increasingly important as banks and credit unions introduce AI tools into operations involving sensitive financial information.
The company reports that Sound Credit Union has reclaimed more than 10,000 business hours through its implementation of PortX technology.
This example highlights the potential for integrated banking infrastructure to reduce repetitive work and improve productivity.
PortX intends to use CIBC’s financing to support continued growth and develop additional platform capabilities.
The financing provides nondilutive capital, allowing the company to expand without issuing additional equity as part of the transaction.
PortX is backed by investors including Fuse, BankTech Ventures, Curql Collective, the American Bankers Association, EJF Capital, and Allied Solutions.
Its investor relationships represent participation from more than 350 financial institutions.
CIBC Innovation Banking provides financing to growth-stage technology and life sciences companies across North America.
The organization has more than $11 billion in funds managed and has supported more than 700 venture capital- and private equity-backed companies over the past six and a half years.
The investment supports PortX’s efforts to expand access to modern financial infrastructure among community banks and credit unions seeking to improve efficiency and introduce additional digital services.
KEY QUOTES:
“Community banks and credit unions have deep relationships with their customers and understand their markets uniquely well. PortX enables them to move faster and more efficiently by connecting their core systems, applications, and payment rails through a modern, API-first platform. Our customers are already seeing significant benefits, Sound Credit Union is one example of more than 10,000 business hours reclaimed. With CIBC Innovation Banking’s support, we’re accelerating our ability to help more institutions unlock similar efficiencies.”
David Wexler, CEO Of PortX
“CIBC Innovation Banking is delighted to support PortX’s growth initiatives with a substantive amount of non-dilutive capital. PortX provides community banks and credit unions with access to core and application banking platform solutions that would otherwise be costly and time consuming to build on their own. We’re excited to be alongside them in their growth journey.”
John Flemming, Managing Director Of CIBC Innovation Banking

Ring Launches With $249.99 Drone Cam And $999.99 Rover Cam For Autonomous Security
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:22 AM
Ring Launches With $249.99 Drone Cam And $999.99 Rover Cam For Autonomous Security
Ring, Amazon’s smart home security company, has announced Ring Robotics, a new category of autonomous security devices designed to patrol, investigate disturbances, and respond to potential threats across homes and businesses. The launch includes two products: Ring Drone Cam, a flying indoor security camera priced at $249.99, and Ring Rover Cam, a mobile security robot for businesses priced at $999.99.
The new product category expands Ring’s traditional security offerings, which have primarily relied on stationary cameras, video doorbells, motion sensors, and alarm systems.
Ring Robotics introduces mobile devices that can autonomously navigate indoor environments, investigate security alerts, and provide video coverage in areas that fixed cameras may not reach.
Both products are powered by AI Pilot, a proprietary navigation and intelligence system that combines cameras, computer vision models, on-device sensors, and cloud processing.
AI Pilot allows the devices to map indoor spaces, identify important locations, and navigate between designated patrol points.
During setup, users can carry Ring Drone Cam through their homes or allow Ring Rover Cam to explore a business environment autonomously.
The system analyzes the environment and generates a floor plan, automatically identifying rooms and suggesting locations that may require additional security attention.
These locations can include entrances, windows, cash registers, storage areas, and corridors.
Customers can customize patrol points and establish routes based on their security preferences.
Once a patrol begins, AI Pilot calculates a route to the selected destination while navigating around furniture, shelving, and other obstacles.
The technology is designed to reduce the manual effort associated with monitoring multiple areas of a property.
Ring Drone Cam For Residential Security
Ring Drone Cam is a flying indoor camera designed to provide security coverage throughout a home without requiring a stationary camera in every room.
The device remains docked when not in use and can be activated manually, through scheduled flights, or in response to compatible Ring security alerts.
Customers can establish custom flight routes and designate areas for the drone to inspect.
When a connected Ring camera, sensor, or alarm detects activity, Ring Drone Cam can automatically travel to previously configured patrol points.
The device provides 2K video resolution, a 148-degree field of view, and the ability to rotate 360 degrees.
Two integrated LED lights automatically activate in low-light conditions to improve visibility.
The camera integrates with existing Ring cameras, doorbells, sensors, and alarms.
Customers can also control the device through the new Alexa Home Map interface.
Ring envisions applications such as checking whether windows are closed before leaving home or investigating an unexpected security notification while traveling.
By allowing a single camera to move between rooms, Ring Drone Cam provides an alternative to installing multiple fixed indoor cameras.
The company plans to begin shipping Ring Drone Cam in the United States on January 27, 2027, at a retail price of $249.99.
The device remains subject to required Federal Communications Commission authorization before it can be offered for sale.
Ring Rover Cam For Business Security
Ring Rover Cam is a purpose-built autonomous security robot designed for commercial environments.
The product was developed partly in response to feedback from Amazon Astro customers who identified mobile security as one of the robot’s most useful capabilities.
Ring incorporated lessons from Astro while developing a device focused specifically on business security applications.
Ring Rover Cam can patrol commercial spaces, investigate disturbances, and provide video coverage throughout a property.
Business owners can send the robot to designated rooms or patrol locations through the Ring app.
Upon reaching a destination, the device performs a 360-degree scan.
Customers can also schedule recurring patrols during periods such as after closing or before opening.
When a connected Ring security device is triggered, Rover can autonomously travel to programmed locations to investigate.
The robot features an adjustable periscope camera that can extend above counters, shelving, and other obstacles.
Customers can configure the camera height for individual patrol points and save those settings for subsequent visits.
The device also includes a siren, a visible light tower, and two-way audio capabilities.
These features are designed to provide active deterrence while allowing business operators to communicate remotely.
Ring Rover Cam supports streaming and recording in up to 4K video while moving or patrolling.
Unlike security systems that record only at fixed monitoring points, Rover can capture footage continuously along its route.
The robot also supports continuous person-motion detection, including while docked.
Ring Rover Cam will begin shipping to U.S. customers on December 16, 2026, priced at $999.99.
AI Integration And Privacy Features
Both Ring Robotics devices integrate with Ring’s existing security ecosystem, providing customers with a centralized interface for managing cameras, alarms, and autonomous patrols.
The products also include privacy controls designed to indicate when recording is occurring.
Ring Drone Cam powers down while docked, with its camera disabled until a flight is activated.
Ring Rover Cam includes a Sleep Mode that retracts its periscope and disables its microphone.
Both devices feature visible recording indicators, while Rover also provides recording information through its onboard screen.

candidates.text:
Scalestack: Alysio Acquisition And Leonis-Led Funding Expand Enterprise AI Agent Controls
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 2:10 AM
Scalestack: Alysio Acquisition And Leonis-Led Funding Expand Enterprise AI Agent Controls
Scalestack has raised new funding led by Leonis Capital and acquired AI agent workspace Alysio, expanding its platform for controlling how autonomous agents access enterprise data, execute tasks and interact with business systems. Zapier, Deel and AAF participated in the financing. Scalestack will use the capital to grow its engineering and go-to-market teams and develop additional governance and orchestration capabilities.
The New York-based company provides infrastructure connecting AI agents with systems such as customer relationship management platforms, applicant tracking software, enterprise resource planning systems and data warehouses.
Its platform supplies agents with business context, applies company rules and controls what they can read, write and spend. It also records actions, changes and associated costs.
Alysio adds a workspace where agents execute tasks, extending Scalestack’s existing context and business rules capabilities into the environment where work takes place.
Scalestack says its platform already processes more than 6 million records per quarter for dozens of enterprise customers. At Typeform, it turns more than 400,000 monthly form submissions into context for downstream workflows, with reported accuracy above 90%.
DigitalOcean uses the platform to apply territory rules before information is written back to Salesforce. Recruiting company Hueman rebuilt candidate screening around workflows that apply hiring policies and record decisions, reducing time to a decision from nine days to the same day, according to the announcement.
At Clio, Scalestack connects a data lake, external data vendors, agent-based research and Salesforce. Clio has built more than 30 autonomous workflows on the platform, with business rules governing information written back to its system of record.
The next development phase includes a gateway that applies enterprise rules to requests from different agents and models, alongside infrastructure for persistent agents operating in cloud and local environments.
KEY QUOTES:
“Soon, most of the work inside any enterprise will be done by agents and, over time, no enterprise will hand that work to a model it doesn’t control. Companies will own the context and the rules their agents run on, and every action will be checked, governed and recorded, whichever model comes next. That is the layer we are building, and our customers already run on it. With Leonis, strong corporate partners, and the Alysio acquisition, we can get there faster.”
Elio Narciso, Co-Founder And CEO Of Scalestack
“As AI agents move from answering questions to taking actions, the bottleneck is shifting from model intelligence to enterprise trust and control. Every company will need a way to give agents the right context, enforce business rules and govern their actions across systems. We believe Scalestack is building a foundational layer of this new enterprise architecture, and its traction with major customers gives us conviction that this shift is already underway.”
Jay Zhao, Managing Partner Of Leonis Capital
“Agents are only as good as the data underneath them. Scalestack’s ability to turn high-volume raw data into actionable context pairs naturally with the workflows our customers run on Zapier. We’re glad to back them.”
Wade Foster, Co-Founder And CEO Of Zapier

candidates.text:
AI Mental Health Startup Siggy Launches With $6 Mn in Pre-Seed Funding
Global Digital Health News
Story By DHN Bureau
•
1 day ago
•
3 Mins Read
•
Last Updated On : 11 Nov 2026
Siggy aims to deliver personalized mental health care through a system that integrates human clinicians with AI tools for patient intake and support between appointments.
AI-enabled virtual mental health provider Siggy has launched out of stealth with $6 million in pre-seed funding to develop a continuous care platform combining therapy, prescription management and AI-powered patient support. The startup is backed by Village Global and several angel investors.
Siggy aims to deliver personalized mental health care through a system that integrates human clinicians with AI tools for patient intake and support between appointments. Its intake process is free, and patients pay only if they choose to proceed with treatment.
Patients begin with a free, anonymous conversation with Siggy’s AI, without requiring an account or login. The system retains their history, allowing them to avoid repeating information when they consult a provider. An AI-powered preliminary diagnosis is reviewed by clinicians, who then present treatment options.
After an initial call with a human provider, patients can log in to add existing providers or relatives to the system and confirm their treatment goals. Those who accept treatment meet a human clinician monthly and can engage with Siggy’s AI between visits.
The AI therapy agent draws on patients’ full histories to help them work through treatment goals, recall prescribed exercises and discuss their progress. It does not answer medical questions and directs patients to human providers for clinical guidance. Safety protocols are also in place to flag patients with higher-acuity needs to clinicians.
Siggy also connects with wearables and offers a one-minute daily check-in covering sleep, mood, physical well-being, and medication side effects. These inputs contribute to a daily Siggy Score, measured on a scale of 0 to 100 and visible to both patients and clinicians. The platform flags emerging patterns to clinicians, while weekly check-ins during the first two months allow providers to assess whether medication doses should be maintained, increased or changed.
“It can build a really detailed picture of you rather fast, and the idea is if there are behavior patterns that are recurrent…[Siggy can] begin to help people gain agency and recognize them before they happen,” Siggy co-founder and CEO Jonathan Sabbagh told Fierce Healthcare.
Sabbagh co-founded the company with Edvard Engesaeth, M.D., who serves as COO and previously co-founded Nurx. Daniel Montville, M.D., a Mayo Clinic-trained psychiatrist, is the company’s chief medical officer. Sabbagh previously spent two decades in finance before pursuing psychology and co-founding Journey Clinical, a US-based psychedelic-assisted therapy network.
The launch comes amid challenges with continuity in mental health treatment. About 16% of American adults take antidepressants, while one-fifth discontinue treatment before completing the recommended course. Siggy can prescribe medications, excluding controlled substances, and clinicians can oversee medication tapering when patients are ready.
The company is covered by major commercial payers across all 50 states, including Blue Cross Blue Shield, Aetna, UnitedHealthcare and Humana. It also accepts Medicaid, Medicare and TRICARE, and offers its services free to veterans.
In the longer term, Siggy plans to use speech analytics, laboratory results, genetic testing and biomarkers to identify other conditions, including diabetes and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). It also aims to develop neural datasets to support clinical trials for technologies such as brain implants.

Backswing Ventures Announces Investment in Ukrainian Defense Technology Company Vigilant Works
News provided by
Backswing Ventures
Nov 12, 2026, 08:30 ET

ORLANDO, Fla. , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Backswing Ventures, the defense venture capital firm, today announced its investment in Vigilant Works , a Ukrainian defense technology company developing autonomous counter-unmanned aerial systems (C-UAS), high-speed interceptor platforms, and radar-based detection capabilities designed to address increasingly sophisticated aerial threats.
Continue Reading
Backswing Ventures logo
The investment will support Vigilant Works' continued development of its autonomous guidance technologies, next-generation radar capabilities, and expansion of its operations as the company prepares to scale production and establish a broader presence across NATO-allied countries.
Backswing Ventures invests selectively in companies addressing critical challenges across defense and national security. As aerial threats continue to evolve in speed, sophistication, and scale, the ability to detect, track, and intercept them autonomously is becoming increasingly important. Vigilant Works is developing an integrated approach to counter-UAS operations, combining high-speed interception, autonomous guidance, and radar technology into a scalable defense ecosystem.
Founded by a team of engineers and defense technology entrepreneurs, Vigilant Works is developing an autonomous counter-UAS ecosystem combining interceptor platforms, proprietary autonomy technologies, and radar-based detection capabilities. Its first-generation Algiz-1 has undergone battlefield testing, providing operational experience that informs the development of its next-generation systems. The company is currently advancing Algiz-2, a next-generation interceptor capable of speeds exceeding 600 km/h and designed to address increasingly sophisticated aerial threats.
Vigilant Works has recently entered active battlefield testing of Algiz-2 and secured its first commercial agreements outside Ukraine. The company is also developing its proprietary autonomy stack and radar solutions in Ukraine, with investment capital supporting continued technology development and preparations to scale production and operations across NATO-allied countries. The company is a member of Brave1, Ukraine's defense technology coordination platform, and was previously selected for the Brave1 / Ministry of Defence EU4UA program.
"We are excited to support Vigilant Works as they continue developing and scaling their autonomous defense capabilities," said Kyle Asman , Managing Partner at Backswing Ventures. "The evolution of aerial threats is creating an increasingly urgent need for effective counter-UAS solutions. Vigilant Works has the benefit of developing its technology in an environment where these capabilities are being tested against real operational requirements. We believe the team's focus on autonomous interception, radar, and high-speed threats addresses an important and growing need across the defense ecosystem."
"We believe the next leap in counter-UAS will come from rethinking the entire interception chain, much like rocketry did decades ago. Detection, radar, autonomy, and high-speed interception cannot be developed in isolation. We're building them as one integrated system, designed from the ground up to push the boundaries of autonomous air defense," said Daniel Korogodski, CEO & Co-Founder of Vigilant Works.
"Building both the autonomy software and the interceptor platform gives us a unique advantage. We learn directly from Ukraine's best interceptor pilots, turn real-world operational experience into data, and iterate at a pace few can match. We're not just automating today's best pilots, we're building autonomy to outperform them," said Bohdan Boryslavski, CTO & Co-Founder of Vigilant Works.
Vigilant Works is continuing to expand its international footprint while preparing to scale production and operations across allied markets. The company's development efforts are focused on building an integrated autonomous counter-UAS ecosystem capable of addressing the next generation of aerial threats.
For more information, visit https://backswingventures.com/ and https://vgw.systems/ .
About Backswing Ventures
Backswing Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm investing in defense and security technology companies. The firm partners with founders building technologies critical to national security, resilience, and the future of defense.
About Vigilant Works
Vigilant Works is a Ukrainian defense technology company developing autonomous counter-unmanned aerial systems, high-speed interceptor platforms, and radar-based detection technologies. Through its Algiz interceptor platform and proprietary autonomy technologies, the company is building next-generation solutions to address evolving aerial threats and support modern air defense operations.

candidates.text:
Kutlerri.ai Raises $4 Mn to Scale AI Agents for Restaurant Businesses
Om Singh
| November 13 | Business Stories , Funding Feed
Share
Houston and Bhubaneswar-based startup Kutlerri.ai has raised $4 million in funding from Houston-based Narahari Investments as it looks to expand its artificial intelligence solutions for restaurant businesses.
The fresh capital will support the expansion of its AI Catering Sales Agent, the launch of three additional AI agents currently in beta testing, and the development of a mobile-first self-service application for restaurant operators, the startup said in a press release.
Founded in December 2025 by Kiran Rana and Payal Tripathy , Kutlerri.ai is developing AI-powered tools to help restaurants generate more sales, control operating expenses and improve profitability. Ankit Narain and Rishabh Srivastav are also part of the founding team.
Unlike conventional software providers that charge fixed subscription fees, Kutlerri.ai follows a performance-linked pricing model. Restaurants are charged based on the additional revenue generated or costs saved through its products.
AI Agent Helps Restaurants Find Catering Customers
Kutlerri.ai’s first commercially available product, the AI Catering Sales Agent, focuses on helping restaurants grow their catering businesses.
The agent identifies potential catering customers within a 30-mile radius of a restaurant and reaches out to them through emails, text messages and phone calls. It also helps restaurants convert incoming enquiries into catering orders.
The product was developed in collaboration with RASA, a five-location fast-casual restaurant group operating in the Washington DC region.
According to Kutlerri.ai, its AI agent helped RASA generate $450,000 in additional catering revenue over a 10-month period. The startup said the revenue was more than 10 times the amount RASA paid for the service, without requiring the restaurant group to hire additional sales personnel.
Plans to Expand Product Portfolio and Team
Kutlerri.ai currently has one commercially available product, three AI agents undergoing beta testing and two more in development.
The latest funding will help the company accelerate product development, expand its teams and bring additional AI-powered solutions to restaurant operators.
The startup has more than 10 signed customers in the US, which remains its primary market. Its product development and engineering operations are based in Bhubaneswar, while it also maintains an office in Houston.
Alongside its US expansion, Kutlerri.ai is exploring business opportunities in India and other markets.

candidates.text:
Google: Gemini 4 Hydrogen Launches With Faster Agentic AI, 1 Million-Token Context Window, And New Multi-Model Orchestration
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 7:36 AM
Google: Gemini 4 Hydrogen Launches With Faster Agentic AI, 1 Million-Token Context Window, And New Multi-Model Orchestration
Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new artificial intelligence model designed to deliver faster execution, improved reasoning, and greater efficiency across software development, enterprise workflows, and everyday AI applications. The model features a 1 million-token context window, four adjustable reasoning levels, and expanded capabilities for autonomous AI agents, while Google is also introducing a multi-model orchestration system that coordinates different Gemini models within a single workflow.
Announced on November 12, 2026, Gemini 4 Hydrogen joins Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon models, which are designed for more demanding reasoning tasks.
While Carbon and Argon focus on complex problems requiring deeper analysis, Hydrogen emphasizes rapid execution across coding, research, data analysis, and other agentic workflows.
Google is making Hydrogen available across Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, Google Search, and Google Antigravity for eligible paid subscribers.
The company has priced Hydrogen at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, with flat pricing across its entire 1 million-token context window.
Google says Hydrogen achieves a score of 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high reasoning setting, compared with 50 for Gemini 4 Argon. Hydrogen reaches 54 at its highest reasoning setting, known as xhigh.
New Orchestrator Coordinates Multiple Gemini Models
One of the most significant additions accompanying Hydrogen is Orchestrator, a new capability within Google Antigravity that dynamically switches between AI models during a single development session.
The technology is designed to use different models for different stages of a task rather than relying on one model throughout an entire workflow.
For example, Gemini 4 Carbon can handle complex architectural decisions or coordinate a development project, while Hydrogen performs code generation, testing, debugging, and verification.
Google says this approach allows developers to combine the reasoning capabilities of its frontier models with Hydrogen’s execution efficiency.
In Terminal-Bench 4.0 testing, Orchestrator achieved task success rates approaching those of Carbon while consuming an average of 24% less quota and completing tasks 19% faster.
The system also supports parallel AI agents operating across isolated workspaces.
These agents can work simultaneously on different parts of a software development project, potentially reducing execution time and resource consumption.
Google believes this multi-model approach can help organizations optimize AI workloads based on task complexity, latency requirements, and operating costs.
Major Improvements Over Gemini 3.8 Flash
Hydrogen represents a significant upgrade over Google’s previous Gemini 3.8 Flash model.
At its default high reasoning setting, Hydrogen completes tasks approximately 2.5 times faster while improving its Terminal-Bench 4.1 score from 18.2% to 57%, according to Google’s evaluations.
The company also reported that Hydrogen reduces fabricated claims by more than fivefold compared with Gemini 3.8 Flash.
The new model is designed to respond more effectively when tools fail, searches return no results, or workflows encounter unexpected obstacles.
For software development, Hydrogen supports repository analysis, issue resolution, debugging, code generation, and iterative testing.
Google says the model can identify and repair problems while limiting unnecessary modifications to unrelated parts of a codebase.
Its ability to perform multiple file-reading and search operations in parallel is intended to improve efficiency when working with large software repositories.
In early partner evaluations involving complex graphs, SQL, and data-intensive enterprise applications, Hydrogen completed tasks between two and 2.8 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash while reducing token usage by 12% to 23%.
Performance Across Agentic AI And Professional Workflows
Google reported improvements across benchmarks measuring autonomous execution, technical reasoning, and professional knowledge work.
Hydrogen ranks fifth on Agent Arena, a live benchmark assessing AI agents performing open-ended tasks.
On HLE-Diamond, a benchmark measuring advanced domain reasoning, the model achieved a score of 58.8%.
Hydrogen also achieved 52.3% on Vals Tax Agent Bench, ranking first overall, and 55.8% on Vals Legal Research Bench, tying for first place.
Google reported that the model leads its class on AutomationBench-AA, which evaluates agentic automation capabilities.
These results reflect Google’s efforts to position Hydrogen for enterprise applications requiring both technical reasoning and reliable execution.
Potential use cases include software engineering, business research, financial analysis, legal research, and workflows involving multiple connected applications.
1 Million-Token Input And Output Capabilities
Hydrogen supports a native 1 million-token input context window and up to 1 million output tokens.
These capabilities are intended to help the model process large volumes of information and produce extensive structured results.
Google says Hydrogen can analyze complex PDFs, spreadsheets, charts, audio, and recorded video while generating reports and other deliverables grounded in source materials.
On the Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark, Hydrogen achieved a score of 53.4%, outperforming other evaluated models on end-to-end tasks involving complex visual files.
The model also scored 71.6% on Agents’ Last Exam version 1.1, a benchmark focused on professional workflows.

candidates.snippet:
Erie Strategic Ventures, the corporate venture capital arm of Erie Insurance, has announced investments in Blitzy and HiddenLayer, two technology companies focused on enterprise AI infrastructure, software modernization, and artificial intelligence security. The investments expand Erie Strategic Ventures' portfolio of companies developing technologies that can help organizations deploy, manage, and secure AI applications.
The post Erie Strategic Ventures: Investments In Blitzy And HiddenLayer To Advance Enterprise AI Infrastructure And Security appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Erie Strategic Ventures: Investments In Blitzy And HiddenLayer To Advance Enterprise AI Infrastructure And Security
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 4:15 PM
Erie Strategic Ventures: Investments In Blitzy And HiddenLayer To Advance Enterprise AI Infrastructure And Security
Erie Strategic Ventures, the corporate venture capital arm of Erie Insurance, has announced investments in Blitzy and HiddenLayer, two technology companies focused on enterprise AI infrastructure, software modernization, and artificial intelligence security. The investments expand Erie Strategic Ventures’ portfolio of companies developing technologies that can help organizations deploy, manage, and secure AI applications.
Blitzy provides an autonomous software development platform designed to modernize large enterprise codebases through coordinated AI agents. HiddenLayer develops security technology that protects generative, predictive, and agentic AI systems throughout their lifecycles.
The investments reflect Erie Insurance’s continued exploration of AI technologies that could support its operations, independent insurance agents, and policyholders.
Erie Strategic Ventures was launched in August 2022 to invest in companies operating across the personal and commercial insurance value chain, as well as adjacent technology markets.
The venture capital program is operated with support from Cerity Partners Ventures, which helps corporations manage strategic investment initiatives.
Through the program, Erie Insurance combines capital investment with opportunities for technology collaboration and business development.
Blitzy Focuses On Autonomous Software Development
Blitzy develops an AI-powered software engineering platform intended to help enterprises modernize legacy systems and accelerate new application development.
The company’s technology uses a proprietary ontology and graph-based architecture to develop a detailed understanding of large software codebases.
This approach is designed to provide AI systems with contextual information about how applications, components, and dependencies interact.
Using that information, Blitzy coordinates thousands of AI agents operating in parallel to perform software development tasks.
The platform is intended to address challenges associated with maintaining and updating complex enterprise software environments.
Large organizations frequently operate systems that have accumulated years of modifications, integrations, and dependencies.
Modernizing these environments can require significant engineering resources because changes to one component may affect other applications or business processes.
Blitzy’s approach seeks to improve efficiency by enabling AI agents to analyze software architecture and coordinate development activities.
The company also supports the creation of new software products, allowing engineering teams to use autonomous agents for development workflows.
For insurance companies and other financial services organizations, software modernization can be particularly important because many essential business processes depend on established technology systems.
Erie Strategic Ventures’ investment provides exposure to technology intended to improve enterprise software development and infrastructure management.
HiddenLayer Develops Security For AI Applications And Agents
HiddenLayer focuses on protecting AI systems against cyber threats throughout the development and deployment lifecycle.
Its platform supports security capabilities involving AI discovery, supply chain protection, attack simulation, and runtime defense.
These technologies are designed to help organizations identify and manage vulnerabilities associated with AI applications and infrastructure.
HiddenLayer’s platform addresses generative AI, predictive AI, and autonomous AI agents.
As enterprises integrate AI into business operations, they face security challenges that differ from those associated with conventional software systems.
AI applications can introduce risks involving model manipulation, unauthorized access, sensitive information exposure, and malicious interactions.
HiddenLayer develops tools intended to help security teams identify these risks and establish protective controls.
Its technology is supported by patented capabilities and adversarial AI research.
The platform includes tools for discovering AI systems within an organization and evaluating security weaknesses.
Attack simulation capabilities allow security teams to assess how AI applications may respond to malicious activity.
Runtime protection is designed to help defend deployed AI systems against threats during operation.
HiddenLayer also supports organizations seeking to protect intellectual property and meet applicable regulatory requirements.
The investment aligns with Erie Insurance’s interest in evaluating technologies that can support secure enterprise AI adoption.
Expanding Erie Insurance’s AI Innovation Strategy
Erie Strategic Ventures was established to identify emerging technologies with potential relevance to the insurance industry.
The fund invests across the personal and commercial insurance value chain while also evaluating adjacent markets.
Its investments in Blitzy and HiddenLayer reflect two different areas of enterprise AI adoption.
Blitzy addresses the development and modernization of the software infrastructure that supports business operations.
HiddenLayer focuses on protecting AI applications and systems against emerging security threats.
Together, the companies represent complementary aspects of enterprise AI infrastructure.
Erie Insurance Senior Vice President for Next Level Innovation Keith Kennedy said the company is continuing to explore ways to apply AI safely.
The investments provide Erie with opportunities to engage with companies developing technologies that could influence how enterprises build and secure AI systems.
The company may also work with portfolio businesses as a customer or strategic partner.

Pune Startup Froncort.AI Gets $2.3 Mn Google.org Grant For AI Disease Screening App
Froncort.AI, a Pune-based healthcare AI startup, has received a $2.3 million grant from Google.org to build a mobile tool that tells frontline health workers which households to screen first for tuberculosis and other infections.
The grant comes with $200,000 in Google Cloud credits and pro bono engineering support. It is Google.org’s second grant to the company, after funding a validation study of its AI-NETRA platform in 2025.
How the Company Was Selected
Froncort.AI is one of 15 organisations worldwide picked for the Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation, a $30 million programme whose recipients were announced on 15 September.
Read More: Sachin Tendulkar Backs Waste Management Startup Recykal
Funding Confido Health Raises $12.5 Million To Automate Healthcare Administration With AI Funding Prodoc AI Raises Seed Funding From Dr A. Velumani Family Office
Google.org said winners were chosen from more than 2,600 proposals. Froncort.AI is one of four recipients in the health category, alongside Flexbone, Helium Health Foundation and the University of Warwick.
Read More: How to Choose the Best Travel Agency in Jaipur for a Memorable Rajasthan Holiday
That ratio explains why the grant matters more than its size. Being selected from 2,600 applicants is third-party validation that a health ministry or a state programme can cite.
What mAI-NETRA Does
The grant funds mAI-NETRA, a mobile version of the company’s public health platform.
Froncort.AI’s system combines government health programme data with satellite-derived insights from Google’s Earth AI models. It also weighs local indicators such as settlement density, land use, rainfall and flood exposure.
From that, it flags higher-risk areas within 300-metre zones and turns them into ranked work plans, household clusters and routes that health workers can follow on field visits.
The Froncort.AI app works offline with automatic sync and offers multilingual voice guidance. Matters in districts where connectivity is patchy.
Why Routing Beats Testing Alone
India’s tuberculosis programme already has tests, drugs and reporting systems. What it lacks is a way to decide where to spend a health worker’s day.
Sending a worker street by street in a high-burden district is expensive and random. Sending the same worker to a ranked cluster of households with recent flooding and dense housing is a different use of the same salary.
Froncort.AI already has TB and malaria modules are already in place. The platform is being built to cover six diseases: TB, leprosy, malaria, dengue, cholera and leptospirosis.
What the Founder Says
“The world does not lack experts. It lacks their reach,” said Ujjwal Rao, founder and chief executive of Froncort.AI. He described AI-NETRA as putting that expertise in the health worker’s hands at the door, showing where to go, whom to screen and when.
India’s health system already collects enormous amounts of data through national programmes. The gap is turning that data into a route a health worker can follow on a Tuesday morning.
Satellite inputs add something the health records cannot: environmental risk. Flood exposure and land use predict leptospirosis and vector-borne outbreaks before a single case is reported.
Froncort.AI’s constraint is field support. A model that guides screening only helps if district officers trust it and if ASHA workers can use it on low-end phones.
The programme is a useful test of whether philanthropy can fund public health AI at the pilot stage, where venture capital rarely goes.
What to Watch
Three things will decide whether this scales. The first is state adoption, because a central pilot that never reaches district workflows changes nothing.
The second is field accuracy. A routing model that sends workers to the wrong households wastes the scarcest resource in the system. Is their time.
The third is data integration. The platform is only as good as the government datasets it can legally and technically connect to. That varies by state.

AI video production startup Lemonpeel has raised $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Rukam Sitara and angel investors. The startup is part of the NVIDIA Inception, AWS Startups, Microsoft for Sta
Gyan Vardhan

14:09

New Update
AI video production startup Lemonpeel has raised $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Rukam Sitara and angel investors. The startup is part of the NVIDIA Inception, AWS Startups, Microsoft for Startups and Claude Startup programmes.
The proceeds will be utilized to develop multi-agent platforms for video creation, editing, quality checks and delivery, marketing and go-to-market capabilities to reach more enterprise creative teams, and build intellectual property around faces and creative workflows, Lemonpeel said in a press release.
Co-founded in Sep. last year by Hardik Goyal, Riddhiman Pal and Abhinav Nikam, Lemonpeel builds AI video production infrastructure for enterprise creative teams that brings together video creation, editing, quality checks and delivery through specialised agents and a model-agnostic engine. It works with customers in India and the UAE.
The Mumbai-based startup combines specialised AI agents with a model-agnostic engine that routes tasks across more than 300 models, including Veo, Kling and Seedance. A quality control layer helps maintain consistency in characters, logos and products.
The platform supports translation and subtitles in more than 100 languages and can also be used from inside AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. The company is turning the production steps its team currently handles into product capabilities.
Lemonpeel is focused on media execution end-to-end: editing, maintaining visual consistency and preparing content for approval at scale. This is particularly relevant to films and campaigns that need multiple regional language versions and formats. The company plans to expand into MENA, US and Canada.
It competes with the other players in this space such as Runway, Google Flow, Higgsfield, Magnific, Flora, Weavy, and Invideo.
Startups in this space are developing AI-led platforms that automate video production workflows, generate multilingual and personalised videos, enable automated editing, and ensure quality and consistency before content is delivered across digital channels.
Meanwhile, Clueso raised $10 million in a Series A round in Oct. this year, led by Dharana Capital, to strengthen its AI agents and automate enterprise video creation and editing workflows.
TrueFan AI also secured $10 million in Series A funding in June this year, led by Baring Private Equity Partners India and Z3Partners, to scale its enterprise video-generation infrastructure. Other emerging players include CRAON, which raised pre-seed funding in May 2026 to develop its prompt-led AI video editing platform.

AI infra startup JohnAIC raises $1.9 Mn in pre-seed round
Bengaluru-based sovereign AI infrastructure startup JohnAIC has raised $1.9 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Crane Venture Partners, with participation from Neon Fund.
Shashank Pathak
17 Nov 2026
09:38
IST
Follow Us
New Update
Bengaluru-based sovereign AI infrastructure startup JohnAIC has raised $1.9 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Crane Venture Partners, with participation from Neon Fund.
The proceeds will be used to expand its manufacturing, configuration and supply capabilities for AI servers. It aims to scale production capacity to up to 100 AI servers per month.
Founded by Sasank Chilamkurthy, JohnAIC builds on-premise AI infrastructure combining GPU servers, inference software, optimised open-source models and local data management. Its integrated systems are designed to help enterprises deploy AI within their own environments while retaining control over computing resources, models and data.
The startup serves public sector organisations and large enterprises, including banks, healthcare companies and public sector undertakings (PSUs). For BFSI institutions, its systems enable AI deployment behind organisational firewalls and are designed to support DPDP and RBI requirements.
JohnAIC is also working with Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL). Its server infrastructure has been deployed for routine operational surveys, converting field data into real-time insights.
The company is expanding its factory and supply chain infrastructure to address demand from Indian enterprises building private AI environments and neocloud infrastructure.
